column1: You scrape the clay off and discard it, leaving you with a gleaming silver ear! Beautifully done! With an ear like this, you could (dare I say it) RULE THE WORLD! Nyah-ha-ha-ha!
column2: 你把黏土刮掉丟棄，留下一只閃閃發亮的銀耳朵！做得漂亮！有這麼一只耳朵，你（我敢說）簡直能統治世界！哈哈哈哈！

column1: Your "ear mold" (yuch!) is now filled with the melted silver from your award medallion. (Y'know, they're NOT going to send Srini another medallion!)
column2: 你的「耳模」（噁！）現在灌滿了獎章融化後的銀水。（你知道嗎，他們才不會再寄一面獎章給斯里尼呢！）

column1: Those two just don't go together.
column2: 這兩樣東西根本兜不起來。

column1: You try tearing open a sack with your bare hands, but in the never-ending battle of Man vs. Burlap, you lose.
column2: 你試著徒手撕開麻袋，但在這場「人類對麻布」的永恆戰爭中，你輸了。

column1: You intended to order one sack of baking soda. Owing to an administrative error, you are now the proud possessor of one hundred forty-four sacks of baking soda... and the superhuman strength required to carry it around. How gross!
column2: 你原本只想訂一袋小蘇打粉。由於行政疏失，你現在自豪地擁有一百四十四袋小蘇打粉……以及扛著它們到處走的超人力氣。真夠噁心的！

column1: With muscles bulging from years of grappling with childproof caps, you deftly wield the church key and wrench the tops from all the beer bottles.
column2: 多年來與兒童安全瓶蓋搏鬥練出的肌肉派上用場，你俐落地揮動開瓶器，把所有啤酒瓶蓋都扭開了。

column1: Sorry, Mr. Anheuser only recently developed the bottle-cap. Mr. Busch hasn't begun to think about the twist-off tops yet!
column2: 抱歉，Anheuser先生才剛研發出瓶蓋，Busch先生根本還沒想到旋轉式瓶蓋這回事！

column1: This is your case of Loebrau, "The Beer that Gave St. Louis Blues." All 24 bottles are tightly stoppered with those newfangled metal bottle-caps.
column2: 這是你那箱「羅布勞」啤酒，「讓聖路易憂鬱的啤酒」。24瓶全都用那種新奇的金屬瓶蓋緊緊封著。

column1: You reach inside your old boots and find... the rotting remains of a pair of nasty old Odor Beaters!
column2: 你伸手探進舊靴子裡，找到……一雙噁心舊除臭墊的腐朽殘骸！

column1: Sigh. These passenger pigeon-skin boots bring back memories... of the days before Kenny the Kid gave you an ear job.
column2: 唉。這雙旅鴿皮靴讓你想起往事……小鬼肯尼幫你「動耳朵手術」之前的日子。

column1: What are you trying to do, open the bullets? Not a smart endeavor!
column2: 你想幹嘛，把子彈打開嗎？這可不是聰明的舉動！

column1: Tons o' ammo! Hot lead! Hollow-points! Dum-dums!
column2: 一堆彈藥！燙手的鉛彈！空尖彈！達姆彈！

column1: You try to mold the wax with your bare hands, but the wax is just a bit too stiff to handle. (A feeling not wholly unfamiliar to you!)
column2: 你試著徒手捏塑蠟塊，但蠟塊硬得有點難處理。（這種感覺你並不陌生！）

column1: With your newly-acquired whittlin' skills, you carve the candle wax into the shape of an ear, one that should theoretically attach snugly to the remains of your original ear. But now look at the gunk on Willy's knife!
column2: 憑著新學會的削木手藝，你把蠟燭雕成一只耳朵的形狀，理論上該能緊密接到你原本耳朵的殘餘部位上。可是你看看威利刀上沾的那些黏糊糊的東西！

column1: I'll toss this knife over here where Willy might find it. He'll probably think he dropped it here!
column2: 我把這把刀丟在這裡，威利應該會找到。他大概會以為是自己掉在這裡的！

column1: Yeah. Sure.
column2: 對啊，可不是嘛。

column1: This puddle of candle wax from the Church is suitable for chewing, but it tends to lose that "Churchy" flavor after only a couple of minutes!
column2: 這灘從教堂弄來的蠟燭蠟很適合拿來嚼，不過才嚼個幾分鐘就會失去那股「教堂味」！

column1: You search for something inside the charcoal, but there's nothing to be found.
column2: 你在木炭裡翻找，但什麼也沒找到。

column1: You swiped this handful of charcoal from the blacksmith's forge. (Remember to wash your hands when you're finished playing the game!)
column2: 你從鐵匠的熔爐裡順了一把木炭。（玩完遊戲後記得洗手！）

column1: The Church key is solid and heavy and refuses to bend.
column2: 教堂鑰匙又硬又重，怎麼也彎不了。

column1: Nobody will miss this key to the Church, since the Church is never locked anyway. But doesn't it have an unusual shape?
column2: 沒人會發現這把教堂鑰匙不見了，反正教堂從來不上鎖。不過它的形狀是不是挺特別的？

column1: You turn the claim check over, searching for a locker combination, but there's nothing written on the other side.
column2: 你把提貨單翻過來，想找置物櫃密碼，但背面什麼也沒寫。

column1: It's a tattered, well-worn claim check, nearly brown with age.
column2: 這是一張破舊不堪的提貨單，因為年代久遠幾乎泛成褐色。

column1: You try to shape the clay, but you're no sculptor. (Maybe you should take up whittling instead!)
column2: 你試著捏塑黏土，但你不是雕塑家的料。（或許你該改行去削木頭！）

column1: Who would steal a handful of clay from a gravesite? If you only had some eye of newt and tongue of bat...
column2: 誰會從墓地偷一把黏土？要是你有蠑螈眼和蝙蝠舌就好了……

column1: You poke around in the gun cleaning kit, but you find nothing useful.
column2: 你在槍械清潔工具裡翻了翻，但沒找到什麼有用的東西。

column1: Hey! Maybe a fella could use this for cleanin' guns?!
column2: 嘿！說不定這玩意兒可以拿來清槍呢？！

column1: Duh!
column2: 廢話！

column1: Sheriff Shift's was so nice to "give" you his gun-cleaning kit. He may be a low-down, evil, corrupt, two-timin' no-good varmint, but he's got the cleanest pistol in town... or so says Madame Ovaree!
column2: 席夫特警長人真好，「送」了你他的槍械清潔工具。他或許是個卑鄙、邪惡、貪腐、腳踏兩條船的爛東西，但他那把手槍是全鎮最乾淨的……至少歐薇莉夫人是這麼說的！

column1: You search through the clothes and see your pants, your jacket, your gun belt, and your hat. All are in apparently still in good condition!
column2: 你翻了翻這些衣服，看到你的褲子、外套、槍帶和帽子，看起來都還保存得不錯！

column1: These are your old ex-gunslinging clothes, including your "Good Guy Model" hat! (Mr. Pharkas's Wardrobe by Festus Lauren of Cheyenne.)
column2: 這些是你以前當槍手時穿的舊衣服，還包括那頂「好人款」帽子！（法卡斯先生的行頭由夏安市的費斯特斯·勞倫提供。）

column1: Only a logger stirs his coffee with his thumb.
column2: 只有伐木工人才會用大拇指攪咖啡。

column1: Mmm, there's nothing like a steaming hot cuppa joe from Mom's Cafe, brewed from mountain-grown beans from the steep-sloped hills of Jamaica! Much better than those shoddy trench-grown coffee beans from the shallow-sloped ditches of Peoria!
column2: 嗯，沒有什麼比得上老媽餐館那杯熱騰騰的咖啡，用牙買加陡峭山坡上種的豆子沖泡而成！比皮奧里亞淺溝裡種的那種劣質咖啡豆好太多了！

column1: You turn the prescription over, looking for a hint of some sort, but there's nothing to see on the other side.
column2: 你把處方箋翻過來，想找點什麼線索，但背面什麼都沒有。

column1: You study Madame Ovaree's prescription, fully amended and corrected by Doc Gillespie: "Madame Ovaree, Estrosterane, 1 paper each morning after."
column2: 你仔細研讀歐薇莉夫人的處方箋，已經過大夫吉勒斯比完全修正：「歐薇莉夫人，雌固烷，每日晨後一包。」

column1: Madame Ovaree, Estrosterane, 1 paper each morning after.
column2: 「歐薇莉夫人，雌固烷，每日晨後一包。」

column1: You dip your finger into the deflatulizer and lick it off. Mmmm! Aminophyllic Citrate really hits the spot!
column2: 你把手指伸進消脹劑裡沾一下再舔掉。嗯嗯！檸檬酸胺非林真是對味！

column1: Taa-daa, your latest invention: Equine Deflatulizer, an exclusive blend of secret ingredients guaranteed to neutralize noxious methane emissions from the lower gastro-intestinal tract of Equus caballus. In other words, it's Gastroentrological- Veterinarian-In-A-Drum!
column2: 鏘鏘，你最新的發明：馬用消脹劑，獨門秘方調配，保證中和馬（Equus caballus）下消化道排放的有害沼氣。換句話說，這是一整桶的「腸胃科獸醫」！

column1: You turn the key over carefully, but it reveals nothing new.
column2: 你小心把鑰匙翻過來看，但沒發現什麼新東西。

column1: This is the key to your safe deposit box, pried from the cold, rigid fingers of your dead pal Phil.
column2: 這是你保險箱的鑰匙，從你死去的老友菲爾冰冷僵硬的手指間撬出來的。

column1: You attempt to do that key-bending routine you used to know when you were a kid, but somehow you've lost your touch.
column2: 你想耍出小時候會的那套彎鑰匙把戲，但不知怎地手感已經生疏了。

column1: This is the key to your roll-top desk.
column2: 這是你捲蓋書桌的鑰匙。

column1: The door key's got a nice heft to it!
column2: 這把門鑰匙拿在手上挺有份量的！

column1: Hey. This looks just like the key to the front door of my pharmacy!
column2: 嘿，這看起來就像我藥局前門的鑰匙！

column1: You open the bottle and take a long, deep whiff. The cilia lining your nose curl up and fall out, your sinuses start to drain, your eyes begin to water, and your face turns red. Say, this stuff is REALLY effective!
column2: 你打開瓶子深深吸了一大口。鼻腔裡的纖毛捲起脫落，鼻竇開始流通，眼睛開始泛淚，臉也紅了起來。哎呀，這玩意兒還真有效！

column1: Dad Gumm's Magic Elixir is "Positively guaranteed to cure myopia, melancholia, the vapors, congestion, consumption, malaria, piles, shingles, rickets, leprosy, bubonic plague, gout, bursitis, arthritis, and the galloping cruds. 190 proof." Obviously, "Truth in Advertising" is still years in the future!
column2: 「老爹岡氏神奇萬靈藥」號稱「保證能治好近視、憂鬱、歇斯底里、鼻塞、肺癆、瘧疾、痔瘡、帶狀皰疹、佝僂病、痲瘋、鼠疫、痛風、滑囊炎、關節炎，以及急性下瀉。酒精濃度190proof。」看樣子，「廣告不實」這種事還要等好幾年才會出現！

column1: You cleverly shove your finger into a bottle and get it stuck there. You manage to twist it out, but not before popping a half-dozen knuckles. Next stop, Arthritis City!
column2: 你自作聰明地把手指插進瓶子裡，結果卡住了。你總算把手指扭出來，但代價是崩了六個指關節。下一站，關節炎之城！

column1: Now that the snails have been eradicated, you're left with a lot of empty beer bottles. Unfortunately, the California Bottle Redemption Act won't be made into law for another 100 years. (After all, that bill was only introduced five years ago!)
column2: 現在蝸牛都清光了，你手上剩下一堆空啤酒瓶。可惜「加州瓶罐回收法」還要再等一百年才會立法。（畢竟這法案才剛提出五年而已！）

column1: You gingerly examine the clay "negative" mold.
column2: 你小心翼翼地檢查這個黏土「陰模」。

column1: (TO SELF) Pretty decent piece of craftsmanship, even if you do say so yourself!
column2: （自言自語）手藝相當不錯嘛，雖然是自己講的！

column1: It's an empty clay mold of an ear.
column2: 這是一個空的耳朵黏土模。

column1: Don't open it! You'll release its precious contents (and probably kill a few locals!).
column2: 別打開它！你會把裡面珍貴的東西放出來（大概還會害死幾個當地人！）。

column1: It's a bagful of something which does NOT meet California Emissions Standards!
column2: 這一袋東西絕對不符合加州排放標準！

column1: You peek inside the bag. Nope, nothing in there yet!
column2: 你往袋子裡瞄了一眼。沒有，裡面還什麼都沒有！

column1: Chester Field's sturdy brown paper bags are suitable for penny candy, two-penny nails, and half-pint containers of Danny's Sourmash-Flavored Yogurt (the kind with the whisky on the bottom!).
column2: 切斯特·菲爾德的堅固牛皮紙袋適合裝一分錢糖果、兩分錢釘子，還有丹尼的酸醪風味優格半品脫裝（就是底下沉著威士忌的那種！）。

column1: You adjust the leather strap just so.
column2: 你把皮帶調整得剛剛好。

column1: Congratulations on making this homemade gas mask. Devilishly good work!
column2: 恭喜你做出這個自製防毒面具，手藝好得邪門！

column1: You're unwilling to touch it any more than necessary.
column2: 你實在不想多碰它一下。

column1: How can we put this delicately? It's a fragrant, freshly-baked, road apple.
column2: 該怎麼委婉地說呢？這是一坨香噴噴、剛出爐的馬糞。

column1: You touch the ice pick to your finger. That thing's sharp! And MEAN!
column2: 你把冰錐碰了一下手指。這東西真利！而且很兇！

column1: You swiped the town ice pick from out back o' the saloon. (Now no one will be able to pick their teeth!)
column2: 你從酒館後面順走了鎮上的冰錐。（現在沒人能剔牙了！）

column1: You can't get it open! Damn these childproof tins!
column2: 你打不開它！這些兒童安全罐頭真該死！

column1: You hope you got this prescription right! (After all, pharmacology is an art, not an exact science!)
column2: 你希望這張處方箋開對了！（畢竟藥學是門藝術，不是精確科學！）

column1: Click here to change your cursor into a Hand, then click the Hand on one of the Inventory objects to do something to it.
column2: 點這裡把游標變成「手」，再點物品欄裡的物品，就能對它做點什麼。

column1: Click here to change your cursor into a Question Mark, then pass the Question Mark over the other icons to learn how they work.
column2: 點這裡把游標變成「問號」，再把問號移到其他圖示上，就能了解它們的用法。

column1: Click here to change your cursor into the Look cursor, then click the Look cursor on the Inventory objects to examine them more closely.
column2: 點這裡把游標換成「看」游標，再用它點物品欄裡的東西，就能仔細端詳。

column1: Click here to close this Inventory window and return to the game.
column2: 點這裡關閉這個物品欄視窗，回到遊戲。

column1: Click here to see more Inventory objects.
column2: 點這裡查看更多物品欄裡的物品。

column1: To use an Inventory item, click here to change your cursor into an Arrow, then click the Arrow on the item you wish to use. The Arrow will change into that item. You may then click the item on other Inventory objects or on "OK" to use that item in the game.
column2: 要使用物品欄裡的物品，先點這裡把游標變成「箭頭」，再點你想用的物品，箭頭就會變成那個物品。接著你可以把它點在其他物品欄物品上，或點「確定」在遊戲中使用該物品。

column1: You close the knife and open it again. Smooth. Silent. Deadly. (Stolen.)
column2: 你把刀合上又打開。滑順，無聲，致命。（偷來的。）

column1: These Confederate Army pen knife replicas are becoming quite popular among the more sophisticated whittlers.
column2: 這種南軍小刀複製品，在講究品味的削木愛好者之間越來越受歡迎。

column1: You make sure the ladder's rungs are nice and tight. (A feeling not wholly unfamiliar to Doc Gillespie!)
column2: 你確認梯子的橫檔又緊又牢。（這種感覺大夫吉勒斯比並不陌生！）

column1: What sort of cad would steal a ladder from the school playground? (Oh, you would!)
column2: 什麼樣的無賴才會從學校操場偷梯子？（喔，你就是啊！）

column1: You have no reason to untie your adroitly-constructed lasso!
column2: 你沒理由把這條巧手打造的套索解開！

column1: I never met a lasso I didn't like!
column2: 我從沒見過不喜歡的套索！

column1: You test the leather strap. Wow, it IS durable!
column2: 你測試了一下皮帶。哇，還真耐用！

column1: A rugged leather strap... your mind reels with the possibilities!
column2: 一條粗獷的皮帶……你的腦袋開始天馬行空了！

column1: You turn the paper over, looking for a return address or something, but there isn't one.
column2: 你把紙翻過來，想找寄件地址之類的東西，但什麼都沒有。

column1: You received this letter a few years back from your recently dearly-departed friend, Phil Graves:
column2: 這封信是幾年前收到的，寄信人是你最近剛過世的朋友，菲爾·葛雷夫斯：

column1:
Dear Freddy, Thank you so very kindly for your recent gracious hospitality during my recent convalescence. The floor of your workroom proved a comfortable bed, and the stale Pharmacy goods you fed me staved off starvation quite adequately.	「親愛的佛萊迪，非常感謝你在我養病期間如此殷勤款待。你工作間的地板證明是張舒適的床，你餵我吃的過期藥局貨也足夠讓我不至於餓死。
I must admit to being a little curious of your request that I retain your safety-deposit key for you; I cannot imagine what you have secured in that bank vault that could create such strong feelings of both revulsion and endearment.
column2: 「老實說，我對你要我替你保管保險箱鑰匙這件事有點好奇；我實在想不出你那銀行金庫裡藏了什麼，竟能同時讓人又噁心又依依不捨。

column1:
However, I have done as you asked and taken your key with me. I vow to you I will never return this key to you nor even allow it within your sight. I further swear to keep it with me wherever I go.	「不過，我還是照你的要求，把鑰匙隨身帶走了。我向你發誓，絕不會把這把鑰匙還給你，也絕不讓它出現在你眼前。我更發誓，無論走到哪裡都會帶著它。
On this you have my word of honor, for I am, Ever your friend, Philip D. Graves"
column2: 「以上所言，我以人格擔保。你永遠的朋友，菲利普·D·葛雷夫斯」

column1: It's solid silver! You can't bend it, break it, or scratch it.
column2: 純銀打造！你彎不了它，也弄不斷、刮不花它。

column1: It's Srini's 99.9% silver medallion, awarded to him by the American Society of Salves, Holistic Ointments, Liniments and Emollients Salesmen. (Think about it!)
column2: 這是斯里尼的99.9%純銀勳章，由「美國藥膏、順勢療法軟膏、擦劑與潤膚劑推銷員協會」頒發給他。（自己想想這縮寫吧！）

column1: I think I'll count my money.
column2: 我想我該來數數自己的錢了。

column1: Never do that when you're sitting at the table. (There'll be time enough for counting when the game is done.)
column2: 坐在牌桌上千萬別這樣做。（等牌局結束後有的是時間數錢。）

column1: Finally, you get your four dollars and eighty-seven cents! Smithie's pharmacy tab is paid in full at last!
column2: 終於，你拿到你的四塊八毛七分錢了！鐵匠史密的藥局帳終於還清了！

column1: Say, let me show you a little trick with a borrowed neckerchief... Now you see it...
column2: 嘿，讓我用一條借來的領巾變個小把戲……看好了，這裡有……

column1: Now you don't!
column2: 現在不見了！

column1: Just kidding.
column2: 開玩笑的啦。

column1: Wow, if your old trusty neckerchief could only talk, boy, the stories this baby would tell!
column2: 哇，要是你那條老領巾會說話，天曉得能講出多少故事！

column1: The tank of nitrous oxide is sealed; there's no way to open its valve with your bare hands. (But tanks for trying!)
column2: 這桶笑氣是密封的，光靠雙手根本打不開閥門。（不過還是謝了，算你有心！）

column1: Sal uses this canister of nitrous oxide, also known as "laughing gas," to make sure his customers leave with a smile!
column2: 阿薩用這桶笑氣，也就是俗稱的「一氧化二氮」，來確保每位客人都笑著離開！

column1: You dip your little finger in one of the open bottles of beer and taste it. Mmm, that hits the spot!
column2: 你把小指頭伸進一瓶開了的啤酒裡沾了沾嚐嚐味道。嗯，這味道正對！

column1: You have a full case of opened Lowebrau. (Don't get caught with it in your buggy!)
column2: 你有一整箱已開封的羅氏啤酒。（可別讓人抓到馬車上藏著這箱酒！）

column1: You squish the pie a bit to see what oozes out. (You sincerely hope them's apples!)
column2: 你捏了捏派，想看看擠出來的是什麼。（你真心希望那是蘋果！）

column1: Ah, there's nothing quite like Mom's Apple Pie. Now if someone would just invent baseball: VOILA! Instant Americana!
column2: 啊，什麼都比不上老媽的蘋果派。現在只要有人發明棒球，瞧！立馬變成道地美國味！

column1: You slip the bullets in the chamber as the old memories come rushing back (including a few featuring you and your first cousin out behind the barn, when you were both curious 8-year-olds!).
column2: 你把子彈裝進彈膛，往事一股腦湧上心頭（包括幾段你和表親躲在穀倉後面，兩個八歲小孩好奇亂搞的回憶！）。

column1: With the Sheriff's cleaning kit, you lovingly clean and polish your old pistols 'til they're like new. Good thing you removed all that nasty rust from your barrel -- the damn thing could'a exploded right in your face!
column2: 你用警長的清潔工具組，仔仔細細地把老手槍擦得跟新的一樣亮。還好你把槍管裡那些討厭的鏽都清乾淨了——不然這玩意兒真有可能當場在你臉上炸開！

column1: After removing the bullets, you clean and polish your pistols 'til they shine like a Coarsegold kid with his first passing grade. Good thing you removed all that rust from your barrel -- the damn thing could'a exploded right in your face! When you're done, you replace the bullets in the chamber.
column2: 卸下子彈後，你把手槍擦得閃閃發亮，亮得像粗金鎮小孩第一次考及格那樣得意。還好你把槍管裡的鏽都清掉了——不然這玩意兒真有可能當場在你臉上炸開！擦完之後，你把子彈裝回彈膛。

column1: You cock the hammers, twirl the pistols, fake a shot, and slowly let the hammers back up. YES! That feels good, damn good!
column2: 你扳起擊錘，轉了轉手槍，假裝開一槍，再慢慢把擊錘放回去。爽！這感覺真是好，好得要命！

column1: You draw your pistol.
column2: 你拔出了手槍。

column1: You don't want to draw until you're ready to fire, and you can't possibly hit anything useful from here.
column2: 沒準備好要開槍前，你可不想拔槍，而且從這裡你也打不中什麼有用的東西。

column1: Your old pistols, looking somewhat tarnished after so many years in storage, are probably still quite serviceable.
column2: 你的老手槍收了這麼多年，看起來有點鏽蝕，但應該還能用。

column1: Your old pistols, now cleaned and restored to their original working condition, bring back a flood of emotions, with memories of yesteryear!
column2: 老手槍如今擦得乾乾淨淨、恢復原本堪用的狀態，勾起你滿滿的往日回憶！

column1: Your pistols are clean and loaded for bear! Now you're cookin'!
column2: 你的手槍擦得乾淨，子彈也上滿了！這下有搞頭了！

column1: Your old pistols are fully loaded with the Sheriff Chickenshift's surplus ammo.
column2: 你的老手槍已經裝滿了席夫特警長留下的剩餘彈藥。

column1: You riffle through the stack of spicy French Postcards, but they just won't animate smoothly.
column2: 你快速翻著那疊養眼法國明信片，但畫面就是動不流暢。

column1: Ooh-la-la and Va-va-voom! No, that's not an exclamation! That's the names of the two ladies prominently featured on Madame's spicy French postcards. (Or, rather, they're the two ladies with the prominent features on Madame's spicy French postcards!)
column2: 「喔啦啦」和「哇哇轟」！不，這可不是感嘆詞！這是歐薇莉夫人那疊養眼法國明信片上，兩位「重點突出」女郎的名字。（或者說，她們就是那兩位「重點」特別突出的女郎！）

column1: You press down on the tube, and it crumples ever so slightly. (What WILL modern technology think of next??)
column2: 你按了按軟管，它稍微皺了一下。（現代科技還能想出什麼花招啊？？）

column1: The tube of Preparation G, the latest anti-hemorrhoidal unguent from the folks at Parke-Loomis, is labeled, "Top Tush Treatments -- since 1848!"
column2: 這支「G痔膏」，是帕克盧米斯家族最新推出的抗痔瘡軟膏，管身標著：「頂級屁股療方——自1848年起！」

column1: You turn the prescription over, looking for a locker combination or something, but there's nothing written on the other side.
column2: 你把處方箋翻過來，想找置物櫃密碼之類的東西，但背面什麼都沒寫。

column1: Penelope Primm, 4 mls Tyloxpolynide orally 2x/5 days.
column2: 潘妮洛普，泰洛西聚醯胺4毫升，口服，每5天2次。

column1: Why, the poor dear! She must be suffering from the vapors, those injurious exhalations produced within the body, creating feelings of hypochondria and depression. (Her prescription is in Doc's usual scrawl, and smells of whisky, so you know it's authentic!)
column2: 哎呀，可憐的姑娘！她一定是得了「氣鬱症」，就是體內產生的那種有害氣息，會讓人疑神疑鬼、意志消沉。（她的處方箋是大夫一貫的鬼畫符筆跡，還帶著威士忌味，一看就知道是真貨！）

column1: You hold the prescription up to the light to see if you can see any secret messages, but nothing is visible.
column2: 你把處方箋舉起來對著光，看看有沒有藏著什麼密文，但什麼也看不出來。

column1: Helen Back's prescription is barely legible due to all the whisky spots, but you eventually decipher it...
column2: 海倫·貝克的處方箋被威士忌漬弄得幾乎認不出來，但你最後還是解讀出來了……

column1: Helen Back, Quinotrazate tabs, 3x/7 days.
column2: 海倫·貝克，奎諾崔唑錠，每7天3次。

column1: You try reading it backwards, but it's still a whisky-sodden, poorly-written prescription. Dang that Doc Gillespie anyway!
column2: 你試著反著讀，但這依然是張被威士忌泡爛、字跡潦草的處方箋。真是的，都怪大夫吉勒斯比！

column1: This prescription is impossible to read. That's what happens when Doc writes a prescription through bleary, whisky-soaked eyeballs!
column2: 這張處方箋根本看不懂。這就是大夫用泡了威士忌、朦朧不清的眼睛開處方的下場！

column1: You shake the solution up a bit, just to make sure it stays well-mixed.
column2: 你把藥水搖了搖，確保成分混合均勻。

column1: This should do the trick! You decide to name it "Pharkas's Patented Anti-Poopulent." (Now if you could only find a way to insure everybody in town gets a dose.)
column2: 這應該管用！你決定把它取名叫「法卡斯特效止臭配方」。（現在只差想辦法讓全鎮的人都吃到一劑了。）

column1: With a few quick movements, you make an authentic Western lasso out of the rope. It's like falling off a log... once you learn how, you never forget!
column2: 三兩下，你就用這條繩子搓出一條道地的西部套索。簡單得就像探囊取物……一旦學會了，這輩子都忘不掉！

column1: This hank of rope is plenty sturdy. (Give yourself enough of it, and you'll hang yourself.)
column2: 這捆繩子相當堅韌。（繩子夠長，就能上吊了。）

column1: You carefully feel the edge of your silver ear. It's a little ragged, but sharp as the dickens!
column2: 你小心摸了摸銀耳朵的邊緣。有點粗糙，但鋒利得要命！

column1: You've honed your silver ear to a deadly razor sharpness.
column2: 你已經把銀耳朵磨得像剃刀一樣致命鋒利。

column1: You scrape some of the dirt off the shovel, but it's still hopelessly dirty.
column2: 你刮掉了鏟子上一些泥土，但它還是髒得沒救。

column1: This shovel was left at ReBoot Hill for the convenience of the gravediggers.
column2: 這把鏟子留在「重開機墓園」，方便掘墓人使用的。

column1: You carefully examine the silver ear. Fine workmanship. Nice socket for your cartilaginous earstump. No rough edges. A spectacular job, especially since this is your first foray into the wonderful world of lost-wax casting!
column2: 你仔細端詳這隻銀耳朵。做工精細，耳窩正好貼合你的軟骨耳根，邊緣毫無粗糙感。做得漂亮，尤其這還是你第一次嘗試脫蠟鑄造這門奇妙技藝！

column1: It's your soon-to-be-world-famous Silver Ear, symbol of truth, justice, and the Pharmacological Way!
column2: 這就是你即將名震天下的銀耳朵，代表著真理、正義與藥學之道的象徵！

column1: You poke the snails, and they recede quickly into their shells. (Kinda reminds you of taking a cold shower!)
column2: 你戳了戳蝸牛，牠們立刻縮回殼裡。（有點像你洗冷水澡的感覺！）

column1: If you only had a few snails mushroom caps to go with these.
column2: 要是能找幾朵蘑菇頭配這些蝸牛就好了。

column1: You pour a small amount of beer on the snails. They quickly begin to weave around uncertainly, as if... as if they were DRUNK! How bizarre!
column2: 你倒了點啤酒在蝸牛身上。牠們立刻搖搖晃晃地爬來爬去，簡直像……簡直像喝醉了一樣！太詭異了！

column1: You run your hand up the length of the blade. Criminy! This baby's SHARP! (You compose a short mental note of complaint to the Franklin Mint.)
column2: 你的手沿著刀刃摸了上去。老天！這傢伙真利！（你在心裡草擬了一封簡短的抗議信，準備寄給富蘭克林鑄幣廠。）

column1: It appears to be a Confederate sword. You wonder if it's sharp?
column2: 這看起來像是一把南方邦聯軍刀。你在想它利不利？

column1: You drop the charcoal into tin can. Now we're gettin' somewhere!
column2: 你把木炭丟進鐵罐裡。這下總算有點眉目了！

column1: You poke around inside the can for a few leftover beans, but no dice. (And no beans, either!)
column2: 你在罐子裡摸來摸去，想找幾顆剩下的豆子，但沒撈到。（豆子也一顆都沒有！）

column1: You gently stir the coal, and a little of it sifts through the holes in the can. (Look, Ma! Black snow!)
column2: 你輕輕攪動煤炭，有一點從罐子的洞裡漏了出來。（老媽你看！黑雪耶！）

column1: You stir the can full of charcoal with your finger. Whee!
column2: 你用手指攪了攪裝滿木炭的罐子。哇呼！

column1: You feel the jagged edges inside the can where the ice pick has poked through the steel. You feel the leather of the strap where it passes through the holes in the side of the can. (And you feel mighty silly standing here feeling a can!)
column2: 你摸了摸罐子內側被冰鑿戳穿鐵皮留下的鋸齒狀邊緣。你也摸了摸皮帶穿過罐子側邊洞口的部分。（站在這裡摸一個罐子，你覺得自己蠢斃了！）

column1: Yep, it feels like those holes go right straight through that can!
column2: 沒錯，摸起來這些洞真的是直接穿透這個罐子！

column1: With all the precision of a serial killer, you deftly poke some holes in the tin can with the ice pick. Hah!
column2: 你以連環殺手般的精準手法，俐落地用冰鑿在鐵罐上戳出幾個洞。哈！

column1: Having accomplished your immediate desire, and in the process hopelessly dulling the ice pick, you exhibit absolutely no regard for this barren piece of locality laughingly called the "environment" by brazenly tossing the ice pick away. You're such a "consumer!"
column2: 達成眼前的目的後，冰鑿也順帶徹底鈍掉了，你完全不顧這片被戲稱為「環境」的荒地，大剌剌地把冰鑿隨手一丟。你還真是個「消費者」！

column1: You slip the leather strap through the holes in the tin can. They fit perfectly. Congrats! You've always wanted a tin feed bag!
column2: 你把皮帶穿過鐵罐上的洞。完全合身。恭喜！你一直夢寐以求的鐵皮飼料袋終於到手了！

column1: The leather strap just won't fit through the holes in the tin can... because there ARE no holes in the tin can!
column2: 皮帶就是穿不過鐵罐上的洞……因為這個鐵罐根本沒有洞！

column1: It's an empty can of beans. Why would Mom keep an empty can of beans on her shelf? Well, Mom's memory ain't what she used to be.
column2: 這是個空豆子罐頭。老媽為什麼要在架上放個空罐頭呢？唉，老媽的記性大不如前了。

column1: The hole-ridden tin can is now chock full of charcoal.
column2: 這個滿是洞的鐵罐現在裝滿了木炭。

column1: This tin can is full'a charcoal.
column2: 這個鐵罐裝滿了木炭。

column1: The tin can, riddled with holes from your trusty ice pick, has a leather strap threaded through two of the holes.
column2: 這個被你那把冰鑿戳滿洞的鐵罐，有條皮帶穿過其中兩個洞。

column1: You've poked major holes in the tin can!
column2: 你在鐵罐上戳出了好大幾個洞！

column1: Careful, you'll get your finger stuck in one of the bottles.
column2: 小心點，手指卡進瓶子裡就好玩了。

column1: Oops.
column2: 糟了。

column1: See! Now pull it out. Gently... carefully...
column2: 你看吧！現在把它拔出來。輕輕地……小心地……

column1: Ooof!
column2: 唔喔！

column1: There. Now you're free again. Now don't do that again, okay?
column2: 好了。你又自由了。別再這樣做了，好嗎？

column1: You've taken one of the empty beer bottles and filled it with water from the water tower. The other bottles are all empty.
column2: 你拿了一個空啤酒瓶，裝滿了水塔裡的水。其他瓶子都還是空的。

column1: You're too precariously balanced to juggle paper and glass. Get on solid ground first!
column2: 你現在站得搖搖欲墜，沒辦法同時耍紙又耍玻璃。先站到穩固的地方再說！

column1: Finally you see the prescription as Doc Gillespie must've seen it when he wrote it: through the bottom of a whisky glass!
column2: 你終於看清了這張處方箋，就像大夫吉勒斯比開處方時看到的樣子：透過威士忌杯底看出去的模樣！

column1: You carefully pack the clay in and around the wax ear, leaving a small opening so that you can pour out the molten wax later.
column2: 你小心地把黏土包在蠟耳朵四周，留下一個小開口，方便之後把融化的蠟倒出來。

column1: You try to attach the wax ear to the small knot of cartilage on the side of your head, but the wax is too slippery to stay on. Apparently you'll need to do something more to the wax ear to build yourself an acceptable prosthesis.
column2: 你想把蠟耳朵黏到頭側那塊軟骨小結上，但蠟太滑黏不住。看來你還得對這隻蠟耳朵做點什麼，才能做出一隻堪用的義耳。

column1: This handsomely-carved wax ear looks very much like one that bastard Kenny the Kid shot off so many years ago!
column2: 這隻雕工精美的蠟耳朵，看起來很像多年前被那混蛋小鬼肯尼一槍轟掉的那隻！

column1: You stir the few remaining drops of whisky around, then lick off your finger. Mmm! Single-malt!
column2: 你攪了攪杯底剩下的幾滴威士忌，然後舔了舔手指。嗯！單一麥芽的！

column1: Poor Doc! What's he gonna do without his whiskey glass?
column2: 可憐的大夫！沒了威士忌杯，他該怎麼辦？

column1: Scraping off the clay now would destroy the mold!
column2: 現在把黏土刮掉會毀掉整個模具的！

column1: This clay mold still contains your original wax "positive" of your ear.
column2: 這個黏土模具裡還留著你原本那隻耳朵的蠟「正模」。

column1: This door is locked.
column2: 這扇門鎖住了。

column1: You don't hear anything.
column2: 你什麼也沒聽到。

column1: This door won't open this way.
column2: 這扇門這樣打不開。

column1: This door is already open and there's really no need for you to lock it.
column2: 這扇門已經開著了，你實在沒必要把它鎖起來。

column1: Whew-ee! You can't. The aroma is simply too overpowering. You don't dare touch the horse without some way to protect yourself from the stench.
column2: 唷呵！你辦不到。那股味道實在太嗆了。沒有東西保護自己不受臭味侵襲，你可不敢碰這匹馬。

column1: Somebody's poor horse seems to be dispelling huge quantities of a noxious methane compound.
column2: 不知是誰家可憐的馬，正在排放大量刺鼻的甲烷氣體。

column1: The horse's tail is fluttering in the breeze! (And what a breeze that is!)
column2: 馬尾巴在風中飄啊飄！（那可真是一陣「好風」！）

column1: Hey, you're a purty li'l paint, aren't ya? Yes, you are! Yes, you are! What a little cutie! I like you, horsie! I sure do! Can I take you home with me? CAN I take you home with me? You'd like that, wouldn't you? Yes, you would! Yes, you would!
column2: 嘿，你這匹小花馬真漂亮，是不是啊？沒錯，就是你！就是你！你這小可愛！我喜歡你，小馬兒！真的很喜歡！我可以帶你回家嗎？可以帶你回家嗎？你會喜歡的，對吧？沒錯，你會喜歡的！你會喜歡的！

column1: (You need to get out more often, Freddy.)
column2: （佛萊迪，你真的該多出門走走了。）

column1: Nice horsey! (You'd BETTER be nice to this horsey. It has the power to cloud men's minds!)
column2: 乖馬兒！（你最好對這匹馬客氣點，牠可是有蠱惑人心的能耐！）

column1: You must be thinking of Dad Gumm's Magic Suppositories! Unfortunately, Dad stopped manufacturing those years ago when they were found to be explosive under pressure!
column2: 你該不會是在想「甘老爹神奇栓劑」吧！可惜的是，甘老爹多年前就已經停產了，因為那玩意兒被發現在受壓時會爆炸！

column1: You don't have nearly enough keys to plug up |c2|all|c| the horses in town!
column2: 你手邊的鑰匙根本不夠塞住鎮上|c2|所有|c|的馬！

column1: Yes, if you wanted, you could capture the "effluvium" in the tin can, but since the tin can doesn't have a top, the effluvium wouldn't stay in there.
column2: 沒錯，如果你想，是可以用鐵罐把那股「臭氣」收集起來，可惜鐵罐沒有蓋子，臭氣根本留不住。

column1: You really think that giving the horses hemorrhoids will make them stop farting?
column2: 你真的以為讓馬得痔瘡就能讓牠們不放屁嗎？

column1: That charcoal might stay in there for a minute or two, but then |c0|BANG!|c| There goes windows all up and down Main Street!
column2: 那塊木炭或許能撐個一兩分鐘，但接下來|c0|轟！|c|大街兩旁的窗戶就全都保不住了！

column1: Yeah, spank 'em, that'll keep the horses from farting. Bet it really starts 'em kicking!
column2: 對啦，打牠們屁股，這樣就能讓馬不放屁了。我賭牠們會踢得更起勁！

column1: You'd need a lot of gas masks, but you're on the right track.
column2: 你會需要一大堆防毒面具，不過方向是對的。

column1: You carefully pour the Deflatulizer into the horse's water trough. The horses greedily lap up the dee-lish- and nu-trish- medicated trough water.
column2: 你小心地把「消脹劑」倒進馬的水槽裡。馬兒們貪婪地舔著那槽既美味又營養的藥水。

column1: Seein' as how his home-brewed "Patootie Sealant" done the trick on these horses, Freddy ran 'round and dumped the stuff into all the horse troughs in town. It warn't long 'afore the folks o' Coarsegold wuz all breathin' a sigh of relief!
column2: 眼看自家土法煉製的「屁股密封劑」對這些馬管用，佛萊迪就跑遍全鎮，把這玩意兒倒進所有的馬水槽裡。沒過多久，粗金鎮的鄉親父老就都鬆了一口氣！

column1: Freddy tossed away his homemade gas mask, kind of a shame too, since he could'a made a purty penny off'n the patent rights. Life returned to normal, fur a short spell anyhooch, until one lazy day when one o' the local inbreeds come a'runnin' up wif the latest calamity...
column2: 佛萊迪把自製的防毒面具扔了，說起來也挺可惜的，畢竟光靠專利權他大可撈上一筆。日子恢復了平靜，至少太平了一陣子，直到某個懶洋洋的日子，鎮上某個腦筋不太靈光的傢伙又跑來通報最新的災難……

column1: Unlike most headwaiters, this horse's ass doesn't accept tips!
column2: 這匹馬的屁股跟大多數的領班可不一樣，牠可不收小費！

column1: You briefly consider pouring beer into the horse's nether regions, but you quickly realize it would only worsen the horse's flatulence... and you'd have a hell of a time recycling that bottle!
column2: 你一度考慮把啤酒倒進馬的「下半身部位」，但很快意識到這只會讓牠更容易脹氣……而且那個瓶子你也很難再回收利用了！

column1: If you did that, you'd have to shoot it afterwards. (The Church Key, not the horse.)
column2: 你要是這麼做，之後就得把它斃了。（是指開瓶器，不是馬。）

column1: You are truly a sick and cruel person. (Oh, you just wanted to climb on board? Oops!)
column2: 你真是個既變態又殘忍的人。（喔，你只是想爬上去騎？抱歉搞錯了！）

column1: The horse would undoubtedly appreciate the "seven knots to heaven" trick, but you've got better uses for that rope in mind!
column2: 這匹馬肯定會很享受「七劫升天結」這一招，不過你這條繩子還有更好的用途！

column1: That might make sense if you were trying to remove their intestinal polyps, but that's not their problem.
column2: 如果你是想幫牠們摘除腸內息肉，這麼做或許還說得通，可惜牠們的問題不是這個。

column1: The sheer force of the wind would break the wax seal instantly. (But you get an "A" for creativity.)
column2: 那股風力大到會瞬間吹破蠟封。（不過創意這塊，算你拿了「甲」！）

column1: You could try that, but then you might have to go looking for it again, and wouldn't that be just TOO disgusting.
column2: 你是可以試試看，但之後你可能還得回頭去找它，那也未免太噁心了吧。

column1: They're not rags, you know, they're your old official Cowboy duds!
column2: 這可不是破布，這是你當年正牌牛仔裝的行頭耶！

column1: You're gonna |c0|need|c| that claim check sooner or later, and if you stick it in there, you're not gonna want it anymore.
column2: 你遲早會|c0|需要|c|那張提領單，要是把它塞進那裡，你以後可就不會想再要它了。

column1: You've got better (and more polite) uses in mind for those boots!
column2: 那雙靴子你另有更好（也更得體）的用途！

column1: That's one interesting place to store the letter.
column2: 把信藏在那裡，還真是個有趣的地方。

column1: (SCOTTY LIKE) She can't take any more, Cap'n! I'm afraid she's gonna BLOW!
column2: （模仿史考特的語氣）她撐不住了，艦長！我怕她要爆炸了！

column1: In what may well be the most revolting idea you've ever had, you hold the brown paper sack up to the horse's anal sphincter and wait. With a reverberating "bbbrrraaatt," the horse reponds, inflating your bag a foul sample of "gas." You quickly twist the bag shut to lock in freshness.
column2: 你想出了這輩子大概最噁心的點子：把牛皮紙袋湊到馬的肛門口等著。伴隨一聲響亮的「噗噗噗——」，馬兒配合演出，把你的袋子吹得鼓鼓的，裝滿一袋難聞的「氣體」樣本。你趕緊把袋口扭緊，把新鮮度鎖住。

column1: A really terrifically disgusting idea! Unfortunately, the horse's tail momentarily blocks your access.
column2: 真是個超級噁心的點子！可惜馬尾巴一時擋住了你的去路。

column1: Someone's horse (at least, you HOPE it was a horse) has decorated the street with a steamin' hot, fly-attracting "pie."
column2: 不知是誰家的馬（至少你希望是馬），在街上留下了一坨熱騰騰、招蒼蠅的「大餅」。

column1: You gingerly pick up the steaming pile and place it in your (ecccch!) pocket. (You make a mental note to burn these clothes when you're done with the game.)
column2: 你小心翼翼地撿起那坨熱騰騰的東西，放進你的（噁！）口袋裡。（你在心裡記下，等這遊戲玩完就把這身衣服燒了。）

column1: unused msg
column2: 未使用的訊息

column1: Taking a serious look at yourself, you decide you like what you see.
column2: 你認真打量了一下自己，覺得看到的還挺不錯。

column1: These little self-introspective chats are fun, aren't they, Freddy?
column2: 這種自我對話挺好玩的，對吧，佛萊迪？

column1: Ahhh! Scratching right there sure feels good, eh, Freddy?
column2: 啊∼抓那個地方真的很舒服，對吧，佛萊迪？

column1: You uncork and swig the elixir, finishing the bottle before you know it.
column2: 你拔開瓶塞，灌了一大口藥水，還沒回過神瓶子就見底了。

column1: How poetic... the dorky and the door key!
column2: 真有詩意啊……「阿呆」和「鑰匙」真是絕配！

column1: You rub the paper all over your hands, but it's still legible!
column2: 你把紙在手上到處搓，但字跡還是看得清清楚楚！

column1: You rub it all over your hands, but it's still legible!
column2: 你在手上到處搓，但字跡還是看得清清楚楚！

column1: You rub it all over your hands, but it's still totally illegible!
column2: 你在手上到處搓，但字跡還是完全認不出來！

column1: Doc's already drained all the whisky from the glass, but hey, nice try!
column2: 大夫早就把杯裡的威士忌喝得一滴不剩了，不過，算你有心！

column1: There's not enough whisky in the glass to drink, and you're not particularly hungry for a sodden piece of paper!
column2: 杯子裡的威士忌不夠喝，你對一張泡爛的紙也沒什麼胃口！

column1: You already have the corrected prescription!
column2: 你已經拿到修正過的處方箋了！

column1: You heave... a sigh of relief!
column2: 你長長地……鬆了一口氣！

column1: You take a swig of the water from the water tower. Uh-oh. Your stomach starts to make strange sounds. Your small intestine begins to whine. Your lower intestine starts complaining loudly.
column2: 你灌了一口水塔裡的水。糟了。你的胃開始發出怪聲。小腸開始咕嚕抱怨。大腸則放聲大聲抗議。

column1: You're having enough trouble balancing on the ladder as it is; now's no time to juggle your inventory items.
column2: 你光是站在梯子上保持平衡就夠費勁了，現在可不是耍弄物品的時候。

column1: It's not a good idea to try that up here! Lose your balance and you'll be nothing more than a particularly large road apple.
column2: 在這麼高的地方可別亂來！一旦失去平衡，你就會變成一坨特大號的路邊「馬糞」。

column1: You had a drink of water just before you went to bed!
column2: 你睡前才剛喝過水了！

column1: Fighting crime is thirsty work, but wait 'til you've dealt with the situation at hand to take your refreshment.
column2: 打擊犯罪是件費口渴的差事，不過先把眼前的事處理完，再來解渴吧。

column1: You try the old trick of flattening the can against your skull. Ring around the forehead! Ring around the forehead!
column2: 你試著用老招數，把罐子壓扁在自己頭上。額頭一圈印！額頭一圈印！

column1: Congratulations! Nice form, Mr. Ripper!
column2: 恭喜啊！姿勢真標準，開膛手先生！

column1: You briefly consider that current craze, the "minstrel" look, but decide there are better uses for the charcoal.
column2: 你一度考慮跟上時下流行的「黑臉秀」造型，但轉念一想，木炭還有更好的用途。

column1: You glance around to make sure no one is watching, then you flagellate yourself just a little bit.
column2: 你四處張望，確定沒人在看，然後小小鞭笞了自己一下。

column1: You take a few deep breaths from the gas mask, clearing your head and enabling you to go on awhile longer!
column2: 你對著防毒面具深呼吸幾口，腦袋清醒了，能再撐一陣子！

column1: You can't fiddle with that while you're on the ladder.
column2: 你站在梯子上沒辦法擺弄那個。

column1: Fortunately, the aroma hasn't permeated the interior of the building. You won't need to use that gas mask in here.
column2: 還好，那股味道還沒滲進屋裡。你在這裡用不著防毒面具。

column1: You can't keep your balance up here AND use the gas mask properly at the same time, Freddy.
column2: 佛萊迪，你沒辦法一邊在這裡保持平衡，一邊好好戴防毒面具。

column1: Unfortunately for you, this Deflatulizer is highly concentrated, far too powerful to be ingested in undiluted form!
column2: 很不巧，這瓶「消脹劑」濃度極高，沒稀釋過根本不能直接喝下肚！

column1: What? Uncooked? And without garlic butter? AUGGGH!
column2: 什麼？沒煮過？還沒加蒜味奶油？啊啊啊！

column1: You thank yourself for last night, and pay yourself the usual amount.
column2: 你為了昨晚的事謝謝自己，還付了平常那個數目給自己。

column1: You rub the bottle cap across your lips, just enough to make sure that everybody knows what a macho stud pharmacist you are!
column2: 你把瓶蓋在嘴唇上抹了抹，好讓大家都見識見識你這位藥師有多猛！

column1: You take a drink of the beer.
column2: 你喝了一口啤酒。

column1: BURRRRRRRRP!!
column2: 呃啊嗝——！！

column1: (Fortunately, you've got MUCH more beer left. You could never drink that much beer, so stop trying!)
column2: （還好你還剩下超多啤酒。你不可能喝得完那麼多，別再嘗試了！）

column1: You coyly avoid a trip to the outhouse... but you refuse to carry that bottle around any more!
column2: 你羞答答地省下一趟茅房之旅……但你說什麼也不肯再帶著那個瓶子到處跑了！

column1: You are amazed to find the church key's shape precisely fits your navel, making a perfect belly-button lint remover.
column2: 你驚訝地發現開瓶器的形狀正好卡進你的肚臍，變成一支完美的肚臍毛清除器。

column1: (LADDER PUN) You rung?
column2: （梯子雙關語）「梯」呼喚我了嗎？

column1: Give yourself enough rope and you know you'll hang yourself!
column2: 給自己夠長的繩子，你知道遲早會上吊的！

column1: You strongly consider lynching yourself, but decide you're hung well enough already!
column2: 你認真考慮過要吊死自己，但轉念一想，覺得自己這方面已經「掛」得夠好了！

column1: You take a swig of the concentrated water purification solution. That'll clean your clock!
column2: 你灌下一大口濃縮淨水劑。這下有你受的了！

column1: You open the valve on the tank of nitrous oxide, and suddenly the game seems much funnier! Unfortunately, you soon die laughing!
column2: 你打開笑氣桶的閥門，突然覺得這遊戲有趣多了！可惜沒多久，你就笑死了！

column1: You foolishly ingest several sacks of the baking soda, creating a major eruption of the worst kind!
column2: 你傻傻地吞下好幾包小蘇打粉，結果引發了一場最糟糕的大爆發！

column1: Don't French postcards. You don't know where those postcards have been!
column2: 別亂搞法國明信片。你根本不知道那些明信片經過哪些人的手！

column1: Trying the ol' hot wax treatment? You're SUPPOSED to have hairy legs, Freddy.
column2: 想試試老派熱蠟除毛？佛萊迪，你本來就該有一雙毛腿。

column1: Good idea! Those fingernails were getting a little dirty!
column2: 好主意！那些指甲是有點髒了！

column1: You cleverly attempt to unlock your head by inserting the desk key into your nose. Apparently this isn't the right key.
column2: 你自作聰明地想用書桌鑰匙插進鼻孔裡，試圖打開自己的腦袋。看來這不是對的鑰匙。

column1: You find the safe deposit box key fits perfectly into several orifices!
column2: 你發現保險箱鑰匙完美地插進了好幾個孔洞裡！

column1: What are you doing? Trying to rob yourself? Who are you trying to kid? Those pistols aren't loaded!
column2: 你在幹嘛？想搶劫自己？你在唬誰啊？那兩把手槍根本沒上膛！

column1: You just can't resist nibbling off a little corner of the crust. No one will ever notice that!
column2: 你實在忍不住，偷咬了一小角派皮。反正沒人會發現的！

column1: Ummm, good to the last drop! That Mom sure can make a good cup of Instant Hazelnut Vanilla Mocha Java. (Maybe she has friends here from Europe!)
column2: 嗯∼喝到最後一滴都好喝！老媽泡的即溶榛果香草摩卡爪哇咖啡真是一絕。（說不定她在歐洲有朋友呢！）

column1: It won't clean THAT "deadly weapon," Freddy!
column2: 佛萊迪，這可清不了「那把致命武器」！

column1: Just where did you intend to stick those bullets, Freddy?
column2: 佛萊迪，你到底打算把那些子彈塞到哪裡去？

column1: Just like you've seen it done at the spas, you apply the clay to your face for a few moments, then scrape it off. Now your complexion is as soft and smooth as a newborn hog's butt!
column2: 就像你在溫泉會館看過的那樣，你把黏土敷在臉上一會兒，然後刮掉。現在你的膚質光滑柔嫩，跟剛出生的小豬屁股一樣！

column1: You will want to wear it later, but only after you have completed your outfit.
column2: 你之後會想穿上它，但要等你把整套裝扮準備齊全才行。

column1: It's too late to wear that thing. Penelope's already seen through your disguise!
column2: 現在穿那玩意兒已經太遲了。潘妮洛普早就看穿你的偽裝了！

column1: You wouldn't |c2|dream|c| of wearing your cowboy clothes around town until you have both your whole ensemble and a damn good reason!
column2: 你才不會|c2|夢想|c|穿著牛仔裝在鎮上晃，除非你湊齊整套行頭又有個像樣的理由！

column1: You already have the Claim Check.
column2: 你已經有提貨單了。

column1: Of course you'll want to wear the boots later, but wait until you have a complete outfit.
column2: 你當然會想晚點穿上這雙靴子，但要等湊齊整套服裝再說。

column1: You'll want to wear your neckerchief later, after you have completed your outfit.
column2: 你會想晚點戴上這條領巾，等你把整套服裝穿齊了再說。

column1: It's too sharp to wear! Turn your head to the right and you'd cut your own jugular!
column2: 這東西太利了不能戴！頭一往右轉，你就會割破自己的頸動脈！

column1: It's bad enough that Penelope's trying to kill you. Now you want to run yourself through?
column2: 潘妮洛普想要你的命就已經夠慘了，你現在還想自己捅自己一刀？

column1: That's not necessary. You already dig yourself.
column2: 用不著。你自己心裡有數。

column1: You are a sick, sick little pharmacist!
column2: 你這個藥師真是病得不輕啊！

column1: You will NOT need to hyperventilate in this game!
column2: 這款遊戲裡你可用不著過度換氣！

column1: How disgusting!!
column2: 噁心死了！！

column1: You'd look a mite silly, walking around with that big lump of clay stuck to the side of your head.
column2: 頭上黏著一大坨黏土到處走，你看起來會蠢得可以。

column1: Mmm... wax and clay! You're not THAT hungry!
column2: 嗯……蠟和黏土！你還沒餓成那樣吧！

column1: You sniff around in the empty mold, but true to its word, it's empty.
column2: 你在空模子裡聞來聞去，果然名副其實，裡面什麼都沒有。

column1: You don't need any extra ear wax!
column2: 你才不需要多餘的耳垢！

column1: You take a sip of the medication. Unfortunately, the first rule of the Old West Medicine Chest is: never trust nobody else's prescription!
column2: 你喝了一口藥。可惜啊，西部藥箱的第一條規矩就是：別人開的處方箋，千萬別亂信！

column2: (c) Copyright 1994 Sierra On-Line， Inc. (c) Copyright 1993 Screw Loose Amusements. 感謝您遊玩《多情藥師酷牛仔》。至少你的槍法有在進步。

column2: (c) Copyright 1994 Sierra On-Line， Inc. (c) Copyright 1993 Screw Loose Amusements 感謝您遊玩《多情藥師酷牛仔》。小子，你用那玩意兒把自己眼睛打瞎了！

column1: Raise this poor fool to increase the amount of incidental animation. Lower him if Freddy seems to slog around like a wagon knee-deep in manure.
column2: 把這可憐傢伙調高，可以增加一些小動作動畫。要是佛萊迪走起路來像陷在及膝糞堆裡的馬車一樣拖泥帶水，就把他調低。

column1: This poor fella here turns up the noise on sound boards and syn-thee-sizers.
column2: 這位可憐的傢伙負責調大音效卡跟那個什麼「合─成─器」的音量。

column1: This varmint here adjusts Freddy's walkin' speed, within the limits of your computer's advanced caperbilities.
column2: 這隻小畜生負責調整佛萊迪走路的速度，範圍就看你電腦那些高深「性能」耐操到哪。

column1: Lower this poor fellow here to make text remain on the screen longer. Raise him if you are a fast reader and got a lot of book learnin'.
column2: 把這可憐的傢伙調低，文字就會在螢幕上停久一點。要是你讀書快又滿腹經綸，就把他調高。

column1: Use this here to save the current state of your game. When you later select Restore, everything'll be right normal, just like it was before, when ya hadn't messed with it.
column2: 用這個來存下目前的遊戲進度。之後選「讀取」的時候，一切都會恢復正常，就跟你還沒亂搞之前一樣。

column1: This restores a game y'all saved earlier on.
column2: 這個會讀取你之前存的遊戲進度。

column1: Use this here to restart the game all over again, from the very beginning.
column2: 用這個從頭把整個遊戲重新來過。

column1: Use this here to slowly back outta the game, real careful-like.
column2: 用這個小心翼翼地慢慢退出遊戲。

column1: Here's where y'all learn more than you wanna about the fellas that put this here game together.
column2: 這裡會讓你知道一堆你根本不想知道、關於做這款遊戲那群傢伙的事。

column1: To learn more about the other items in this here window, first click here, then pass yer question mark over those other items there.
column2: 想多了解這個視窗裡的其他項目，先點這裡，然後把問號游標移到其他項目上頭。

column1: Use this here to close this panel here and resume game play.
column2: 用這個關掉這個面板，繼續遊戲。

column1: Use this here button to choose "text" (havin' the words displayed onscreen) or "audio" (havin' the words spoken out loud by real actorlike humans).
column2: 用這個按鈕選擇「文字」（把台詞顯示在螢幕上）或「語音」（由像模像樣的真人演員唸出台詞）。

column1: Yes, sir! By gum, by cracky! With his one good ear all mangled and grody, Freddy managed to leap from the schoolhouse just seconds before it went up in the biggest conflagration Coarsegold'd ever seen!
column2: 沒錯，老兄！我的老天鵝啊！佛萊迪那隻好端端的耳朵都被震得稀巴爛，他還是在校舍付之一炬——粗金鎮史上最大一場火——的前幾秒硬是跳了出來！

column1: The credits aren't in need of anything you've got.
column2: 工作人員名單才不需要你手上那些東西。

column1: This is a credit. This wasn't actually found in Coarsegold in the 1880's, but if they WERE, they'd have looked a lot like this one!
column2: 這是一則工作人員名單。1880 年代的粗金鎮其實沒有這種東西，不過如果真的有，八成就長這樣！

column1: Talking to credits? You are in need of counseling.
column2: 跟工作人員名單講話？你需要去看心理醫生了。

column1: You can't take credit for something you haven't done!
column2: 沒做過的事，你可不能邀功！

column1: That person doesn't want what you're offering. What an ungrateful wretch!
column2: 那個人才不想要你給的東西。真是個忘恩負義的傢伙！

column1: It looks like the name of a hardworking employee with a large ego.
column2: 這看起來像是某個自我感覺良好的認真員工的名字。

column1: Shhhh, that person's already working on another game.
column2: 噓，那個人已經在忙別款遊戲了。

column1: What's the matter, you don't like your OWN name, so you want to take somebody else's?
column2: 怎麼了，不喜歡自己的名字，想搶別人的來用？

column1: It's Ezekial Jacob Methuselah Andrew Washington Madison Johnson Hallelujah, the preacher's kid.
column2: 這位是以西結·雅各·瑪土撒拉·安德魯·華盛頓·麥迪遜·強森·哈利路亞，牧師的兒子。

column1: I ain't got time. I put peanut butter in the offering plate and now my pa is after me! He said I was wasting good peanut butter!
column2: 我沒空啦。我把花生醬放進奉獻盤裡，現在我老爸在後面追我！他說我在浪費好好的花生醬！

column1: Jeez, buddy. Get yer hands off me!
column2: 天啊，老兄。手拿開！

column1: My parents say I'm not supposed to accept inventory items from strangers.
column2: 我爸媽說我不可以跟陌生人拿東西。

column1: A good thought, but let his father take care of him.
column2: 想法是不錯，不過還是讓他老爸來管教他吧。

column1: Carrie Sue ought to be in school, but she's wandering the streets instead.
column2: 凱莉蘇這時候應該在學校才對，她卻在街上到處閒晃。

column1: My mama sez I'm not spozed to talk with strangers. And you're stranger than most!
column2: 我媽說我不可以跟陌生人講話。而你呢，比誰都更「陌生」——怪咖一個！

column1: MAMA! THAT MAN TRIED TO TOUCH ME!!
column2: 媽！這個男的想要摸我！！

column1: No thank you, sir! I'm in a hurry!
column2: 不用了，謝謝，先生！我在趕時間！

column1: That's a severe punishment for playing hookey, don't you think?
column2: 翹課落到這種下場也太慘了吧，你不覺得嗎？

column1: Rover earned his name the hard way. He lives from paw to mouth all around the town.
column2: 阿旺這名字可不是白得的，牠在鎮上到處靠一爪一口討生活。

column1: Arf.
column2: 汪。

column1: Grrrrrr...
Best leave him alone, Freddy. Sounds like he got up on the wrong side of the doggy bed.
column2: 佛萊迪，還是別惹牠比較好。聽起來牠今天狗窩起床氣很重。

column1: That dog has pride. He doesn't need your CHARITY!
column2: 這隻狗有牠的骨氣。牠才不需要你的施捨！

column1: What are you trying to do, put him out of his misery? How would you like it if that dog decided to put YOU out of YOUR misery?
column2: 你想幹嘛，讓牠早點解脫？要是這隻狗也想讓「你」早點解脫，你會作何感想？

column1: Once Lucky was as coordinated as any other mongrel, but that was before he had that run in with the owl at the west end of town. Now he hates the owl as much as the rest of us!
column2: 幸運以前跟其他雜種狗一樣手腳俐落，直到牠在鎮西跟那隻貓頭鷹槓上了。現在牠跟我們大家一樣痛恨那隻貓頭鷹！

column1: How are you?
column2: 你好嗎？

column1: Wh-wh-what did you say???
column2: 你、你剛剛說什麼？？？

column1: Bow arrrooo?
column2: 汪嗚嗚嗚？

column1: Pant, pant, pant...
column2: 喘、喘、喘……

column1: He's not very stable on his three legs. If you pet him he'll fall right over!
column2: 牠三隻腳站得不太穩，你摸牠一下牠就會整隻翻倒！

column1: Bowff.
column2: 汪夫。

column1: Translation: No thanks, but if you run across any wooden doggie legs, I'll take two... one for a spare.
column2: 翻譯一下：不必了，謝謝。不過你要是撿到木頭狗腿，幫我留兩隻……一隻備用。

column1: Now, now. Lucky's had a hard enough life without you ending it suddenly.
column2: 好啦好啦。幸運這輩子已經夠苦了，你就別突然幫牠結束生命了。

column1: Everybody in town knows Trixie the Accommodating Sheep. She used to belong to a bachelor farmer, but he died of some strange disease.
column2: 鎮上人人都認識翠西，那隻很「隨和」的羊。牠本來是某個單身農夫養的，不過那農夫染上什麼怪病死了。

column1: Baaaaaa.
Translation: I'm terribly sorry, sir, but I can't accommodate you right now.
column2: 翻譯：真的很抱歉，先生，我現在沒辦法「配合」你。

column1: Baaad boooy!
Trixie's well provided for by her new boyfriend. Supposedly, he's quite the wolf!
column2: 翠西現在有新男朋友罩著，過得挺不錯。聽說那傢伙可是隻不折不扣的大野狼！

column1: There are better ways to get sheep thrills in this game than by shooting Trixie!
column2: 這款遊戲裡想找「羊」樂子，開槍打翠西可不是什麼好辦法！

column1: Contemplating duck dinner, Freddy?
column2: 佛萊迪，在盤算烤鴨大餐嗎？

column1: Talking to ducks? Desperate for company?
column2: 跟鴨子講話？寂寞到這種地步了？

column1: Quack! <hic> Quack! <hic>
column2: 呱！<hic> 呱！<hic>

column1: The duck can't have it. He's already got an unpaid bill.
column2: 這隻鴨子拿不了。牠自己的「嘴」（帳單）都還沒付清呢。

column1: That's Doc Gillespie's duck, Duck Gillespie. The ol' Doc wouldn't appreciate your cooking his goose.
column2: 那是吉勒斯比大夫養的鴨子，鴨子吉勒斯比。老大夫可不會欣賞你把他的「鵝」給燉了——雖然那明明是隻鴨。

column1: Henny Penny she ain't.
column2: 她可不是童話裡那隻自以為天要塌下來的母雞。

column1: Buck buck-AKKK.
column2: 咕咕──咯！

column1: Freddy, you don't need to steal that bird. You can buy one for chicken feed.
column2: 佛萊迪，你用不著偷那隻雞。花點小錢就能買一隻了。

column1: You want to give that to a CHICKEN? What the pluck is he going to do with that?
column2: 你想把那個給一隻雞？牠拿那玩意兒是要幹「拔」嘛？

column1: Ever tried to pick lead out of a chicken carcass? No? Well, you don't wanna start now!
column2: 你試過從雞屍體裡挑鉛彈嗎？沒有？那你現在也不會想開始的！

column1: Pork chops on the hoof!
column2: 會走路的豬排！

column1: Carpe oink. OINK Emptor. Carborundum squeal. Angelus oink. SQUEAL sic transit OINK!
column2: 卡佩·哼哼。哼哼·愛姆特。卡博倫登·唧唧叫。安傑勒斯·哼哼。唧唧叫，浮生若哼！

column1: That pig is one smooth conversationalist! If only you spoke pig-latin.
column2: 這隻豬還真是個健談的傢伙！可惜你不會說「豬式拉丁文」。

column1: You contemplate capturing the pig, but think twice when you realize that every single inventory item you have is carried in one pocket. After all, pigs are not the cleanest animals and their fragrance can be unusually pungent. Not the best way to make friends and influence people.
column2: 你盤算著要不要抓這隻豬，但一想到你身上所有的道具都塞在同一個口袋裡，就打消了念頭。畢竟豬不是什麼乾淨的動物，那股味道有時候濃得驚人。這可不是交朋友、拉關係的好辦法。

column1: The pig turns up its snout at your offer.
column2: 這隻豬對你的東西嗤之以鼻。

column1: You're not interested in makin' bacon right now.
column2: 你現在沒興趣把牠做成培根。

column1: (SINGING) "Rollin', rollin', rollin', got to keep on rollin...."
column2: （唱著）「滾滾滾，滾滾滾，滾滾滾個不停……」

column1: It don't say nothin'. It just keeps rollin' along.
column2: 牠什麼話也不說，就只是一路滾啊滾。

column1: And get your hands all full of prickles?
column2: 還讓你滿手都是刺？

column1: Don't practice your target-shooting in the middle of Main Street!
column2: 別在大街正中央練習打靶！

column1: The snot-nosed brat adds a lot to the charm of downtown Coarsegold.
column2: 這個鼻涕蟲小鬼，讓粗金鎮市中心更添了幾分「風情」。

column1: What do YOU want? Can't you tell I got things to do?
column2: 你想幹嘛？看不出來我正忙嗎？

column1: My, but the children in this town are polite!
column2: 哎呀，這鎮上的小孩還真是有禮貌啊！

column1: Don't try it mister! I know haiku!
column2: 別想耍花招，先生！我可是會俳句的！

column1: Stow it, Mister! I don't need that, I don't know where it's been!
column2: 收起來啦，先生！我才不要，天曉得那東西碰過什麼！

column1: Sure. You'd be doing his parents a favor, but even so, tough luck.
column2: 是啊，你這樣算是幫了他爸媽一個忙，不過話說回來，還是沒門。

column1: The child appears perfectly happy with her lot in life. Of course, what child wouldn't be happy to be dirty?
column2: 這孩子看起來對自己的日子挺滿意的。話說回來，哪個小孩不喜歡把自己弄得髒兮兮的呢？

column1: Say, shouldn't you be in school?
column2: 話說，你不是應該在學校嗎？

column1: Yeah, and who's gonna make me?
column2: 是啊，那你要怎麼逼我？

column1: You and what army, mister?
column2: 就憑你？先生，你哪來的軍隊啊？

column1: My Dad already has one of those, and it's bigger than yours!
column2: 我爸早就有一個那玩意兒了，還比你的大！

column1: Gee! How did he know THAT?
column2: 天啊！他是怎麼知道的？

column1: That's morbid, cruel, and entirely uncalled-for. Besides, we were too cheap to put in the animation of you shooting a child!
column2: 這樣做太病態、太殘忍，也完全沒必要。而且啦，我們窮到沒錢做你開槍打小孩的動畫！

column1: Old Pete's been around since the gold was here. He and Willy are the only two codgers left.
column2: 老皮從這裡還有金礦的年代就在了。他跟威利是這鎮上僅剩的兩個老頭子。

column1: Well, by gum! How ya doin', young feller, by gum! Nice to see ya, by gum!
column2: 哎呀我的天！你好啊，年輕人，我的天！見到你真高興，我的天！

column1: Hey, old timer! Ain't seen you around in a dog's age. What're you up to these days?
column2: 嘿，老傢伙！好久沒見到你了。這陣子在忙什麼啊？

column1: What does it LOOK like I'm doing, by gum? I'M TRYIN' TO SELL GUM! Damn ijit.
column2: 我的天，你看我像在幹嘛？我在賣口香糖啦！你這笨蛋。

column1: Now, doncha try it. I'm right ticklish!
column2: 你可別亂來。我可是很怕癢的！

column1: I couldn't take nothin' from ya, kiddo. You keep that and put it towards yer edukashun. Don't never stop gettin' an edukashun. I dropped outta school when I was eight, and I ain't never had no fiduciary solvency to fall back on.
column2: 小夥子，我可不能拿你的東西。你留著，拿去唸書用。唸書這件事千萬別停。我八歲就輟學了，這輩子都沒個殷實的家底可以靠。

column1: Careful, you don't want to be arrested for assaulting a miner!
column2: 小心點，你可不會想因為打了個「礦工」被抓去關吧！

column1: This poor guy got left behind when his troop went through. He had dysentery. He's since recovered, but Doc Gillespie's cure seems to have affected his mind as he still thinks his company will return for him.
column2: 這個可憐的傢伙在部隊經過時被留了下來，因為他得了痢疾。他後來是好了，不過吉勒斯比大夫開的藥好像影響了他的腦子，他到現在還以為部隊會回來接他。

column1: Yessir. Nice day sir. Good to see you sir.
column2: 是的長官。今天天氣真好，長官。見到您真高興，長官。

column1: Hands off, sir. I'm spoken for, sir.
column2: 手拿開，長官。我已經名花有主了，長官。

column1: No, thank you, SIR! Uncle Sam gives me everything I need, SIR!
column2: 不用了，謝謝，長官！山姆大叔什麼都給我準備好了，長官！

column1: That would be the ultimate indignity, wouldn't it? Shooting a down-on-his-luck soldier who'd never done you any harm. Well, you can't. You just can't.
column2: 那可真是奇恥大辱，不是嗎？對一個倒楣、又從沒傷害過你的士兵開槍。不行，你就是下不了手。

column1: Why, he's with the Texas Rangers! What's he doing here?
column2: 咦，他是德州騎警隊的！他跑來這裡幹嘛？

column1: No time! Gotta save the country!
column2: 沒時間了！我得去拯救國家！

column1: You'd be trampled by the horse, silly.
column2: 你會被那匹馬給踩扁的，傻瓜。

column1: No thanks, son! I'm travelin' light, travelin' light!
column2: 不用了，小子！我輕裝上路，輕裝上路！

column1: He's on a mission. Don't interfere.
column2: 他正在執行任務。別去打擾他。

column1: Why, he's with the Pony Express!
column2: 咦，他是小馬快遞的！

column1: No time! Gotta deliver the mail!
column2: 沒時間了！我得去送信！

column1: He'd knock you down and let his horse trample you. After all, the Pony Express must get through!
column2: 他會直接把你撞倒，讓馬把你踩過去。畢竟小馬快遞可是使命必達！

column1: Sorry, that ain't got no stamp on it.
column2: 抱歉，那東西沒貼郵票。

column1: Tampering with the Pony Express by shooting the rider is frowned upon.
column2: 開槍打快遞騎士、妨礙小馬快遞送信，這種事可是要被人白眼的。

column1: This is one of the few remaining townspeople. Why they stay, no one knows...
column2: 這是鎮上僅剩不多的居民之一。他們為什麼還留在這裡，沒人知道……

column1: You talkin' to ME?
column2: 你在跟「我」講話？

column1: Well, I...
column2: 呃，我……

column1: What am I, some sort of CLOWN to you?
column2: 我在你眼裡是什麼，小丑嗎？

column1: No...
column2: 不是……

column1: What, do I walk funny or something?
column2: 怎樣，我走路很好笑嗎？

column1: No, and please don't hurt me...
column2: 不是，拜託別傷害我……

column1: Good! Nice talkin' to ya. Seeya 'round.
column2: 很好！跟你聊得挺愉快。回頭見。

column1: You touchin' ME?
column2: 你在碰「我」？

column1: I was just...
column2: 我只是……

column1: Maybe you're tryin' to pick my pocket?
column2: 你該不會是想扒我口袋吧？

column1: Not at all, I just...
column2: 才沒有，我只是……

column1: Maybe you need a lesson! Well, I'm just the guy to teach it to you!
column2: 看樣子你需要上一課！好啊，我正好是教你這課的最佳人選！

column1: But...
column2: 可是……

column1: If you're going to pick someone's pocket, you have to simultaneously apply some sort of pressure to another part of their body. F'rinstance, squeeze their upper arm, and at the same time, gently remove their wallet. Here, let's run through it a few times...
column2: 想扒別人的口袋，你得同時在他身體別的地方施點壓力。比方說，捏一下對方的上臂，同時輕輕把他的錢包摸走。來，我們多練幾次……

column1: I'm sorry, I really don't have the time. Thanks, anyway.
column2: 抱歉，我真的沒時間。還是謝謝你。

column1: Okay, well, let me know!
column2: 好吧，那你想通了再說！

column1: Don't GIVE it to me! Hide it in my pocket! Sneak it into my jacket! Try to... oh, never mind, you'll never be any good at pick-pocketing.
column2: 別直接「給」我！要藏進我口袋裡！偷偷塞進我外套！要不然……唉，算了，你這輩子都當不了扒手的料。

column1: There's no need to waste your ammo on HIM. You could pump twenty rounds into him and he STILL wouldn't shut up.
column2: 用不著在他身上浪費子彈。就算你賞他二十發，他還是閉不了嘴。

column1: One of the few remaining townspeople wanders around, trying to find a decent opera house that's still open.
column2: 鎮上僅剩不多的居民之一，到處晃來晃去，想找一間還在營業、像樣的歌劇院。

column1: Hi.
column2: 嗨。

column1: Talkative fella, ain't he?
column2: 這傢伙話還真多，是吧？

column1: You like the poncho, eh? The poncho, she's pretty, eh? I getta you a poncho some day!
column2: 你喜歡這件斗篷齁？這斗篷，水啦，對吧？改天我也弄一件給你！

column1: No thanks, sonny, but have you thought about purchasing some life insurance? You know, in these days of toil and strife, we have to prepare for the...
column2: 不用了，小夥子，不過你有沒有考慮過買份人壽保險啊？你知道的，這年頭辛苦又動盪，我們得先做好準備，以防……

column1: Pardon me, I think I hear someone burning or something.
column2: 不好意思，我好像聽到有人在燒什麼東西還是怎樣的。

column1: You can't be serious! What's his crime? What did he ever do to you?
column2: 你該不會是認真的吧！他犯了什麼罪？他到底哪裡得罪你了？

column1: That's Mrs. Tucker, one of the respectable women of the town. "Respectable" meaning she doesn't SELL it!
column2: 那是塔克太太，鎮上「正經」女士之一。所謂「正經」，意思是她不「賣」那個！

column1: Nice day, ain't it?
column2: 今天天氣真好，是吧？

column1: Please! Do you always go shoving people?
column2: 拜託！你老是這樣推人嗎？

column1: I didn't shove you.
column2: 我又沒推你。

column1: I accept your apology.
column2: 我接受你的道歉。

column1: I work for what I have. I don't want people giving me things.
column2: 我擁有的一切都是自己掙來的。我不需要別人施捨東西給我。

column1: Golly, I was just trying to help.
column2: 天啊，我只是想幫忙而已。

column1: Hmph!
column2: 哼！

column1: Just because she's unpleasant doesn't mean she deserves to die.
column2: 她討人厭歸討人厭，也不代表她就該死。

column1: That's Ima Flurt, the lunch room lady. Of course, since the schoolhouse only consists of one room, there's not much for Ima to do but waltz around town waiting for someone to build a cafeteria. Nice work if you can get it!
column2: 那是艾瑪芙勒特，午餐室的女士。不過呢，學校就只有一間教室，艾瑪也沒什麼事好做，只能在鎮上晃來晃去，等哪天有人蓋間餐廳出來。這種美差，誰不想要！

column1: Howdy, ma'am.
column2: 您好啊，女士。

column1: She smiles at you. If your heart didn't already belong to Penelope, you might be tempted to ask her to join you for a glass of sarsaparilla.
column2: 她對你微笑。要不是你的心早就給了潘妮洛普，你可能會忍不住想約她喝杯沙士。

column1: Ooooh! Right here? In front of everyone?
column2: 喔喔喔！就在這裡？當著大家的面？

column1: I suppose that would be indiscreet. Meet me in the parking lot, after the game.
column2: 這樣好像是不太得體。遊戲結束後，停車場見。

column1: Okay! <tee-hee> My, you're CUTE!
column2: 好啊！<tee-hee> 哎呀，你還真「可愛」！

column1: She casts her eyes downward, as if to indicate that she's too shy to accept such a gracious offer. Isn't that endearing?
column2: 她低下眼睛，好像在表示自己太害羞，不敢接受這麼大方的邀請。是不是很惹人憐愛？

column1: Hey, you're supposed to be one of the GOOD GUYS! You LIKE this woman! Remember?
column2: 嘿，你可是「好人」耶！你「喜歡」這個女人！記得嗎？

column1: Why, it's Mrs O'Hanahan and her darling little boy, Rocko. The last time they were in your shop you only lost $17.39 in breakables. God willing, they won't be needing any prescriptions filled today!
column2: 咦，是歐哈納翰太太跟她的寶貝兒子洛可。他們上次來你店裡，你也才損失十七塊三毛九的易碎品而已。老天保佑，他們今天不用來配藥！

column1: Do I look like I have time for idle chit-chat? Honestly! Some people think that just because a woman works at home she has scads of free time. Well, let me tell you, I don't! I have the washing, the ironing, the cow to milk, the butter to churn, the barber shop to sweep out, the books to keep... Why, I could just go on and on. But as usual, I'm in too much of a hurry and a lady never complains about her lot in life.
column2: 我看起來像有空閒聊嗎？講真的！有些人以為女人在家做事就有一大堆空閒時間。告訴你，我才沒有！洗衣服、燙衣服、擠牛奶、攪奶油、打掃理髮店、記帳……唉呀，這清單我可以一直數下去。不過老樣子，我總是忙得要命，而淑女是從不抱怨自己命苦的。

column1: Not that all the women around here are ladies of course! Why the stories I could tell you about SOME of these women! Not that I know any of them personally of course, but one does hear talk around the barber shop, you know. But really, I am TOO busy to be standing around like this. Good day!
column2: 當然啦，這附近的女人也不是個個都算淑女！有些女人的故事，我可以講給你聽呢！當然我跟她們沒有私交，不過在理髮店裡總會聽到些風聲的。不過說真的，我實在太忙了，不能在這站著閒聊。再見！

column1: Obviously she's a married lady, and that kid looks like he might bite!
column2: 她顯然是有夫之婦，而且那小鬼看起來會咬人！

column1: Land sakes, I don't need one of those. My Salvatore gives me everything I need! And I DO mean "everything." Why, just the other day, he plum near worn me out...
column2: 我的老天，我才不需要那玩意兒。我的薩瓦多什麼都給我準備好了！而且我是說「什麼都」。就前幾天，他還把我給累得夠嗆呢……

column1: Gee, I'd love to hear all about it, but I've got to run.
column2: 天啊，我很想聽你講完，可是我得走了。

column1: Yes, they're offensive, but try to avoid retaliation. Remember, you're here to HELP!
column2: 沒錯，他們是很討人厭，不過盡量別報復。記住，你是來這裡「幫忙」的！

column1: Hop Sing is the only chinese person left after the railroad was built. He took a shine to Helen at Mom's Cafe and stayed to help her make a go of it.
column2: 阿星是鐵路建好後，鎮上僅剩的中國人。他看上了老媽餐館的海倫，便留下來幫她把生意撐起來。

column1: Hop Sing doesn't speak English, and your Mandarin is a little rusty.
column2: 阿星不會說英文，而你的國語也有點生疏了。

column1: Hello, Hopalong Singh!
column2: 哈囉，阿星大俠！

column1: Hi-yah!!!
column2: 哈呀！！！

column1: This not my table!
column2: 這不是我的桌子！

column1: Hop Singh's a friend, not a foe! So quit pointing that thing at everyone.
column2: 阿星是朋友，不是敵人！別再拿那東西對著大家揮來揮去了。

column1: Main Street is its usual busy self today.
column2: 大街今天一如往常地熱鬧。

column1: What are you going to do? Holler loud enough for the whole town to hear?
column2: 你打算怎麼辦？扯開嗓子讓全鎮的人都聽見嗎？

column1: You'd fall off the balcony if you tried to reach them from here!
column2: 你要是想從這裡搆到那些東西，肯定會從陽台上摔下去！

column1: You can't try that from up here!
column2: 你在這上面沒辦法這麼做！

column1: Don't waste your ammo shooting at innocents!
column2: 別把子彈浪費在無辜的人身上！

column1: Caution: the Surgeon General has determined that you've gotten EXACTLY what you deserved.
column2: 警告：衛生署長認定，你得到的下場正是你應得的。

column1: Next time, don't inhale.
column2: 下次記得別吸進去。

column1: Poor, poor Freddy... died for lack of garlic butter!
column2: 可憐的佛萊迪啊……就這樣死於缺了大蒜奶油！

column1: The Second Rule of the Old West Medicine Chest: Never drink your own mistakes!
column2: 西部藥箱第二守則：千萬別喝下自己調錯的藥！

column1: Next time, try drinking something healthier... like radiator sealant.
column2: 下次試著喝點更健康的東西……比如水箱防漏劑。

column1: Next time, don't inhale!
column2: 下次記得別吸進去！

column1: Rest in pieces.
column2: 屍骨已碎，安息吧。

column1: Guess you're a flatlander.
column2: 看來你就是那種平地來的生手。

column1: As the town hero, you've been given the sack.
column2: 身為鎮上的英雄，你這下可被炒了魷魚。

column1: A crushing defeat!
column2: 被壓得粉碎的慘敗！

column1: Rest in pieces, Freddy Pharkas.
column2: 屍骨已碎，安息吧，佛萊迪·法卡斯。

column1: That's what you get for firing a weapon that hasn't been cleaned since Lincoln was assassinated!
column2: 誰叫你去開一把從林肯遇刺後就沒清過的槍！

column1: Shooting people point-blank is frowned upon in polite society.
column2: 在文明社會裡，近距離對人開槍可是很不得體的。

column1: A bubblin' crude! Blood, that is. Red gold. Tourniquet Tea.
column2: 汩汩冒泡的原油啊！其實是血啦。紅色黃金，止血良藥。

column1: You come to a sworded end!
column2: 你就這樣命喪劍下，劃下句點！

column1: Maybe if you could've caught him red-handed...
column2: 或許你當初該人贓俱獲逮個正著才對……

column1: It's Slime Time!
column2: 黏答答的時刻到了！

column1: Take a burn!
column2: 給你點顏色燒燒！

column1: Coarsegold's shot to hell now!
column2: 粗金鎮這下徹底完蛋了！

column1: That death is too disgusting to describe!
column2: 這種死法噁心到沒法形容！

column1: Dammit, Freddy, you're a pharmacist, not a veterinarian!
column2: 該死，佛萊迪，你是藥劑師，不是獸醫！

column1: You've sold out. Some Western Hero YOU are!
column2: 你出賣了自己。你算哪門子的西部英雄！

column1: An' that's how Freddy met his ironic ol' death... fum ingestin' horsey products that wuz never meant to be ingested. A few days later, all o' Coarsegold got bought up by some mysterious East Coast consortium, and... well... The rest, as they's fond of sayin', is history.
column2: 這就是佛萊迪那諷刺的死法……吃了根本不該吃下肚的馬用藥品給毒死的。沒過幾天，整個粗金鎮就被東岸一個神秘財團給買走了，然後嘛……剩下的，就跟人家常說的一樣，都成了歷史囉。

column1: Too bad about thet, y'know. Guess Freddy's constitution couldn't handle th' noxious fumes that wuz expectoratin' through town. Seems to me a man with his edukashun shoulda known whut to do about a simple bit o'flatulence, but hey, I'm just a simple whittlin' sorta story-tellin' entertainin' kinda guy. And thet's m'story for now. Now git along into bed, it's past yer bedtime.
column2: 唉，說來也真可惜。俺猜佛萊迪的身子骨就是扛不住那股在鎮上竄來竄去的毒氣。照理說，像他那麼有學問的人，該懂得怎麼處理個小小的脹氣才對嘛，不過俺呢，也不過是個愛削木頭、愛講古逗人開心的老頭子罷了。今兒個的故事就講到這，快去睡吧，早就過了你的睡覺時間囉。

column1: And thet's how Freddy done up and died... from eatin' mollusks without the proper accompanying condiments. And as fer Coarsegold, well, it wuzn't long before it was wiped from the face of the earth. (sob) (sob) (sniffle) (retch)
column2: 這就是佛萊迪的死法……吃了軟體動物，卻沒配上該有的佐料給害死的。至於粗金鎮嘛，沒過多久就從地表上消失了。（啜泣）（啜泣）（抽鼻子）（乾嘔）

column1: So, sorry to say, thet's how Freddy Pharkas done up and died. Takin' medication he didn't need were the death of him, and it warn't long afterwards that Coarsegold fell into the hands of... of... Gol durn it, I'm too choked up to tell yuz how it all ended. <sniff>
column2: 唉，說來遺憾，佛萊迪·法卡斯就是這麼死的。吃了根本不需要的藥，要了他的命，沒多久粗金鎮就落到了……落到了……哎呀，俺哽咽得說不下去了，沒法跟你講後來怎麼了。〈抽鼻子〉

column1: 'Course, the rilly ironic thang is thet Freddy shoulda known better'n to drink that arful patent medicine. It wuz like to pourin' a bottle of grain alkyhol down yer gullet. Freddy died jes' a li'l while later, foamin' at the mouth and pointin' at sum purple wild dingos he thought he wuz seein'. Coarsegold came to a nasty end, whut with the... well, I don't like t' talk about it, it gimmee the ol' white trash blues.
column2: 說真的，最諷刺的是佛萊迪應該早知道不該喝那瓶劣質成藥。那味道就跟灌一整瓶穀物酒精下肚差不多。沒過多久佛萊迪就死了，嘴裡直冒白沫，還一直指著他以為看見的紫色野狗。粗金鎮的下場也很難看，那個……唉，俺不想多講，一講就讓俺心裡發悶。

column1: Poor ol' Freddy Pharkas done laughed hisself to death... but the folks of Coarsegold, they wuzn't laughin' two weeks later when the whole town got bought up from underneath 'em. Ol' Willy's done spinnin' yarns fer now. This one always makes me go all teary-eyed and phlegmy.
column2: 可憐的老佛萊迪·法卡斯竟然是笑死的……不過兩星期後，整個鎮子被人從腳底下買走時，粗金鎮的鄉親們可就笑不出來了。老威利今兒個講古就講到這。這故事每次都讓俺紅了眼眶、哽咽不已。

column1: Well, you gots to admit the fella died tryin' to defend his town. Now, we all either hadda leave town or get shot up anyways, so it's not as if Freddy'd done any real good, but it were still excitin' to have him around fer awhile. I guess that story don't end so good. Lemme see, have I told you th' one about the travelin' band uniform salesman and the librarian? Welp, it seems there was trouble in River City, and they had this pool table, and...
column2: 好啦，你也得承認，那小子好歹是為了保衛自己的鎮子才死的。俺們後來不是離鄉背井，就是照樣挨槍子兒，所以說佛萊迪其實也沒幫上什麼真正的忙，不過有他在的那陣子，倒也挺熱鬧的。俺猜這故事結局不怎麼好。讓俺想想，俺跟你講過那個賣樂隊制服的推銷員跟圖書館員的故事沒？欸，聽說是河城出了麻煩，他們有張撞球檯，然後……

column1: So thet's how Freddy's brilliant career done come to a screechin' halt. He sank into the swamp and wuz never seen again. A shame, too, 'cuz the rest of us were kinda plannin' on bein' in the sequel. That ain't one of my better stories, anyhoo. Say, did I ever tell ya the story about ol' King Graham? It seems there wuz this evil wizard, and he got Graham into just a peck o' trouble...
column2: 佛萊迪那輝煌的前程，就這麼嘎然而止。他沉進了沼澤裡，再沒人見過他。也真可惜，俺們其他人本來還盤算著要在續集裡露臉呢。反正這也不算俺講得最好的故事。對了，俺跟你講過老葛拉漢國王的故事沒？聽說有個邪惡巫師，把葛拉漢害得麻煩纏身……

column1: Kinda silly, but yep, that's how Freddy died... crushed by a load of bicarbonate while tryin' to put out the fire at the ol' Assay office. The whole town burned to the ground that night, and the British troops got turned back. British Troops? Waitaminnit, I'm getting confused. OH, okay, now I remembers. It wuzn't Freddy that got squashed by them sacks of powder, that wuz sumthin' else. Lemme go back and figger out what actually DID happen to Freddy Pharkas.
column2: 說來有點蠢，不過沒錯，佛萊迪就是這麼死的……在老驗金所滅火時，被一堆碳酸氫鈉粉包給壓死了。整個鎮子那晚燒個精光，英軍還被擊退了。英軍？等等，俺越講越糊塗了。喔，對，俺想起來了。被那堆藥粉包壓死的不是佛萊迪，是別的什麼東西。讓俺重新想想佛萊迪·法卡斯到底是怎麼回事。

column1: Yep, Freddy fell down, went "boom." It were a sad day, we found 'em all squished and not really livin' anymore. 'Course, we had our own problems to deal with, all of a sudden-like. Thet's about when the town of Coarsegold ceased to exist, as we'd done known it. But thet's another story, boys 'n girls. I gots to be alone wif my thoughts fer awhile.
column2: 沒錯，佛萊迪摔了一跤，「碰」的一聲。那天真悲傷，俺們發現他被壓得扁扁的，早就沒了氣。當然啦，俺們自己突然間也有一堆麻煩事要應付。大概就是從那時候起，俺們熟悉的粗金鎮就不復存在了。不過那又是另一個故事囉，孩子們。俺得自個兒靜一靜。

column1: Nope, Freddy didn't quite make it outta that schoolhouse alive. Nope, nope, nope, nope, nope. Nunh-unh. Penelope, she bought up the whole town, or whut wuz left of it after the explosion, and made a fortune with the oil rights. How wuz we to know the town wuz built on oil fields? We didn't even know whut oil wuz! We warn't STUPID, y'know. Just nobody'd told us whut OIL were! Fer corn's sake! Now I'm riled. Go tell yerself stories fum now on. Don't even talk to me.
column2: 不，佛萊迪根本沒能活著走出那間校舍。不、不、不、不、不。沒有的事。潘妮洛普把整個鎮子——或者說爆炸後剩下的部分——全買了下來，靠石油權大賺了一筆。俺們哪裡曉得這鎮子是蓋在油田上頭？俺們連石油是啥都不知道！俺們才不是笨蛋咧，只是沒人跟俺們說過石油是什麼玩意兒罷了！老天爺啊！現在俺可火大了。從今以後你自個兒去講故事吧，別再跟俺說話了。

column1: Guess ol' Freddy just warn't thinkin' too well thet day. Them guns hadn't been fired in decades. The resultin' explosion took off Freddy's hands, his forearms, shattered his clavicle and broke his whutcha call your left tibia. He died kinda messy-like a couple hours later. As fer the rest of Coarsegold, well... let's just say it wuz laid to rest not long afterwards.
column2: 俺猜老佛萊迪那天腦子就是沒轉過來。那些槍已經幾十年沒開過火了。結果那一炸，把佛萊迪的雙手、前臂都炸沒了，鎖骨碎裂，連那個叫什麼……左邊的脛骨也斷了。幾個鐘頭後，他就這麼慘兮兮地死了。至於粗金鎮剩下的部分嘛……這麼說吧，沒多久也跟著入土為安了。

column1: Yip, Freddy's itchy trigger finger got th' best of him. The sheriff wuzn't about to let Freddy git away with shootin' folks in cold blood. 'Course, the Sheriff pretty much shut down the town a few days later, throwin' everybuddy out inta the street. Never did figger out who he was actin' on behalf of, anyways. And thet's m'story fer now, boys and girls. Mah ol' epiglottis ain't whut she used ta be.
column2: 沒錯，佛萊迪那按耐不住的扳機指終究害了他。警長可不會放過他冷血殺人這件事。當然啦，沒過幾天警長就把整個鎮子給封了，把大伙兒統統趕到街上去。俺們始終沒搞清楚他是替誰辦事的。今兒個的故事就講到這，孩子們。俺這把老喉嚨，也不比從前囉。

column1: So Freddy were left fer dead, oozin' blood inta the hard-packed dirt of the streets of Coarsegold. Not long afterwards, those who wouldn't git outta their beloved Coarsegold ended up the same way. Life's a real bitch sumtimes, ain't she? Pardon me now, nature's callin'.
column2: 佛萊迪就這麼倒在地上等死，血滲進了粗金鎮那堅硬的街土裡。沒過多久，那些捨不得離開心愛的粗金鎮的人，也落得同樣下場。人生有時候還真是磨人哪，是吧？俺先失陪了，內急啊。

column1: Yip, Freddy met his death at the tip of a sword. Too bad, 'cuz he'd gotten so close to savin' Coarsegold from fallin' into Penelope's mercenary clutches. So Penelope went ahead with her little scheme. She bought up the town real cheap and made millions in the oil industry. She died just a few years back, but she wuz so rich that she had herself froze solid 'til they could find a way to bring her back to life. Ain't that a hoot?
column2: 沒錯，佛萊迪死在劍尖底下。真可惜，他當時眼看就要救下粗金鎮，不讓它落入潘妮洛普那雙貪婪的手裡了。於是潘妮洛普就這麼把她的小算盤打成了。她用低價買下整個鎮子，靠石油生意賺進幾百萬。她幾年前才過世，不過她有錢到把自己冷凍起來，等著哪天有辦法讓她死而復生。這不挺妙的嗎？

column1: ...Mebbe if Freddy'd found sum way to stop "Aces" before he'd won up all the deeds to the town, there'd still be a Coarsegold today. 'Course, Aces weren't actin' on his own, sumbuddy'd put him up to it. Never found out who or why, though. And as fer me, I got outta town by sundown and hightailed it to the Ozarks, where a man kin still be a man wifout other men questionin' me about bein' manly or not. But that ain't neither here nor there. Now get outta here.
column2: ……要是佛萊迪能在「阿牌」把鎮子的地契全贏走之前想個法子攔住他，今天說不定還有粗金鎮在。當然啦，阿牌不是自己一個人搞的，是有人在背後指使。不過俺始終沒查出是誰、又是為了什麼。至於俺自己嘛，天黑前就逃出了鎮子，一路跑到歐扎克山區去，在那兒男人還能堂堂正正做男人，沒人管你夠不夠男子氣概。不過這都是題外話了。你現在給俺滾吧。

column1: Now it wuzn't as if Freddy didn't have enuf time to stop them snails, but somehow, he screwed it up but good. The snails ran over Coarsegold and slimed it to kingdom come. Those of us thet wuzn't kilt hadda leave town without bringin' anything with us. I wuz one of the ones that didn't make it. Thet's right, sonny! Yer talkin' to a GHOST! BOO!!! Nyah-ha-ha... <cough> <wheeze> <hack>
column2: 這倒不是說佛萊迪沒時間攔住那些蝸牛，不知怎麼搞的，他就是搞砸了。那些蝸牛橫掃粗金鎮，把整鎮黏得一塌糊塗。沒被害死的俺們，只能兩手空空逃離家鄉。而俺呢，就是沒能逃過一劫的那一個。沒錯，小子！你現在正跟一個鬼魂說話呢！哇啊啊！呀哈哈……〈咳嗽〉〈喘氣〉〈咳〉

column1: So 'cuz Freddy couldn't think of a way to put out the fire, all of Coarsegold was in ashes by the next mornin'. The loss of life wuz tree-menjus, but somewhere, sumbuddy was sure happy about it, 'cuz before you knew it... Well, thet's another story, boys 'n girls.
column2: 就因為佛萊迪想不出法子滅火，隔天早上整個粗金鎮就成了一片灰燼。死傷慘重得不得了，不過在某個角落，有人肯定是樂歪了，因為不知不覺間……這個嘛，又是另一個故事囉，孩子們。

column1: ...and them rowdy cowhands, whom sumbody'd hired to come in and skare folks off a bit, ended up shootin' Freddy and chasin' everbody outta town. And as fer Coarsegold, well, none of us ever found out who wuz behind all the evildoin's. Not that we cared. It warn't that much of a town, anyways. Say, did I ever tell ya the story about a little nose-pickin' brat named Willy Beamish? Welp, it all started in this town that wuz mostly strip-malls...
column2: ……那些被人請來嚇唬鄉親的鬧事牛仔，後來把佛萊迪給斃了，還把大伙兒統統趕出鎮外。至於粗金鎮嘛，俺們始終沒查出這些壞事背後是誰搞的鬼。反正俺們也不怎麼在乎，這鎮子本來也沒多了不起。對了，俺跟你講過那個愛挖鼻孔的小屁孩威利·畢米許的故事沒？欸，一切都是從一個滿是購物商場的小鎮開始的……

column1: That's how it all ended. Freddy'd let the whole dang town die o' the creepin' cruds. I wuz lucky, I stuck to whisky so's I wouldn't get poizoned by the town's drinkin' water. Iffn only Freddy'd used his pharmacological powers fer the good o' the town. <sigh> Then this story'd mighta had a happier endin'.
column2: 這一切就這麼結束了。佛萊迪讓整個該死的鎮子染上怪病死光光。俺算幸運，俺只喝威士忌，才沒被鎮上的飲用水給毒到。要是佛萊迪能把他那身藥學本事用在鎮子的福祉上就好了。〈嘆氣〉這故事說不定就會有個圓滿一點的結局。

column1: So after awhile, most folks in town plum passed out from the noxious fumes. Them that didn't get kilt by the aroma got kilt when sum idjit struck a flint. Anyways, it was a painless way t' go, even if it were kinda nauseating. And Freddy, well, at least he didn't have to reckon with his secret past anymore. Now if Freddy had just thunk a little bit faster an' a little bit smarter, things mighta turned out a mite different. Now, how 'bout another story, or did you wanna hear this one again?
column2: 過了一陣子，鎮上大部分人都被那股毒氣熏得昏死過去。沒被臭氣熏死的人，又被某個蠢蛋擦火石給引爆炸死了。反正，這死法倒是不怎麼痛苦，就是有點噁心。至於佛萊迪嘛，好歹他再也不必去面對自己那段秘密的過去了。要是佛萊迪當初能想得快一點、聰明一點，事情或許會有點不一樣的結局。好啦，要不要俺再講一個，還是你想再聽一遍這個？

column1: So before he hardly got nowhere, Freddy sold out to the Banker and walked outta Coarsegold with enough cash to start a new life somewheres else. Naah, we don't keep in touch no more. I kinda resent the guy, him sellin' us all down the river and sich. We all hadda give up our propitty after that. For all I know, he died in a pharmacy, and good riddance to him. He wuz never nuttin' special, anyway. I forgit why I even brought him up.
column2: 所以還沒怎麼折騰，佛萊迪就把自己賣給了那個銀行家，揣著足夠的現金離開粗金鎮，到別處展開新生活去了。不，俺們早就沒聯絡了。俺其實挺恨那小子的，他這樣把大伙兒都給賣了。俺們後來都被迫放棄了自己的財產。就俺所知，他大概是死在哪間藥局裡吧，死了也好，少了個禍害。反正他也從來不是什麼了不起的人物。俺都忘了自己幹嘛提起他了。

column2: 在下雖感激你的好意，卻必須留在這裡。在下絕不能傷害任何一隻螞蟻，而目前也想不出任何能不傷及其他生靈，又能離開這蟻丘的辦法。

column1: How gracious to offer me an empty can of beans! I am afraid I am having not a use in mind for such a can of nothing.
column2: 你竟願意給在下一個空豆子罐頭，真是太慷慨了！只可惜在下實在想不出這種空罐頭有什麼用處。

column1: I am afraiding the ice pick will not present me with any assistance.
column2: 在下恐怕這把冰鑿幫不上任何忙。

column1: The charcoal is a most gracious offer, however I am having no hibachi at this moment.
column2: 這炭真是慷慨的贈禮，不過在下此刻並沒有火盆可用。

column1: Rein? Rein? Go away, come again another day. That is a poem which I just conceived.
column2: 韁繩？韁繩？快走開，改天再來。這是在下剛剛即興作的一首詩。

column1: I do not eat beef, snails, or ham. I do not eat them, Fred, I am.
column2: 在下不吃牛肉、蝸牛，也不吃火腿。在下就是不吃這些，佛萊迪，不吃就是不吃。

column1: I am not needing empty bottles. I have already evacuated myself several times, with great ceremony.
column2: 在下不需要空瓶子。在下已經隆重地排解過好幾次了。

column1: I am thinking a key is not opening the way to escape for me, though yours is a most gracious offer.
column2: 在下認為一把鑰匙開不出逃脫的路，不過你的好意在下心領了。

column1: The ladder might assist my situation, however I am not in positioning to maneuver it thusly to facilitate escapage.
column2: 梯子或許能幫上在下的處境，不過在下目前的姿勢實在無法操作它來助在下脫身。

column1: Unfortunately, I am not conversant with the traditional rope-climbing trick of my countrymen, and thus your rope will not be of helpage.
column2: 很不巧，在下並不熟悉同胞那套傳統的爬繩戲法，因此你這條繩子幫不上忙。

column1: I am not caring to be lassoed, thank you! I prefer to die with dignity than be yanked so unceremoniously like a most common livestock.
column2: 在下可不想被套索套住，謝了！在下寧可有尊嚴地死去，也不願像尋常牲畜一樣被這麼粗魯地拖走。

column1: A candle wax is a most beautiful thing to become one with, but I am afraid my ability to commune with paraffin has been impaired upon my present situation.
column2: 蠟燭是件能與之合而為一的美妙之物，但在下恐怕以目前的處境，實在無法與石蠟好好溝通了。

column1: I am appreciating the offer now! However, no matter which clothes I am appareling, my predicament remains a puzzlement.
column2: 在下此刻十分感激你的好意！不過，無論在下穿上哪件衣物，眼下的困境依然是個謎團。

column1: It will be ready Tuesday. Just having a joke upon you. I know nothing of this claim check.
column2: 星期二就會好了。開個玩笑罷了，在下對這張取件單一無所知。

column1: Wanna put the boots on? That way, at least you wouldn't be walking on ants in your bare feet!
column2: 要不要把靴子穿上？這樣至少你不會光著腳踩在螞蟻上！

column1: Ah, that is generously of an idea, but I still would end up putting to an end the lives of many precious ants.
column2: 啊，這主意真是慷慨，不過在下終究還是會結束許多寶貴螞蟻的性命。

column1: I am not caring to read your personal mail right this dying moment!
column2: 在下這垂死的時刻，可沒興趣讀你的私人信件！

column1: I prefer not to ingest the prescriptions of others, although I am thanking you presently.
column2: 在下寧可不服用他人的處方箋，不過此刻仍要謝謝你。

column1: These snails are the leading edge of a stampede of imported French escargot, recently escaped from a haughty San Francisco restaurant, being chased by a posse of snooty San Francisco chefs. They appear to stretch to the horizon, and they're heading straight for town. If you don't do something soon to prevent them, they'll slime the entire city.
column2: 這些蝸牛只是大批進口法國田螺的先鋒，牠們剛從舊金山一家傲慢的餐廳逃出來，後頭還有一群自命不凡的舊金山主廚窮追不捨。牠們一路綿延到天邊，直直朝鎮上而來。你要是不趕快想辦法阻止，牠們會把整座城都黏得一團糟。

column1: Here, snails. Here, boy! Er, here, girl... ah, Here, whatever!
column2: 過來，蝸牛們。過來，好孩子！呃，還是好女孩……啊，管牠是什麼，過來就對了！

column1: Oh, what's the use? You decide you'll never be able to train a snail to come when you call, let alone sit up and beg!
column2: 唉，何必呢？你認定自己絕對沒辦法訓練蝸牛聽你叫喚過來，更別說叫牠坐下、作揖了！

column1: Slurp.
column2: 唏溜。

column1: Slurp!
column2: 唏溜！

column1: SLURP!
column2: 唏溜！！

column1: Ahhhhhh.
You grab a couple of snails from the front of the pack while imagining the aroma of warm drawn butter.
column2: 你從蝸牛隊伍最前面抓了幾隻，腦海中浮現溫熱奶油的香氣。

column1: You have more than enough snails already!
column2: 你手上的蝸牛已經夠多了！

column1: Umm. Skewered snails sound so special! (But wrong.)
column2: 嗯……串烤蝸牛聽起來還挺特別的！（不過不對。）

column1: You could try to kill all those snails by smashing each of them with your beer bottles, but it would take forever. However, they DO look thirsty.
column2: 你是可以拿啤酒瓶一隻隻把蝸牛砸死，但那樣要砸到天荒地老。不過，牠們看起來確實挺渴的。

column1: Hey, boys! It's Miller time!!
column2: 弟兄們，美樂時間到了！！

column1: And with that, you cleverly pour bottle after bottle of Sam Andreas's St. Louis brew onto the dusty road in an attempt to divert the stampede. Will it work? Will the snails fall for your ruse? Will they accept a "domestic?"
column2: 於是你靈機一動，把一瓶又一瓶山姆安德烈亞斯牌聖路易啤酒倒在塵土飛揚的路上，想藉此引開這波蝸牛大軍。這招管用嗎？蝸牛會上你的當嗎？牠們會賞臉喝這款「國產貨」嗎？

column1: Slurping their little hearts out (if snails may be said to slurp, or to have hearts for that matter!), the little guys "follow your lead" straight over to the cliff beside Blackwater Creek.
column2: 這群小傢伙拚了命地嗦（如果蝸牛也算得上「嗦」，或者算得上有「心」的話！），乖乖「跟著你的腳步」，一路走向黑水溪旁的懸崖。

column1: Isn't that cute? They're so gullible! Don't they look just like little lemmings, marching over that cliff?
column2: 是不是很可愛？牠們也太好騙了！看牠們一隻隻走向懸崖，像不像一群小旅鼠？

column1: The local insect population has been thriving, what with all the dry weather Coarsegold's been having lately. This is one of the smaller anthills around the town.
column2: 這陣子粗金鎮天氣乾燥，當地的昆蟲反倒繁殖得很旺盛。這是鎮上比較小的一座螞蟻窩。

column1: Hey, what are you ants dune here, anyway?
column2: 欸，你們這些螞蟻在這沙丘上到底搞什麼名堂？

column1: They don't even stop, let alone crack a smile!
column2: 牠們連停都不停一下，更別說笑一個了！

column1: You really have no desire to touch that anthill, nor do you wish to further your entomologic collection at this time.
column2: 你實在沒有想碰那座螞蟻窩的慾望，此刻也不想再擴充你的昆蟲收藏。

column1: I've got it, Srini! I know how I can help you!
column2: 我有辦法了，斯里尼！我知道該怎麼幫你！

column1: Here you go, pardner. Hoof your way across this!
column2: 拿去吧，夥計。踩著這個過去！

column1: Ooooh! My balance sense is stretching now.
column2: 喔喔！我的平衡感快撐不住了。

column1: You made it!
column2: 你辦到了！

column1: Oh, thank you, Mr. P! You saved me!
column2: 噢，謝謝你，P先生！你救了我！

column1: Please don't call me that.
column2: 拜託別這樣叫我。
