column1: Don't leave the ladder lying around unless you have a specific reason to do so!
column2: 沒有特別的理由，別把梯子隨便亂放！

column1: The ants aren't hurting anyone! Why dig up their home? How would you like someone to come along and throw dirt around YOUR home? (Okay, bad example.)
column2: 螞蟻又沒惹到誰！幹嘛去挖牠們的家？換作有人跑來把泥土撒得你家到處都是，你會高興嗎？（好啦，這例子舉得不太好。）

column1: As far as the eye can see, the landscape is filled with rocks... and not much else.
column2: 放眼望去，這片地形除了石頭還是石頭……別無其他。

column1: Prickly pear cactus is one of your favorite examples of the species.
column2: 刺梨仙人掌是你最愛的仙人掌品種之一。

column1: You simply can't stand the thought of pricking yourself.
column2: 你光想到會被刺到就受不了。

column1: The road leads off around the Sierra Nevada foothills to Oakhurst... and its famous floppy disk mines.
column2: 這條路沿著內華達山脈的山腳，一路通往橡赫斯特……以及當地聞名的軟碟礦場。

column1: The road is dusty and uninformative.
column2: 這條路滿是塵土，看不出什麼名堂。

column1: (BEATNIK LIKE) The road is packed solid. You just can't dig it, man.
column2: （披頭族腔）這條路夯得死硬。老兄，你根本沒法融入它啦。

column1: The rickety old bridge over Blackwater Creek has seen better days. At least it's in better shape than the railroad trestle over there.
column2: 這座橫跨黑水溪的老橋搖搖欲墜，風光不再。不過至少比那邊的鐵路棧橋狀況好一些。

column1: But... but... but that's the piece that holds together the ENTIRE BRIDGE! (Well, actually, it's not, but you were really scared there for a second, eh? You weren't?)
column2: 可是……可是……可是那塊木頭撐著整座橋耶！（好啦，其實沒有，不過你剛剛真的嚇了一跳，對吧？沒有嗎？）

column1: Old timers tell of bygone days when the Fish Camp & Pacific Railroad's heavy industrial traffic kept these rails as bright as new. No more.
column2: 老一輩的人說，當年費許營太平洋鐵路的重型貨運絡繹不絕，把這些鐵軌磨得閃閃發亮。如今風光不再。

column1: Once the Fish Camp & Pacific Railroad ran through here, but when their trestle washed out back in '73, they never got around to rebuilding it. It remains there today, a blatant assault on liability standards everywhere.
column2: 費許營太平洋鐵路曾經行經此地，但七三年那場大水沖垮了棧橋後，他們就一直沒空重建。棧橋就這麼留到今天，簡直是對各地公共安全標準的公然挑釁。

column1: The rails glisten in the sun, covered with homebrew.
column2: 鐵軌沾滿了自釀啤酒，在陽光下閃閃發亮。

column1: Oh, railroad tracks, what do I DO? What do I DO?
column2: 喔，鐵軌啊，我該怎麼辦？我該怎麼辦？

column1: You hope they'll put you on the right track. But they don't answer. And now you've lost your train of thought!
column2: 你希望它們能指點你「正確的軌道」。可是它們沒回應。而現在你的思路也「出軌」了！

column1: You slide your hand back and forth across the rusty tracks, getting a little rust-burn in the process.
column2: 你的手在生鏽的鐵軌上來回摩擦，結果被鏽蝕輕輕燙傷了一下。

column1: The rusty tracks now feel a little sticky from the sun-dried beer that the snails missed.
column2: 生鏽的鐵軌現在有點黏，因為上面還沾著蝸牛沒喝完、被太陽曬乾的啤酒。

column1: While you love the drama of breaking open a bottle of beer on a ribbon of steel, you'll retain more brew by using a bottle opener.
column2: 雖然你很愛那種把啤酒瓶敲在鐵軌上開瓶的戲劇效果，但用開瓶器能留住比較多的酒。

column1: You don't have time to be walking around dumping beer all over the place. You've got flatulent horses to attend to!
column2: 你沒空四處閒晃、到處倒啤酒。你還有一堆放屁的馬要照顧呢！

column1: The locals say this creek wasn't nearly so deep back in the old days. You suppose it's just another example of the creative activities of that famous Armenian landscape artist: Soil Erosion.
column2: 當地人說，這條溪以前根本沒這麼深。你猜這又是那位知名亞美尼亞地景藝術家「土壤侵蝕先生」的傑作之一。

column1: You just can't face exploring that cliff face!
column2: 那面峭壁，你實在沒臉去爬。

column1: A few buzzards have landed here, waiting for some unfortunate life form to become "Vulture Chow."
column2: 幾隻禿鷹落在這裡，等著哪個倒楣的生物變成牠們的「禿鷹口糧」。

column1: Poor Cedric the Owl! He'll never delay another scene change!
column2: 可憐的貓頭鷹賽德里克！他再也沒機會拖延下一個場景轉換了！

column1: Leave that poor owl alone, you vicious fiends!
column2: 放過那隻可憐的貓頭鷹吧，你們這些狠毒的畜生！

column1: They ignore you completely.
column2: 牠們完全不理你。

column1: Farewell, Cedric! We hardly knew ye.
column2: 再會了，賽德里克！我們幾乎還來不及認識你呢。

column1: While you might want to do something to those buzzards, they're simply living out their portion of the West's ecology.
column2: 雖然你可能很想找那些禿鷹算帳，但牠們也只是在扮演西部生態鏈中屬於自己的一環。

column1: As much as you want to join in, leave Cedric's carcass for the buzzards.
column2: 你再怎麼想插一腳，還是把賽德里克的屍體留給禿鷹吧。

column1: Your sharp eyes spot a distinctive cloud of dust. It's snailsign! Thar's a stampede a'comin'!
column2: 你眼尖瞧見一團與眾不同的塵雲。那是蝸牛的蹤跡！有一大群蝸牛要衝過來啦！

column1: They can't hear you from this far away.
column2: 隔這麼遠，牠們聽不見你的聲音。

column1: There's nothing you can do from this far away, Freddy.
column2: 佛萊迪，隔這麼遠，你什麼也做不了。

column1: Cedric the Owl looks lost and out-of-place in the hot desert sun. If you listen close, you can almost hear him say, "Freddy, if you're going to go in THERE, I'm going to wait out HERE." (He always has some flimsy excuse!)
column2: 貓頭鷹賽德里克在炙熱的沙漠豔陽下，顯得茫然又格格不入。你若仔細聽，幾乎能聽見他說：「佛萊迪，你要是打算進去『那邊』，我就在『這邊』等你。」（他總有些站不住腳的藉口！）

column1: It's the torn, bloody remains of a talking owl.
column2: 那是一隻會說話的貓頭鷹留下的殘骸，血跡斑斑、支離破碎。

column1: Hey! You!
column2: 喂！你！

column1: (CEDRIC LIKE) You can almost hear Cedric squawk, "I'm waiting here! It's too dangerous out there!" Apparently some adventurer is out in the desert, and the owl's waiting to annoy him when he gets back.
column2: （賽德里克腔）你幾乎能聽見賽德里克尖聲說：「我在這裡等！外面太危險了！」看樣子有個冒險者正在沙漠裡，而這隻貓頭鷹正等著他回來好繼續煩他。

column1: Cedric? Can you hear me?
column2: 賽德里克？你聽得見我嗎？

column1: You almost believe you can hear a weakly-croaked, "Ohhhhh nooooo... I'll... stay... out... here... <gasp>"
column2: 你幾乎相信自己聽見一聲有氣無力的哀鳴：「喔……不……我要……留在……這裡……〈喘〉」

column1: Gee whillikers, you can't quite reach that owl from here. (Too bad; you'd like to wring his neck!)
column2: 唉呀媽呀，你從這裡搆不到那隻貓頭鷹。（真可惜；你還挺想扭斷牠脖子的！）

column1: You dare not; those buzzards will vigorously defend their capture.
column2: 你可不敢；那些禿鷹會拚了命保護牠們的獵物。

column1: Nasty fire ants are swarming around the poor potential Indian Sidekick seated at the top of their anthill. Why, a hungry gaggle of ants like that could strip the flesh off an Indian Sidekick in minutes, leaving nothing but white Sidekick Bones. Better find some way to get him offa there!
column2: 兇惡的火蟻正成群圍著那位可憐、可能成為印第安夥伴的傢伙，他就坐在蟻窩頂上。這麼一大群餓紅眼的螞蟻，幾分鐘內就能把一個印第安夥伴啃得只剩白骨。你最好想個辦法把他弄下來！

column1: A dense swarm of dense fire ants diligently attempts to collect plenty of sand for the coming winter. Just a few more trips and they'll have it all!
column2: 一大群笨頭笨腦的火蟻正勤奮地想為即將到來的冬天囤積沙子。再跑個幾趟，牠們就能全部搬完了！

column1: The majesty of the painted desert stretches out into infinity, seemingly lasting forever yet going nowhere at all... just like life in Coarsegold!
column2: 這片彩色沙漠的壯闊景致無邊無際地延伸開來，看似永無止境，卻又哪裡都到不了……就像粗金鎮的生活一樣！

column1: There's nothing there to talk to except dust and dirt (none of which makes for stimulating conversation).
column2: 那裡除了塵土和泥沙，沒什麼好聊天的對象（而且這兩者都聊不出什麼精彩內容）。

column1: The desert and sky are much too far away for you to feel anything except a rapidly-approaching sunburn.
column2: 沙漠和天空離你太遠，你感覺不到什麼，除了即將上身的曬傷。

column1: There's nothing under the sand and rocks but more sand and rocks. Oh, perhaps a few scorpions, out trolling for adventurers.
column2: 沙子和石頭底下，除了更多沙子和石頭，什麼也沒有。喔，也許還有幾隻蠍子，正到處覓食、專找冒險者下手。

column1: You've cleverly used the ladder as a bridge between the rocks and the anthill, allowing Srini to escape without crushing any ants. (And you got some points, too!)
column2: 你機靈地把梯子架成石堆和蟻窩間的橋樑，讓斯里尼順利脫身，一隻螞蟻都沒壓死。（順便還讓你加了點分！）

column1: Some splendid saguaro cacti dot the countryside.
column2: 幾株漂亮的巨柱仙人掌點綴著這片鄉野。

column1: You're not thirsty for cactus juice right now!
column2: 你現在還不渴，不想喝仙人掌汁！

column1: Oh, no! You've taken too long! You'll NEVER turn those snails back now!
column2: 噢，不！你花了太多時間！你再也沒辦法讓那些蝸牛回頭了！

column1: So Freddy headed on back to the Pharmacy, followed by the eternally grateful Srini Lalkaka Bagdnish. Seems like Freddy'd not only found hisself a new assistance at the Pharmacy, but also a good friend as well!
column2: 於是佛萊迪動身回藥局，斯里尼·拉爾卡卡·巴格尼許則感激不盡地跟在後頭。看樣子佛萊迪不只在藥局找到了新幫手，還交到了一個好朋友！

column1: Looks like Hop Singh is headed out of town, along with his student, Kwai Chang Grasshopper.
column2: 看樣子阿星要離開鎮上了，還帶著他的徒弟——快樟蚱蜢。

column1: Hey, Hop!
column2: 嘿，阿星！

column1: Freddy! Hey, take care, man. I'm outta here.
column2: 佛萊迪！嘿，保重啦，老兄。我要走了。

column1: But... why?
column2: 可是……為什麼？

column1: Well, Mom's closed, and I hear the streets of San Francisco are paved with snails. So I'm going to take my unique blend of culinary expertise (specializing in traditional American frontier fare executed with a Near Eastern blend of herbs and spices) and quaint, rustic Chinese movie dialect, and open a restaurant with my old partner, Dhap Dhance!
column2: 唉，老媽餐館收攤了，我聽說舊金山的街上到處都是蝸牛。所以我打算帶著我獨門的廚藝（專精用中東香料調理傳統美式邊疆料理）和古樸道地的中國電影腔調，跟我的老搭檔踏普唐斯合開一間餐廳！

column1: Oh, no! Singh and Dhance, together again!
column2: 噢，不！阿星和唐斯，再度聯手！

column1: Well, take care, Hop. Good luck to you.
column2: 好吧，保重了，阿星。祝你好運。

column1: Same to you, Freddy!
column2: 你也是，佛萊迪！

column1: Please! Not in front of grasshopper!
column2: 拜託！別在蚱蜢面前這樣！

column1: No thanks, Freddy... I'm travelin' light!
column2: 不用了，謝謝，佛萊迪……我要輕裝上路！

column1: You'd never do something like that to your friend Hop Singh! (It would be a waste of ammo.)
column2: 你才不會對朋友阿星做這種事呢！（那樣太浪費子彈了。）

column1: The rusty tracks of the Fish Camp & Pacific Railroad used to continue across the trestle here, and wended their way to exciting, far-off places like Fresno. The train doesn't come here anymore, ever since the trestle collapsed and the train sunk into the swamp. No more lumber shipments. No more ice deliveries. No more personal hygiene products.
column2: 費許營太平洋鐵路生鏽的鐵軌，以前就是從這裡繼續穿過棧橋，一路蜿蜒通往弗雷斯諾之類令人嚮往的遠方。自從棧橋坍塌、火車陷進沼澤後，火車就再也沒來過這裡。木材運不來了。冰塊送不來了。個人衛生用品也沒有了。

column1: You never dreamed this rusty track would be slick enough for those snails to slide off into Blackwater Creek.
column2: 你作夢也沒想到，這條生鏽的鐵軌居然滑得能讓那些蝸牛一路滑進黑水溪裡。

column1: It's the Old Bridge. The only thing that keeps this Bridge out of the river's mouth is Poly-Grip!
column2: 這是老橋。唯一讓這座橋沒掉進河口裡的，就是那罐「保麗黏」！

column1: Whew! That was a close one! Considering the condition of this old bridge, you may only have about three crossings left.
column2: 呼！好險！看這座老橋的狀況，你大概只剩三次過橋的機會了。

column1: That's too stupid an idea to even justify a funny response.
column2: 這主意蠢到連個好笑的回應都不值得。

column1: Say... what have those horses and sheep been up to, anyway?
column2: 話說……那些馬跟羊到底在搞什麼名堂？

column1: Reverend Hallelujah's horses mosey around in his corral.
column2: 哈利路亞牧師的馬兒在圍欄裡悠哉閒晃。

column1: Reverend Hallelujah's replaced his horses with sheep. Perhaps it's their day in the sun.
column2: 哈利路亞牧師把他的馬換成了羊。也許今天輪到牠們曬太陽了。

column1: Reverend Sy Hallelujah's corral is empty.
column2: 賽伊·哈利路亞牧師的圍欄是空的。

column1: Don't open the corral! You'll let the... the... what are they, anyway? Shorses? Heeps? Anyway, you'll let them out.
column2: 別打開圍欄！你會放跑那些……那些……牠們到底算什麼？馬羊？羊馬？反正，你會把牠們放出去。

column1: Don't open the corral! You'll let the horses out.
column2: 別打開圍欄！你會放跑那些馬。

column1: Don't open the corral! You'll let the sheep out.
column2: 別打開圍欄！你會放跑那些羊。

column1: Don't open the corral! There's nothing inside to see.
column2: 別打開圍欄！裡面沒什麼好看的。

column1: You can't go digging in the Reverend's corral!
column2: 你不能在牧師的圍欄裡亂挖！

column1: You wonder why the waters of Blackwater Creek are so black. And gooey. And disgusting.
column2: 你很納悶，黑水溪的水怎麼會這麼黑、這麼黏、這麼噁心。

column1: Wouldn't it be nice to trail your hand lazily in the cool waters of Blackwater Creek? No, it wouldn't, because the currents would lazily rip your arm off.
column2: 悠哉地把手伸進黑水溪的清涼溪水裡，是不是很愜意？才不會，因為那股水流會悠哉地把你的手臂扯下來。

column1: The cliffs here drop off sharply, plummeting dramatically to the water below. A guy could get killed walking off there! You make a mental cliffs note to avoid doing so.
column2: 這裡的懸崖陡然而下，戲劇性地墜向下方的水面。一個人要是從那裡走下去，可是會沒命的！你在心裡記下一筆「懸崖筆記」，提醒自己千萬別這麼做。

column1: You can't reach the cliffs from here. Besides, your specialty is pharmacology, not geology.
column2: 你從這裡搆不到懸崖。再說，你的專長是藥學，不是地質學。

column1: What were you going to try to do, MOVE the cliff one shovelful at a time?
column2: 你到底打算怎麼做，一鏟一鏟把整座懸崖搬走嗎？

column1: The Robertson Cliffs overlook the thick, beautiful, shimmering waters of Blackwater Creek. The Old Bridge still offers shaky access to the desert to the west.
column2: 羅伯森懸崖俯瞰著黑水溪那濃稠、美麗又波光粼粼的溪水。老橋依然搖搖晃晃地通往西邊的沙漠。

column1: Who, or what, do you think you're talking to?
column2: 你以為自己在跟誰，或跟什麼東西講話？

column1: Yes, the scenery is so beautiful that you'd love to take it with you. But you can't. This is real life, not some weird computer game.
column2: 沒錯，這片景色美得讓你想把它帶走。但你辦不到。這是真實人生，不是什麼怪電腦遊戲。

column1: There's nothing there to be dug up!
column2: 那裡沒什麼好挖的！

column1: A gush of some sort of thick gooey sludge slops over the rapids below.
column2: 一股濃稠黏膩的爛泥，嘩啦嘩啦地沖過下方的急流。

column1: You can't reach it from here... fortunately for you! It looks disgusting!
column2: 你從這裡搆不到……算你走運！那東西看起來噁心極了！

column1: Ah, a child is playing by the side of the bridge. How delightful!
column2: 啊，有個孩子在橋邊玩耍。真是討人喜歡！

column1: 'Morning, son! I can remember playing right by this very bridge when I was your age!
column2: 早安啊，孩子！我記得我像你這麼大的時候，就是在這座橋邊玩的！

column1: What a liar you are. You were born in Old St. Louie!
column2: 你這人真會扯謊。你明明是在老聖路易出生的！

column1: Oh, yeah?
column2: 噢，是嗎？

column1: Yeah, I listened to the Prologue like everybody else. In fact, I can't get the darned thing out of my head. I've been hearing it in my sleep. Thanks, loads.
column2: 對啊，我跟大家一樣聽過序章。老實說，那玩意兒在我腦子裡揮之不去。我連睡覺都在聽。真是謝謝你囉。

column1: Even during these violent and lawless times, kidnapping is frowned upon.
column2: 即使是在這個暴力又無法無天的年代，綁架小孩還是會被人白眼的。

column1: This child's parents always said not to take strange objects from pharmacists.
column2: 這孩子的爸媽總是說，別隨便收下藥劑師給的怪東西。

column1: How nice! Clarice, one of the Reverend's sheep, is grazing in the grass where the horses once frolicked. (No doubt the Reverend, sooner or later, will have both sheep for dinner!)
column2: 真好！牧師的其中一隻羊克萊麗絲，正在馬兒曾經嬉戲的草地上吃草。（毫無疑問，牧師遲早會把這兩隻羊都拿來當晚餐！）

column1: One of Reverend Sy's horses is out frolicking in the spring sun. Well, maybe it's not FROLICKING exactly.
column2: 賽伊牧師的其中一匹馬正在春陽下嬉戲。呃，也許稱不上是「嬉戲」啦。

column1: It's a horse! No, it's a sheep! No need to fight, kids! It's BOTH! It's a "heep!" (Or maybe a shorse?)
column2: 是馬！不，是羊！孩子們，別吵了！兩個都是！這是隻「羊馬」！（或者該說是「馬羊」？）

column1: Here, sheep, sheep, sheep!
column2: 過來，羊羊羊！

column1: Clarice the Lamb remains silent. She seems to be smiling quietly to herself about something. How mysterious!
column2: 羔羊克萊麗絲一聲不吭。她似乎在為某件事暗自竊笑。真是神秘！

column1: Here, horsey, horsey, horsey!
column2: 過來，馬兒馬兒馬兒！

column1: There's no response. Maybe he's too horse to talk right now!
column2: 沒有反應。也許牠現在「馬」不出話來！

column1: Here, heep, heep, heep!
column2: 過來，羊馬羊馬羊馬！

column1: This creature ignores you, so you try again.
column2: 這隻生物不理你，於是你又試了一次。

column1: Here, shorsey, shorsey, shorsey!
column2: 過來，馬羊馬羊馬羊！

column1: This one is apparently way too concerned with racial separatism and the effects of cross-breeding in the barn to bother with you.
column2: 這隻顯然正忙著煩惱穀倉裡的種族隔離問題和雜交效應，沒空理你。

column1: You don't need a sheep to finish the game. (Though we wanted to put one in the box for each and every one of you!)
column2: 你不需要一隻羊也能破完這款遊戲。（雖然我們本來想在每個包裝盒裡都塞一隻真羊給大家！）

column1: The horse is humming "Don't Fence Me In" and doesn't care to be petted.
column2: 這匹馬正哼著〈別把我關起來〉，沒興趣讓你摸。

column1: You can't reach that heep from here! And you're not sure you want to!
column2: 你從這裡搆不到那隻羊馬！而且你也不太確定自己想不想搆到！

column1: The good Reverend has set Hannibal, one of his sheep, out to graze.
column2: 這位善心的牧師把他的其中一隻羊漢尼拔放出來吃草。

column1: This is one of Reverend Sy Hallelujah's horses. (Or so you've herd!)
column2: 這是賽伊·哈利路亞牧師的其中一匹馬。（起碼馬群裡是這麼傳的！）

column1: Hmmm, maybe the Reverend should separate the horses from the sheep in the stables from now on!
column2: 嗯，也許牧師從現在起該把馬廄裡的馬和羊分開來養！

column1: Hannibal the Lamb remains silent. He appears to be stealing glances back at the stable, where the horses are hanging out. What GIVES between these animals?
column2: 羔羊漢尼拔一聲不吭。他似乎不斷偷瞄馬廄那邊、馬兒閒晃的地方。這些動物之間到底是怎麼回事？

column1: Here, horsey! Here, horsey!
column2: 過來，馬兒！過來，馬兒！

column1: The horse seems to be saying, "Here, meaning what? Here, meaning if I come over there, I'll get a patronizing pat on the nose for my trouble? I smell no carrots on you! I smell no lumps of sugar! Forget you!"
column2: 這匹馬似乎在說：「過來？過來是什麼意思？過來的意思是說，我走過去只換來你敷衍地拍拍我的鼻子？我可沒聞到你身上有紅蘿蔔！也沒聞到方糖的味道！休想！」

column1: He... she... IT... doesn't even look your way, so you try another approach:
column2: 牠……她……牠……根本連看都不看你一眼，於是你換個方式再試一次：

column1: This one seems to be way too burdened with its own identity problems to bother conversing with you.
column2: 這隻似乎正忙著煩惱自己的身分認同問題，沒空跟你聊天。

column1: The sheep doesn't need any of your help to climb over the fence!
column2: 這隻羊爬過圍籬不需要你幫忙！

column1: The horse is too far back from the fence for you to touch.
column2: 這匹馬離圍籬太遠了，你摸不到。

column1: The shorse is way out of reach. Which is probably a good thing!
column2: 那隻馬羊根本搆不到。這樣或許還比較好！

column1: That block of iron is just a wee bit too heavy for you to cart around.
column2: 那塊鐵疙瘩對你來說重了那麼一點點，扛不動。

column1: It's an anvil, cast of iron and really very heavy.
column2: 這是一座鐵鑄的鐵砧，真的非常重。

column1: That street is staying right where it's been not paved.
column2: 那條街依然待在它一直沒鋪好的地方。

column1: Balance Street leads to the north side of town between the bank and the saloon.
column2: 貝倫斯街通往鎮北，就夾在銀行和酒館之間。

column1: The Bank's locked. That's odd! Where's P.H. Balance?
column2: 銀行鎖著。真奇怪！P·H·貝倫斯人跑哪去了？

column1: It's night. The Bank is locked. You can either wait 'til morning when it opens again, or wait 95 years 'til they install a 24-hour ATM.
column2: 現在是晚上，銀行鎖著。你可以等到早上開門，或者乾脆等個九十五年，等他們裝上二十四小時提款機。

column1: Here stands the only bank in town, The First Bank of Bob. The original owner must've had a hard time coming up with an original name for his establishment.
column2: 這裡矗立著鎮上唯一一間銀行——鮑伯第一銀行。當初的老闆一定是絞盡腦汁，才想出這麼有創意的店名。

column1: You daringly insert your finger into the bullet hole for no good reason.
column2: 你毫無理由地大膽把手指伸進彈孔裡。

column1: That bullet hole has been in the front window of the bank ever since that outlaw came through these parts way back in the demo.
column2: 打從那個亡命之徒在試玩版時代闖過這一帶開始，這個彈孔就一直留在銀行前面的窗戶上。

column1: This is Reverend Sy Hallelujah's corral.
column2: 這是賽伊·哈利路亞牧師的圍欄。

column1: As generous as he is, Reverend Hallelujah wouldn't appreciate your digging up his corral.
column2: 哈利路亞牧師人再怎麼大方，也不會樂見你把他的圍欄挖得亂七八糟。

column1: For one brief shining moment, there truly was a place called "Cattle Lot!"
column2: 曾經，就那麼短暫又閃耀的一刻，真的有個地方叫做「牛群空地」！

column1: You've already taken the really great charcoal hunks.
column2: 你已經拿走那些上等的大塊木炭了。

column1: Digging through Smithie's formerly white-hot forge, you find an unused hunk of charcoal which you decide may well be of use to you. So you keep it.
column2: 你翻找鐵匠史密那座曾經燒得炙白的爐子，找到一塊沒用過的木炭，覺得這東西說不定派得上用場。於是你留了下來。

column1: You better keep your hands outta that forge, Freddy... it's hotter than a Fresno roofer in August! (To use the local vernacular.)
column2: 佛萊迪，你最好別把手伸進那座爐子……那可比八月天在弗雷斯諾鋪屋頂的工人還燙！（借用一下當地的說法。）

column1: Smithie's once-proud forge is cold and dark.
column2: 鐵匠史密那座昔日引以為傲的爐子，如今又冷又暗。

column1: Smithie is proud to have the biggest forge in the Sierra!
column2: 鐵匠史密很自豪，他擁有整個內華達山區最大的爐子！

column1: Hay is for horses.
column2: 乾草是給馬吃的。

column1: Smithie keeps some hay baled up here, just for while the horses are in the shop.
column2: 鐵匠史密在這裡堆了些成捆的乾草，就是為了馬兒在店裡待著的時候用。

column1: You bravely, stupidly grab ANOTHER steaming, fly-laden horse plop. This is getting old!
column2: 你既勇敢又愚蠢地又抓起了一坨熱騰騰、爬滿蒼蠅的馬糞。這招都用老了！

column1: How convenient! There's another horse plop on the street. (Why don't people learn to curb their horses?)
column2: 真是方便！街上又有一坨馬糞。（怎麼都沒人學著管好自己的馬呢？）

column1: Never approach a horse from the rear! (For several reasons, at least one of which is utterly disgusting.)
column2: 千萬別從後面靠近馬！（理由很多，至少有一個噁心到爆。）

column1: Apparently, most of the lower half of the horse is in a chop shop somewhere in Los Angeles by now!
column2: 看樣子，這匹馬的下半身此刻大概已經在洛杉磯某間拆車廠裡了！

column1: Poor girl! Did some vandals come by and strip you down?
column2: 可憐的女孩！是哪個惡霸跑來把妳扒光的嗎？

column1: Stop being silly. No one can talk to a horse. (Of course.)
column2: 別傻了。沒有人能跟馬講話。（這是當然的。）

column1: With his refurbished shootin' skills, Freddy wuz able to blast the Lever Brothers to smithereens! Now, with those varmints outta the way, Freddy'd figured that wuz the end of the story... that somehow the Lever Brothers wuz responsible for ever'thang that'd bin goin' on in town.
column2: 憑著重新練回來的槍法，佛萊迪把利華兄弟轟得粉身碎骨！這下子，那些惡棍總算解決了，佛萊迪原本以為故事就這麼結束了……以為鎮上發生的這一切，都是利華兄弟搞的鬼。

column1: But Freddy wuz WRONG! The Lever Brothers had been hired fer the task of gittin' rid of Freddy, by whomever'd hired the cowhands... and whomever wuz in cahoots with Sheriff Shift and P.H. Balance! And no sooner had Freddy's guns stopped smokin', than he heard a familiar twang and a few chords o' someone's theme music.
column2: 但佛萊迪錯了！利華兄弟其實是被人雇來除掉佛萊迪的，雇用那些牛仔的人……正是跟席夫特警長和P·H·貝倫斯勾結的幕後黑手！佛萊迪的槍口硝煙才剛散去，就聽見一聲熟悉的琴弦聲，還有幾個屬於某人主題曲的和弦。

column1: What was that? Could it be? Nah. What would he be doing way out here, in the middle of nowhere? You haven't heard that chord in years, and yet, here it is again, strangely recognizable after all this time.... In your heart, you know it must be him. And, yet...
column2: 那是什麼聲音？難道是……不會吧。他跑來這鳥不生蛋的地方幹嘛？你已經好幾年沒聽過那個和弦了，可它卻又出現了，過了這麼久，聽起來還是莫名地熟悉……你心裡明白，那一定是他。然而……

column1: How did he find you? Will he be fooled by your disguise? Does he still eat paste?
column2: 他是怎麼找到你的？他會被你的偽裝騙過去嗎？他還在吃漿糊嗎？

column1: Dummy Msg.
column2: 測試訊息。

column1: What's that rotten smell? Oh, no! It can't be! You recognize that smell from your old days as a lawman... More dangerous than Jesse James... Meaner than Johnny Ringo... Deadlier than William Muny... (More fun at cocktail parties than Rooster Cogburn!) ...it's the legendary Lever Brothers!
column2: 那股腐臭味是什麼？噢，不！不會吧！你認得這股味道，那是你當年還是執法者時就熟悉的氣味……比傑西·詹姆斯還危險……比強尼·林戈還兇殘……比威廉·莫尼還致命……（在雞尾酒派對上還比魯斯特·科本更會炒熱氣氛！）……那就是傳說中的利華兄弟！

column1: Dummy msg.
column2: 測試訊息。

column1: Yep, it's us, handsome silver-eared stranger!
column2: 沒錯，是我們，你這位耳朵鑲銀的帥氣陌生人！

column1: And we're here to put you six feet under!
column2: 我們是來送你入土為安的！

column1: Under what?
column2: 在什麼底下？

column1: Your fervent prayer is that your few minutes of target practice with Srini will be sufficient preparation for odds like this....
column2: 你在心裡拚命祈禱，跟斯里尼練的那幾分鐘打靶，足夠讓你應付眼前這種局面……

column1: You tug on the rail, but it seems firmly planted.
column2: 你拉了拉欄杆，但它看起來牢牢固定著。

column1: This is a good place to get hitched!
column2: 這裡正是拴馬——呃，喜結良緣的好地方！

column1: The corner of Balance and Main isn't going anywhere. (At least, not until the next big earthquake hits California!)
column2: 平衡街和大街的路口哪兒也不會去。（至少要等加州下次大地震才會動！）

column1: You're here at the busy corner of Balance Street, which runs north-south, and Main Street. Well, it's USUALLY busy. Well, it was busy once.
column2: 你現在站在平衡街（南北向）與大街交會的熱鬧路口。呃，通常很熱鬧啦。好吧，曾經熱鬧過。

column1: Your shovel would break. And you'd get splinters in your hands and dirt in your eyes.
column2: 你的鏟子會斷掉，手上會扎滿木刺，眼睛裡還會進沙。

column1: Funny, there's no answer from that.
column2: 奇怪，那東西沒有回應。

column1: You take the rope. Now that Smithie's closed up shop, he won't be missing it.
column2: 你拿走了繩子。反正鐵匠史密已經關店走人，不會少這條繩子的。

column1: Smithie left behind a coil of rope.
column2: 鐵匠史密留下了一捆繩子。

column1: You can't reach him from here!
column2: 你這個角度碰不到他！

column1: Matt Shaker is shaking his doormat out the window again. It's best not to walk underneath.
column2: 麥特·薛克又在窗邊甩門墊了，最好別站在下面。

column1: Hey, Matt! Quit that! You're getting dust all over everything!
column2: 喂，麥特！別甩了！灰塵沾得到處都是！

column1: Funny, Matt pays no attention to you.
column2: 奇怪，麥特根本沒理你。

column1: You don't have a horse, whatta you need a saddle for?
column2: 你又沒有馬，要馬鞍幹嘛？

column1: If this old worn-out saddle could only talk... it would probably complain about the prevalence of beans in the standard cowhand diet.
column2: 這副破舊的馬鞍要是會講話，大概會抱怨牛仔的伙食裡豆子放太多了。

column1: From the condition of Coarsegold's sidewalks, it's easy to surmise the town lawyer left for greener pastures years ago!
column2: 看粗金鎮這人行道的慘狀，不難猜到鎮上的律師早幾年就跑去別處發財了！

column1: You know it does no good to close the barn door once the Smithie's gone away!
column2: 鐵匠都走了，現在關門也於事無補！

column1: Let Smithie decide if he wants his doors open or closed.
column2: 門要開要關，讓鐵匠史密自己決定吧。

column1: Smithie has truly left town for good.
column2: 鐵匠史密是真的離開這個鎮了，不會再回來。

column1: It's the door to Smithie's Blacksmith shop.
column2: 這是鐵匠史密打鐵舖的門。

column1: I don't use none o' that moustache wax, Pharkas! I let muh soup keep muh moustache plastered in place!
column2: 俺才不用那種鬍子蠟，法卡斯！俺靠喝湯把鬍子黏得服服貼貼的！

column1: Dab-nab it, Pharkas! Real men jes' don' go 'round a'touchin' other real men! 'Specially when they're as homophobic as we is!
column2: 該死，法卡斯！純爺們才不會到處亂摸別的爺們！尤其咱倆這麼恐同的傢伙！

column1: Har! Muh hide's tough as leather, Pharkas. That thang'd just break off at the handle.
column2: 哈！俺這張皮跟牛皮一樣硬，法卡斯。那玩意兒只會斷在握把上。

column1: Smithie, the village blacksmith, is a real hulk of humanity.
column2: 鐵匠史密是鎮上的打鐵匠，塊頭大得像座山。

column1: Whut the Sam Hill y'expeck me to do with that medicine, Pharkas? I'm a strong, beefy kinda guy, I don't need no wuss medication!
column2: 你到底要俺拿那藥怎麼辦，法卡斯？俺可是個又壯又猛的漢子，才不需要那種軟腳藥！

column1: I don' know nuttin' 'bout writin', Pharkas. That's more in your depar'ment.
column2: 俺對寫字這檔事一竅不通，法卡斯。那是你的專長。

column1: You know, Smithie, I've been wondering about that horse of yours. What happened?
column2: 話說，史密，俺一直很好奇你那匹馬怎麼了？

column1: Consarn neighborhood kids! Ya jes' can't leave anything outside at night any more without 'em strippin' it right down to the axles!
column2: 該死的鄰居小鬼！東西晚上放在外面，現在都會被扒得只剩車軸！

column1: How's business, Smithie?
column2: 生意怎麼樣啊，史密？

column1: Flatter'n cow plop, Pharkas! An' you?
column2: 比牛糞還扁，法卡斯！那你呢？

column1: Actually, I'm doing okay. Not great, but I'm making it... in spite of this mild economic downturn we've been experiencing.
column2: 其實俺過得還行。不算好，但撐得下去……就算最近景氣有點差。

column1: Bah! If'n I could find me a buyer, I'd unload this dump in a second!
column2: 哼！要是找得到買主，俺立刻把這破地方脫手！

column1: Whoa! Thank ya, Mr. Pharkas. I always love a belt about this time o' the mornin'!
column2: 哇！謝了，法卡斯先生。俺這時間就愛來一口！

column1: You recall with fondness, that wonderful old blacksmith who used to operate this shop. What the hell was his name, anyway?
column2: 你懷念地想起以前在這開店的那位老鐵匠。他到底叫什麼名字來著？

column1: Under the village chestnut tree, the spreading smithie stands... ...No wait, that's not how it goes.
column2: 「村中栗樹下，枝繁葉茂的鐵匠站著……」……不對，不是這樣唱的。

column1: Mr. Smith, the village blacksmith, is locally known as "Smithie" to his friends and customers.
column2: 史密斯先生，鎮上的鐵匠，朋友和顧客都叫他「史密」。

column1: To the best of your recollection, you've never even heard his first name, not that it matters much. "Smithie" seems like a perfect name for a smithie!
column2: 就你印象所及，你從沒聽過他的名字，不過也無所謂。「史密」這名字給鐵匠正合適！

column1: Hey, knock off the sound effects already!
column2: 喂，音效可以停了吧！

column1: You take the leather strap. Smithie won't be needing it now, wherever he is!
column2: 你拿走了皮帶。鐵匠史密不管人在哪，反正都用不著了！

column1: A length of leather bridle hangs on the Smithie's door.
column2: 一條皮製馬轡掛在鐵匠舖的門上。

column1: Feels just like the streets of St. Louis... only some of the streets of St. Louis are paved!
column2: 感覺就像聖路易的街道……只不過聖路易好歹有幾條街鋪了路！

column1: Once Coarsegold's brave pioneer settlers predicted Main Street would rival the Champs d'Elysee, Van Ness Boulevard, or Broadway. Now it rivals the Oregon Trail and is about as smooth!
column2: 粗金鎮當年勇敢的拓荒者曾預言，大街將媲美香榭麗舍大道、凡尼斯大道，甚至百老匯。如今它倒是媲美奧勒岡小徑，路面一樣顛簸！

column1: There's nobody buried under the street here. (After all, this is when the word Teamsters began with a lowercase T!)
column2: 這條街底下沒埋人。（畢竟那年頭，趕車工會還只是個老實行業，可沒黑道傳聞！）

column1: You don't need any algae.
column2: 你不需要什麼藻類。

column1: Horses always appreciate a drink of nice fresh water from these green slimy troughs.
column2: 馬兒總喜歡從這些綠油油、黏答答的水槽裡喝口新鮮水。

column1: It's just an old wreck. It won't help you.
column2: 這只是個破爛殘骸，幫不上你的忙。

column1: This wagon has been lying here in this sad state of disrepair ever since Mr. Leech, the carriage-maker, headed back East to Detroit.
column2: 自從馬車工匠利奇先生回東岸底特律後，這輛馬車就一直癱在這兒，破爛成這副慘樣。

column1: Oooph!
column2: 唔喔！

column1: You've always assumed the Golden Balls Saloon must once have been a pawn shop.
column2: 你一直以為金球酒館以前八成是間當舖。

column1: You leave that Saloon right where it is, buckaroo.
column2: 那間酒館你就讓它待在原地吧，牛仔老兄。

column1: Mom's Cafe must have good food-- it's where all the stagecoaches stop!
column2: 老媽餐館的菜一定不錯——所有驛馬車都在這兒停靠！

column1: You can't reach it from here, but you can just see that thin layer of cooking grease glistening off the building.
column2: 你這裡搆不著，但可以看到那層薄薄的油光在建築物上閃閃發亮。

column1: Peering through Mom's greasy glass, you can see she's open for business. You've always been fond of Mom's cooking... at least, the first time it goes down!
column2: 透過老媽那油膩膩的玻璃窗望進去，看得出她還在營業。你一直很喜歡老媽的手藝……至少第一口吞下去的時候是這樣！

column1: You feel a twinge of guilt, knowing you were at least partially responsible for Mom's closing. You vow to make it up to her, somehow.
column2: 你隱隱感到愧疚，畢竟老媽餐館歇業多少跟你脫不了關係。你發誓總有一天要補償她。

column1: If Mom catches you smearing her windows, she'll smear your face.
column2: 要是被老媽逮到你亂抹她的窗戶，她會把你的臉也抹一頓。

column1: Rain barrels are such an important aspect of life in an arid, drought-scourged landscape like this. Water running off the buildings' roofs is channeled through gutters and downspouts into storage... Oh, wait a minute. This is just an old whisky barrel. Forget it!
column2: 在這種乾旱缺水的地方，集雨桶可是生活中不可或缺的一環。屋頂的雨水經由排水溝和落水管收集儲存……喔，等等。這只是個舊威士忌桶。當我沒說！

column1: No, no, no! |c2|Tuesday|c| is your turn in the barrel!
column2: 不、不、不！|c2|星期二|c|才輪到你進桶子！

column1: You do your "Peeping Freddy" routine with the Hotel window. Furtive shadows steal across the walls inside. What little light seeps into the Hotel plays teasingly at vague forms and shapes. (How nauseatingly poetic!)
column2: 你對著旅館窗戶來一段「偷窺佛萊迪」戲碼。鬼鬼祟祟的影子在牆上晃過，透進屋內的微光曖昧地勾勒出模糊的形體。（噁心到有詩意了！）

column1: You address the hotel window:
column2: 你對旅館窗戶說道：

column1: You've made yourself perfectly clear! Hee hee hee!
column2: 你表達得再清楚不過了！嘿嘿嘿！

column1: (You're losing it, Freddy.)
column2: （你快瘋了，佛萊迪。）

column1: Rubbing your finger on the hotel window barely removes any dirt. (Apparently there was more dirt going on INside than OUTside!)
column2: 你用手指抹了抹旅館窗戶，幾乎抹不掉什麼髒污。（看來裡頭發生的骯髒事，比外面的灰塵還多！）

column1: You really can't reach that window from here. But hey, a Pharmacist's reach should exceed his grasp!
column2: 你這裡真的搆不到那扇窗戶。不過話說回來，藥師的野心本該超越自己的臂長！

column1: It's locked, stock and barrel!
column2: 鎖得死死的，一點縫都沒有！

column1: Your arms aren't quite that long!
column2: 你的手臂沒那麼長！

column1: Mom's Cafe awaits the hearty traveler who has a thing for good food-- but isn't afraid to eat here anyway!
column2: 老媽餐館正等著那些愛吃美食——卻又不怕死照樣進來吃的硬漢旅人！

column1: A crudely-lettered sign reads, "Mom's's Cafe's dun bin closed by order of the sheriff. Health Code violations is all the reason he needs!"
column2: 一塊字跡潦草的告示寫著：「老媽餐館已依警長命令歇業。違反衛生法規，理由夠充分！」

column1: Mom's closes up at night, ever since the Great Kerosene Shortage of '85.
column2: 自從八五年那場煤油大缺貨後，老媽餐館晚上就不營業了。

column1: Heeeelllloooooow!
But there is no response from within Mom's Cafe.
column2: 但老媽餐館裡沒有任何回應。

column1: Mom! I'm hungry!
column2: 老媽！我餓了！

column1: From inside, you hear Mom reply, "You'll get indigestion! It's not good to eat so close to bedtime! Come back tomorrow!"
column2: 你聽見老媽從裡面回話：「你會消化不良的！這麼晚吃東西不好！明天再來吧！」

column1: It's locked! Mom's is closed! Sheriff Shift strikes again! (And stomachs all over town are heaving... sighs of relief!)
column2: 鎖住了！老媽餐館關門了！席夫特警長又出手了！（全鎮的胃都在翻騰……鬆一口氣的那種翻騰！）

column1: Mom's seems to be locked.
column2: 老媽餐館似乎鎖住了。

column1: Going to swing down like Tarzan? Wrong kinda movie!
column2: 想學泰山盪下去？你認錯片場了！

column1: The Golden Balls Saloon is presently open. Since it only has swinging doors, it's ALWAYS open!
column2: 金球酒館目前是開著的。反正它只有一扇彈簧門，永遠都是開著的！

column1: The remains of the Sugar Pine & Coarsegold's Engineer's Shack lie rotting on the south side of Main Street.
column2: 「糖松與粗金鎮鐵路」工程師小屋的殘骸，在大街南側逐漸腐朽。

column1: Don't go poking in that hazardous eyesore. (The same warning applies to the Brothel!)
column2: 別去戳那個危險的眼中釘。（這句警告對妓院也一樣適用！）

column1: These hitching posts serve as an excellent means of stabilizing unmanned horses.
column2: 這些拴馬柱可是固定無人看管馬匹的絕佳工具。

column1: You deliver a swift karate chop to the post. Excellent! One or two more and you'll have it completely broken. (Your hand, not the post.)
column2: 你朝柱子俐落地劈了一記手刀。太好了！再來一兩下就會徹底斷掉。（斷的是你的手，不是柱子。）

column1: Peering between every crack in the hotel's board sidewalk makes you 'board' yourself!
column2: 盯著旅館木板人行道的每道縫隙看，看得你都要「木」然了！

column1: You rip the porch off of the hotel and put it in your pocket, just in case you need a porch later in the game. Kidding. Just a little adventure game humor there. Don't bother looking in your inventory.
column2: 你把旅館的門廊拆下來塞進口袋，以防遊戲後面用得到門廊。開玩笑的啦，不過是冒險遊戲的老哏。別費心去道具欄找了。

column1: You can't reach the porch from here.
column2: 你這裡搆不到門廊。

column1: Ah, many's the young cowpoke who had to quickly lower himself off of this balcony with a bunch of knotted sheets. (Usually stark nekkid!)
column2: 啊，不少年輕牛仔曾靠著打結的床單，匆忙從這陽台溜下去。（而且通常是一絲不掛！）

column1: Considering all the abuse given to this balcony over the years from stuntmen, it's in surprisingly good shape.
column2: 想想這些年特技演員對這陽台的各種摧殘，它的狀況出乎意料地好。

column1: Mom's front porch is almost as large as her rear entry.
column2: 老媽餐館的前門廊，幾乎跟她的後門一樣大。

column1: Poor Mom. You almost wish you hadn't dumped that horse patty inside her eating area. But-- you vow to make it up to her somehow!
column2: 可憐的老媽。你幾乎後悔把那坨馬糞丟進她的用餐區。不過——你發誓總有一天會補償她！

column1: Many an early-morning customer of yours has spent the night sleeping on these well-stained boards.
column2: 你不少一大早上門的顧客，前一晚都是睡在這片滿是污漬的木板上。

column1: They hang porch-rustlers in these parts.
column2: 這一帶，偷門廊的人是要被吊死的。

column1: The door to the Hotel is locked. The hotel was shut down unexpectedly. This put a total of two desk clerks and five working girls out of jobs. (Fortunately, there weren't any maids, or they'd have been fired, too!)
column2: 旅館的門鎖著。這間旅館無預警歇業，害兩名櫃檯人員和五位「服務小姐」都丟了飯碗。（幸好沒請女傭，不然也一起被炒魷魚！）

column1: Anybody in there?
column2: 有人在裡面嗎？

column1: There's no response.
column2: 沒有回應。

column1: Okay, I'll take that as a "no!"
column2: 好吧，俺就當作是「沒有」了！

column1: You yank the knob a few times, but nothing happens. Then you try to open the door to the closed Hotel. No luck there, either.
column2: 你扭了幾次門把，什麼事也沒發生。接著你試著推開這間停業旅館的門，一樣沒用。

column1: That would be quite a trick... opening the Hotel door from the balcony. You're not quite up to it. (Or down to it, as the case may be!)
column2: 從陽台開旅館大門，那可是個大絕活……你可沒那本事。（或者該說，沒那個「高」度！）

column1: Once the heart of a thriving business district, there's not much left of beautiful downtown Coarsegold now.
column2: 這裡曾是繁華商圈的心臟地帶，如今粗金鎮的美麗市中心，也沒剩下什麼了。

column1: Und chust how long haf you had zees desire to talk mit inanimate objects?
column2: 那麼，你這種想跟死物講話的癖好，到底有多久了，嗯？

column1: It feels like part of the ambience that makes Coarsegold so priceless! (Or should that be "worthless"?)
column2: 這正是粗金鎮那種「無價」氛圍的一部分！（還是該說「一文不值」？）

column1: The ground is too hard-packed here.
column2: 這裡的地面太硬，踩得死死的。

column1: Sam Andreas has a tough time keeping these large plate glass windows intact, since he's developed a habit of throwing rowdies out through them!
column2: 山姆·安德列斯很難讓這些大片玻璃窗保持完整，畢竟他養成了把鬧事的傢伙直接扔出窗外的習慣！

column1: Careful, you never know when some airborne wino is going to come flying outta that window.
column2: 小心點，你永遠不知道什麼時候會有個醉漢從那扇窗飛出來。

column1: Now there's a guy who's in constant pane!
column2: 這下這傢伙，真是痛（窗）苦不堪啊！

column1: Poor fellow. It doesn't pay to pick a fight with Sam Andreas!
column2: 可憐的傢伙。跟山姆·安德列斯打架真的不划算！

column1: There's no use talking to him. He's out cold.
column2: 跟他講話沒用，他已經昏過去了。

column1: You'd like to help him. But he IS full of shards of glass, and you HATE the sight of blood!
column2: 你是想幫他啦。但他身上插滿玻璃碎片，而你最怕看到血了！

column1: He doesn't need anything except a lifetime supply of Mercurochrome!
column2: 他什麼都不需要，只需要一輩子份量的紅藥水！

column1: The window has been smashed into teeny weeny pieces. Fortunately, Sam has the foresight to install Safety Glass!
column2: 這扇窗被砸成細碎小片。幸好山姆有先見之明，裝的是安全玻璃！

column1: Cutting yourself on the sharp edges of the broken window might make for some memorably disgusting animation, but it would also be an incredibly stupid thing for you to do.
column2: 被碎玻璃的尖銳邊緣割傷，或許能做出一段令人印象深刻的噁心動畫，但這麼做真的蠢到家了。

column1: Poor Sam Andreas! It's a good thing he waters down his whisky so much, or else all of his profits would be consumed by glaziers.
column2: 可憐的山姆·安德列斯！還好他的威士忌摻水摻得夠兇，不然賺的錢全都要拿去付玻璃工的錢了。

column1: You are surprised to see Billy, the town handyman, boarding up The Dirty Sheet Hotel.
column2: 你驚訝地看到鎮上的雜工比利，正在把「髒床單旅館」的門窗釘上木板。

column1: Don't you find it frustrating to keep replacing that plate glass, Billy?
column2: 比利，老是要換那片玻璃，你不覺得很煩嗎？

column1: Nope. I find it a real crack-up.
column2: 不會啊，俺覺得挺「破」有意思的。

column1: Billy, the town handyman and jack-of-all-trades, is boarding up yet another Coarsegold business, the "Dirty Sheets Hotel," the finest hostelry in all of Eastern Madera County. (Okay, so maybe it was only the best after that other hotel shut down, but in its day, The Dirty Sheet was really something!)
column2: 比利，鎮上的萬能雜工，又在把粗金鎮另一家店面釘上木板——「髒床單旅館」，馬德拉郡東部最高檔的旅店。（好吧，其實是等另一家旅館關門後才變最高檔的，不過「髒床單」當年可真是了不起！）

column1: Say, Billy! When did the ol' Dirty Sheet fold?
column2: 欸，比利！那間老「髒床單」是什麼時候倒的？

column1: Oh, g'mornin' Mr. Pharkas. Why, just yestaday. It was a surprise to me too. Nobody told me nuttin' 'bout it until they gave me these boards.
column2: 喔，早安啊，法卡斯先生。就昨天的事。俺也是嚇了一跳，誰都沒跟俺說，直到他們把這些木板塞給俺。

column1: I'd like to shake your hand, Billy. You are doing a fine job!
column2: 俺想跟你握個手，比利。你做得很好！

column1: He looks at you a little funny.
column2: 他用有點奇怪的眼神看著你。

column1: Here, Billy!
column2: 拿去，比利！

column1: No thanks, Mr. Pharkas! I've already got one of those!
column2: 不用了，謝了，法卡斯先生！俺已經有一個了！

column1: Shhhyeah, right.
column2: 是喔，隨便你說。

column1: How nice! A pile of horse plop is baking in the sun, right in the middle of the road. (You make a mental note: hurry up and get around to inventing the Poop Scoop.)
column2: 真棒！一坨馬糞正在路中央曬太陽。（你在心裡記一筆：得趕快發明「便便鏟」了。）

column1: You bravely, stupidly grab ANOTHER steaming, fly-laden horse plop. This one is even more texturey than the last one!
column2: 你英勇又愚蠢地抓起另一坨熱騰騰、蒼蠅環繞的馬糞。這坨的「口感」比上一坨還豐富！

column1: Apparently Mom's jumping on the comedy club bandwagon. The sign reads, "Coming soon -- Open Megaphone Night. Take your best shot! You'll die laughing!"
column2: 看來老媽也想搭喜劇酒吧的順風車。招牌寫著：「即將開張——開放麥克風之夜。使出你的看家本領！保證笑到你斷氣！」

column1: It's too dark to make out what's written on that bunting.
column2: 天色太暗，看不清那面彩布上寫了什麼。

column1: The fabric has been pre-treated to resist those pesky dust storms, stampedes, flash floods, tsunamis, monsoons, and droughts.
column2: 這塊布料經過特殊處理，能抵擋惱人的沙塵暴、牛群暴衝、山洪、海嘯、季風和乾旱。

column1: Not from down here, you can't!
column2: 你在這下面可辦不到！

column1: You've got no reason to put the canister on the railing. (At least, not YET.)
column2: 你沒理由把罐子放在欄杆上。（至少現在還沒有。）

column1: |c0|FORESHADOWING ALERT! FORESHADOWING ALERT!|c|
column2: |c0|伏筆警報！伏筆警報！|c|

column1: It's the canister of nitrous oxide. You put it there yourself. Remember?
column2: 這是氧化亞氮罐，你自己放在那裡的，記得嗎？

column1: You decide that the canister of nitrous oxide would look better somewheres else.
column2: 你覺得那罐氧化亞氮擺在別的地方會更好看。

column1: Just fly there. (NOT!!)
column2: 飛過去就好啦。（才怪！！）

column1: Freddy Pharkas? You wuz askin' about Freddy Pharkas? The man whut saved Coarsegold, only nobody knowed it wuz him? Why, jes' hop up here on ol' Whittlin' Willy's lap and I'll tell ya all about it.
column2: 佛萊迪·法卡斯？你在打聽佛萊迪·法卡斯？那個救了粗金鎮、卻沒人知道是他救的傢伙？來，坐到老削木威利的腿上來，俺跟你從頭說起。

column1: Apparently Mom's jumping on the comedy bandwagon. The banner reads, "Coming soon -- Open Megaphone Night. Take your best shot! You'll die laughing!"
column2: 看樣子老媽也想搭上喜劇的風潮。布條上寫著：「即將登場——開放麥克風之夜。使出全力！保證笑死你！」

column1: You've got no reason to put the canister on the railing. At least, not YET.
column2: 你沒理由把罐子放在欄杆上。至少現在還沒有。

column1: Mom's Cafe must have good food -- all the stagecoaches stop there!
column2: 老媽餐館的菜一定不錯——所有驛馬車都在那停靠！

column1: You decide that the canister of nitrous oxide would look better somewhere else.
column2: 你覺得那罐氧化亞氮擺在別的地方會更好看。

column1: Please, stranger. I'm simply not in the mood. Why don't you go bother Trixie, the Accommodating Sheep?
column2: 拜託，陌生人。俺現在沒那個心情。你何不去煩「隨和的羊」翠西呢？

column1: Here, Chester. Maybe it'll help you through these tough times.
column2: 拿去，切斯特。或許能幫你撐過這段苦日子。

column1: No thank you, sir. I still have my dignity. That's the one thing they can't take away from me.
column2: 不用了，謝謝你，先生。俺還有尊嚴，那是他們唯一奪不走的東西。

column1: You've never seen Chester Field look so downtrodden. Why, he looks like he's lost his best friend. He's wearing a sandwich board, upon which has been VERY hastily scribbled, "Will polish ears for stagecoach fare."
column2: 你從沒見過切斯特·菲爾德這麼落魄的樣子。他看起來就像失去了最好的朋友。他身上掛著一塊三明治廣告牌，上頭潦草地寫著：「代客擦耳朵，換一張驛馬車票。」

column1: Polish your ear, Mister? I'm trying to get stagecoach fare to Chicago.
column2: 幫你擦擦耳朵吧，先生？俺想湊點錢買去芝加哥的驛馬車票。

column1: No thanks, Chester. I'm broke. But hey, doesn't the trip to Chicago by stagecoach take just about forever?
column2: 不用了，切斯特，俺身上沒錢。不過話說回來，坐驛馬車去芝加哥不是要花上一輩子嗎？

column1: Well, yes, but I've always wanted a life on the stage!
column2: 呃，是沒錯，不過俺一直很想過「舞台」上的生活嘛！

column1: (ba-dump bump!)
column2: （登楞！）

column1: Hoping Chester won't recognize you with your new disguise, you approach him with a friendly smile.
column2: 你希望切斯特認不出偽裝後的你，於是帶著友善的笑容走向他。

column1: Say, pardner, that's a woeful little sign you're carrying there, "Will polish ears for stagecoach fare." What's the problem? Why so down on your luck?
column2: 老兄，你掛的這塊牌子挺可憐的啊，「代客擦耳朵，換一張驛馬車票」。怎麼回事？為什麼這麼倒楣？

column1: Well, I'll tell you, even though I usually don't talk to silver-disguised strangers. There's a man inside who's the best gol-damned poker cheat I've ever seen. I never even knew he's was stealing my store until it wuz all over. You see, I bet everything I owned, including my store, on a queen-high straight flush! And that son of a gun had a king-high!
column2: 好吧，俺就告訴你，雖然俺一般不跟穿一身銀的陌生人講話。裡面有個傢伙，是俺見過最會出老千的撲克牌高手。俺一直到全輸光了才發現他在坑俺。俺把身家全押上去，連店都賭了，手上是Q高順子！結果那狗娘養的是K高！

column1: Don't feel bad, fella, I would have probably done the same. By the way, did you get this gambler's name?
column2: 別難過，老兄，換作是俺大概也會這樣。對了，你有問到那個賭徒的名字嗎？

column1: Name? Shore did. Wheaton Hall is his name, but everybody calls him 'Aces.' And I kin see why!
column2: 名字？當然問了。他叫惠頓·霍爾，不過大家都叫他「王牌」，俺完全懂為什麼！

column1: Thanks for your time, and I hope things work out for you! I think I might just pay Mr. Aces a little call!
column2: 謝謝你撥空，也希望你順利！俺想俺該去拜訪一下這位「王牌」先生了！

column1: Good luck to you stranger, if'n yur a'gonna git inta that game!
column2: 祝你好運了，陌生人，要是你真打算進去玩那一局的話！

column1: Thanks. I'm wearing my lucky neckerchief, so I'm not too worried.
column2: 謝了。俺戴著幸運圍巾呢，不太擔心。

column1: Shhyeah, right. Are those bloodstains on there?
column2: 是喔，隨便你說。那上頭是血漬嗎？

column1: The door to the Hotel is locked. The ol' Dirty Sheet was shut down unexpectedly putting a total of two desk clerks and five working girls out of jobs. (Fortunately, there weren't any maids, or they'd have been fired, too!)
column2: 旅館的門鎖著。老「髒床單」無預警歇業，害兩名櫃檯人員和五位「服務小姐」都丟了飯碗。（幸好沒請女傭，不然也一起被炒魷魚！）

column1: Peering between every crack in the hotel's board sidewalk makes you "board" yourself!
column2: 盯著旅館木板人行道的每道縫隙看，看得你都要「木」然了！

column1: You really can't reach that window from here. But hey, a pharmacist's reach should exceed his grasp!
column2: 你這裡真的搆不到那扇窗戶。不過話說回來，藥師的野心本該超越自己的臂長！

column1: You do your "Peeping Freddy" routine with the hotel window. Furtive shadows steal across the walls inside. What little light seeps into the hotel plays teasingly at vague forms and shapes. (How nauseatingly poetic!)
column2: 你對著旅館窗戶來一段「偷窺佛萊迪」戲碼。鬼鬼祟祟的影子在牆上晃過，透進屋內的微光曖昧地勾勒出模糊的形體。（噁心到有詩意了！）

column1: It's locked! Mom's is closed! Sheriff Shift strikes again! Stomachs all over town are heaving... but this time it's sighs of relief!
column2: 鎖住了！老媽餐館關門了！席夫特警長又出手了！全鎮的胃都在翻騰……不過這次是鬆一口氣的翻騰！

column1: (OFF MIKE) You'll get indigestion! It's not good to eat so close to bedtime! Come back tomorrow!
column2: （畫外音）你會消化不良的！這麼晚吃東西不好！明天再來吧！

column1: You deliver a swift karate chop to the post. Excellent! One or two more and you'll have it completely broken. (Your hand, that is!)
column2: 你朝柱子俐落地劈了一記手刀。太好了！再來一兩下就會徹底斷掉。（斷的是你的手！）

column1: It feels like part of the ambience that makes Coarsegold so priceless! (Or should that be "worthless?")
column2: 這正是粗金鎮那種「無價」氛圍的一部分！（還是該說「一文不值」？）

column1: What are you gonna do, hang off the balcony and steal their hats? Dream on!
column2: 你想幹嘛，吊在陽台上偷他們的帽子？想得美！

column1: A whole fleet of rowdy cowhands seems to have invaded Main Street. They're shooting around indiscriminately (the barbarians!). Did they do this just for the fun of it? Or did somebody put them up to it?
column2: 一整批粗魯的牛仔似乎入侵了大街。他們亂開槍掃射（真是野蠻！）。他們是純粹找樂子，還是有人在背後唆使？

column1: That's the germ of an idea. Unfortunately, you need some way to make SURE that gas gets set off!
column2: 這算是個點子的雛形。可惜你還需要想個辦法，確保那些氣體一定會被引爆！

column1: |c0|Hey, you guys! CUT IT OUT!|c|
column2: |c0|喂，你們這些傢伙！住手啦！|c|

column1: They can't even hear you above the sound of their own obnoxious yelling and the frequent gunshots. Looks like you'll have to be just a |c2|bit|c| more forceful.
column2: 他們自己吵吵嚷嚷加上槍聲不斷，根本聽不見你在喊什麼。看來你得再強硬|c2|一點|c|才行。

column1: You encounter dozens of rowdy cowhands from that cattle drive outside of town who are carelessly firing their guns everywhere and frightening (not to mention killing) the locals.
column2: 你遇上一群從鎮外趕牛隊來的粗魯牛仔，足足有好幾十個，正到處亂開槍，嚇壞（更別說殺傷）當地居民。

column1: Luckily, the rowdy cowboys don't notice you from down below.
column2: 幸好，樓下那群粗魯的牛仔沒注意到你。

column1: The Barber Shop is locked up tight at night.
column2: 理髮店晚上鎖得緊緊的。

column1: This door leads to Salvatore O'Hanahan's combination barber shop and dental emporium. Just don't ask him about his heritage. He's VERY confused.
column2: 這扇門通往薩瓦多·歐哈納翰的理髮兼牙醫複合店。千萬別問他祖籍的事，他自己也搞得很亂。

column1: Salvatore O'Hanahan, the town barber, doesn't appreciate men touching his pole.
column2: 鎮上的理髮師薩瓦多·歐哈納翰，可不喜歡別人碰他的旋轉燈柱。

column1: Like all proud red-blooded Italian-Irish-American barbers, Salvatore O'Hanahan is extremely proud of his pole. (Actually, he almost had to give it up when they levied an expensive pole tax!)
column2: 就像所有血氣方剛的義裔愛爾蘭裔美籍理髮師一樣，薩瓦多·歐哈納翰對他的燈柱格外自豪。（其實他們一度課了很貴的「柱子稅」，差點讓他被迫放棄！）

column1: Do you have any relatives named Gallup?
column2: 你有沒有姓蓋洛普的親戚？

column1: Salvatore O'Hanahan's barber shop and dental emporium is still open for business.
column2: 薩瓦多·歐哈納翰的理髮兼牙醫店仍在營業中。

column1: Hey, don't take that sign, it isn't yours. It's Salvatore's. He stole it from a barber shop in San Jose!
column2: 喂，別拿那塊招牌，那不是你的。是薩瓦多的，他是從聖荷西一家理髮店偷來的！

column1: The sign says "O'Hanahan's Barber Shop."
column2: 招牌上寫著「歐哈納翰理髮店」。

column1: You can't talk to the sign! (It only knows sign language!)
column2: 你沒辦法跟招牌講話！（它只懂「手語」！）

column1: You wipe a smudge of something off the window.
column2: 你把窗戶上的一團污漬擦掉。

column1: Hey, this isn't road dirt! It's hair oil!
column2: 喂，這不是路上的泥巴！是髮油！

column1: Peering through the window, you think you see a barber inside!
column2: 你透過窗戶望去，似乎看到裡面有個理髮師！

column1: The stage wuz set fer Freddy's showdown. Wait, did I say "slowdown?" I meant "showdown. No, I DID say "showdown," didn't I? I thought I did, I warn't sure.
column2: 舞台已經為佛萊迪的對決搭好了。等等，俺剛是不是說成「對付」了？俺是說「對決」啦。不對，俺是不是真的說了「對決」？俺以為俺有說，不太確定。

column1: You can't reach it from here. Be VERY thankful!
column2: 你這裡搆不著。你該萬分慶幸！

column1: Apparently old Mrs. Murphy is either having a bladder control problem or some sort of lower gastro-intestinal difficulty. In either case, she's certainly doing her part to add to Coarsegold's unique "ambience!"
column2: 看樣子墨菲老太太不是膀胱有點失禁，就是腸胃出了什麼毛病。不管是哪一種，她都為粗金鎮獨特的「氣息」做出了貢獻！

column1: Hey, Mrs. Murphy! Stop by the Pharmacy, maybe I can help you out.
column2: 嘿，墨菲太太！來藥局一趟吧，說不定我能幫上忙。

column1: She calls you something under her breath.
column2: 她小聲罵了你一句什麼。

column1: Nothing in there worth sticking your finger in. (The same can be said of the brothel!)
column2: 裡面沒什麼值得你伸手指進去的東西。（妓院裡大概也是如此！）

column1: The south side of Main Street holds the remains of the railroad's telegraph office.
column2: 大街南側殘留著鐵路電報局的遺跡。

column1: Yep, solid Hotel!
column2: 沒錯，結實的旅館！

column1: The Dirty Sheet Hotel is the latest victim to the present Coarsegold business slump. They suffered from a severe lack of marketing expertise, as witnessed by their choice of names.
column2: 「髒床單旅館」是粗金鎮近來景氣蕭條下的最新受害者。從他們取的店名就看得出，行銷手腕嚴重不足。

column1: You can't get the Post Office to move no matter how hard you push it. (And it's been that way ever since!)
column2: 不管你怎麼推，郵局都紋風不動。（打從一開始就是這樣！）

column1: The town Post Office was one of the first victims of the city's demise. It's been closed for years
column2: 鎮上的郵局是這座城市衰亡最早的犧牲品之一，已經關閉多年了

column1: No need to touch it; it's about to fall off entirely. (Much like tourism in Coarsegold!)
column2: 不用碰它，反正就快整個掉下來了。（就跟粗金鎮的觀光業一樣！）

column1: This sign proclaims this as the "Post Office."
column2: 這塊招牌宣稱這裡是「郵局」。

column1: You can't talk to the sign. (It only knows sign language!)
column2: 你沒辦法跟招牌講話。（它只懂手語！）

column1: From inside, you think you can hear a voice say, "Sorry, that's not my window."
column2: 你似乎聽到裡面有個聲音說：「抱歉，這不是我的窗口。」

column1: The former post office is staffed by a complete work crew. None of them has yet noticed the place closed down years ago.
column2: 這間舊郵局裡有一整組員工在上班，沒有一個人發現這地方早在多年前就已經關門了。

column1: Those boards are nailed in place with rusty, self-tapping 10-penny locking nails with barbed ends. (In other words: no, you can't pry them off!)
column2: 那些木板是用生鏽的自攻十號倒刺鎖釘釘死的。（換句話說：不行，你撬不開！）

column1: Looks like the door to the Post Office has been removed and replaced with a less attractive barrier.
column2: 看來郵局的門被拆掉了，換上一道更不討喜的障礙物。

column1: It feels rough, unpleasant, and cheap. (Just like life in Coarsegold!)
column2: 摸起來粗糙、討人厭又廉價。（跟在粗金鎮過日子一樣！）

column1: Coarsegold's Main Street was once the center of a thriving metropolis, driven by the tons of gold found hereabouts. Now it's only a shadow of its former self. Mercantile Street leads away into the distance.
column2: 粗金鎮的大街曾是繁華都會的中心，靠著這一帶挖出的大量黃金撐起來。如今卻只剩過往榮景的影子。商業街往遠方延伸而去。

column1: The road doesn't need any more potholes, thank you! (But there'd probably be plenty for you to do in Illinois, where potholes are a source of pride!)
column2: 這條路不需要更多坑洞，謝了！（不過在伊利諾州，坑洞可是他們的驕傲，你去那邊大概有得忙！）

column1: In general, you'll have better luck if you try talking to things with MOUTHS!
column2: 一般來說，找有「嘴巴」的東西講話，運氣會好一點！

column1: You encounter dozens of those silly ol' rowdy cowhands from that cattle drive outside of town who are carelessly firing their guns everywhere and frightening (not to mention killing) the locals.
column2: 你遇上一大票鎮外趕牛隊裡那些傻里傻氣的粗魯牛仔，他們到處亂開槍，嚇壞了（更別提打死了）當地居民。

column1: Suddenly you feel a sharp pain in the chest...
column2: 你突然感到胸口一陣劇痛……

column1: You won't need any shcrub.
column2: 你用不著什麼「雜灌」。

column1: An unusual plant grows here; it's a cross between scrub grass and shrubs. It's called "Shcrub."
column2: 這裡長著一種奇怪的植物，是雜草和灌木雜交出來的東西，叫做「雜灌」。

column1: Chester Field runs one of Coarsegold's few remaining shops. Inside you'll find anything you want (if you don't want anything!).
column2: 切斯特·菲爾德經營著粗金鎮碩果僅存的幾家店之一。裡面應有盡有，只要你什麼都不想要就行！

column1: The store's sealed up tight. Locked. Shuttered. Off-limits. Verbotten. Out of Service. Padlocked. Folded. Bolted. Latched. Finished. Kaput. Ceased to be. It has expired. This is an ex-General Store.
column2: 這家店封得死死的。上鎖。拉下鐵門。禁止進入。閒人勿進。暫停營業。掛上大鎖。倒了。閂上。扣住。結束。完蛋。不復存在。它已經過期了。這是一家「前」雜貨店。

column1: If it wasn't nailed to the sidewalk, it would be pushing up the daisies. Incidentally, if you're wondering what happens to Chester Field as a result of what happens in this story: He went to Illinois and opened up a store there. They also made him Town Marshal, and he adjusted the name of his store accordingly.
column2: 要不是被釘死在人行道上，它早該進土裡陪雛菊了。順帶一提，如果你好奇切斯特·菲爾德後來怎麼了：他搬去了伊利諾州，在那裡開了間店。他們還讓他當上了鎮警長，於是他把店名也跟著改了。

column1: That's right! He called it, "Marshal Field's." (Gaak! Ptooey! Hork!)
column2: 沒錯！他把店取名叫「警長菲爾德百貨」。（嘔！呸！噁！）

column1: The General Store looks closed. Maybe it's your keen intuition. Maybe it's that razor-sharp second sense you have. Maybe it's that "closed" sign on the door that you'd trip over if it were any bigger.
column2: 這間雜貨店看起來關門了。或許是你敏銳的直覺。或許是你那第六感般的洞察力。也或許，是門上那塊「休息中」的牌子，再大一點你大概會被它絆倒。

column1: Chester Field's is closed at night.
column2: 切斯特·菲爾德的店晚上不營業。

column1: If you pushed this door, it might open.
column2: 推推看這扇門，說不定會開。

column1: You can't take it, it's been specially designed to blend in with Coarsegold's unique and progressive skyline.
column2: 你拿不走它，它是特別設計來融入粗金鎮這獨特又前衛的天際線的。

column1: This sign says, "Chester Field's Mercantile Co." It may indicate there's a store inside this building.
column2: 這塊招牌寫著：「切斯特·菲爾德商行」。看來這棟建築裡可能有間店。

column1: You consider writing "wash me" in the dust in the window, but you're way too mature for that.
column2: 你想過在窗上的灰塵裡寫「洗我」，但你成熟多了，不會做這種事。

column1: You just love to window-shop through windows so dirty you can't see through them. Maybe you should give Chester some window cleaner for Christmas.
column2: 你就是喜歡隔著髒到看不透的窗戶逛櫥窗。或許聖誕節該送切斯特一瓶玻璃清潔劑。

column1: With superhuman effort, you lift the wagon and rescue the little girl who was trapped underneath for God-knows-how-long.
column2: 你使出超人般的力氣抬起貨車，救出了不知道被困在底下多久的小女孩。

column1: Chester Field has been unloading this wagon since last winter.
column2: 切斯特·菲爾德從去年冬天就開始卸這輛貨車的貨了。

column1: The pharmacy door is locked. This ain't Mayberry, pardner!
column2: 藥局的門鎖著。這裡可不是梅伯里小鎮，老兄！

column1: It's the door to your pharmacy.
column2: 這是你藥局的門。

column1: I knew that!
column2: 我早就知道了！

column1: You unlock the door. Ta-daa! You're halfway through the game.
column2: 你打開了門鎖。鏘鏘！遊戲已經玩到一半了。

column1: You cleverly lock the door.
column2: 你機靈地把門鎖上了。

column1: You unlock the door.
column2: 你打開了門鎖。

column1: Dang it, no points this time.
column2: 可惡，這次沒加分。

column1: That's the wrong key for this door.
column2: 這把鑰匙不對，開不了這扇門。

column1: Whoops! Wrong key!
column2: 哎呀！鑰匙拿錯了！

column1: That's not the right key for the Pharmacy door!
column2: 這不是藥局大門的鑰匙！

column1: You added this hitch a few years ago, out of necessity. As they said when you moved in, "You'll never get this pharmacy off the ground without a hitch."
column2: 這根拴馬柱是你幾年前基於需要加裝的。你剛搬來時，大夥都說：「沒根拴馬柱，這藥局絕對開不成。」

column1: You can yank on that hitchin' post all you want, but you won't get it up. (You may, however, get a hernia.)
column2: 你要怎麼拉扯那根拴馬柱都行，反正你拔不起來。（倒是可能拉出疝氣。）

column1: The Sheriff must be out. Where could he be? It's over 550 miles to the nearest Dunkin' Donuts!
column2: 警長一定出門了。他能去哪呢？最近的甜甜圈店可有五百五十多哩遠呢！

column1: The door to Sheriff Checkum P. Shift's office. The office also contains a small jail cell, just big enough to hold one or two innocent bystanders.
column2: 這是警長切肯·P·席夫特辦公室的門。辦公室裡還有個小牢房，大小剛好關得下一兩個無辜的路人。

column1: The Sheriff's window. Not very good at keeping out the rain, but at least nobody's liable to break in. 'Course, who'd wanna break IN?
column2: 警長辦公室的窗戶。擋雨的效果不怎麼樣，但至少沒人會想從這破窗闖進去。話說回來，誰會想「闖進」牢房呢？

column1: The bars are set solidly in the mortar. Give it up!
column2: 這些欄杆牢牢嵌在灰泥裡。死心吧！

column1: This was Coarsegold's opera house, P.P.'s Playhouse. It was shut down by unpopular demand several months ago, after the owner was found necking with a lamb during a performance of "Ba-aa-aa-bette's Feast."
column2: 這裡曾是粗金鎮的歌劇院「P.P.戲院」。幾個月前，老闆被抓到在《巴~咩~咩特的盛宴》演出中跟一隻小羊親熱，劇院就在群情激憤下被勒令關閉了。

column1: Leave it to the wrecking crew.
column2: 這種事就交給拆除隊吧。

column1: The sign says "Tall & Thin Shop." And hey, it's right! That's just about the tallest and thinnest shop you've ever seen!
column2: 招牌寫著「高瘦商店」。嘿，還真的沒錯！這大概是你見過最高最瘦的一間店了！

column1: Leave the sign alone. Let it serve as a reminder to other shopkeepers who would incur the wrath of the good citizens of Coarsegold.
column2: 別動這塊招牌。就讓它留著，警惕其他可能惹惱粗金鎮善良居民的店家吧。

column1: The Tall & Thin shop. The owner narrowly escaped with his life once when he was discovered shortchanging customers.
column2: 高瘦商店。老闆有次被抓到少找顧客零錢，差點沒能保住小命。

column1: This place is boarded up tighter than a sheep's heinie on the Ponderosa.
column2: 這地方封得比龐德羅莎牧場的羊屁股還緊。

column1: The sign says "PP's Playhouse." Or it used to, anyway. Now it looks more like "PP's dlayhous."
column2: 招牌寫著「P.P.戲院」。至少以前是這樣。現在看起來比較像「P.P.戲阮」。

column1: You can barely reach that first letter, but even so, you don't feel like taking a big "p" right now.
column2: 你勉強搆得到那第一個字母「P」，不過你現在沒有「尿」的興致。

column1: This is your pharmacy, your home, the center of your universe. The Pharkas Pharmacy. You envision a day when there'll be a string of Pharkas Pharmacy phranchises phrom coast-to-coast.
column2: 這是你的藥局，你的家，你的世界中心。法卡斯藥局。你夢想著有一天，法卡斯藥局的連鎖店會從東岸開到西岸。

column1: You don't have room in your pockets for an entire pharmacy.
column2: 你口袋裡可沒地方裝下整間藥局。

column1: This is Sheriff Checkum P. Shift's jail and armory. The Sheriff does a mighty fine job of infiltrating the criminal element in town. In fact, he IS the foremost criminal element in town.
column2: 這是警長切肯·P·席夫特的牢房兼武器庫。警長打擊鎮上犯罪份子的功夫一流。事實上，他自己就是鎮上頭號犯罪份子。

column1: It's the most solidly-built structure in town.
column2: 這是鎮上蓋得最堅固的建築。

column1: You opted for a Colonial-style pharmacy.
column2: 你選了殖民地風格的藥局造型。

column1: You give a resounding thump to the columns. The termites hold their collective breath. The columns seem to be holding! (You and the termites heave a sigh of relief.)
column2: 你用力敲了敲柱子，發出響亮的咚咚聲。白蟻們全都屏住了呼吸。柱子看來撐住了！（你和白蟻們都鬆了一口氣。）

column1: These remnants of the Coarsegold depot are all tumbledown and shot.
column2: 粗金鎮車站的這些殘骸，早已破敗不堪、搖搖欲墜。

column1: This clutter is a local landmark, and as such is protected under the Eastern Madera County "Don't Touch That, It's A Landmark" Act of 1855.
column2: 這堆雜物是本地地標，依照 1855 年東馬德拉郡頒布的「別碰，那是地標」法案受到保護。

column1: The sign says "Pharkas Pharmacy." This must be the place.
column2: 招牌寫著「法卡斯藥局」。就是這裡沒錯了。

column1: You're too short to give it the white-glove test.
column2: 你個子太矮，搆不到做白手套檢查。

column1: Someone with a higher I.Q. than most of the folks in town correctly painted "Sheriff" here.
column2: 有個智商比鎮上大多數人都高一點的傢伙，在這裡正確地漆上了「警長」兩個字。

column1: Stealing the Sheriff's sign is something you might've done in your college days, but now you're too... chickenshift.
column2: 偷警長招牌這種事，你大學時代或許幹過，但現在你膽小得像隻雞，活脫脫是個「膽小席夫特」。

column1: Can't you read? The sign on the door says CLOSED.
column2: 你不識字嗎？門上的牌子寫著「休息中」。

column1: You rattle the doors a bit, but they seem locked for good.
column2: 你搖了搖門，但它們似乎鎖得死死的。

column1: That's the left pharmacy window. With all the dust out here, it's a pane to keep clean.
column2: 那是藥局左邊的窗戶。這裡灰塵這麼多，想維持窗明，可真是一大「創」痛。

column1: You'll smudge the dirt.
column2: 你會把灰塵抹得更髒。

column1: With all the dust out here, these windows are a pane to keep clean.
column2: 這裡灰塵這麼多，這些窗戶想保持乾淨，可真是一大「創」痛。

column1: Careful! You'll smear the filth.
column2: 小心！你會把污垢弄得到處都是。

column1: It's your ordinary water trough, favorite hangout of Coarsegold horses and town drunks. In brighter days, this trough would be filled with sparkling clear, pure mountain spring water, the kind they make into lousy domestic beer. These days, though, all you see in the trough is muddy, dirty ol' stagnant water with a bunch of dead flies floating on top.
column2: 這是個普通的飲水槽，是粗金鎮馬匹和鎮上酒鬼最愛聚集的地方。在風光的年代，這水槽會裝滿清澈晶瑩的純淨山泉水，就是拿去釀那種難喝的國產啤酒的那種水。不過如今，水槽裡只剩渾濁骯髒的死水，上面還漂著一堆死蒼蠅。

column1: You stick your hand into the stagnant water, and all you get is a damp, muddy forearm with a lotta dead flies stuck to it.
column2: 你把手伸進死水裡，結果只換來一隻濕答答、沾滿泥巴的手臂，上面還黏著一大堆死蒼蠅。

column1: You don't wanna get that all soaked with mucky ol' water!
column2: 你可不想讓它被那髒兮兮的爛水浸濕！

column1: This is one of the Eastern legs of Main Street.
column2: 這是大街東側的其中一段。

column1: That right there is one lousy conversationalist!
column2: 那傢伙的談話功力真是爛透了！

column1: Leave the street alone. It hain't hurtin' nobody.
column2: 別管這條街了。它又沒礙著誰。

column1: You must have this game confused with the arcade smash "Dig Dug Dog."
column2: 你一定是把這款遊戲跟大型電玩神作《打洞狗》搞混了。

column1: A gigantic pile of 50-pound sacks of baking soda fills the sidewalk in front of your store, nearly blocking the entrance. The baking soda is the "LeGand Hammer" brand, named for the famous international industrialist. His slogan: "Keep one sack in the smokehouse... and another in the stable, to help keep IT clean and fresh-smelling!"
column2: 一大堆五十磅裝的小蘇打粉袋，堆滿了你店門前的人行道，幾乎擋住了入口。這些小蘇打粉是「勒岡鐵鎚」牌的，以那位知名的國際實業家命名。他的廣告詞是：「燻肉房放一袋……馬廄再放一袋，幫『那裡』保持乾淨清爽！」

column1: Summoning up superhuman strength, you heft the huge pile of baking soda! Then, with a horrible wrenching, tearing sound, you cram the sacks of baking soda into your pants pocket.
column2: 你使出超人般的力氣，舉起了那一大堆小蘇打粉！接著，伴隨著一陣可怕的撕扯聲，你把那些袋子硬塞進了褲子口袋。

column1: It's Dominick, one of your part-time Native American employees. He works under the professional name "Running Gag." The Union told you that you |c0|had|c| to have a "Cigar Store"-style Indian out in front when you opened your pharmacy, but since there were lots of out-of-work real Indians in the neighborhood, you decided it would be politically correct to hire them.
column2: 這是多明尼克，你這裡兼職的美國原住民員工之一。他的藝名叫「老哏跑不掉」。工會告訴你，開藥局時門口|c0|必須|c|擺一尊「雪茄店」風格的印第安人像，但因為附近有不少失業的真印第安人，你覺得雇用他們才符合政治正確。

column1: Morning, Dominick.
column2: 早安，多明尼克。

column1: Morning, Freddy.
column2: 早安，佛萊迪。

column1: What's new?
column2: 有什麼新鮮事？

column1: Let's see. I finished reading "A Century of Dishonor" last night; quite impressive. That Helen Hunt Jackson really knows how to evoke an image of the white man's treachery. Do you know how many treaties your people have signed and then broken in the past 20 years alone?
column2: 讓我想想。我昨晚讀完了《恥辱的世紀》，寫得相當不錯。海倫·亨特·傑克森真的很會描繪白人背信棄義的樣子。你知道光是過去二十年，你們族人簽了又被毀掉多少份條約嗎？

column1: Er, excuse me, I hear someone calling me or something.
column2: 呃，不好意思，我好像聽到有人在叫我還是什麼的。

column1: Please don't take my cigars, Freddy. This is how I make tips. Standing out in front of the store doesn't really do much to guarantee me a secure retirement.
column2: 拜託別拿走我的雪茄，佛萊迪。我就靠這個賺點小費。光站在店門口，可保障不了我安穩的退休生活。

column1: No, thank you, Freddy. I've already got the sun in the morning, and the moon at night.
column2: 不了，謝謝你，佛萊迪。我早上有太陽，晚上有月亮，已經夠了。

column1: Use any more and you'll have to pay a royalty.
column2: 再多用一點，你就得付版稅了。

column1: It's Herbert, one of your part-time employees. Herbert spent the past five years as a Security Guard at F.W. Fleeceworth's in Utica, New York. They downsized, so Herbert moved out West to be closer to his family.
column2: 這是赫伯特，你的兼職員工之一。赫伯特過去五年在紐約州尤蒂卡的「F.W.費爾斯沃斯百貨」當保全。公司縮編後，赫伯特就搬到西部，好離家人近一點。

column1: Herbert, how's it hanging?
column2: 赫伯特，最近如何啊？

column1: As usual, Mr. Pharkas. Er... permission to speak freely?
column2: 老樣子，法卡斯先生。呃……可以讓我暢所欲言嗎？

column1: Of course.
column2: 當然可以。

column1: I've had an offer from a Bank in Scottsdale. They'd like me to stand inside the lobby and hold checking account brochures.
column2: 史考特戴爾的一家銀行找上我了。他們想請我站在大廳裡，拿著支票帳戶的宣傳單。

column1: How much are they offering you?
column2: 他們開多少？

column1: Five cents a day, plus a commission on the brochures.
column2: 一天五分錢，外加宣傳單的抽成。

column1: Let me look at the books and we'll talk in a couple days. I don't want to lose you.
column2: 讓我看看帳本，過幾天再談。我可不想失去你。

column1: Thank you, Mr. Pharkas. I don't want to lose you either.
column2: 謝謝你，法卡斯先生。我也不想失去你。

column1: We've spoken about this before, Mr. Pharkas. If you keep touching me, I'll have to speak up if you ever run for office.
column2: 這件事我們談過了，法卡斯先生。你要是再繼續碰我，哪天你選公職的時候，我可是會站出來說話的。

column1: What a generous offer, Mr. Pharkas! Unfortunately, Union rules specify that I must turn down tips or gratuities of any sort, unless they're in the form of canoes.
column2: 這提議真大方啊，法卡斯先生！可惜工會規定我必須拒絕任何形式的小費或饋贈，除非是……獨木舟形式的。

column1: What? You expect me to tip a CANOE?
column2: 什麼？你要我用「獨木舟」給小費？

column1: It's Pete, one of your part-time employees. Pete used to work for a lawn jockey company, but he was fired after puberty when he grew too tall for the business. He's insecure, but he's a good worker.
column2: 這是彼特，你的兼職員工之一。彼特以前在一家草坪騎師雕像公司上班，但青春期後長太高，不符合公司的需求就被解雇了。他缺乏安全感，但工作很認真。

column1: How goes it, Pete?
column2: 最近好嗎，老皮？

column1: Just fine, Mr. Pharkas, just fine! Sure is a nice day today!
column2: 挺好的，法卡斯先生，挺好的！今天天氣真不錯！

column1: Yes, Pete, it's beautiful out.
column2: 沒錯，彼特，外頭天氣好極了。

column1: I was wondering if it might be possible for me to knock off a little early today.
column2: 我在想，今天能不能讓我早點下班。

column1: Something in particular going on?
column2: 有什麼特別的事嗎？

column1: Well, it's just such a nice day, I thought I'd spend a little quality time with the buffalo. Maybe take him to Yosemite, let him run around and do some grazing. You know, the usual.
column2: 嗯，就是今天天氣這麼好，我想說陪水牛好好相處一下。或許帶牠去優勝美地，讓牠到處跑跑、吃吃草。你知道的，老樣子。

column1: I suppose that'd be okay. Sure, you can leave early. Just watch out for poachers now, hehe!
column2: 我想這樣可以。好啊，你可以早點走。小心點，別遇上偷獵的，嘿嘿！

column1: Haha! That's a funny one, Mr. Pharkas! I'll be sure to do that! Poachers. Haha! Like anyone would want to do THAT to buffalo! Hehehe!
column2: 哈哈！這笑話真好笑，法卡斯先生！我一定會小心的！偷獵的。哈哈！誰會想對水牛做那種事啊！嘿嘿嘿！

column1: What's the matter? Did I do something wrong?
column2: 怎麼了？我做錯什麼了嗎？

column1: No, Pete, I was just picking a hair off your outfit.
column2: 沒有啦，彼特，我只是幫你把衣服上的毛撿掉。

column1: Oh. Yeah, my buffalo is shedding again. Happens every spring. You should see my teepee!
column2: 喔。對啊，我的水牛又在掉毛了。每年春天都這樣。你真該看看我的帳篷！

column1: That's an extremely nice offer, sir! But I've already got one!
column2: 這提議真是太好了，長官！不過我已經有一個了！

column1: Are you sure?
column2: 你確定嗎？

column1: Oho, yes, it's very nice!
column2: 喔呵，當然，那東西挺不錯的！

column1: How!
column2: 你好！

column1: Yeah, yeah.
column2: 是啦，是啦。

column1: Time for you shift over!
column2: 換你上工的時候到了！

column1: Oh, puh-leeze. You've been reading too many dime novels. Stop talking like that.
column2: 喔，拜託。你廉價小說看太多了吧。別再那樣說話了。

column1: Just trying to please the tourists, Herb.
column2: 只是想討好觀光客啦，赫伯。

column1: Sure, sure. Tourists. Whatever. Seeya later, I'm goin' to go soak my corns.
column2: 好啦好啦。觀光客。隨便你說。晚點見，我要去泡泡我的雞眼了。

column1: My people call it "maize."
column2: 我們族人管這個叫「玉米」。

column1: Sheeeeesh.
column2: 嘖嘖嘖。

column1: So Freddy wuz forced to shut down the ol' Pharmacy agin his will. But he vowed to keep the place up, knowin' that someday he'd be openin' it up again. Problem bein', the Sheriff, an ornery cuss if ever there wuz one, wuz doin' this all over town: the hotel, the Playhouse, the Smithie, the Tall 'n Thin Shop, closin' 'em all down on some flimsy pretext.
column2: 於是佛萊迪被迫違背自己的意願，把老藥局給關了。但他發誓要把這地方維持好，知道總有一天會重新開張。問題是，那個脾氣壞得沒話說的警長，正對全鎮做著同樣的事：旅館、戲院、鐵匠鋪、高瘦商店，全都被他用些站不住腳的藉口給關了。

column1: Board up yer winders 'n' doors! Lock up the wimmen and children! Run fer the border, Louise! Thar's a |c2|stampede|c| a-comin'! A |c2|stam-peeeeede!|c| Hurry up, Freddy! Ya only got a week and a half a'fore they git here.
column2: 快把你家窗戶跟門都釘起來！把婦孺都鎖好！快跑去邊境啊，露易絲！|c2|獸群暴衝|c|要來啦！是|c2|獸——群——暴——衝——啊！|c|快點，佛萊迪！牠們一個半禮拜後就要到啦。

column1: A week and a half?
column2: 一個半禮拜？

column1: They'se SNAILS!
column2: 牠們是蝸牛啦！

column1: Snails? SNAILS??
column2: 蝸牛？蝸牛？？

column1: Good heavens, this is the worst thing to happen to Coarsegold since the great Hail of Clams back in '83!
column2: 我的老天，這是粗金鎮自從'83年那場「蛤蜊冰雹」以來最慘的事了！

column1: Those flies are really enjoying that by-product!
column2: 那些蒼蠅還真愛這坨「副產品」！

column1: You bravely, stupidly grab the steaming, fly-laden horse plop. Fortunately, it seems to be holding together well as you place it in your pocket.
column2: 你既勇敢又愚蠢地抓起那坨還冒著熱氣、爬滿蒼蠅的馬糞。所幸把它放進口袋時，它看起來還算成形。

column1: It's a "closed" sign. The Sheriff had Billy nail it up after he shut you down as a fire hazard. Hmph!
column2: 這是塊「休息中」的牌子。警長把你藥局當成消防隱患勒令關閉後，就叫比利把它釘上去了。哼！

column1: You can't talk to it. (It only knows sign language!)
column2: 你沒辦法跟它講話。（它只懂手語！）

column1: You'd better leave it up until you've settled this matter once and for all.
column2: 你最好先別碰它，等把這件事徹底解決了再說。

column1: That's "Gluteus" Maximillian and his horse (who appears to be wearing one of those hilarious "Whoopee Saddles"). They call him "Gluteus" because he's the butt of every practical joke in town!
column2: 那是「屁股」馬克西米倫和他的馬（那馬似乎裝著一副滑稽的「整人馬鞍」）。大家叫他「屁股」，是因為他是全鎮惡作劇的頭號笑柄！

column1: Hey, Max!
column2: 嘿，麥克斯！

column1: Max ignores you, but he seems to flinch a bit. Perhaps he thinks you're in on yet another nasty prank!
column2: 麥克斯不理你，但似乎微微縮了一下。他大概以為你又要來搞什麼惡整了！

column1: Stop teasing him, he's too easy a mark.
column2: 別再逗他了，他太容易被整了。

column1: He just wants to be left alone!
column2: 他只想一個人靜靜！

column1: There's something to be said for putting him out of his misery... but he'll recover.
column2: 讓他解脫一下或許也不錯……不過他會挺過去的。

column1: You don't need any more activated charcoal!
column2: 你用不著更多活性碳了！

column1: It's boarded up, but there's nothing in there anyway except some worthless old rocks and few petrified cinnamon rolls. Insert your own nauseating joke about "rock and roll" here!
column2: 它被封起來了，不過裡面反正也只有些不值錢的舊石頭，和幾個石化的肉桂捲。「石頭」加「捲」，自己接個噁心的雙關笑話吧！

column1: Hot! WHOA, that's hot, boy! Very, very hot!
column2: 燙！哇喔，真的很燙，老兄！非常非常燙！

column1: The char-broiled and blackened remains of the Old Abandoned Assay Office stand on the corner of Main and Edukashun. You suspect that this was the work of either whoever's behind all the destructive goings-on in town... or voracious Louisiana chef Paul Prudhomme!
column2: 那間老驗金所燒得焦黑的殘骸，矗立在大街與「教鬱遜」街的轉角。你懷疑這不是鎮上搞破壞的幕後黑手幹的，就是路易斯安那那位貪吃的名廚保羅·普魯多姆搞的鬼！

column1: It's the Old Abandoned Assay Office, once owned by a subsidiary of the Old Abandoned Mine Company. Before the mine shut down, this is where you got your nuggets appraised. (Now you have to go to Madame's for that!)
column2: 這是老驗金所，曾經是老礦業公司旗下子公司的產業。礦場關閉之前，你都是在這裡讓人估你的金塊斤兩。（現在這種事得去夫人那裡辦了！）

column1: It's the Old Abandoned Assay Office, once owned by a subsidiary of the Old Abandoned Mine Company. It's burning merrily, which is a source of some concern to you since your pharmacy is right next door. Did somebody purposefully torch it? Wasn't this a "no-burn" day?
column2: 這是老驗金所，曾經是老礦業公司旗下子公司的產業。它燒得正歡，這讓你有點擔心，因為你的藥局就在隔壁。是有人故意縱火的嗎？今天不是「禁止焚燒日」嗎？

column1: Leave it alone. It's too burnt out to talk right now!
column2: 別管它了。它現在燒得連話都說不出來了！

column1: <rim shot!>
column2: <鼓聲一響！>

column1: You just went cow-tipping last night. You can go shanty-tipping some other time. (What percentage does one tip a shanty, anyway?)
column2: 你昨晚才去推倒睡牛玩過了。棚屋要推改天再說吧。（話說回來，推棚屋這種「小費」該給幾成啊？）

column1: It's a sea shanty. (See? Shanty!)
column2: 這是一首水手號子。（妙吧？「號子」跟「棚屋」，還真是傻傻分不清楚！）

column1: Freddy dragged his bleedin' self over to the Schoolhouse... the anger and hurt wuz jus' rippin' at his gut like a swarm of botflies on roadkill, only worse 'cuz Freddy, unlike roadkill, wuz still alive. The schoolhouse door wuz unlocked fer once, and Freddy walked right on in.
column2: 佛萊迪拖著渾身是傷的身子走向學校……怒火與傷痛在他肚裡翻攪，像一群馬蠅叮著路邊的死屍，只是更慘，因為佛萊迪跟那死屍不一樣，他還活著。學校的門難得沒上鎖，佛萊迪就這麼直接走了進去。

column1: The Old Abandoned Assay Office is ablaze, threatening to burn down not only itself and your pharmacy, but the whole town!
column2: 老驗金所燒起來了，不只威脅到它自己和你的藥局，還可能把全鎮都燒掉！

column1: Don't go poking in there; that's where the tramps hang out. If you wanna poke some tramps, go to the Brothel!)
column2: 別去那裡亂戳，那是流浪漢聚集的地方。你要是想「戳」流浪漢，去妓院找吧！)

column1: Shrubs and weeds grow amongst the wreck of the old train depot.
column2: 灌木和雜草在老火車站的殘骸間叢生。

column1: Stop trying to horn in on their game. This one's for high rollers only.
column2: 別想插一腳玩他們的遊戲了。這局只有大戶才能上桌。

column1: The boy doesn't look very receptive to your offer.
column2: 這男孩看起來對你的提議沒什麼興趣。

column1: It's one of the young townsboys, diligently trying to make his point. (In this case, it's a six.)
column2: 這是鎮上的一個小男孩，正努力想「拚出個點數」。（這次是六點。）

column1: Are you trying to make a point? Because the best way to make a point is to explain your position calmly and succinctly.
column2: 你是想「講出個道理」嗎？因為要講道理，最好的辦法是冷靜又簡潔地說明你的立場。

column1: (The boy looks at you with exasperation and returns to his game.)
column2: （男孩一臉不耐煩地看著你，然後回去繼續玩他的遊戲。）

column1: The boy shrugs you off. He seems awfully intent on getting control of the dice.
column2: 男孩不理你，聳聳肩。他似乎一心一意想搶到骰子的控制權。

column1: He doesn't want them unless they're a new pair of shoes for baby.
column2: 除非那是要給孩子買新鞋，不然他才不想要。

column1: It's a little boy, rolling dice and muttering something about baby shoes.
column2: 這是個小男孩，一邊擲骰子，一邊嘀咕著什麼孩子的鞋子。

column1: So, you boys playing jacks? Where are the jacks?
column2: 你們這些小鬼在玩抓子兒嗎？抓子兒在哪？

column1: They snicker at your naivete and return to their game.
column2: 他們嘲笑你的天真，然後繼續玩他們的遊戲。

column1: Penelope keeps this door locked all the time, to keep the kids in and the rabble out. Thank goodness there's no such thing as a fire code yet!
column2: 潘妮洛普總是把這扇門鎖著，好讓孩子們留在裡面、閒雜人等擋在外面。還好這年頭還沒有消防法規這種東西！

column1: This is the schoolhouse door.
column2: 這是學校的門。

column1: You try to get close enough to throw it, but are forced back by the extreme heat and accomplish nothing but a large white splat on the ground.
column2: 你想靠近到能丟出去的距離，卻被高溫逼退，結果只在地上留下一大攤白色的痕跡，什麼都沒達成。

column1: Don't be a fool! You may be tough, but you're not THAT tough!
column2: 別傻了！你雖然夠硬，但還沒硬到那種地步！

column1: Throwing that into the fire will only make the conflagration worse!
column2: 把那東西丟進火裡，只會讓火勢燒得更旺！

column1: Flames jut from every loose board and hole in the old Assay Office! It must be arson,! 'cuz everything flammable in the Assay Office was stolen ages ago!
column2: 老驗金所的每一塊鬆脫木板和每一個破洞都竄出火舌！這一定是縱火，因為驗金所裡所有能燒的東西早就被偷光了！

column1: The ladder, held in place by a couple of old loose screws, easily comes away from the slide. You somehow cram it into your pocket along with the rest of the junk you're carrying. Way to go, Freddy! Wreck the little kids' playground equipment! (If only they knew how good and true your heart is.)
column2: 那座梯子只靠幾顆鬆脫的舊螺絲固定，輕輕鬆鬆就從溜滑梯上拆了下來。你不知怎麼地把它硬塞進口袋，跟你身上一堆雜七雜八的東西擠在一起。幹得好啊，佛萊迪！去破壞小朋友的遊樂設施吧！（要是他們知道你的心地有多善良真誠就好了。）

column1: Someone's using the ladder at this very moment.
column2: 現在有人正在用那個梯子呢。

column1: It's a ladder, propped up against the slide so the kids can play.
column2: 那是個梯子，靠在溜滑梯旁邊，讓小朋友可以玩耍。

column1: No thank you, Frederick. I don't drink, and I hope you don't either. After all, lips that touch liquor will never touch mine!
column2: 不用了，謝謝，佛萊迪。我不喝酒，也希望你也別喝。畢竟，沾過酒的嘴唇，永遠碰不到我的！

column1: Hey, I hear ya, Penelope! Lips that lick... yes, what you just said!
column2: 嘿，我聽懂了，潘妮洛普！舔嘴唇的……對，就是妳剛剛說的那樣！

column1: Wherever did you find a pair of boots like ruffians and hooligans wear?
column2: 你這雙靴子到底是打哪兒弄來的？看起來就像流氓惡棍在穿的。

column1: Oh, I just... they were in... um, I forget. Yes, that's it, I forget.
column2: 噢，我只是……它們原本在……呃，我忘了。對，就是這樣，我忘了。

column1: Hm. Well, I'd get rid of them before somebody gets the idea that you're some sort of gunslinger!
column2: 嗯。你最好趕快處理掉，免得有人誤以為你是什麼槍手！

column1: Look, Penelope... candle wax!
column2: 看，潘妮洛普……蠟燭油！

column1: Why, yes it is, Frederick. How lovely for you. Are you starting some sort of collection?
column2: 哎呀，沒錯，佛萊迪。真替你高興。你是在收集什麼東西嗎？

column1: No. I mean, yes.
column2: 不是。我是說，是。

column1: Oh. Well, if I run across any myself, I'll be glad to save some for you.
column2: 噢。這樣的話，我要是遇到了，很樂意幫你留一些。

column1: How quaint, a handful of charcoal. You'll pardon me if I don't take those off your hands, won't you? I don't want to muss my dress.
column2: 好古樸啊，一把木炭。你不介意我不接手吧？我可不想弄髒我的裙子。

column1: Shoot, no problem, Penelope. I'll take care of this.
column2: 唉呀，沒問題，潘妮洛普。這個我來處理就好。

column1: Look, Penelope, see what I have here!
column2: 看，潘妮洛普，瞧我這兒有什麼！

column1: A key?
column2: 一把鑰匙？

column1: Yep!
column2: 沒錯！

column1: I'm very happy for you, Frederick.
column2: 我真替你高興，佛萊迪。

column1: See this claim check, Penelope? Does it mean anything to you?
column2: 看看這張提貨單，潘妮洛普？妳知道這是什麼嗎？

column1: I'm sure it doesn't, Frederick. I'm sorry. Perhaps one of our local shopkeepers would recognize it.
column2: 我肯定不知道，佛萊迪，抱歉。也許鎮上哪個店家會認得。

column1: Look, Penelope! Clay!
column2: 看，潘妮洛普！黏土！

column1: Hmmm, this is quite interesting. Hydrous aluminum silicate, mixed with powdered feldspar, quartz, sand, iron oxides and other minerals. Very malleable!
column2: 嗯，這還挺有意思的。含水矽酸鋁，混了長石粉、石英、沙子、氧化鐵和其他礦物。延展性很好！

column1: Penelope, you've never looked more beautiful to me than you do now, analyzing the chemical makeup of this compound.
column2: 潘妮洛普，妳現在分析這化合物成分的樣子，是我見過妳最美的時刻。

column1: Thank you, Frederick. I kinda like you, too.
column2: 謝謝你，佛萊迪。我也，有點喜歡你。

column1: Freddy, I beg you! Not in front of the children!
column2: 佛萊迪，拜託你！別在孩子們面前！

column1: Why, isn't that the key to your Pharmacy?
column2: 哎呀，那不是你藥局的鑰匙嗎？

column1: Yes, it is!
column2: 沒錯，就是！

column1: Well, for goodness' sake, Frederick, don't be waving it around so! Somebody might steal it and rob the store!
column2: 天哪，佛萊迪，別這樣揮來揮去的！萬一被人偷走，店可就要遭殃了！

column1: You chuckle smugly to yourself as you pocket the key.
column2: 你得意地竊笑著，把鑰匙收進口袋。

column1: Here, Penelope.
column2: 拿去，潘妮洛普。

column1: I'm sorry, Frederick, you know those drugstore remedies don't do me any good!
column2: 抱歉，佛萊迪，你知道那些藥局偏方對我一點用都沒有！

column1: Some empty bottles, Penelope?
column2: 幾個空瓶子，潘妮洛普？

column1: What a... |c2|thoughtful|c|... gift, Frederick. Tell you what: why don't YOU hang onto these for me, since I'm at work right now. Thank you so much.
column2: 真是……|c2|貼心|c|……的禮物啊，佛萊迪。這樣好了：你先幫我保管這些，反正我現在還在上班。太謝謝你了。

column1: Sure. A-yuh.
column2: 當然。嗯哼。

column1: No, thank you, Frederick. I haven't purposefully hyperventilated since my college days!
column2: 不用了，謝謝，佛萊迪。我從大學畢業後，就沒故意過度換氣了！

column1: That certainly looks sharp and pointy, Frederick! Please, take it away before I cut myself!
column2: 那東西看起來又尖又利，佛萊迪！拜託快拿走，免得我割到自己！

column1: This looks like somebody else's prescription, Frederick! You'd better get back to work and give it to him right away. It might be important!
column2: 這看起來是別人的處方箋，佛萊迪！你最好趕緊回去把它交給人家，說不定很重要！

column1: Good thought! You're so smart, Penelope.
column2: 好主意！妳真聰明，潘妮洛普。

column1: You're so obedient and puppy-doggish, Frederick. Now straight off with you!
column2: 你真是又乖又像隻小狗一樣聽話，佛萊迪。好了，快去吧！

column1: That looks like the ladder from our playground slide, Frederick. Now I'm not saying you took it, but I'm going to close my eyes for a count of five, and when I open them, I want that ladder returned... IF that's our ladder. Ready?
column2: 那看起來像是我們遊樂場溜滑梯的梯子，佛萊迪。我不是說是你拿的，但我要閉上眼睛數到五，睜開眼的時候，我希望那個梯子已經物歸原處……如果那真的是我們的梯子的話。準備好了嗎？

column1: Penelope closes her eyes and count to five, while you stand there awkwardly hiding the ladder behind you.
column2: 潘妮洛普閉上眼睛數到五，你則尷尬地站在原地，把梯子藏在身後。

column1: I see the ladder is not back in place. Perhaps it was somebody else who stole it. I apologize for wrongly accusing you, Frederick. Can you forgive me?
column2: 我看梯子還沒歸位。也許是別人偷走的吧。我為錯怪你道歉，佛萊迪。你能原諒我嗎？

column1: Oh, for ANYthing, Penelope!
column2: 噢，什麼都可以，潘妮洛普！

column1: Look, Penelope! It's my lasso! I made it out of rope!
column2: 看，潘妮洛普！這是我的套索！我用繩子做的！

column1: That's VERY good, Frederick. VERY good!
column2: 做得非常好，佛萊迪。非常好！

column1: I certainly hope you're not expecting ME to use that leather strap, Frederick. I do not go in for those unusual games.
column2: 我可希望你不是要我用那條皮帶，佛萊迪。我對那種奇怪的玩法沒興趣。

column1: Uh, no, I was just showing it to you.
column2: 呃，不是啦，我只是給妳看看而已。

column1: Well, then, that's fine.
column2: 嗯，那樣的話就好。

column1: Oh, did you need me to read this to you?
column2: 噢，你需要我唸給你聽嗎？

column1: No, no... I was just seeing if you wanted it.
column2: 不、不用……我只是想看妳要不要。

column1: It's addressed to you, Frederick. Why would I want it?
column2: 這是寫給你的，佛萊迪。我要它做什麼？

column1: Don't tell me you were just wandering around, trying to give items to people at random? That's no way to be a Western Hero.
column2: 你該不會只是到處閒晃，隨便找人塞東西吧？這樣可當不成西部英雄。

column1: No, no, I wasn't, I swear.
column2: 不、不是，我發誓沒有。

column1: That's good, let's keep it that way, all right?
column2: 那就好，繼續保持，好嗎？

column1: Yes, yes, whatever you say, Penelope.
column2: 好、好，妳說了算，潘妮洛普。

column1: It's Penelope Primm: Full-time Schoolmarm, Full-time Single Frontier Woman, and Part-time Heartthrob! How does she do it all? Easy! She's incredibly uptight and has numerous stress-related diseases!
column2: 她是潘妮洛普：全職女教師、全職邊疆單身女子，還兼職萬人迷！她是怎麼辦到的？很簡單！因為她緊張兮兮，還得了一堆壓力病！
