column1: You don't owe me any money, Frederick. You take it, I insist.
column2: 你不欠我錢，佛萊迪。這個你拿去，我堅持。

column1: Yes, I was just showing you.
column2: 對啊，我只是給妳看看。

column1: Oh! Well, it's a very nice bankroll, Frederick.
column2: 噢！這疊鈔票挺好看的嘛，佛萊迪。

column1: Thank you.
column2: 謝謝。

column1: Would you like some beer, Penelope?
column2: 想來點啤酒嗎，潘妮洛普？

column1: Brewed malt beverages are an acquired taste, preferred by lowbrows and ruffians. Surely you don't drink them, do you, Frederick?
column2: 麥芽釀造飲品是粗人和無賴才會愛喝的東西。你該不會也喝吧，佛萊迪？

column1: No, but this is beer.
column2: 不喝，不過這就是啤酒。

column1: Beer IS a brewed malt beverage.
column2: 啤酒就是麥芽釀造飲品啊。

column1: Oh... I knew that. No, I don't drink beer, that's why I was offering it to you.
column2: 噢……這我知道。不是，我不喝啤酒，所以才拿來請妳的。

column1: Oh. I see. Hmmmm.
column2: 噢。原來如此。嗯……

column1: Are you insinuating that I might have a need for such a... a..
column2: 你是在暗示我可能需要這種……這種……

column1: No, no, no, I was just thinking... um... this is something I have in the store, see?
column2: 不、不、不，我只是在想……嗯……這是店裡本來就有的東西，妳看？

column1: Frederick, have you been out in the sun too long? Perhaps you should go back into the store and attend to your customers!
column2: 佛萊迪，你是不是曬太陽曬太久了？你也許該回店裡去照顧客人了！

column1: Uh... yes, I'll do that! Thanks!
column2: 呃……對，我這就去！謝了！

column1: This is somebody's prescription, Frederick! I shouldn't been looking at this.
column2: 這是別人的處方箋，佛萊迪！我不該偷看的。

column1: You're right, as usual, Penelope. You're always right.
column2: 妳說得對，一如往常，潘妮洛普。妳總是對的。

column1: Thank you, Frederick Pharkas. I try to be.
column2: 謝謝你，佛萊迪·法卡斯。我盡量做到。

column1: Penelope, I just whipped this up in the lab. It should purify all the contaminated drinking water in town, if I can just figure out how to get it in the water supply!
column2: 潘妮洛普，我剛在實驗室裡調出這個。應該能淨化全鎮受污染的飲用水，只要我能想辦法把它加進供水系統裡！

column1: That is a daunting task, Frederick. But if I'm not mistaken, don't we all get our water from the same place?
column2: 那可是件艱鉅的任務，佛萊迪。不過如果我沒記錯，我們大家不都是從同一個地方取水的嗎？

column1: Say, you're right! No wonder you're the schoolmarm!
column2: 哎呀，妳說得對！難怪妳是女教師！

column1: Thank you, Frederick. And you're a whiz in the laboratory!
column2: 謝謝你，佛萊迪。你在實驗室裡可真是一把好手！

column1: Oh, I'd never do that.
column2: 噢，我才不會那樣做呢。

column1: Pardon?
column2: 你說什麼？

column1: Oh, you mean... I mean, never mind.
column2: 噢，妳是說……我是說，沒事了。

column1: Look, rope!
column2: 看，繩子！

column1: Yes, Frederick, it certainly is.
column2: 對，佛萊迪，這的確是繩子。

column1: Want it?
column2: 要嗎？

column1: No. Don't you?
column2: 不要。你不要嗎？

column1: Yes, but I was just checking.
column2: 要，不過我只是問問看。

column1: Oh! That was considerate of you, thank you!
column2: 噢！你真體貼，謝謝！

column1: These are snails from the stampede. Do you like snails?
column2: 這些是那場蝸牛暴衝留下的蝸牛。妳喜歡蝸牛嗎？

column1: I find them fascinating from an academic standpoint, but I would not care to carry them around or ingest them.
column2: 從學術角度來看，我覺得牠們挺有意思的，但我可不想帶著牠們到處走，更不想吃下肚。

column1: That's exactly the way I feel. I love you, Penelope.
column2: 我也是這麼想的。我愛妳，潘妮洛普。

column1: Frederick! You do surprise me sometimes.
column2: 佛萊迪！你有時候真的會讓我嚇一跳。

column1: Penelope!
column2: 潘妮洛普！

column1: Freddy! How nice to see you! Did you leave work just to come see me?
column2: 佛萊迪！見到你真好！你是特地放下工作來看我的嗎？

column1: Er... uh... YEAH! Just being able to look at you makes my day seem to fly by.
column2: 呃……啊……對啊！光是能看著妳，就讓我覺得這一天過得飛快。

column1: Penelope titters and tilts her head coyly.
column2: 潘妮洛普嬌笑著，俏皮地歪了歪頭。

column1: (TITTERS) You do know how to flatter a girl, don't you? Now you get back to work, so you'll have enough money to take me to the Sadie Hawkins Day Dance next week!
column2: （嬌笑）你還真懂得討女孩子歡心，是吧？好了，快回去工作，這樣你才有錢下星期帶我去參加莎蒂霍金斯舞會！

column1: As you wish, milady!
column2: 遵命，夫人！

column1: Tee-hee!
column2: 嘻嘻！

column1: Hello again, Penelope.
column2: 又見面了，潘妮洛普。

column1: Freddy, you rogue! Courting a girl in broad daylight and all. Why, I'm going to get a reputation!
column2: 佛萊迪，你這個壞胚子！大白天就跑來獻殷勤。哎呀，我的名聲都要被你搞壞了！

column1: I just needed to hear the music of your voice. Now I can muddle through the rest of the day with the memory of your smile and your kind voice.
column2: 我只是想聽聽妳那如音樂般的聲音。現在，帶著妳的笑容和溫柔嗓音的回憶，我就能撐過這一天剩下的時間了。

column1: You do lard it on, don't you? You make me all giggly.
column2: 你還真會灌迷湯呢，是吧？你把我逗得咯咯直笑。

column1: Only because I love to hear you laugh.
column2: 純粹是因為我愛聽你笑。

column1: Penelope...
column2: 潘妮洛普……

column1: Hold on, at least wait 'til she's out of the schoolhouse!
column2: 等等，至少也等她走出校舍再說吧！

column1: Hello, Penelope!
column2: 妳好，潘妮洛普！

column1: Frederick, my sweet! This is turning out to be quite the busy day for you, isn't it?
column2: 佛萊迪，我的甜心！看來你今天可真忙呢，是吧？

column1: It sure is. But I'm really looking forward to that Sadie Hawkins Dance.
column2: 是啊。不過我真的很期待那場莎蒂霍金斯舞會。

column1: And I as well, Freddy. Romance does make my heart flutter so!
column2: 我也是，佛萊迪。戀愛的滋味讓我心裡小鹿亂撞呢！

column1: 'Til later, my dear!
column2: 待會兒見，親愛的！

column1: 'Til then, my sweet! Tee-hee!
column2: 到時候見，甜心！嘻嘻！

column1: (GAGGING SOUNDS) <gag>
column2: （作嘔聲）<gag>

column1: Penelope?
column2: 潘妮洛普？

column1: Yes, Frederick?
column2: 什麼事，佛萊迪？

column1: Uh... we're still "go" for that dance, right?
column2: 呃……我們那場舞會還是照原定計畫，對吧？

column1: Yes, Frederick, a thousand times yes!
column2: 是的，佛萊迪，千真萬確！

column1: Frederick! You were magnificent, the way you stopped that stampede and cured those crapulent horses.
column2: 佛萊迪！你太厲害了，不但擋下那場暴衝，還治好了那些醉醺醺的馬。

column1: Gosh, Penelope... you know I'd move a mountain for you, if I could.
column2: 天哪，潘妮洛普……妳知道，只要我做得到，我願意為妳移山倒海。

column1: I think maybe I've misjudged you, Frederick.
column2: 我想，我大概是看走眼了，佛萊迪。

column1: Misjudged me?
column2: 看走眼？

column1: I used to think you were a little... you know... mild-mannered. But I like a man who knows how to use his wits AND his muscles. I do believe we may be ready to take this relationship to its next step.
column2: 我以前總覺得你有點……你知道的……溫吞。可是我喜歡既有腦袋又有肌肉的男人。我想我們這段關係，也許該邁向下一步了。

column1: YEE-HAW! I mean... oh, that would be something I think is feasible.
column2: 呀呼！我是說……噢，我想這件事應該是可行的。

column1: Yes, I'm quite sure of it. The upcoming Sadie Hawkins Day dance should be a memorable one.
column2: 對，我很肯定。這次的莎蒂霍金斯舞會，一定會是個難忘的夜晚。

column1: Penelope, you've made me the happiest... I mean, you're going to make me the happiest... aw, heck. Penelope, you're a pal!
column2: 潘妮洛普，妳讓我成了最幸福……我是說，妳將會讓我成為最幸福……唉，管它的。潘妮洛普，妳真是個好夥伴！

column1: Hi, Penelope!
column2: 嗨，潘妮洛普！

column1: Frederick, you've certainly got a gleam in your eye!
column2: 佛萊迪，你眼裡可閃著光呢！

column1: Don't be teasing me, now, Penelope. You KNOW why!
column2: 別逗我了，潘妮洛普。妳明明知道為什麼！

column1: I believe I do. Tee-hee!
column2: 我想我知道。嘻嘻！

column1: Penelope, quick, you're in danger!
column2: 潘妮洛普，快，妳有危險了！

column1: Why... Frederick, you're all flushed! What's wrong?
column2: 哎呀……佛萊迪，你滿臉通紅的！怎麼了？

column1: There's a stampede headed this way. Well... slowly, but still. If I don't act quickly, the whole town's gonna get slimed.
column2: 有一群暴衝的東西正朝這裡來。嗯……雖然慢，但還是在來。要是我不快點行動，全鎮都要被黏液淹沒了。

column1: I don't understand! Slimed? That sounds distasteful!
column2: 我聽不懂！黏液淹沒？聽起來真噁心！

column1: It's snails, Penelope. You've got to get the children inside!
column2: 是蝸牛啦，潘妮洛普。妳得把孩子們帶進屋裡！

column1: If it's only snails, Frederick, I'm sure we've got enough time for recess, don't we?
column2: 如果只是蝸牛，佛萊迪，我們應該還有時間下課吧？

column1: Well... yeah.
column2: 呃……是啦。

column1: Frederick, why don't you run be a man and divert the stampede or do whatever a real hero would do? I'll keep my eye on the children for the time being.
column2: 佛萊迪，你何不去當個真男人，把那群暴衝的東西引開，做點真英雄會做的事？我先在這兒看著孩子們。

column1: I'll make you proud, Penelope. You'll see!
column2: 我會讓妳為我驕傲的，潘妮洛普。妳等著瞧！

column1: Penelope, I'm doin' my best to get rid of that pesky snail stampede.
column2: 潘妮洛普，我正在盡全力擺平那群討厭的暴衝蝸牛。

column1: You know I'm right behind you, Frederick. I'd help you if I didn't have to look after the children.
column2: 你知道我永遠支持你，佛萊迪。要不是得看著孩子們，我一定會去幫你。

column1: That's okay, Penelope, I'm on the job!
column2: 沒關係，潘妮洛普，這事包在我身上！

column1: Thank you, Frederick. We're all depending on you!
column2: 謝謝你，佛萊迪。大家都靠你了！

column1: Oh, Penelope...
column2: 噢，潘妮洛普……

column1: She ignores you. Looks like Penelope's headed inside the school for a while; maybe you can catch her on the way out.
column2: 她沒理你。看樣子潘妮洛普要進校舍待一會兒；也許等她出來時你能逮到她。

column1: It's only natural to want to speak to Penelope. But wait 'til she's out here and paying attention.
column2: 想找潘妮洛普說話也是人之常情。但得等她出來、注意到你才行。

column1: Empty can of beans?
column2: 空的豆子罐頭？

column1: No, but thank you for asking!
column2: 不用了，謝謝你問起！

column1: You're most welcome.
column2: 不客氣。

column1: Care for a sip?
column2: 要不要喝一口？

column1: No, thank you, Frederick. Beer is the opiate of the masses, I always say.
column2: 不用了，謝謝，佛萊迪。我常說，啤酒就是大眾的鴉片。

column1: This isn't beer, it's water.
column2: 這不是啤酒，是水。

column1: Tsk, tsk. Lying about your drinking is the first sign of addiction.
column2: 嘖嘖。對自己喝酒說謊，正是上癮的第一個徵兆。

column1: I'm not lying.
column2: 我沒說謊。

column1: Uh-oh, denial. That's the second sign.
column2: 噢喔，否認。這是第二個徵兆。

column1: Look, it's only water, I swear! Here, I'll drink it myself!
column2: 妳看，這真的只是水，我發誓！來，我自己喝給妳看！

column1: No, don't do it! Drinking by yourself is the third sign! Frederick, you really ought to get some help for this problem.
column2: 不，別這樣！獨自喝酒正是第三個徵兆！佛萊迪，你真的該找人幫幫你這個毛病了。

column1: Penelope, see how I've put this illegible prescription under the whisky glass? Now I can see what Doc Gillespie was writing!
column2: 潘妮洛普，妳看我把這張看不清的處方箋放到威士忌杯底下？這樣我就能看清吉勒斯比大夫寫了什麼了！

column1: That's excellent, Frederick! I do hope you got a good deal of points for that.
column2: 太棒了，佛萊迪！希望你因此拿到不少分數。

column1: What's this?
column2: 這是什麼？

column1: Doc Gillespie's whisky glass.
column2: 吉勒斯比大夫的威士忌杯。

column1: Frederick, you are a dear, sweet man, and I am growing more fond of you each day.
column2: 佛萊迪，你真是個貼心又善良的人，我一天比一天更喜歡你了。

column1: But I don't think that taking away his glass is going to keep that poor, sad old man from drinking. He'll just find another one somewhere.
column2: 不過我不認為拿走他的杯子，就能讓那可憐悲傷的老人戒酒。他只會再找一個杯子罷了。

column1: You're right, as always. But it was worth a try.
column2: 妳說得對，一如往常。不過總是值得一試。

column1: You are so very noble, Frederick!
column2: 你真是太高尚了，佛萊迪！

column1: Leave the roof on the schoolhouse. It's doing such a bang-up job of keeping meteorites from hitting Penelope and the schoolkids.
column2: 校舍的屋頂就別動了。它可是盡忠職守，擋著隕石不讓它砸到潘妮洛普和孩子們呢。

column1: But, there are no meteorites anywhere around here!
column2: 可是，這附近根本沒有隕石啊！

column1: See? It's working!
column2: 看吧？很有效呢！

column1: The schoolhouse roof is steeply-pitched.
column2: 校舍的屋頂坡度很陡。

column1: Sorry, you'll have to leave the scenery right where it is.
column2: 抱歉，這片景致你得留在原地，不能動。

column1: This is the corner of Main and Edukashun Street. The assay office and the schoolhouse are on the west and east sides of the street, respectively; clutter prevents your passage to the south.
column2: 這裡是大街和教育街的轉角。驗金所和校舍分別在街道的西側和東側；南邊則被雜物擋住，過不去。

column1: If you dug here, some little schoolchild would be liable to trip and break his neck!
column2: 你要是在這裡挖洞，說不定會害哪個小朋友摔斷脖子！

column1: You simply have nothing to say to that.
column2: 你對此無話可說。

column1: Keep your hands off the kids! They're Penelope's responsibility!
column2: 別對孩子們動手動腳！他們是潘妮洛普負責的！

column1: This girl's got her hands full with that jumprope.
column2: 這女孩正忙著跳繩，一刻都不得閒。

column1: It's Weebix, one of the little orphan girls.
column2: 這是薇比克絲，孤兒院的小女孩之一。

column1: Hello, Weebix! How are you this morning?
column2: 妳好，薇比克絲！今天早上好嗎？

column1: She pointedly stares away from you, counting to herself and looking just a bit peeved.
column2: 她故意把頭撇開，自顧自地數著數，看起來有點不高興。

column1: One, five, nine, three, four, seven, two, six... heh, heh, heh! I've confused you now, haven't I?
column2: 一、五、九、三、四、七、二、六……嘿嘿嘿！這下把你搞糊塗了吧？

column1: Weebix's eyes get very large and well up with tears. She sets her jaw firmly and keeps jumping... starting with "one." You are not proud of yourself!
column2: 薇比克絲瞪大了眼睛，眼眶泛淚。她咬緊牙關繼續跳繩……重新從「一」數起。你一點都不覺得光榮！

column1: Hey, be careful! It IS a solidly-built structure compared to most of the buildings around here, but that's not saying much.
column2: 嘿，小心點！比起這附近大多數建築，它算是蓋得挺紮實的了，不過那也沒什麼好比的。

column1: This is the old red schoolhouse, one of the few buildings that still seems solid and safe.
column2: 這是那間老舊的紅色校舍，是這裡少數幾棟看起來還算堅固安全的建築物之一。

column1: You've teetered enough.
column2: 你已經搖搖晃晃夠久了。

column1: Of course you want to play on the children's equipment, don't you? But shouldn't you put out the fire first?
column2: 你當然想去玩孩子們的遊樂器材吧？不過你是不是該先把火撲滅？

column1: You can't play now.
column2: 現在還不能玩。

column1: You're going to play on the seesaw, when the whole town is about to be gassed? I think not.
column2: 全鎮都快被毒氣籠罩了，你還想玩蹺蹺板？我看不必了。

column1: You're not quite skillful enough to make a perfect three-point landing from the swing to the seesaw without breaking every bone in your body. (In other words, try it and you'll be the man with the flopping trapezium!)
column2: 你的身手還沒好到能從鞦韆完美三點著地跳上蹺蹺板，還全身骨頭完好無缺。（換句話說，你敢試，骨頭就等著散架！）

column1: You've got no reason to put that particular item on the seesaw.
column2: 沒理由把那東西放上蹺蹺板。

column1: It's a long plank firmly attached to some sort of axle, allowing one side to pivot upwards while the other side descends. When kids play on it, one of them teeters at the top and the other totters at the bottom. Say, you've got an idea for what you could call this thing...
column2: 這是一塊長木板，牢牢固定在某種軸心上，一邊翹起、另一邊就會下沉。小孩玩的時候，一個在上頭搖搖晃晃，一個在下頭顛顛簸簸。說起來，你倒是想到該幫這東西取什麼名字了……

column1: (JUBILANTLY) A "kiddie-pult!"
column2: （興高采烈）一台「投童機」！

column1: The seesaw and the whole playground is deserted, no doubt because of the aroma. Funny, considering how infrequently the kids around here bathe, you wouldn't think they'd have noticed the horsey smell!
column2: 蹺蹺板跟整座遊樂場都空無一人，八成是因為那股臭味。說也奇怪，這裡的小孩本來就難得洗澡，你還以為他們根本聞不出馬騷味呢！

column1: Sissy is in a foul mood. He'll bite your finger clean off.
column2: 娘娘腔心情很差，會把你的手指整根咬斷。

column1: The child's sullen stare prevents you from attempting to interact in a constructive way.
column2: 這孩子陰沉的眼神讓你打消了跟他好好互動的念頭。

column1: It's Sissy, playing on the slide! The boys call him that because his mother dresses him so effeminately!)
column2: 是娘娘腔，在溜滑梯玩呢！男孩們這樣叫他，是因為他媽把他打扮得太娘了！)

column1: Hello, Sissy. My, your golden locks are looking pretty today!
column2: 你好啊，娘娘腔。哎呀，你今天的金髮真好看！

column1: Sissy glares at you with a look that says, "I know 1,000 ways to cause pain to a human body. You wanna start counting?"
column2: 娘娘腔狠狠瞪著你，那眼神彷彿在說：「我知道一千種讓人吃苦頭的方法，你要不要開始數？」

column1: After you went to all the trouble of stealing the ladder, now you want to try and redeem yourself by putting it back? Too late!
column2: 你好不容易把梯子偷來，現在想放回去贖罪？太遲了！

column1: Kids climb to the top of this long curved plank and then slide down. Geez, ain't technology wonderful?
column2: 小孩爬上這塊長長的彎木板頂端，然後溜下來。天啊，科技真是了不起，是吧？

column1: It's not polite to point at the street.
column2: 對著街道指指點點不太禮貌。

column1: It's Edukashun Lane. Which reminds you of a little joke. What does the "N" on the Nebraska Cornhuskers helmet stand for? Knowledge!
column2: 那是「教育巷」（原文故意拼錯成 Edukashun）。這讓你想起一個冷笑話：內布拉斯加玉米剝殼隊(Cornhuskers)頭盔上的「N」代表什麼？知識(Knowledge)！

column1: You've swung enough.
column2: 鞦韆盪夠了。

column1: The swing is in use.
column2: 鞦韆有人在用。

column1: Yes, the swing would let you get up a few feet in the atmosphere and perhaps escape the horrible fumes, but it wouldn't last long.
column2: 沒錯，盪鞦韆是能讓你飛高個幾呎，暫時逃離這股恐怖臭氣，但撐不了多久。

column1: It's a short plank on two ropes, hung from a tree. Another high-tech children's amusement device!
column2: 這是一塊短木板，靠兩條繩子吊在樹上。又一項高科技兒童娛樂設施！

column1: There's nobody playing on the swing right now, doubtless due to the toxic fumes.
column2: 現在沒人在盪鞦韆，八成是因為那股毒氣。

column1: You consider shimmying up the tree, but your pelvis is simply too narrow to accommodate the girth of that trunk! (A feeling not wholly unfamiliar to Madame Ovaree!)
column2: 你考慮爬上樹，但你的骨盆實在太窄，容不下那樹幹的粗細！（這種感覺，歐薇莉夫人應該不陌生！）

column1: It's either a spreading chestnut tree or a shedding sprucenut tree.
column2: 這不是枝繁葉茂的栗子樹，就是落葉紛飛的雲杉樹，搞不清楚。

column1: The windows can only be opened or closed from the inside.
column2: 這些窗戶只能從裡面開關。

column1: You can see the inside of the schoolhouse through the windows. It looks pretty much like the interior of a schoolhouse.
column2: 你能透過窗戶看到校舍內部，看起來就跟一般校舍內部差不多。

column1: This ladder is propped up against the slide so the kids can play.
column2: 這座梯子靠在溜滑梯旁，方便小孩玩耍。

column1: Good idea, Freddy! Wreck the little kids' playground equipment! You meany!
column2: 好主意啊，佛萊迪！去破壞小孩的遊樂設施吧！你這個壞心眼！

column1: Don't go poking in there; that's where the tramps hang out. If you wanna poke some tramps, go to the Brothel!
column2: 別往那裡戳，那是流浪漢聚集的地方。想戳流浪漢，去妓院找吧！

column1: The old red schoolhouse, the most solidly-built structure in town.
column2: 那間紅色老校舍，是鎮上蓋得最堅固的建築。

column1: Hey, be careful! It IS the most solidly-built structure in town, but that's not saying much.
column2: 嘿，小心點！它確實是鎮上蓋得最堅固的建築沒錯，但這也沒什麼好說嘴的。

column1: Flames jut from every loose board and hole in the old Assay Office! It must be arson! 'Cuz everything flammable in the Assay Office was stolen ages ago!
column2: 老驗金所每一塊鬆脫木板和破洞都竄出火焰！這一定是縱火！因為驗金所裡能燒的東西早就被偷光了！

column1: You're too uncoordinated to heave the baking soda AND hold onto the swing at the same time. Maybe you should practice on smaller accomplishments first... like walking and chewing tobacco at the same time!
column2: 你手腳不夠協調，沒辦法一邊抓緊鞦韆一邊丟小蘇打粉。也許你該先從小事練起……比如邊走路邊嚼菸草。

column1: Baking soda is everywhere, the result of your clever (though inadequate) solution to putting out the fire.
column2: 到處都是小蘇打粉，這是你那聰明（但不太夠力）的滅火妙計留下的成果。

column1: The piles of baking soda aren't worth picking up. But, hey, it was thrifty of you to try!
column2: 這堆小蘇打粉不值得撿。不過，嘿，你想省著點用，精神可嘉！

column1: What pluck! What prowess! What a ridiculous solution! (Still, you thought of it!)
column2: 好膽識！好本領！好荒謬的解決辦法！（不管怎樣，是你想出來的！）

column1: You singlehandedly quenched the flames of the Assay Office by using the seesaw as a catapult for the baking soda! Too bad nobody was here to see it. They'll never believe you in the morning.
column2: 你獨力用蹺蹺板當彈射器，把小蘇打粉射出去撲滅了驗金所的大火！可惜沒人在場親眼看見。明天早上講出去，誰都不會信。

column1: You've deposited your load of baking soda on one end of the teeter-totter. (Let's hope you know what you're doing!)
column2: 你把手上那堆小蘇打粉放上蹺蹺板的一端。（希望你知道自己在幹嘛！）

column1: You can't reach the baking soda from way up here!
column2: 你在這麼高的地方，根本碰不到小蘇打粉！

column1: This big ol' water tower was previously used by the train station; now it's junk.
column2: 這座老舊的大水塔以前是火車站在用的，現在只是堆廢鐵。

column1: It's dangerously rickety; you don't want to go around disturbing it. Like Ol' Doc, it'll fall over eventually anyway.
column2: 它搖搖欲墜、危險得很，你可不會想去驚動它。反正就跟老大夫一樣，遲早會倒的。

column1: You've got more important matters to attend to than pulling down this old wreck of a water tower!
column2: 你還有更重要的事要辦，沒空拆這座破水塔！

column1: There's no need to lasso the water tower; you'll yank it right down!
column2: 沒必要用套索套水塔，你會把它整座扯倒的！

column1: Over yonder is the Old Abandoned Miner's Commissary, where the miners used to eat before the mine closed down. Of course, the food over there is as fresh now as the day it was made!
column2: 那邊是廢棄礦工福利社，礦坑關閉前礦工們都在那裡用餐。當然，那裡的食物到現在還跟做好那天一樣「新鮮」！

column1: You can't possibly reach that house from here.
column2: 你不可能從這裡碰到那間房子。

column1: (SING BADLY) It's the last train to Coarsegold, and it's sunken at the station.
column2: （五音不全地唱）這是開往粗金鎮的末班車，如今已沉沒在車站裡。

column1: I |c2|thought|c| I could, I |c2|thought|c| I could, I |c2|thought|c| I could...
column2: 「我|c2|以為|c|我可以，我|c2|以為|c|我可以，我|c2|以為|c|我可以……」

column1: You don't feel like taking the train right now! (And you can't get over to it, nohow.)
column2: 你現在沒興致搭火車！（反正你也沒辦法過去啦。）

column1: This is the thick, bubbly, foul dark water that seems to be oozing from the ground all through town and creating nothing but a messy problem for the townsfolk.
column2: 這是那種又濃又冒泡的惡臭黑水，似乎從鎮上到處的地底滲出來，只為鎮民添了一堆麻煩。

column1: You don't want to touch it. It gets all over everything, smells bad, and won't come off.
column2: 你不會想碰它的。沾到哪都是，臭得要命，又洗不掉。

column1: Why not just walk on out there to the middle of the swamp and give it a try?
column2: 何不乾脆走到沼澤中央試試看？

column1: Main Street comes to an end here in the thick, mucky swamp; beyond it lies the Old Abandoned Mine.
column2: 大街到這裡就沒入濃稠泥濘的沼澤，再過去便是那座廢棄礦坑。

column1: Your words bounce over the swamp and echo into nothingness.
column2: 你的話音掠過沼澤，回盪一陣後便消散無蹤。

column1: You leave that right where it is, ya young whippersnapper!
column2: 你把那東西原封不動放著，小屁孩！

column1: That would be like trying to dig up mud.
column2: 那就跟想挖泥巴沒兩樣。

column1: That's the Old Abandoned Mine, once run by the Old Abandoned Mine Company, Inc. You remember blowing it up in the demo! (It was Coarsegold's original "'Ore House!")
column2: 那是廢棄礦坑，以前由「廢棄礦業股份有限公司」經營。你還記得在試玩版裡把它炸掉的事！（那可是粗金鎮原本的「礦」業重鎮！）

column1: You can't take it, it's not yours! Besides, there's no way over to the mine anymore, what with the swamp getting wider, thicker and deeper all the time.
column2: 你不能拿，那不是你的東西！再說，現在也沒辦法過去礦坑了，沼澤越來越寬、越來越稠、越來越深。

column1: This tree isn't doing too well, what with its roots soaking up all that mucky swampwater.
column2: 這棵樹長得不太好，畢竟樹根整天泡在那些泥濘的沼澤水裡。

column1: It feels solid on the outside. (But it's retching on the inside!)
column2: 摸起來外表挺結實。（但內心正翻騰作嘔呢！）

column1: Could I have misjudged the surface tension?
column2: 難道是我錯估了表面張力？

column1: The swamp seems thick enough to hold your weight!
column2: 這沼澤看起來夠濃稠，撐得住你的體重！

column1: Some unhealthy-looking scrub grows in the area.
column2: 這一帶長著一些看起來病懨懨的灌木叢。

column1: You've got no use for these sickly shrubs.
column2: 這些病懨懨的灌木，你派不上用場。

column1: The shrubs here by the swamp are particularly sad-looking.
column2: 沼澤邊這些灌木叢，長得特別可憐。

column1: You don't want to be carrying around any sickly plants.
column2: 你不會想隨身帶著這些病懨懨的植物。

column1: You remember a time, not too long ago, when these leaves were glossy and healthy.
column2: 你還記得不久之前，這些葉子曾經油亮又健康。

column1: The leaves are far out of reach, along with everything else on the far side of the swamp.
column2: 這些葉子遠在沼澤對岸，跟其他東西一樣搆不著。

column1: The tree leaves here are dying and diseased.
column2: 這裡的樹葉正在枯萎、生著病。

column1: You wouldn't want those leaves even if you could reach 'em.
column2: 就算搆得到那些葉子，你也不會想要。

column1: The Old Abandoned Mine Office is no longer used. But it's still fondly remembered!
column2: 廢棄礦坑辦公室早就沒人用了。但大家仍懷念著它！

column1: The Old Abandoned Mine Office is too far away to reach.
column2: 廢棄礦坑辦公室太遠了，搆不著。

column1: These old mining car tracks are rusted and beyond their useful lives.
column2: 這些老舊的礦車軌道早已鏽蝕，壽命也到頭了。

column1: You can't reach those tracks from this side of the swamp!
column2: 從沼澤這一側，你搆不到那些軌道！

column1: Something awful and fetid is bubbling up in great big blurps from the murky depths of the swamp.
column2: 從沼澤幽暗的深處，冒出一團團惡臭難聞的大氣泡。

column1: Yuck! Your skin crawls at the very thought.
column2: 噁！光是想到就讓你渾身起雞皮疙瘩。

column1: Chances are you'll need that. Don't be tossing it into the swamp.
column2: 你八成用得到那東西，別把它丟進沼澤裡。

column1: Why not just walk on out there to the bubbles and try to do some digging?
column2: 何不乾脆走到那些氣泡那裡，試著挖挖看？

column1: This is the west end of Bluff Street, which runs parallel to Main Street. Collier Bluff sweeps across the north side the street here; beyond it stretches the great painted desert. But you can't get there from here! (In fact, you can't get there from anywhere.)
column2: 這裡是斷崖街西端，與大街平行。柯利爾斷崖橫亙街道北側，再過去便是遼闊的彩繪沙漠。但你沒辦法從這裡過去！（其實，你從哪裡都到不了那裡。）

column1: You start to say something to that, but think better of it.
column2: 你正想開口說些什麼，但轉念作罷。

column1: Bluff Street is just a little too large to take with you.
column2: 斷崖街這條路，你可沒辦法打包帶走。

column1: The ground here is too hard for digging.
column2: 這裡的地面太硬了，挖不動。

column1: The trees of Coarsegold, like the citizens, grow gnarled and bent.
column2: 粗金鎮的樹，跟鎮民一樣，長得歪七扭八。

column1: These branches are high out of reach. It's a perspective thing.
column2: 這些樹枝高得搆不著，這是透視角度的問題。

column1: That's Hyman Untertaekker's shop. He's the town undertaker.
column2: 那是海曼·安德泰克的店。他是鎮上的殯葬業者。

column1: The place appears to be locked and shuttered. Come to think of it, you haven't seen Hyman in a couple of days. Ordinarily, that would be suspicious. But given what's been happening in town lately, it seems pretty normal.
column2: 這地方看起來門窗緊鎖。仔細想想，你已經好幾天沒看到海曼了。照理說這很可疑，但看看鎮上最近發生的種種怪事，這其實還算正常。

column1: High in the sky stands the town gallows. (Ernest & Julio GallowsO4 Brand Lynching Equipment: "We will hang no man before his time.")
column2: 高聳入天的是鎮上的絞刑架。（「歐內斯特與胡里奧」牌私刑器材：「我們絕不提早吊死任何人。」）

column1: It's Temple Beth-Gesundheit.
column2: 這是「貝斯健康」猶太會堂。

column1: The Synagogue is closed. There are no Jews in Coarsegold, there never were. But the building contractor and the architect sure had fun scaring the folks of Coarsegold!
column2: 這座猶太會堂沒有開放。粗金鎮從來沒有猶太人，一個也沒有。不過建商跟建築師倒是拿這件事把鎮民唬得一愣一愣，玩得挺開心！

column1: An Old Abandoned shack stands by the alleyway between Bluff and Main Streets.
column2: 斷崖街與大街之間的巷弄旁，立著一間廢棄小屋。

column1: Hands off, this property belongs to the Old Abandoned Company.
column2: 手拿開，這是「廢棄公司」的財產。

column1: The sign says "Hyman Untertaekker... Und You're Not!"
column2: 招牌寫著：「海曼·安德泰克……你可不是（死人）！」

column1: If you're looking for a sign, maybe you should play one of those Bible Trivia games.
column2: 你要是在等什麼「啟示」，或許該去玩那種聖經問答遊戲。

column1: They started to build an outhouse here, but municipal funds ran out during construction. So the builder did a half-assed job!
column2: 他們本來要在這裡蓋一間戶外茅廁，但蓋到一半市府經費用完了。所以建商只做了半調子！

column1: It seems unusually wobbly, even for an outhouse.
column2: 就算是茅廁，這棟也搖得太誇張了。

column1: The tall stone fenceposts are pebbled and worn from years of rain, wind and tourists.
column2: 這些高聳的石頭籬柱，經年累月被風吹雨打、遊客摸來摸去，表面坑坑疤疤。

column1: The fenceposts feel pebbled and rough from years of wind, rain and tourists. Of course, you could have known THAT just by looking at them!
column2: 摸起來這些籬柱坑坑疤疤又粗糙，那是多年風吹雨打加遊客把玩的痕跡。當然啦，這種事光用看的你也知道！

column1: That's a Shears Craftsperson Graveyard-Quality Shovel standing in the dirt.
column2: 那是一把插在土裡的「席爾斯工匠墓園級」鏟子。

column1: You consider doing your crooning routine, using the shovel as a mike stand. But hey, where's the audience?
column2: 你考慮來一段深情獻唱，把鏟子當麥克風架用。但是，嘿，觀眾在哪呢？

column1: Glancing furtively around to see if Doug's within sight, you grab his shovel.
column2: 你偷偷張望四周，確認道格不在附近後，抓起了他的鏟子。

column1: You can't reach the shovel from out here.
column2: 你在這裡搆不到那把鏟子。

column1: There's a recently-filled grave in ReBoot Hill.
column2: 「重啟山莊」裡有座剛填好土的新墳。

column1: It's bad enough that you want to take dirt from someone's grave... but do you have to do it with your bare hands, too?
column2: 你想從別人墳墓上挖土已經夠糟了……難道還非得徒手挖不可？

column1: You don't need any more clay from the grave.
column2: 你不需要再從墳墓挖更多黏土了。

column1: You can't reach the grave from this side of the fence.
column2: 從籬笆這一側，你搆不到那座墳墓。

column1: You start to dig up the freshly-laid grave. Muscles that haven't been used in years begin to groan and whine. But with the gritty determination of a professional grave-robber, you toil on... and on... and on...
column2: 你開始挖掘這座新墳。多年沒用過的肌肉開始又痠又痛。但你憑著職業盜墓者的堅毅精神，不斷挖著……挖著……挖著……

column1: You can't dig up the grave from here!
column2: 你在這裡沒辦法挖那座墳墓！

column1: Finally, after digging for what seems to be hours (but through the miracle of computer animation, only takes YOU a few seconds), you uncover the casket of... your ol' buddy Phil Graves! You open up the casket and take a look.
column2: 終於，挖了彷彿好幾個鐘頭（但多虧電腦動畫的神奇魔力，你其實只花了幾秒鐘），你挖出了一具棺材……裡頭躺的正是你的老朋友菲爾·格雷夫斯！你打開棺材看了一眼。

column1: Y'know, most people can't carry off this "rigor mortis" thing and still look stylish and relaxed. But Phil wears it really well.
column2: 你知道嗎，大部分人搞不定「屍僵」這回事，還能看起來時髦又放鬆。但菲爾穿起這身「行頭」倒是挺合適。

column1: Doug McCarkus, the town's lone gravedigger, performs his sad, solitary task at graveside. (If you listen close, you can hear him muttering something about Union rules.)
column2: 道格·麥卡克斯，鎮上唯一的掘墓人，獨自在墓旁埋頭做著這件悲傷的差事。（仔細聽，還能聽見他喃喃唸著工會規定什麼的。）

column1: Hey, Doug, you big lug! How's it going?
column2: 嘿，道格，你這個大塊頭！最近怎樣啊？

column1: Doug shrugs.
column2: 道格聳了聳肩。

column1: Don't bug Doug 'til his digging's dug.
column2: 道格還沒挖完之前，別去煩他。

column1: It's a pile of rich, reddish dirt from the grave. (In fact, it's more clay than dirt, which explains all the lush growth around here!)
column2: 這是一堆從墳墓挖出來、肥沃的紅褐色土。（其實與其說是土，不如說是黏土，難怪這一帶長得這麼茂盛！）

column1: You grab a handful of clay from the pile beside the grave. (Well, you never know, it COULD come in handy.)
column2: 你從墳墓旁的土堆抓了一把黏土。（誰知道呢，說不定用得到。）

column1: You can't reach that pile of dirt from here.
column2: 從這裡搆不到那堆土。

column1: You've already got enough clay for one game.
column2: 這局遊戲裡，你手上的黏土已經夠用了。

column1: You've taken your clay; now lie in it.
column2: 黏土你拿了，現在就躺在裡頭吧。

column1: It's an open grave. Even a world-weary, seen-it-all Pharmacist like yourself, one who deals with cold sores, headaches, and diarrhea on a daily basis, still can't shake that uneasy feeling one gets when standing close to Death.
column2: 這是一座敞開的墳墓。就算是你這種見多識廣、看破紅塵的藥劑師，天天處理唇皰疹、頭痛、拉肚子這些小毛病，站在死亡旁邊，還是會有股揮之不去的不安。

column1: What are you looking for, gold fillings? C'mon, you've defiled Phil Graves' unfilled grave enough already!
column2: 你在找什麼，金牙填充物嗎？得了吧，你褻瀆菲爾·格雷夫斯這座還沒填土的墳墓，次數也夠多了！

column1: You carefully search through the many pockets of Graves's three-dollar suit, until you discover... the safe deposit box key you entrusted to Phil oh so many years ago!
column2: 你仔細翻遍格雷夫斯那套三塊錢西裝的每個口袋，終於發現……多年前你託付給菲爾保管的保險箱鑰匙！

column1: You can't reach the open grave from here.
column2: 從這裡搆不到那座敞開的墳墓。

column1: That's okay, you just keep that key. Phil doesn't need it back.
column2: 沒關係，鑰匙你留著就好。菲爾不需要拿回去了。

column1: In a touching display of emotion (and a hidden desire to carry a little less around with you), you fold up Philip's letter and place it under his folded hands.
column2: 你動情地（其實也是想少帶點東西在身上）把菲利普的信摺好，放進他交疊的雙手底下。

column1: I guess this makes Phil a correspondence corpse!
column2: 這樣看來，菲爾也算是個「通信」屍體了吧！

column1: You begin the arduous task of replacing the heaping mound of dirt, one shovelful at a time... over... and over... and over...
column2: 你開始吃力地把那堆土一鏟一鏟填回去……一次……又一次……又一次……

column1: You can't use the shovel on the grave from out here.
column2: 從這裡沒辦法拿鏟子填那座墳墓。

column1: Finally, after what seems like only a few seconds (but which, through the miracle of good programming, actually takes you several hours), you carefully fill up Philip's grave!
column2: 終於，感覺上只過了幾秒鐘（但多虧優良程式設計的神奇魔力，其實花了你好幾個鐘頭），你仔細把菲利普的墳墓填好了！

column1: A noose swings lazily in the breeze... always a gloomy sign.
column2: 一條絞繩隨風懶洋洋地搖曳……向來不是什麼好兆頭。

column1: You know what I always say... "No noose is good noose!"
column2: 你知道我常說什麼……「沒有絞繩才是好消息！」

column1: Hey, what's noose? How's it hangin'?
column2: 嘿，絞繩，最近怎樣？吊得還好嗎？

column1: The noose seems to say, "Knot too well. Can't talk now, I'm all tied up!"
column2: 絞繩彷彿在說：「不太『結』實。現在沒空講話，我可是被綁得死死的！」

column1: But it's knot within reach!
column2: 但它「結」果搆不著！

column1: A rickety old fence stands by Collier Bluff, ready to fall down at any second.
column2: 柯利爾斷崖旁立著一道搖搖欲墜的老籬笆，隨時都可能倒塌。

column1: You give it a shake, and the whole length of fence quivers. Dry rot and bullet holes have sapped the wood of its strength.
column2: 你搖了一下，整道籬笆都跟著顫抖起來。木頭朽壞加上彈孔累累，早就沒了強度。

column1: One of those bottles is full of water; drink it before you do anything else!
column2: 那些瓶子裡有一瓶裝滿了水；做別的事之前，先把它喝了吧！

column1: There's no point in setting up target practice until you're ready to start shooting!
column2: 你都還沒準備好開槍，擺靶練習根本沒意義！

column1: You can't reach the fence from here. But keep stretching; you'll add inches to your biceps and tone those lateral obliques!
column2: 從這裡搆不到籬笆。不過繼續伸展也好，能練壯你的二頭肌，順便雕塑一下腹外斜肌！

column1: Srini's waiting for you to start your target practice.
column2: 斯里尼正等你開始練靶呢。

column1: From here, it looks like Srini, your faithful Indian sidekick!
column2: 從這裡看過去，那是斯里尼，你忠實的印度裔夥伴！

column1: Srini is patiently waiting for you to get your gunslingin' outfit together.
column2: 斯里尼耐心等著你把槍手行頭準備齊全。

column1: Welp, Srini, I think I'm ready to try some target-shooting. You ready?
column2: 好啦，斯里尼，我想我準備好要練靶了。你呢？

column1: Of certainly. I am without a desire to wait any further for to stand in front of your blazing guns and take my life in your hands to help you perfect your shooting.
column2: 那是自然。我毫無意願再多等一刻，好站到你那把火熱的槍口前，把自己的性命交到你手上，助你練就完美槍法。

column1: How do you wanna start?
column2: 你想怎麼開始？

column1: Perhaps it would be besting if you placed some targets upon the fenceposts, for a commencement.
column2: 或許，作為開端，將靶子安放於籬柱之上，乃是較佳之選。

column1: Don't yell from here. You'll wake the dead!
column2: 別在這裡大吼大叫，你會把死人都吵醒的！

column1: Srini, what are you waiting for?
column2: 斯里尼，你在等什麼？

column1: You! The soonest you can arrange a disguisement of your right ear, and complete an outfit most befitting of a gunslinging-type person, the soonest we can get you dressed!
column2: 你啊！你越早把右耳的偽裝安排妥當，把最適合槍手身分的行頭備齊，我們就能越早把你打扮好！

column1: Close physical contact between men is frowned upon in your country, is it not?
column2: 在你的國家，男人之間的親密肢體接觸是不被允許的，對吧？

column1: I guess so.
column2: 我想是吧。

column1: Good! Please to keeping it thusly.
column2: 很好！還請如此保持下去。

column1: You can't poke Srini from here!
column2: 你在這裡沒辦法戳斯里尼！

column1: You'll have to get closer to him.
column2: 你得靠他近一點才行。

column1: Those bottles would be making excellent target practice targets, Freddy! If it were not for the filling of water in one of them. Drink up!
column2: 佛萊迪，那些瓶子拿來當練靶靶子再好不過了！只可惜其中一瓶裝滿了水。喝了它吧！

column1: In my country, we have struggled for years to learn to do without the need for ice picks.
column2: 在我的國家，我們花了多年苦心鑽研，學會不需要鑿冰錐也能過活。

column1: Provided you are prepared to practice shooting, set the bottles upon the fenceposts and we can commence to begin starting!
column2: 只要你準備好練習射擊，就把瓶子放上籬柱，我們便可以著手開始起頭了！

column1: You are a most fortunate individual to be holding keys. I struggle much of my life to find keys.
column2: 你能握有鑰匙，實在是個幸運至極之人。我這輩子多半的時間都在苦苦尋覓鑰匙。

column1: Srini, my boy, you just have to know where to click.
column2: 斯里尼老弟，你只需要知道該點在哪裡。

column1: You do? Humph and humph! I have never thought of clicking!
column2: 是嗎？哼哼！我從未想過「點擊」這回事！

column1: The ladder that saved my life! I remember it finely!
column2: 那座救了我一命的梯子！我記得可清楚了！

column1: Are these for keepsies?
column2: 這些是要送我的嗎？

column1: Um... I was just showing them to you.
column2: 呃……我只是拿給你看看而已。

column1: I do not want them. Your American women are too skinny as it is.
column2: 我不需要那些。你們美國女人本來就已經太瘦了。

column1: Do not threaten me, Freddy Pharkas! I am working out as well as I am!
column2: 別威脅我，佛萊迪·法卡斯！我這身鍛鍊可不是蓋的！

column1: I am dodging too fast for you to see. That is the way of my people.
column2: 我閃躲的速度快得你看不見。這是我族人的方式。

column1: Ah, apple pie. I look at it and can think only of the screams of thousands of apples dying for your pie. I do not understand how a thinking person can partake of it. But I love us both for our differences.
column2: 啊，蘋果派。看著它，我只能想到成千上萬顆蘋果為了這塊派犧牲時的哀嚎。我不明白一個有思想的人怎麼能夠享用它。但我倆的差異，正是我喜愛之處。

column1: I prefer Golden Shower Herbal Tea. I like mine tepid... with a twist!
column2: 我比較喜歡「金雨」花草茶。我喜歡溫溫的……再加點花樣！

column1: Ooh, you keep that now, Freddy Pharkas. You can be using it to ensure guns are clean enough to use with impunity.
column2: 喔，你留著那個吧，佛萊迪·法卡斯。你可以用它確保槍枝夠乾淨，用起來才不會出岔子。

column1: They appear as though to be most effective, they are having to be propelled with much force from a firing chamber!
column2: 這些東西看來效果十足，得靠槍膛使勁的力道才能發射出去！

column1: Oh! You have clay! Now you are really the hero I thought you were!
column2: 喔！你有黏土了！現在你真的是我心目中的英雄了！

column1: That is a most handsome and clever use of my medallion! Now all you need is other things for your disguise.
column2: 這真是巧妙又體面地運用了我的勳章！現在你只需要其他東西來完成偽裝了。

column1: What else do I need?
column2: 我還需要什麼？

column1: I believe you should have something different than your current shoes, something other than your current clothes, loaded and cleaned pistols, and something for good luck! Then wear your ear, and I will know you are ready to be all dressed up like a big cowboy!
column2: 我認為你該換雙不同的鞋、換套不同的衣服、備妥上膛清潔好的手槍，還要有個帶來好運的東西！接著戴上你的耳朵，我就知道你已經打扮妥當，像個道地的西部牛仔了！

column1: You keep those, Freddy Pharkas! They can help make you look like a real Western Hero!
column2: 這些你留著吧，佛萊迪·法卡斯！它們能幫你看起來像個真正的西部英雄！

column1: As, yes! It will be ready on Tuesday! Hee hee hee. I have made a funny. Excuse my jocularity. I do not know whence this piece of paper comes.
column2: 啊，對！星期二就會好了！嘻嘻嘻。我開了個玩笑。請見諒我的詼諧。我也不知道這張紙是打哪來的。

column1: Yes, they are truly boots worthy of a Western Hero! May you have an opportunity to wear them with pridefulness.
column2: 沒錯，這雙靴子真是配得上西部英雄！願你有機會自豪地穿上它們。

column1: I do not recognize it, but it is a handsome addition to any wardrobe.
column2: 我不認得這東西，但它絕對是衣櫃裡體面的一員。

column1: This is your personal mail. I am not reading it now or ever!
column2: 這是你的私人信件。我現在不看，以後也不看！

column1: You are walking around with a shovel. Surely that is unusual.
column2: 你扛著一把鏟子到處走。這肯定不太尋常。

column1: That Freddy Pharkas! I never know what to expect from you yet!
column2: 那個佛萊迪·法卡斯啊！我永遠猜不透你下一步要幹嘛！

column1: I am full up of that. But thanks to you anyway.
column2: 那個我已經吃很飽了。不過還是謝謝你。

column1: You are a lost-wax casting fool, Freddy Pharkas! Ways to go!
column2: 佛萊迪·法卡斯，你真是個脫蠟鑄造狂！厲害！

column1: That appears most empty! Perhaps it needs to be filled with a substance that will make an impressive ear!
column2: 這看起來空得很啊！或許得填點什麼進去，才能做出一隻像樣的耳朵！

column1: That is a most beautiful likeness! But it is of your left ear. You need one of your right ear.
column2: 這雕得維妙維肖！不過雕的是你的左耳。你要的可是右耳啊。

column1: WHAT??
column2: 什麼？？

column1: Haha, I am pulling down your pants! You have carved correctly!
column2: 哈哈，我是在唬你的啦！你雕得完全正確！

column1: The door to the outhouse is the only part they got right! The rest of it is a real half-assed job!
column2: 茅房的門是他們唯一做對的地方！其餘的根本是隨便亂搞！

column1: You can't get to the outhouse from inside the cemetery!
column2: 你沒辦法從墓園裡走到茅房！

column1: Say, Freddy Pharkas! You are not so bad after all at this shooting gig!
column2: 說真的，佛萊迪·法卡斯！你這身槍法還真不賴嘛！

column1: Why, thanks, Srini. My life -- and the lives of every man, woman, and ruminant in this town -- depend on my being quick with a gun.
column2: 哎，謝了，斯里尼。我的命——還有這鎮上每個男人、女人和反芻動物的命——都得靠我槍快才保得住。

column1: Did you not mention earlier that your life is in danger most forthcoming?
column2: 你方才不是才提過，你的性命正面臨迫在眉睫的危險嗎？

column1: Something like that.
column2: 差不多是那樣。

column1: Might I then suggest that you might be excellent to placing a disguise upon your person, thereby making it to appearances that Freddy Pharkas has no longer around in this locality?
column2: 那麼容我建議，不妨在您身上加些偽裝，如此一來便能造成佛萊迪·法卡斯已不在此地的假象？

column1: Good thinking, Srini. I'll need a disguise of some sort; something that will strike terror into the hearts of the bad guys.
column2: 好主意，斯里尼。我需要某種偽裝；能讓壞人心生恐懼的那種。

column1: I know, a BAT! I'll disguise myself as a bat, and you can be Srini, the Boy Wonder. Do you have any leotards?
column2: 有了，蝙蝠！我扮成蝙蝠俠，你就當神奇小子斯里尼。你有緊身衣嗎？

column1: Pardon me for asserting, but this "bat" thing is really hokey.
column2: 恕我直言，這個「蝙蝠」的點子實在有點老掉牙。

column1: You're right, too juvenile. Let's see. How about...
column2: 你說得對，太幼稚了。讓我想想。那這個如何……

column1: Might I suggest a skin-tight costume with flowing cape, and placed upon the manly chest thereof a large "F," for "Pharkas?"
column2: 容我建議一套緊身裝配上飄逸披風，再於雄壯的胸膛上繡個大大的「F」，代表「法卡斯」？

column1: No, that'd never work. I don't want people to know I'm Freddy, remember?
column2: 不行，那絕對行不通。我可不想讓人知道我是佛萊迪，記得嗎？

column1: Then perhaps you are needing to do something about that right ear. Or rather, the lack of that right ear.
column2: 那麼或許您該想想右耳的問題。正確來說，是右耳「不見了」的問題。

column1: Dang it, you're right! Everyone knows me as the one-eared Pharmacist. I need to make a new one somehow... maybe forge one out of metal or something. I'll give it some thought and meet you back at the Pharmacy once I've completed my disguise.
column2: 該死，你說得對！大家都認得我是那個獨耳藥師。我得想辦法弄一隻新耳朵……或許用金屬打造一隻之類的。我會好好想想，等偽裝完成後在藥局跟你碰面。

column1: This is world-famous "Bad Rock," so-called because of the day many years ago that part of it dislodged and just missed a carriagefull of students on their way to Chowchilla. It was a black, black day. (Which is why they eventually turned it into a movie, "Black Day at Bad Rock.")
column2: 這就是舉世聞名的「壞岩」，得名於多年前的某一天，岩石有一部分崩落，差點砸中一車正要前往喬奇拉的學生。那是漆黑的一天。（所以後來才拍成了電影，片名叫「壞岩黑暗日」。）

column1: You can't reach it, which is a damn good thing. Otherwise you'd have the weight of the world on your shoulders!
column2: 你摸不到它，這其實是件好事。不然你可就要扛起全世界的重量了！

column1: Someone made a mesa the desert!
column2: 有人把沙漠弄得亂七八糟，還順便堆了座台地！

column1: The horizon is way off in the background. You can't reach it from here.
column2: 地平線遠在天邊的背景裡。你從這裡根本碰不到。

column1: Here Lies Eric DeUnreddie 1830-1875 He Had a Fatal Error Reading Drive B.
column2: 「長眠於此：艾瑞克·迪安瑞迪 1830-1875 讀取B磁碟機時發生了致命錯誤。」

column1: Hello down there!
column2: 喂，下面的！

column1: You think you hear some worms, trying to talk with their mouths full.
column2: 你好像聽到幾隻蟲子，滿嘴食物含糊地想說話。

column1: You're not going to do any gravestone-tipping in THIS game, buster!
column2: 老兄，在這款遊戲裡你可別想推倒墓碑搞破壞！

column1: Here lies Les Moanly. He died with his shrinkwrap still on. 1861-1883
column2: 「長眠於此：雷斯·莫恩利。他死時身上的塑膠膜都還沒拆。1861-1883」

column1: Yo! Wake up and help me!
column2: 喂！醒醒，來幫幫我！

column1: You hear a disembodied voice telling you that there are no on-line hints in this game.
column2: 你聽到一個不知從哪傳來的聲音，告訴你這款遊戲沒有線上提示。

column1: The heavy gravestone is being held in place by a mysterious force! Perhaps it's "gravity."
column2: 這塊沉重的墓碑被一股神秘力量固定住了！或許那就是所謂的「地心引力」。

column1: Pardon our Dust, but Here We Grow Again! A New Grave is Being Erected on this Site in Honor of Philip D. Graves.
column2: 「施工中請見諒，我們又要擴建了！此處正為菲利普·D·格雷夫斯先生建造新墓，以茲紀念。」

column1: Looks like your dear friend Philip has passed on. Gee, it seems like only a day or two ago you filled a prescription for him.
column2: 看來你的好友菲利普已經過世了。天哪，感覺才不過一兩天前你還幫他配過藥呢。

column1: Uh, oh!
column2: 呃，糟了！

column1: Hey! Is there life after death?
column2: 喂！死後真的有來生嗎？

column1: There's no answer.
column2: 沒有回應。

column1: Should I take that as a "no"?
column2: 這樣算是「沒有」嗎？

column1: Hey, these temporary headstones are set in place real good!
column2: 嘿，這些臨時墓碑固定得真牢靠！

column1: Here Lieth James Ernest Haupher. 1824-1880
column2: 「長眠於此：詹姆士·厄尼斯特·霍佛。1824-1880」

column1: Ah-ha! You'd always wondered where Jim E. Haupher was buried!
column2: 哈！你一直很好奇吉姆·霍佛究竟葬在哪裡呢！

column1: Hey, how'd you die, anyway?
column2: 嘿，你到底是怎麼死的？

column1: A ghostly voice carries in the wind, saying, "Violently!"
column2: 風中飄來一個幽幽的聲音：「死得很慘烈！」

column1: This stone seems to be set in place with cement overshoes.
column2: 這塊墓碑看起來是用水泥鞋固定住的。

column1: Here Lies Butch Casualty. He Also Cheats, Steals, Murders, And Writes Bad Checks. 1849-1882
column2: 「長眠於此：布奇·凱舒亞提。他還會騙人、偷竊、殺人，順便開空頭支票。1849-1882」

column1: Hey, tell me something only you dead guys would know!
column2: 嘿，跟我說點只有你們死人才知道的事吧！

column1: You think you hear a muffled, faint voice saying, "Okay, you asked for it... April 23rd, in your sleep!"
column2: 你好像聽到一個模糊微弱的聲音說：「好吧，你自己要問的……四月二十三號，睡夢中死去！」

column1: Don't steal this headstone. That's the worst kind of graverobbing.
column2: 別偷這塊墓碑。那可是最惡劣的盜墓行為。

column1: Under this rock lies Ernie Fleabeak. Mere text cannot describe how he'll be missed. 1858-1886
column2: 「這塊石頭下長眠著厄尼·弗利比克。文字實在難以形容大家有多想念他。1858-1886」

column1: How's the weather down there?
column2: 下面天氣如何啊？

column1: A voice filters up: "Rottin'!"
column2: 一個聲音從下面傳來：「爛透了！」

column1: The stone wobbles slightly, but it's far too heavy to move any more than that.
column2: 這塊石頭稍微晃了一下，但實在太重，沒辦法再移動了。

column1: The stone is immoveable.
column2: 這塊石頭紋風不動。

column1: Oh, boy! It's one of those rare "Burma Shave" headstones:
column2: 哦，天哪！這是那種罕見的「Burma Shave 廣告體」墓碑：

column1: Beneath This Plot Lies Edward Fiskers. His Time Grew Short, But Not His Whiskers. Burma Shave 1845-1885
column2: 「這塊墓地下長眠著愛德華·費斯克斯。他的日子雖短，鬍子卻沒少長。Burma Shave 1845-1885」

column1: Hey! I like your gravestone!
column2: 嘿！我喜歡你的墓碑！

column1: A voice drifts up from somewhere beneath your feet, and says:
column2: 一個聲音從你腳下某處飄了上來，說道：

column1: I'm in a box That's six feet deep, So shut your mouth And let me sleep!
column2: 「我躺在六呎深的箱子裡，你給我閉嘴，讓我好好安息！」

column1: You'd give yourself A hernia, And hear from Ed's attorneya. Burma-Shave
column2: 你會把自己弄出疝氣，還會收到愛德的律師信。Burma-Shave

column1: The epitaph reads:
column2: 墓誌銘寫著：

column1: Poor Prudence Brown Was Merely Dozing. Never Woke, Now Decomposing. 1839-1880
column2: 「可憐的普魯登絲·布朗只是在打盹。從未醒來，如今已然腐化。1839-1880」

column1: Sorry to hear you're decomposing!
column2: 聽到你正在腐化，還真是遺憾！

column1: You think you hear a voice say, "Yeah, I'm all broken up about it myself!"
column2: 你好像聽到一個聲音說：「是啊，我自己也整個都散了架！」

column1: Poor Prudence Brown Would moan and groan If you attempt To steal her stone.
column2: 可憐的普魯登絲·布朗，若你膽敢偷她的墓碑，她定會呻吟哀嚎。

column1: Reboot Hill isn't very creepy. (The Coarsegold Founding Fathers Cemetary Committee couldn't afford creepy. Creepy cost extra.)
column2: 重開機丘其實沒那麼陰森。（粗金鎮開國元老墓園委員會出不起陰森的預算。陰森是要加錢的。）

column1: Leave the graveyard there. It's being used by the residents.
column2: 別把墓園拿走。這裡的「住戶」還在用呢。

column1: What makes you think there's something under THAT plot that you need?
column2: 你怎麼會覺得那塊墓地底下有你需要的東西？

column1: This grave has yet to be filled. There's nothing in it.
column2: 這座墳墓還沒下葬，裡面什麼都沒有。

column1: You can't see into the grave from this side.
column2: 你從這一側看不到墓穴裡面。

column1: You can't take an empty hole! This is REALITY!
column2: 你沒辦法把一個空洞的坑帶走！這可是「現實」！

column1: You can't reach the grave from this side of the fence!
column2: 你沒辦法從圍籬這一側碰到墳墓！

column1: A robust, healthy prickly pear cactus grows near the edge of ReBoot Hill. (Must be all the nitrogen-rich fertilizer in the local soil!)
column2: 重開機丘邊緣長著一株健壯茂盛的仙人掌。（想必是當地土壤裡富含氮肥的緣故！）

column1: Go prick on somebody your own size!
column2: 找跟你差不多大的傢伙去扎吧！

column1: Perched on top of the post is an angel, her arms outstretched. At the base of the statue is a small plaque which reads, "I love you |c3|THIS MUCH!|c|" (Couldn't you just surrender your lunch?)
column2: 柱子頂端站著一尊天使雕像，雙臂張開。雕像底座有塊小牌子寫著：「我愛你|c3|這~麼~多！|c|」（你是不是也想把午餐都吐出來了？）

column1: Teen angel, can you hear me?
column2: 小天使，你聽得到我說話嗎？

column1: If she can, she's not interested in chatting.
column2: 就算聽得到，她也沒興趣跟你聊天。

column1: You give the angel a friendly pat on the behind. She seems to glare at you. (Apparently she doesn't love you THAT much!)
column2: 你友善地拍了拍天使的屁股。她似乎狠狠瞪了你一眼。（看來她沒有愛你「那~麼~多」！）

column1: Hmmmm... not much privacy, but the ventilation is EXCELLENT!
column2: 嗯……隱私是不太夠，不過通風效果倒是一流！

column1: This is the central area of Bluff Street, which runs parallel to Main Street.
column2: 這是斷崖街的中央地帶，與大街平行。

column1: That's not one of the more talkative inanimate objects in the game.
column2: 這可不是遊戲裡比較愛講話的無生命物體。

column1: You take Bluff Street and put it in your pocket. (Sorry, just bluffing!)
column2: 你把斷崖街整條塞進口袋。（抱歉，只是唬你的啦！）

column1: You can't find a good spot to dig here.
column2: 這裡找不到適合開挖的地方。

column1: You locked it, remember?
column2: 你自己鎖上的，記得嗎？

column1: The door clearly shows the beauty of natural wood-grain finish. (In other words, it needs a coat of paint!)
column2: 這扇門清楚展現出天然木紋的美感。（換句話說，該上漆了！）

column1: This looks just like the door where you stole that church key.
column2: 這扇門看起來就跟你偷教堂鑰匙的那扇一模一樣。

column1: You can't look through the keyhole; it's blocked.
column2: 你沒辦法從鑰匙孔看進去，被擋住了。

column1: That key doesn't work in the church door.
column2: 這把鑰匙開不了教堂的門。

column1: You unlock the Church door.
column2: 你打開了教堂的門鎖。

column1: You lock the Church door.
column2: 你鎖上了教堂的門。

column1: That's the wrong key for this lock.
column2: 這把鑰匙不對，開不了這個鎖。

column1: That key doesn't seem to fit in this lock!
column2: 這把鑰匙看來插不進這個鎖！

column1: ReBoot Hill was opened in 1849. Disease and violent death were so popular back then that the cemetery plots were auctioned off at the Coarsegold Plot Exposition of '52. Ten years later, due to overcrowding, the bodies were exhumed and buried off the top of Half-Dome in Yosemite. The plots were re-auctioned off. It's been that way ever since. (Thank you for reading this plot synopsis!)
column2: 重開機丘開墓於1849年。當年疾病與暴斃盛行，墓地在52年的粗金鎮墓地博覽會上被拍賣一空。十年後，因為墓地過於擁擠，遺體被挖出，改葬到優勝美地半圓頂的山頂上。墓地又重新拍賣了一輪，從此就這麼延續至今。（謝謝你耐心讀完這段「劇情」簡介！）

column1: It feels like the life cycle begins anew here, as we go from the top of the food chain to the bottom.
column2: 這裡讓人感覺生命循環又重新開始了，我們從食物鏈的頂端一路來到了最底層。

column1: Reverend Sy Hallelujah lives here.
column2: 賽伊·哈里路亞牧師住在這裡。

column1: The Reverend's house is locked and shuttered. Has he left town? Who's running the Church?
column2: 牧師的房子門窗緊閉、上了鎖。他離開鎮上了嗎？那教堂現在是誰在打理？

column1: It's the Old Abandoned Synagogue.
column2: 這是一座廢棄已久的老猶太會堂。

column1: You can't get into the Synagogue. You're not one of the Chosen People.
column2: 你進不了這座猶太會堂。你可不是「上帝的選民」。

column1: A gnarled old tree stretches above the Old Abandoned Synagogue.
column2: 一棵盤根錯節的老樹，在廢棄的老猶太會堂上方伸展著枝椏。

column1: You can't reach the tree from down here.
column2: 你在下面碰不到這棵樹。

column1: This is the Reverend Sy Hallelujah's Church. Nobody's going in or out. What with everyone leaving town, the Reverend seems to have lost his following. Yes, he's been deflocked!
column2: 這是賽伊·哈里路亞牧師的教堂。沒人進出。隨著大家紛紛離開小鎮，牧師似乎也失去了他的信眾。沒錯，他的「羊群」都散了！

column1: The Church is feeling a little warm. Maybe it's got shingles.
column2: 這座教堂摸起來有點溫熱。或許它得了皮蛇——畢竟屋頂鋪的正是木瓦。

column1: A creaking old windmill tower, haphazardly assembled from rotting timbers, graces the beautiful Coarsegold skyline.
column2: 一座嘎吱作響的老舊風車塔，用腐朽的木材隨便拼湊而成，妝點著粗金鎮美麗的天際線。

column1: This ladder is falling apart. You'll never climb the windmill tower.
column2: 這座梯子都快散架了。你絕對爬不上風車塔。

column1: The windmill turns steadily in the arid Coarsegold trade winds.
column2: 風車在粗金鎮乾燥的信風中穩定地轉動著。

column1: I'm one of your biggest fans!
column2: 我可是你的頭號粉絲！

column1: (Now THAT'S the pot calling the kettle black!)
column2: （這真是五十步笑百步啊！）

column1: Have you ever had your hand sliced off by a propeller? Would you LIKE to? Then don't try sticking your hand in the windmill!
column2: 你的手曾經被螺旋槳削掉過嗎？你「想要」嗎？那就別把手伸進風車裡！

column1: There seems to be something in the lock! You wisely reconsider your idea of pushing on the stained glass to see if it's still in good shape.
column2: 鎖裡好像卡著什麼東西！你聰明地打消了推推彩繪玻璃、看看它還完不完好的念頭。

column1: You take the key to the Church.
column2: 你拿走了教堂的鑰匙。

column1: A wrought-iron and stone archway beckons all to ReBoot Hill. Perhaps YOU'LL be the next occupant! Bwah-ha-ha-haaa! (Are you scared yet? Huh? Huh??)
column2: 一座鍛鐵與石造的拱門，招喚著眾人前往重開機丘。或許「你」就是下一位住客！哇哈哈哈哈！（怕了嗎？嗯？嗯？？）

column1: Despite the years of wear, the archway seems solid.
column2: 儘管歷經多年風霜，這座拱門看起來依然堅固。

column1: A stagecoach converted to a hearse is mired in the mud here, minus one wheel. Once this was a one-hearse town... now it's a NO-hearse town!
column2: 一輛改裝成靈車的驛馬車陷在泥地裡，還少了一個輪子。這裡曾經是「一輛靈車鎮」……現在成了「沒有靈車鎮」！

column1: This wrecked hearse feels just like a wrecked hearse.
column2: 這輛報廢的靈車，摸起來就跟報廢的靈車一模一樣。

column1: One of Hyman Untertaekker's coffins is lying in disrepair off near ReBoot Hill. (It looks like a Cedar Model #7: "Eternal Slumber... And No Moths!")
column2: 海曼·安德塔克的一具棺材，殘破地棄置在重開機丘附近。（看起來像是雪松7號款：「永眠安息……還不怕蟲蛀！」）

column1: Hello? Anyone in there?
column2: 哈囉？裡面有人嗎？

column1: There's no answer. Apparently there's nothing in there but old jokes that have gone to die.
column2: 沒有回應。看來裡面只有一堆去世的老笑話。

column1: You rap on the coffin, but hear nothing special.
column2: 你敲了敲棺材，但沒聽到什麼特別的聲響。

column1: You attempt, but fail, to s'nail the coffin shut.
column2: 你試著把棺材釘上，但失敗了。

column1: A variety of polypetalous, green, fleshy, spiny members of the family |c3|Cactaceae|c| grow in spurts around the foundation of the Church. (Aren't you sorry you asked?)
column2: 教堂地基周圍，零星長著幾株多瓣、翠綠、多肉帶刺的|c3|仙人掌科|c|植物。（你是不是有點後悔問了？）

column1: Don't touch the cacti; you'll prick yourself.
column2: 別碰這些仙人掌，你會被刺到的。

column1: The Church door is chipped and yellowed.
column2: 教堂的門又缺角又泛黃。

column1: That reminds me... I'm supposed to have my teeth cleaned next week!
column2: 這讓我想起……我下星期該去洗牙了！

column1: Feels like wood. Smells like termites. (Don't fight, kids... it's BOTH!)
column2: 摸起來像木頭。聞起來像白蟻。（別吵了，孩子們……兩個都對！）

column1: The keyhole appears to be empty. And whose fault is THAT?
column2: 鑰匙孔看起來是空的。這又是誰的錯呢？

column1: What? You want to steal something else from the church? Haven't you committed enough sacrilege for one game?
column2: 什麼？你還想從教堂偷別的東西？這款遊戲裡你褻瀆神明還不夠多嗎？

column1: An squeaky old sheep vane turns gently on top of Reverend Hallelujah's house. Perhaps he's trying to get people to join his flock.
column2: 哈里路亞牧師家屋頂上，一座吱嘎作響的老舊羊形風向標緩緩轉動著。或許他正想拉更多人加入他的「羊群」。

column1: (SINGING) "You're so vane! I bet you think this game is about you? Don't you? Don't you?"
column2: （唱）「你這風向標真自戀！我猜你以為這遊戲是繞著你轉的吧？是不是？是不是？」

column1: You can't reach that sheep weather vane; it's way up on Sy Hallelujah's roof.
column2: 你碰不到那座羊形風向標；它高高地立在賽伊·哈里路亞的屋頂上。

column1: The Church has a belfry. (So named because somebody donated a bell!)
column2: 教堂有座鐘樓。（之所以叫鐘樓，是因為有人捐了一口鐘！）

column1: You can't reach the belfry, which is just as well since you'd disturb the bats.
column2: 你碰不到鐘樓，這樣也好，免得你去驚動裡面的蝙蝠。

column1: The candles in the Church foyer are glowing with a holy light.
column2: 教堂門廳裡的蠟燭，散發著聖潔的光芒。

column1: You would never dream of stealing a candle from a church. But... they wouldn't miss one of these puddles of candle wax.
column2: 你做夢也不會想從教堂偷走一根蠟燭。不過……少了一灘蠟油，他們應該不會發現。

column1: You've got as much wax as you'll need.
column2: 你手上的蠟已經夠用了。

column1: The stained-glass windows are, miraculously, intact.
column2: 說也神奇，這些彩繪玻璃窗竟然完好無缺。

column1: You wisely reconsider your idea of pushing on the stained glass to see if it's still in good shape.
column2: 你聰明地打消了推推彩繪玻璃、看看它還完不完好的念頭。

column1: You see some votive candles burning just inside the door.
column2: 你看到門內燃著幾根許願蠟燭。

column1: You slowly open the coffin.
column2: 你緩緩打開了棺材。

column1: <Cough!> <Hack!> <Cough!>
Say! You oughta do something about that coffin!
column2: 喂！你該對那具棺材做點什麼吧！

column1: The back door to the Barbershop is currently locked.
column2: 理髮店的後門目前鎖著。

column1: Your arms are too short to do any roofing work from down here.
column2: 你的手太短了，在下面根本沒辦法做屋頂的工程。

column1: You can see the roof of one of the Main Street buildings from here.
column2: 從這裡你可以看到大街上某棟建築的屋頂。

column1: You can't walk that way. It's too treacherous! (Of course, you can walk to lots of other too-treacherous places in the game! You just can't walk here.)
column2: 你不能走那條路。太危險了！（當然，遊戲裡還有很多同樣危險的地方你走得過去！就是這裡不行。）

column1: The bakery's closed for good.
column2: 這間麵包店已經永久歇業了。

column1: This used to be the Bakery, where Letta Rysawyle sold all sorts of delicious breads, pies, and cakes. There was a sudden surge in muffin popularity on the East Coast, so Letta closed up shop and moved out East to take advantage of it.
column2: 這裡以前是麵包店，萊塔·萊梭懷爾曾在這裡賣各式美味的麵包、派和蛋糕。後來東岸突然吹起一股瑪芬熱潮，萊塔便關店搬去東岸，想趁機大撈一筆。

column1: You just can't do that while you're up here, where the air is thin and the walking uncertain.
column2: 你在這高處根本辦不到，這裡空氣稀薄，走路都搖搖晃晃的。

column1: Well, howdy, Mr. Pharkas! Er... I wuz just leavin', I swear. Gimme one more minute.
column2: 呃，你好啊，法卡斯先生！呃……我正要走了，我發誓。再給我一分鐘。

column1: Perfectly okay, Billy, no need to get up. Just move over a little.
column2: 沒關係的，比利，不用起來。挪一下就好。

column1: Umm... well, I... geez, Mr. Pharkas, invade my personal space, why dontcha!
column2: 嗯……那個，我……天哪，法卡斯先生，你乾脆直接侵犯我的個人空間算了！

column1: The water, obviously contaminated, has really "opened up your sluices." You spend a few minutes in extreme discomfort.
column2: 這水顯然被污染了，徹底「打開了你的水閘」。你花了好幾分鐘，極度不舒服。

column1: It looks like half the town is in line for the outhouse! How odd. Usually, they follow a "staggered" schedule. This seems particularly alarming given that recent horse-feed poisoning!
column2: 看起來鎮上半數的人都在排隊等茅房！真奇怪。平常大家不是都「錯開時間」上的嗎。想到最近才發生的馬飼料中毒事件，這狀況格外令人擔心！

column1: You turn the faucet off.
column2: 你把水龍頭關上了。

column1: You turn the faucet on, and water gushes out.
column2: 你打開水龍頭，水嘩啦嘩啦地流了出來。

column1: There's a spigot at the base of the water tower.
column2: 水塔底部有個水龍頭。

column1: Holy cow, you've never seen such a long line at the outhouse!
column2: 我的媽呀，你從沒見過茅房前排這麼長的隊伍！

column1: Something's rotten in the state of Coarsegold's bowels!
column2: 粗金鎮的「腸胃」裡，肯定出了什麼亂子！

column1: Those damn kids! Don't they have anything better to do than hide joy buzzers under the outhouse seat?
column2: 這些死小孩！就不能幹點正經事，非得在茅房座位下藏電擊玩具？

column1: Don't go over there; they shoot strangers, revenoors, horses, and pharmacists.
column2: 別過去那邊；他們見到陌生人、查稅員、馬和藥師都開槍。

column1: Once this was the Mayor's mansion, before he turned old and gray. Yep... the Old Gray Mayor ain't what he used to be!
column2: 這裡以前是鎮長的宅邸，在他變得又老又灰白之前。沒錯……這位「老灰鎮長」早已不復當年了！

column1: It's abandoned.
column2: 這裡已經廢棄了。

column1: That house used to belong to the Mine foreman, back when the Mine was still operating.
column2: 這棟房子以前屬於礦場工頭，那時候礦場還在運作。

column1: Pardon me, this stall is occu-pewed.
column2: 不好意思，這間茅坑目前「佔用」中喔。

column1: Excuse me VERY MUCH! I believe this stall is taken.
column2: 真是非常抱歉喔！我想這間茅坑已經有人了。

column1: Oops! Sorry, Judge. Everything comin' out okay?
column2: 哎呀！抱歉，法官。一切都還「順利」吧？

column1: Of course, same old story. Thank you for asking.
column2: 當然，老樣子。謝謝關心。

column1: Hey! Didn't we talk about this? You're really upsetting my concentration.
column2: 喂！我們不是講過這個了嗎？你這樣真的很打擾我專心。

column1: Oops, sorry, I forgot you were in here. You going to be long?
column2: 唉唷，歹勢，我忘了你在裡面。還要很久嗎？

column1: Every time you open this door, it gets longer and longer!
column2: 每次你打開這扇門，隊伍就變得更長！

column1: Judge, I was just wondering...
column2: 法官，我只是在想……

column1: Jumpin' Jehosophat, sonny! Close that damn door, I've got business to attend to!
column2: 我的老天爺啊，小子！把那扇該死的門關上，我這裡有正事要辦！

column1: You grab the ladder.
column2: 你抓住了梯子。

column1: The ladder is propped up against the water tower's infrastructure.
column2: 這座梯子靠在水塔的結構上。

column1: It feels as solid as it looks.
column2: 摸起來跟看起來一樣堅固。

column1: The lasso won't reach from down here.
column2: 套索從下面搆不到。

column1: This water tower still has a solid infrastructure and a good strong base. It seems to be holding up well.
column2: 這座水塔的結構依然穩固，底座也很堅實。看起來撐得住。

column1: You've seen enough dismembered limbs to know not to fool around with old farming equipment.
column2: 你見過夠多斷肢的慘況，知道不該亂碰老舊的農耕機具。

column1: Some old farming and milling equipment sits in disrepair further back on Collier Bluff.
column2: 柯利爾崖後方，擺著一些破損的老舊農耕與磨坊機具。

column1: You can't get into the mine. Nope, no way, nohow.
column2: 你進不了礦坑。不行，絕對不行，想都別想。

column1: It's one of the entrances to the Old Abandoned Mine, now boarded up for safety's sake.
column2: 這是廢棄老礦坑的其中一個入口，為了安全已經封了起來。

column1: The town's only working outhouse stands here.
column2: 鎮上唯一還能用的茅房就立在這裡。

column1: It may be awhile. It looks like everyone's exercising those lower abdominals!
column2: 可能要等一會兒。看起來大家都在鍛鍊下腹肌呢！

column1: Wait your turn. It's just like at the bank. (Other people want to make their deposits first.)
column2: 排隊等等吧，這就跟銀行一樣。（人家也想先進去「辦點事」呢。）

column1: You can't reach the outhouse from up here.
column2: 你從這裡構不到茅房。

column1: The outhouse door has a signature half-moon cutout.
column2: 茅房門上有個招牌半月形鏤空。

column1: (STAR TREK) The engines are already at maximum reverse thrust, Captain! They're givin' it all they've got!
column2: （星艦迷航記）「引擎已經全速反推到底了，艦長！它們已經卯足全力啦！」

column1: You haven't seen a line this long here since Mom served her famous Chicken Sushi w/Egg Tartare.
column2: 自從老媽端出她那道著名的「雞肉壽司佐韃靼蛋醬」以來，這裡就沒排過這麼長的隊了。

column1: Hey, you guys! You feel okay?
column2: 喂，各位！你們還好吧？

column1: The only response is a chorus of churning stomachs, roiling bowels, and floodgates straining to open.
column2: 回應你的只有此起彼落的腸鳴、翻攪的腹部，還有拼命想開閘的水門。

column1: |c2|"Hey, buddy, no cutting!"|c|
column2: |c2|「喂，老兄，不准插隊！」|c|

column1: |c3|"It's people like you that give people like you a bad name!"|c|
column2: |c3|「就是你這種人，讓你這種人名聲都臭掉了！」|c|

column1: A few moments later, you emerge feeling refreshed.
column2: 過了一會兒，你神清氣爽地走了出來。

column1: Gee! That water's got a nasty kick to it.
column2: 哇！這水後座力還真不小。

column1: Don't touch him, Captain! He's liable to blow any second!
column2: 別碰他，艦長！他隨時都會爆炸！

column1: He's really gotta go.
column2: 他真的憋不住了。

column1: Don't talk to him, he's concentrating.
column2: 別跟他說話，他正在集中精神。

column1: (SCOTTY OF STAR TREK) I canna tell how much more she kin take, Captain!
column2: （星艦迷航記的史考特）「俺說不準她還能撐多久啊，艦長！」

column1: How long can she wait? Not long, if she keeps bouncing like that!
column2: 她還能撐多久？照這樣一直扭來扭去，看來撐不了多久！

column1: She can't hear you over the mighty roar of her lower gastro-intestinal tract.
column2: 她下腹那雷鳴般的腸胃巨響，蓋過了你說的話，她根本聽不見。

column1: (SCOTTY) He's gonna explode, Captain, and neither you or I or anyone in the Universe can stop it!
column2: （史考特）「他就要爆炸了，艦長，這事兒不管是你、是俺，還是全宇宙誰都攔不住！」

column1: This one appears to be practicing the Jitterbug.
column2: 這位看起來正在練搖擺舞。

column1: Say! Do any of you guys know how to Madison?
column2: 喂！你們哪個會跳麥迪遜舞步啊？

column1: Nobody's laughing.
column2: 沒有人笑。

column1: Boi-oi-oing! That one hit a 9.0 on the Free Plug-O-Meter!
column2: 咚啊咚啊咚！那個在「置入式廣告指數」上飆到 9.0 分！

column1: Plug-O-Meter
column2: 置入式廣告指數

column1: That pulley never worked right in the first place. It's not going to work for you now.
column2: 那個滑輪打從一開始就沒好用過，現在也不會突然聽你的話。

column1: A block-and-tackle was erected here for unloading wagons. Unfortunately, it couldn't block and tackle at the same time.
column2: 這裡架了一組滑輪吊索，是用來卸貨的。可惜它沒辦法一邊「擋」一邊「拉」。

column1: As you reach the top of the water tower, the crowd cheers!
column2: 你爬上水塔頂端的那一刻，群眾歡聲雷動！

column1: |c2|"Thank God, It's Freddy!"|c|
column2: |c2|「謝天謝地，是佛萊迪！」|c|

column1: |c3|"We're number one! We're number one!"|c|
column2: |c3|「我們是第一！我們是第一！」|c|

column1: |c0|"What are you going to do now, Freddy?"|c|
column2: |c0|「你接下來打算怎麼辦，佛萊迪？」|c|

column1: I'm going to SierraLand!
column2: 我要去雪樂樂園！

column1: You reached the top. Too bad nobody was here to applaud your achievement!
column2: 你爬到頂了。可惜沒人在這裡替你鼓掌喝采！

column1: The bluff stays put, no matter how hard you tug.
column2: 不管你怎麼拉，那片峭壁都紋風不動。

column1: This is the eastern portion of Bluff Street, so-named for scenic Collier Bluff.
column2: 這是峭壁街的東段，因風景優美的柯里爾峭壁而得名。

column1: Didn't anyone warn you about digging near an outhouse?
column2: 都沒人警告過你，別在茅房附近亂挖嗎？

column1: You're tongue-tied.
column2: 你舌頭打結了，說不出話。

column1: You can't reach the rope from here!
column2: 你從這裡構不到那條繩子！

column1: The lasso dangles from the top of the water tower.
column2: 套索垂掛在水塔頂端。

column1: Your snare the tower top! The crowd eats it up!
column2: 你套住了塔頂！群眾看得如癡如醉！

column1: |c3|"Who's the shmuck with the rope?"|c|
column2: |c3|「拿繩子的那個傻蛋是誰啊？」|c|

column1: |c2|"Be careful you don't put an eye out!"|c|
column2: |c2|「小心別把自己眼睛戳瞎了！」|c|

column1: Hot dog, you roped the top of the water tower! What a shame there's no audience to appreciate your deed.
column2: 太厲害了，你套中水塔頂端了！可惜沒有觀眾能欣賞你這番壯舉。

column1: You wash your hands. (A feeling wholly unfamiliar to you!)
column2: 你洗了手。（這種感覺你可完全不熟悉！）

column1: You don't need any water right now!
column2: 你現在不需要水！

column1: You carefully fill one of your empty beer bottles with water from the tower.
column2: 你小心翼翼地用塔裡的水，把一個空啤酒瓶裝滿。

column1: You don't need any water at the moment.
column2: 你目前不需要水。

column1: One bottle full of water is enough.
column2: 一瓶水就夠了。

column1: You can't do that from up here!
column2: 你在這麼高的地方沒辦法這麼做！

column1: Water's running from the spigot.
column2: 水龍頭正在流水。

column1: The water just babbles.
column2: 水只是潺潺地流著。

column1: You don't need to fill the whisky glass with water. (Besides, some folks in town would consider it sacrilegious!)
column2: 你不需要把威士忌杯裝滿水。（再說，鎮上有些人會覺得這根本是褻瀆！）

column1: Trying to make the World's Largest Fizzy?
column2: 想調出全世界最大杯的氣泡飲嗎？

column1: The Deflatulizer is for the horses only. That's the water supply for the whole town!
column2: 除脹氣機是專門給馬用的。那邊可是全鎮的水源！

column1: You can't reach the water tank hatch from down here.
column2: 你從這麼下面構不到水塔的艙口。

column1: There's a small hatch on top of the water tank.
column2: 水塔頂端有個小艙口。

column1: That would taint the town's water supply!
column2: 那樣會污染全鎮的水源！

column1: Watered-down beer for the whole town? That's Sam Andreas's job!
column2: 讓全鎮喝到摻水的啤酒？那是山姆·安德列斯的活兒！

column1: You can't pour the purification solution into the water tank from down here.
column2: 你從這麼下面沒辦法把淨化液倒進水塔裡。

column1: Open the hatch first instead of pouring the purification solution on the roof of the water tank!
column2: 先把艙口打開，別把淨化液直接倒在水塔屋頂上！

column1: You carefully pour the purification solution into the town's water supply. Excellent job!
column2: 你小心地把淨化液倒進了全鎮的水源裡。幹得漂亮！

column1: It warn't more 'n a few hours, the folks of Coarsegold wuz feelin' a whole heckuva lot better, their bowels all settled down and happy. Freddy knew he could relax now; ever'thing was calm 'n' peaceful. But round 'bout midnight that very same night, trouble struck again. Freddy was in his own bed, sound asleep, when...
column2: 不消幾個時辰，粗金鎮的鄉親們都覺得舒坦多了，一個個腸胃安穩、心滿意足。佛萊迪心想這下總算能鬆口氣了，一切歸於平靜安寧。誰知就在當天半夜，麻煩又找上門來。佛萊迪正在自己床上睡得香甜，這時……

column1: Hello in there!
column2: 裡面有人嗎！

column1: (FUNNY VOICE) "There's nobody in here but us E. Coli!"
column2: （搞笑怪聲）「這裡只有咱們大腸桿菌，沒別人啦！」

column1: You can't seem to get a good grip on the shingles.
column2: 你怎麼樣都抓不牢那些屋瓦。

column1: You can't reach the roof of the water tank from here.
column2: 你從這裡構不到水塔的屋頂。

column1: The shingled roof of the water tank protects the entire water supply of the village of Coarsegold from dust, dirt, and bird droppings.
column2: 水塔那鋪著木瓦的屋頂，替粗金鎮全村的水源擋住了灰塵、髒污和鳥糞。

column1: The building's closed. There's no use milling around here.
column2: 這棟建築已經打烊了，你在這兒磨蹭也沒用。

column1: It's the Old Grist Mill. Since Mr. Grist left town, not much happens there.
column2: 這是老磨坊。自從葛里斯特先生離開小鎮後，這裡就沒什麼動靜了。

column1: The metal top of the tower is held very firmly in place. No amount of pulling could possibly budge it.
column2: 塔頂的金屬蓋固定得非常牢，你怎麼拉都休想撼動分毫。

column1: Your lasso isn't quite long enough to reach the top of the water tank from down here.
column2: 你的套索長度不夠，從這麼下面構不到水塔頂端。

column1: Using the lasso, you manage to climb up to the tippy-top of the tower.
column2: 你靠著套索，總算爬上了塔的最頂端。

column1: A short strong metal pole projects from the roof of the water tank.
column2: 一根粗短的金屬柱從水塔頂上突出來。

column1: Remembering your father's advice about never using the topmost rungs of a ladder, you stop just short of the ladder top.
column2: 想起老爸交代過絕不能踩梯子最頂那幾階，你便在快到頂端前停了下來。

column1: You can't reach the ladder from up here.
column2: 你在這麼高的地方構不到梯子。

column1: You can't seem to pick up the ladder right now. It suddenly seems so much heavier, for some strange reason!
column2: 你現在好像搬不動這梯子。不知道為什麼，它突然重了好多！

column1: The ladder is propped up against the side of the water tower tank.
column2: 梯子靠在水塔塔身的一側。

column1: You'll have to climb back down the rope first.
column2: 你得先順著繩子爬下去才行。

column1: It's wood, what more did you need to know?
column2: 就是木頭做的，你還想知道什麼？

column1: The ladder doesn't quite reach far enough.
column2: 這梯子的長度還不夠遠。

column1: You can't get a good throw while standing on the ladder.
column2: 你站在梯子上沒辦法好好瞄準投擲。

column1: (BONES LIKE) Dammit, Jim, you're a Pharmacist, not a cattle rustler!
column2: （模仿骨頭的口吻）「該死，吉姆，你是個藥劑師，不是偷牛賊！」

column1: This tank stores the whole town's drinking water supply.
column2: 這座水塔裝著全鎮的飲用水。

column1: There's nothing inside or outside the wagon worth taking.
column2: 這輛篷車裡裡外外都沒什麼值得拿的東西。

column1: By the side of the road sits an old covered wagon. (It's covered for theft and fire.)
column2: 路邊停著一輛老舊的篷車。（篷布嘛，就當它「有保」防盜防火險吧。）

column1: The tower is falling apart. You can't get to the top of it safely.
column2: 這座塔搖搖欲墜，你沒辦法安全爬到頂端。

column1: A creaking old windmill tower, haphazardly assembled from now-rotting timbers, graces the beautiful Coarsegold skyline.
column2: 一座嘎吱作響的老舊風車塔，用一堆早已腐朽的木料東拼西湊搭成，為粗金鎮美麗的天際線增色不少。

column1: Have you ever had your hand sliced off by a propeller? Would you LIKE to? Then don't try sticking your hand in the windmill blades!
column2: 你有被螺旋槳削掉手的經驗嗎？你會想要嗎？那就別把手伸進風車葉片裡！

column1: Now THAT's the pot calling the kettle black!
column2: 這下可真是五十步笑百步了！

column1: Ye Olde 'Orehouse usually isn't open during the day. Wait until dark, cowboy!
column2: 「金屋藏嬌樓」白天通常不營業，牛仔，等天黑了再來吧！

column1: That's the door to the brothel.
column2: 那是妓院的門。

column1: Freddy! Your store is ready to burn. You must save your town from sure destruction!
column2: 佛萊迪！你的店就快燒起來了。你得拯救全鎮，別讓它毀於一旦！

column1: The boss is more than a little upset. Seems that our "friend" has been thwarting every plan so far.
column2: 老大可不只是有點不高興而已。看來咱們那位「朋友」，到目前為止把每個計畫都搞砸了。

column1: Yep. Sumpin's gots to be done about it.
column2: 沒錯，這事兒非得處理不可。

column1: Absolutely. Now let's get down to business. What is the best way to get rid of our little problem -- PERMANENTLY?
column2: 一點沒錯。那咱們就開門見山吧，要怎麼樣才能徹底、永久地解決掉這個小麻煩？

column1: How 'bout hanging?
column2: 吊死他怎麼樣？

column1: No. Too quick and merciless. Poison?
column2: 不行，太快也太乾脆了。下毒呢？

column1: Nah. Too unsure. Ancient Egyptian dagger?
column2: 不行，太不保險了。古埃及匕首呢？

column1: I can't find mine. Got one on ya?
column2: 俺那把找不到了，你身上有帶嗎？

column1: Not at the moment. It don't matter how we do it, s'long as we do it soon. And we don't want no proof it was us, neither, and nuttin' to connect it to da Boss.
column2: 現在沒有。怎麼下手不重要，反正得快點動手。而且咱們不能留下任何證據，更不能讓人查到跟老大有關。

column1: Excellent thought. And the Boss has arranged for a bit of muscle to come on in and make sure the entire town's cleaned out PDQ. We'll be rid of that do-gooder and all his flea-bitten friends in no time! Ha, ha!
column2: 這主意妙。老大已經安排好幾個打手進來，保證把整個鎮子麻溜地清乾淨。咱們很快就能擺脫那個多管閒事的傢伙和他那票邋遢朋友了！哈哈！

column1: (CRUEL LAUGH) Bwah, hah hah!
column2: （奸笑）「哇哈，哈哈哈！」

column1: Laughing cruelly, they sit back to reflect on their villainy.
column2: 兩人奸笑著往後一靠，細細回味自己的惡行。

column1: It's P. H. Balance, the town banker, relaxing on the brothel porch with a good cigar. The thought of him "conversing" with one of Madame's nubile young professionals is enough to make you swear off banking forever.
column2: 是鎮上的銀行家P·H·貝倫斯，正叼著上等雪茄，在妓院門廊上悠哉休息。一想到他跟歐薇莉夫人手下哪位年輕「專業人士」「交流意見」，你就恨不得從此再也不跟銀行打交道。

column1: Am I interrupting anything?
column2: 我打擾到你們了嗎？

column1: OH! Er... why, of course not, Mr. Pharkas, we were just talking about y...UGH!
column2: 噢！呃……當然沒有啊，法卡斯先生，我們正在談你……唔！

column1: What he means is, we were simply chatting after an invigorating, ah, workout.
column2: 他的意思是，我們只是在一番，呃，提振精神的「運動」過後閒聊幾句。

column1: Did I hear you fellas say something about getting rid of somebody?
column2: 我剛剛是不是聽到你們在講要「解決掉」什麼人？

column1: No.
column2: 沒有。

column1: Yes.
column2: 有。

column1: Rats. Err, we were talking about getting rid of rats. Rats at the Bank, terrible problem. Sheriff Shift was telling me ways to eradicate the vermin.
column2: 老鼠。呃，我們在講怎麼除掉老鼠。銀行裡鬧老鼠，麻煩得很。席夫特警長正在跟我說怎麼滅這些害蟲。

column1: (SOTTO VOCE) |c1|You're the only rat at the bank.|c|
column2: （壓低聲音）|c1|銀行裡唯一的老鼠就是你。|c|

column1: I'm sorry, what was that?
column2: 不好意思，你說什麼？

column1: I said, "If only you had a cat at the bank."
column2: 我是說：「銀行裡要是有隻貓就好了。」

column1: Oh. Yes, I suppose that would work.
column2: 噢，對啊，我想那應該有用。

column1: Well, I'll leave you gentlemen to continue your conversation.
column2: 好啦，我就不打擾兩位先生繼續聊了。

column1: They snicker softly to themselves.
column2: 他們兩人低聲竊笑起來。

column1: You briefly consider showing P. H. Balance what you think of him... with a knuckle sandwich! But if they were talking YOU, the Sheriff is just itching to get you out the way. A fight would give him all the provocation he needs. Discretion wins out over raw virile manliness.
column2: 你一度考慮讓P·H·貝倫斯嚐嚐你的「拳頭三明治」，好好表達一下對他的看法！但如果他們剛才是在講你，警長可正巴不得找藉口把你除掉。動手打架正好給他一個現成的理由。三思而後行，終究還是勝過逞一時血氣之勇。

column1: Now then, Frederick. Please don't disturb us anymore.
column2: 好了，佛萊德里克。請你別再打擾我們了。

column1: You can barely see a glint from the nitrous oxide canister.
column2: 你勉強能看到笑氣鋼瓶反射出的一點光。

column1: You take careful aim with your pistol and slowly squeeze off a shot.
column2: 你舉起手槍仔細瞄準，緩緩扣下扳機。

column1: You did it! You shot off the canister's valve.
column2: 你成功了！你把鋼瓶的閥門射了下來。

column1: Good idea, but you just don't have a straight shot from here.
column2: 這主意不錯，但你從這裡沒有直射的角度。

column1: Oh, no you don't! You can't shoot the canister the EASY way, from up close! Try it from far away, just like you'd HAVE to in real life!
column2: 喔，不行不行！你不能用近距離這種「簡單模式」射那個鋼瓶！得從遠處下手，就跟現實生活中你「必須」做到的一樣！

column1: Yiparooni, Freddy done made them cowhands laugh themselves to death with a well-placed bullet.
column2: 呀呼，佛萊迪靠著一發精準的子彈，把那些牛仔們笑到活活斷氣。

column1: It's too dark for you to make out any details of that thing hanging from the hotel balcony.
column2: 天色太暗了，你看不清楚旅館陽台上掛著的那個東西的細節。

column1: You can't see the hotel through the brothel. You left your X-Ray glasses at the Pharmacy!
column2: 你沒辦法隔著妓院看穿到旅館。你的X光眼鏡忘在藥局了！

column1: You can't reach the bunting from here.
column2: 你從這裡構不到那面彩旗。

column1: Good idea, but you missed!
column2: 主意不錯，可惜你沒射中！

column1: There's no longer any need to shoot the bunting.
column2: 現在已經沒必要再射那面彩旗了。

column1: Potshots at the hotel? From here? Save your ammo!

column2: 那面彩旗上明明白白寫著「老媽餐館開放麥克風喜劇之夜」的廣告。既然旅館已經倒了，老媽正好白撿一塊免費廣告版面！

column2: 你能看得一清二楚，但從這裡根本不可能構得到。

The thought of Shift and Balance messin' around with Madame's working girls makes you thankful you don't participate in any disease-tradin' activities!
column2: 警長奇肯·P·席夫特正坐在夫人門廊上，跟村裡的銀行家P·H·貝倫斯一起抽著雪茄。夜色中飄來一絲煤油味……是從他身上傳來的！一想到席夫特和貝倫斯跟歐薇莉夫人手下姑娘們鬼混的畫面，你就慶幸自己沒摻和這種互通有無的「疾病交流活動」！

column1: Sheriff, you know about the fire down at the Assay Office?
column2: 警長，你知道驗金所那邊失火的事嗎？

column2: 沒有！

column1: Ya don't say!
column2: 不會吧！

column2: 那可真是糟透了。

column2: 哎呀，俺要是沒猜錯，那場火可能把大街給燒掉大半！連你那間藥局也一併陪葬！這事兒想都不敢想啊！<竊笑>

column2: <哼笑，竊笑>

column2: 你說啥？

column2: 你幹嘛要去做那種事？

column2: 那樣可能會有人受傷的！你該不會希望我放著火燒下去吧？

column2: 席夫特警長和菲尼斯互看了一眼。

column2: 想到警長密謀的對象八成就是你，你忍不住想一拳把他腦袋打飛。但真正神奇的是——你居然忍住了！

column1: Leave Madame's sign alone. You wouldn't want her running off with the Pharmacy sign, would you?
column2: 別動夫人的招牌。你總不希望她把藥局的招牌也順手牽走吧？

column1: That's just one of the many dried-out, half-dead trees found in the area.
column2: 那不過是這一帶眾多枯萎、半死不活的樹之一。

column2: 看來有人正在挑燈夜戰……還是說在「揉」燈油呢！

column2: 這片多岩的山坡上，坐落著歐薇莉夫人的產業，一棟仿「柔彩哥德式」風格量身打造的風月場所。當然，蓋房子之前，他們得先把地上的石頭清乾淨才行。

column1: The wood on the outside of the brothel is chipped, rotting, and nearly useless. (In other words, it's nearly ex-siding!)
column2: 妓院外牆的木板缺角又腐爛，幾乎沒用了。（換句話說，這外牆已經「牆」途末路啦！）

column1: You consider writing "Wash Me" with your finger in the dirt on the glass. However, Madame would never guess you meant the window!

column1: Madame had this gazebo built as part of her "Real Ol' Fashioned Romance Special," which cost an additional $1.25. It was never used. Coarsegold is filled with unromantic cheapskates.
column2: 夫人蓋了這座涼亭，是她「復古浪漫特別方案」的一部分，得另外加收1.25美元。結果從沒人用過。粗金鎮裡到處都是不解風情的小氣鬼。

column2: 這是一道白色尖木柵欄，把夫人的地產和南邊的大沙漠谷地隔開。

column2: 你要是去抗議，情況只會更糟。

column2: 這是一株仙人掌，長在柵欄外頭不遠處。

column1: Touch that cactus and you may get a little prick.
column2: 碰那株仙人掌，你可能會被扎一下，還可能碰上個「小刺頭」。

column1: Here on the "other side of the tracks," in the baddest part of town, stands Madame Sadie Ovaree's "Ye Olde 'Ore House," a gazebo, and a lot of foxtail, scrub, and brush. (Or "Scrub Brush," as Madame's fond of calling it.) You can also see parts of Main Street off in the distance.
column2: 在這「鐵軌另一頭」，也就是鎮上治安最差的地帶，坐落著莎蒂·歐薇莉夫人的「金屋藏嬌樓」、一座涼亭，還有大片的狐尾草、灌木叢和雜樹。（夫人喜歡管這叫「灌木刷子」。）你還能望見遠處的大街一角。

column1: You don't say! (Though you certainly try.)
column2: 少來了！（雖然你還真的試著說了。）

column1: That's going to stay right where it's painted.
column2: 這東西畫在哪裡，就會一直留在哪裡。

column1: Sadie Ovaree would probably not appreciate you digging up her carefully cultivated dirt.
column2: 莎蒂·歐薇莉大概不會樂見你挖掘她精心整理過的泥土地。

column2: 工程師小屋裡沒什麼值得你亂碰的東西。

column1: You can't possibly reach it from here!
column2: 你不可能從這裡搆到它！

column1: The cupola on top of the Bank of Bob is faintly visible over the Brothel's roof.
column2: 鮑伯銀行屋頂上的小圓頂，隱約可以從妓院的屋頂上方看見。

column1: Get real.
column2: 醒醒吧。

column1: Sam Andreas's Golden Balls are... is... right there at the end of the dirt path, across the railroad tracks.
column2: 山姆安德列亞斯當舖的金球招牌就在……就是……在那兒，土路盡頭，鐵軌對面。

column1: You'll have to go over to Main Street if you want to do that.
column2: 你得去大街那邊才能做那件事。

column1: You can kinda see the front of Mom's Cafe from here. It's the only 1-and-a-half star dining experience in the entire San Jokin' Valley!
column2: 你勉強可以從這裡看到老媽餐館的正面。這可是整個聖笑金山谷唯一一家「一顆半星」等級的用餐體驗！

column1: In your dreams.
column2: 你想得美。

column1: It's the lovely and winsome Chastity, a girl who really knows her stuff! In fact, every man in town knows her stuff!
column2: 是可愛迷人的貞潔，一個很懂門道的姑娘！事實上，鎮上每個男人都懂她的門道！

column2: 哈囉，貞潔！

column2: 噢，佛萊迪！你一碰我，我心裡就變得怪怪的！

column1: Hope you mean it!
column2: 希望你是真心的！

column2: 那是純潔。她有百分之九十九點四四不純潔……但照樣浮得起來！

column1: Evening, Purity!
column2: 晚安啊，純潔！

column1: Evening, Freddy! Has Madame still got you under lock 'n' key, or are you gonna let us get ahold of you one of these days?
column2: 晚安，佛萊迪！歐薇莉夫人還把你鎖得死死的嗎？還是哪天你會讓我們也抓到你？

column2: 好吧，甜心，要是你哪天改變心意……你知道去哪裡找我們！

column1: (And when, and how often, and for how much!)
column2: （還有什麼時候、多常一次、還有多少錢！）

column1: You're such a handsome man! Girls like me really go for men like you!
column2: 你真是個帥哥！像我這樣的姑娘就愛你這種男人！

column1: It's Virtue, one of the Madame's best-laid plans.
column2: 是美德，歐薇莉夫人「精心安排」的傑作之一。

column1: Howdy, Miz Virtue! You sure are a vision of loveliness!
column2: 哈囉，美德小姐！你真是美得像一幅畫！

column2: 太謝謝你了，佛萊迪！而你呢，先生，簡直是一身精壯的活教材！

column2: 謝謝！

column2: 你那雙男人的手一碰，還有看到你鼓起的肌肉，就讓我內心的野性激情整個被喚醒了！

column2: 她真正的意思是，看到一個鼓得飽飽的男人「錢包」，才真的會喚醒她內心的野性激情！

column1: Hey, big boy! It's about time you showed up. Time to take my pharmacy bill out in trade?
column2: 嘿，大帥哥！你總算來了。要用「以物易物」來抵我的藥局帳單了嗎？

column1: <gulp> Sure!
column2: <倒抽一口氣> 好啊！

column1: Then get over here before I have to come get you, sweetie!
column2: 那就快過來，甜心，不然我可要親自去抓你囉！

column1: Right here in public??
column2: 就在這種大庭廣眾之下？？

column1: It's Olga, for those who don't want to spend another sheepless night!
column2: 這位是奧爾嘉，專門服務不想再過「無羊之夜」的人！

column2: 咩－啊－啊－啊！

column2: （翻譯：妳到底怎麼收費？）

column1: Ba-aa-aa-aa-aa!
column2: 巴－啊－啊－啊－啊！

column2: （翻譯：「哎呀，你這個人類長得真好看，手法也真溫柔！」）

column1: Ba-aa-aa baa-aah!
column2: 巴－啊－啊 咩－啊！

column1: (Translation: "Hope you mean it!")
column2: （翻譯：「希望你是真心的！」）

column1: The room is a riot of plush red velvet. The girls are impatiently waiting for customers so that they can go upstairs and lie down awhile.
column2: 房間裡到處是華麗的紅色天鵝絨。姑娘們正不耐煩地等著客人上門，好上樓躺一會兒。

column1: The room is a riot of plush red velvet. The girls are upstairs, lying down. (This time, on their stomachs!)
column2: 房間裡到處是華麗的紅色天鵝絨。姑娘們都在樓上躺著。（這次是趴著的！）

column1: The plush walls effectively deaden the sound of your voice as you try to talk to the accoutrement.
column2: 這些華麗的牆壁把你對著擺設說話的聲音，吸得一乾二淨。

column1: You can't take the whole brothel, like the other customers you'll just have to take it one piece at a time.
column2: 你沒辦法把整間妓院都帶走，跟其他客人一樣，你只能一次來一點。

column1: From down here, that looks like a curtain of rich, crushed velour.
column2: 從下面看過去，那像是一幅華麗的縐絨窗簾。

column1: The curtain's upstairs, and you NEVER go upstairs at the Brothel! Madame insists on keeping you all to herself.
column2: 窗簾在樓上，而你「絕對」不能上妓院的樓！歐薇莉夫人堅持要把你整個人獨佔。

column1: The balustrade lends an opulent ambience to the brothel's ornamentation. (Shoot, where'd all them ten-dollar words come from?)
column2: 這欄杆為妓院的裝飾增添了一股奢華的氣息。（見鬼，這些文謅謅的大字眼是打哪冒出來的？）

column1: It's upstairs, and you can't reach it from here.
column2: 它在樓上，你從這裡搆不到。

column1: A splendid chandelier hangs in the center of the room.
column2: 一盞華麗的吊燈掛在房間正中央。

column1: You have a thing for swinging from chandeliers, eh?
column2: 你對盪吊燈這種事還挺有興趣的，嗯？

column1: It's a plush red velvet loveseat.
column2: 是一張華麗的紅色天鵝絨情人椅。

column1: You'd love to sit and chat, but you're not here for relaxation.
column2: 你是很想坐下來聊聊，但你來這裡不是為了放鬆。
