column2: 房間裡刻意擺了幾張華麗的紅色天鵝絨椅子，好讓客人能看到姑娘們最迷人的角度。

column1: You won't need any plush red velvet chairs in your quest for truth, justice, liberty, and a good time.
column2: 追求真理、正義、自由與快活人生的路上，你用不著什麼紅絲絨軟椅。

column1: The windows and entryways are festooned with plush red velvet curtains. (Festooned: from the Latin "festus," to drawl in a southern accent and shlep around in a lazy fashion and just sort of drape yourself over furniture.)
column2: 窗戶和門口都掛滿了華麗的紅色天鵝絨窗簾。（「掛滿」一詞源自拉丁文「festus」，意思是拖著南方腔調懶洋洋地晃來晃去，然後隨便把自己攤在家具上。）

column1: You can't open or close them; they're nailed just the way they are, with sensuous curves and folds vaguely suggestive of female anatomy. Or Shar Pei puppies, depending on your point-of-view.
column2: 你沒辦法把它們打開或關上；它們就這樣被釘死，帶著性感的曲線與皺褶，隱約讓人聯想到女性的身體曲線。或者，看你怎麼想，也像沙皮狗幼犬。

column1: There's a handsome silver tea set on the coffee table. It stands out, since it's just about the only thing in the room that isn't plush red velvet!
column2: 咖啡桌上有一套精美的銀質茶具。它特別顯眼，因為這幾乎是房間裡唯一不是華麗紅色天鵝絨的東西！

column1: You prefer sarsaparilla, thank you very much. (In a cracked, dirty bottle.)
column2: 謝了，你比較想喝沙士。（裝在破舊骯髒的瓶子裡的那種。）

column1: The clock's pendulum swings constantly. Just like Madame's girls!
column2: 這座鐘的鐘擺不停地擺動。就跟歐薇莉夫人的姑娘們一樣！

column1: The clock never needs winding... just a little jiggle now and then.
column2: 這座鐘從不需要上發條……只要三不五時搖它一下就好。

column1: These cupids decorate the stair banister.
column2: 這些小愛神雕像裝飾著樓梯扶手。

column1: Aren't they just too too?
column2: 是不是可愛得不得了？

column1: A charming picture window looks out over the side of the house. The view's a little blurry, though, owing to all the slobber on the outside of the window.
column2: 一扇迷人的觀景窗望向屋子側面。不過視野有點模糊，因為窗外沾滿了口水。

column1: Madame's windows don't open. She doesn't want anyone chickening out at the last moment.
column2: 歐薇莉夫人的窗戶都打不開。她可不希望有人在最後關頭臨陣脫逃。

column1: A brass cuspidor, known as a "spittoon," sits next to the plush red velvet armchair. (Spittoons for FREDDY PHARKAS, FRONTIER PHARMACIST furnished by Louie Loogie, Phlegmy, Mass.)
column2: 一個黃銅痰盂，俗稱「唾壺」，擺在華麗的紅色天鵝絨扶手椅旁。（本作《多情藥師酷牛仔》劇中所有痰盂，均由麻州痰渣鎮的路易痰痰提供。）

column1: There's nothing in the spittoon that you can't come up with on your own.
column2: 痰盂裡的東西，你自己也吐得出來。

column1: These stairs lead to the girls' private rooms.
column2: 這些樓梯通往姑娘們的私人房間。

column1: You can't go up there, Freddy. Penelope would never forgive you. And neither would Madame!
column2: 你不能上去，佛萊迪。潘妮洛普絕不會原諒你的。歐薇莉夫人也一樣！

column1: Madame's set out some wine and glasses. A few drinks helps the customers loosen up. The girls are already loose enough. No, wait... the customers drink wine and get tight, and the girls aren't... oh, never mind.
column2: 歐薇莉夫人擺了些酒和酒杯出來。喝幾杯有助於讓客人放鬆一下。姑娘們早就夠放得開了。不對，等等……是客人喝了酒會醉醺醺，而姑娘們並不……唉，算了。

column1: No wine for you, Freddy Pharkas! You need to maintain a clear, unmuddled head in order to uphold crime and defeat justice! (Or something like that.)
column2: 你不准喝酒，佛萊迪·法卡斯！你得保持頭腦清醒，才能繼續「維護犯罪、打敗正義」！（大概是這個意思吧。）

column1: It's a coffee table, big enough for those extra-kinky encounters.
column2: 是張咖啡桌，大得足以應付那些格外重口味的場面。

column1: There's no reason to move the coffee table.
column2: 沒理由去搬那張咖啡桌。

column1: It's a plush red velvet carpet! You love the way it squishes between your toes. (Er... not that you were ever bare-footed in here... certainly not...)
column2: 是一張華麗的紅色天鵝絨地毯！你很喜歡它擠壓在你腳趾間的感覺。（呃……並不是說你曾經在這裡光著腳……絕對沒有……）

column1: You cautiously peek beneath the rug, and see a maze of twisty passages, all alike. Just kidding. There's nothing under |c0|this|c| rug.
column2: 你小心翼翼地掀開地毯一角，看見一座「錯綜複雜、彼此雷同的通道迷宮」。開玩笑的啦。|c0|這張|c|地毯底下什麼都沒有。

column1: Why, it's a lovely painting of Fred and Ginger. (You know, Fred Mertz and Ginger Grant, that hot new minstrel team!)
column2: 哎呀，是一幅佛瑞德與金潔的可愛畫像。（就是佛瑞德·莫茲跟金潔·格蘭特啦，那對當紅的黑人歌舞新搭檔！）

column1: Someday, I'm going to go to the big city and see your act!
column2: 總有一天，我要進城去看你們的表演！

column1: The painting is unimpressed by your empty promises.
column2: 這幅畫對你的空頭支票一點也不感興趣。

column1: There's nothing behind the painting except plush red flocked wallpaper.
column2: 畫後面除了華麗的紅色植絨壁紙外什麼都沒有。

column1: There are some candles burning in the anteroom. They not only add atmosphere, but their fresh springtime scent covers up those embarrassing odors!
column2: 前廳裡點著幾根蠟燭。它們不只營造氣氛，那股清新的春天香氣還能蓋掉一些尷尬的味道！

column1: These fancy-shmancy imported candles are dripless, unlike most of Madame's customers. (Hey, you've got a dirty mind. That means, most of Madame's customers are the biggest drips around!)
column2: 這些花俏的進口蠟燭不會滴蠟，不像歐薇莉夫人的大多數客人。（嘿，你這個人腦子真髒。我是說，歐薇莉夫人的大多數客人都是些超級「滴滴答答」的無趣傢伙！）

column1: It's a large statuette of Shmeros, the God of Can't We Just Be Good Friends.
column2: 是一尊「舒莫斯」的大雕像，也就是「我們就不能單純當好朋友嗎」之神。

column1: Shmeros, will Penelope and I be married and live happily ever after?
column2: 舒莫斯啊，我跟潘妮洛普會結婚、從此過著幸福快樂的日子嗎？

column1: A small window in the statue's head reveals the message, "All signs point to yes."
column2: 雕像頭部有個小窗口，露出一則訊息：「種種跡象都指向肯定答案。」

column1: You touch the statue gently. Shmeros glares at you as if to say, "I trusted you to just BE FRIENDLY, and what did you do? I told you, we no longer have a physical relationship."
column2: 你輕輕碰了碰雕像。舒莫斯瞪著你，彷彿在說：「我相信你只是想『友善』一下，結果你幹了什麼好事？我早說過，我們之間不再有肉體關係了。」

column1: The working girls keep their clothes in here.
column2: 上班的姑娘們把衣服放在這裡。

column1: Opening the cabinet and touching the girls' dainty underthings costs two bucks extra. Just send $2 to Sierra On-Line, Dainty Underthings Dept. (No, wait, don't. Send it to Ken Williams, personally!)
column2: 打開櫃子摸姑娘們的精緻內衣，得額外加收兩塊錢。請將這兩塊錢寄給雪樂達公司「精緻內衣部門」收。（不對，等等，別寄那邊。直接寄給肯·威廉斯本人就好！）

column1: A variety of plush red velvet and green glass lamps can be found here.
column2: 這裡擺著各式各樣華麗的紅色天鵝絨與綠色玻璃燈具。

column1: Mmmmm! You do so love the smell of scorching flesh as you feel the lamps under your calloused pharmacist's fingertips.
column2: 嗯－！你用長滿老繭的藥師手指觸摸燈具時，就是喜歡那股燒焦皮肉的味道。

column1: A stack of naughty French Postcards sits on the coffee table, in order to titillate some of the less forward customers.
column2: 咖啡桌上放著一疊調皮的法國明信片，用來挑逗那些比較放不開的客人。

column1: You snatch the French Postcards.
column2: 你順手抄走了那些法國明信片。

column1: This chamber leads into Madame's private boudoir. No "unaccompanied" males allowed.
column2: 這個房間通往歐薇莉夫人的私人閨房。不准「單獨」男性進入。

column1: There's nothing worth snatching in this anteroom.
column2: 這間前廳裡沒什麼值得順手牽走的東西。

column1: Wow, Chastity! You sure know how to kiss!
column2: 哇，貞潔！你還真懂怎麼接吻！

column1: All in a day's work, Freddy, all in a day's work.
column2: 這都是家常便飯啦，佛萊迪，家常便飯。

column1: Freddy, I... I think you should leave.
column2: 佛萊迪，我……我覺得你該走了。

column1: Why, Sadie? Just because I'm just using you for cheap, tawdry pleasure when my heart belongs to Penelope Primm, the gorgeous, young, obviously more virtuous, new town Schoolmarm?
column2: 為什麼，莎蒂？就因為我只是把你當成廉價、庸俗的享樂工具，而我的心其實屬於潘妮洛普·普林姆——那位美麗、年輕、顯然更加貞潔的鎮上新來的女教師？

column1: |c0|What??? WHO???|c|
Oh, nothing, never mind. What were you saying?
column2: 噢，沒事，別在意。你剛剛說到哪了？

column1: Oh... I was just saying I think you should leave. Leave TOWN, that is! There's... oh Freddy, there's just no easy way to say this. The girls say the Sheriff and the Banker talk in their sleep. They hate you, Freddy. They want you dead. They're out to get you.
column2: 噢……我剛剛是說我覺得你該走了。是說離開這個「鎮」！這……唉，佛萊迪，這實在不知道該怎麼開口。姑娘們說警長跟銀行家說夢話的時候都提到你。他們恨你，佛萊迪。他們想要你的命。他們正打算對付你。

column1: Now don't you worry, Sadie. I've been doing a pretty good job up 'til now using just my wits and my pharmacological knowledge, haven't I? I'm not gonna just turn tail and run and leave you (and Penelope) and Coarsegold behind me to fend for yourselves.
column2: 別擔心，莎蒂。到目前為止，我光靠我的機智跟藥學知識就撐得挺好的，不是嗎？我才不會夾著尾巴逃跑，把你（還有潘妮洛普）跟粗金鎮丟下不管。

column1: You're not LISTENIN' to me, Freddy Pharkas! Thar's MEN a comin', men with GUNS. BIG guns! Guns with LONG barrels. Long, HARD barrels. Long, hard, STEELY barrels and low-slung holsters... and... and... (SLAP!)
column2: 你根本沒在聽我說話，佛萊迪·法卡斯！有一票男人要來了，帶著「槍」的男人。大「槍」！槍管很「長」的槍。又長又「硬」的槍管。又長又硬又「冰冷」的鋼鐵槍管，還有低垂的槍套……還有……還有……（啪！一巴掌）

column1: Sadie, snap out of it.
column2: 莎蒂，清醒一點。

column1: Oh, sorry, I was just visualizin'. Anyway, you'll never be able to outthink men with GUNS! If you're set on stayin' in town, you'll have to... you know, go back to your old ways!
column2: 噢，抱歉，我剛剛在腦補畫面。總之，你是沒辦法靠腦子打贏拿「槍」的男人的！你要是鐵了心要留在鎮上，那就得……你知道的，重操舊業！

column1: That's out of the question. I left gunslingin' behind me years ago. I'm not like that anymore, and I don't want to discuss it.
column2: 那絕對不可能。我多年前就已經放下快槍手的生活了。我早就不是那樣的人了，我也不想討論這件事。

column1: Stop it. You've gotta choose, an' that's all there is to it. Either leave town and save yer hide, or pull yourself together and face reality. Quit talkin' about potions and liniments; they're not gonna stop no bullets. It's time to get offa yer cute li'l butt and give these men a taste o' Frontier JUSTICE!
column2: 夠了。你非得做個選擇不可，就這麼簡單。要嘛離開鎮上保住小命，要嘛振作起來面對現實。別再扯什麼藥水跟藥膏了，那些東西擋不了子彈。是時候把你那可愛的屁股從椅子上抬起來，讓這些傢伙嚐嚐「邊疆正義」的滋味了！

column1: Now, what're you gonna do?
column2: 那，你打算怎麼做？

column1: I don't know... I don't know... Hold me, Sadie. Press me to your ample bosom, and let me decide tomorrow.
column2: 我不知道……我不知道……抱緊我吧，莎蒂。讓我埋進你那豐滿的胸口，明天再讓我決定。

column1: 'Kay!
column2: 好啦！

column1: The sign says, simply, "Rooms," referring to the Dirty Sheets Hotel.
column2: 招牌上簡簡單單寫著「客房」，指的是髒床單旅館。

column1: This window looks in on the kitchen of Mom's Cafe.
column2: 這扇窗可以看到老媽餐館的廚房內部。

column1: Hey, Mom! Come to the window, why don't you!
column2: 嘿，老媽！過來窗邊一下嘛！

column1: You wait. Apparently Mom hasn't caught on to the "drive-up window" concept yet.
column2: 你等著。看來老媽還沒搞懂什麼叫「得來速」。

column1: Mom wants it open. And you don't want to cross Mom!
column2: 老媽要這扇窗開著。你可不會想惹老媽生氣！

column1: This is the alternate route into the Saloon. It lacks the characteristic Western feel of swinging doors... but it has the distinct advantage of being lockable!
column2: 這是進酒館的另一條路。少了那種西部片經典的雙開彈簧門味道……但它有個明顯的優點，就是可以上鎖！

column1: It's the roof of Reverend Sy Hallelujah's house.
column2: 這是哈利路亞牧師家的屋頂。

column1: The Reverend's house is locked and shuttered. Who's minding the Church?
column2: 牧師家門窗緊閉上了鎖。這下誰來看管教堂呢？

column1: Dad Gumm's Traveling Medicine Show wagon sits nearby, awaiting the return of Dad Gumm and start of the Traveling Medicine Show season.
column2: 岡姆老爹的江湖賣藥秀馬車就停在附近，等著岡姆老爹回來，展開新一季的賣藥秀。

column1: There are a few assorted old trunks sitting on top of Dad Gumm's wagon.
column2: 岡姆老爹的馬車上堆著幾個雜七雜八的舊皮箱。

column1: You can't reach them. There's nothing in them. They're not your property. They'd crumble if you'd touch them. Basically, you're too lazy.
column2: 你搆不到。裡面什麼都沒有。那不是你的東西。你一碰它們就會碎掉。說穿了，你就是懶。

column1: A gnarled old tree grows next to the Synagogue and stretches up, forming a canopy over the yard.
column2: 一棵盤根錯節的老樹長在猶太會堂旁，枝葉向上伸展，在庭院上方形成一片樹蔭。

column1: Even the lowest branch is far too high up for you to climb.
column2: 就連最低的樹枝也高得你爬不上去。

column1: These stairs lead up to the balcony of the closed hotel.
column2: 這些樓梯通往那間已歇業旅館的陽台。

column1: The stairs feel solid enough, though they sag a bit.
column2: 這樓梯感覺還算穩固，雖然有點下陷。

column1: The blue sign is advertising "large, clean rooms, daily & weekly." No wonder the Dirty Sheets Hotel closed; they advertised the competition!
column2: 這塊藍色招牌打的廣告是「寬敞、乾淨的客房，論日論週皆可」。難怪髒床單旅館會倒——他們居然幫對手打廣告！

column1: Hung crookedly on the side of the Hotel is an advertisement for Atticus's Bath House, a local institution that didn't last a year. Folks in Coarsegold have traditionally been fiercely proud of how unwashed they are.
column2: 旅館側邊歪歪斜斜掛著阿提克斯浴堂的廣告，那是本地一間開不到一年就倒的老店。粗金鎮的居民向來對自己有多不愛洗澡感到無比自豪。

column1: Oh, leave it alone, it's part of Americana.
column2: 噢，別去動它，這可是美式文化的一部分。

column1: This is the back of what once was the Dirty Sheets Hotel. Now it's the Dirty Sheets hangout for vagrants, hobos and bums. Hmmm. Nothing's much changed 'cept the prices!
column2: 這裡是曾經的髒床單旅館後方。現在成了流浪漢、遊民跟廢柴的「髒床單」聚集地。嗯……除了價錢，其他好像也沒什麼變！

column1: You can't take it, push it, pull it, turn it, open it, close it, or basically do anything with it.
column2: 你沒辦法拿走它、推它、拉它、轉動它、打開它、關上它，基本上拿它一點辦法也沒有。

column1: A colorful poster for Nunstyle Beer hangs on the back of Mom's Cafe. |c2|"Nunstyle Beer... pure-brewed in God's Country."|c| Now in redeemable bottles!
column2: 老媽餐館後方掛著一張色彩繽紛的修女牌啤酒海報。|c2|「修女牌啤酒……在上帝的國度裡純釀而成。」|c|現有可回收瓶裝上市！

column1: You've got a great eye for memorabilia. Unfortunately, it won't be collectible for another 100 years.
column2: 你對紀念品還真有眼光。可惜這東西要再過一百年才會變得有收藏價值。

column1: Somebody's posted a flier here, trying to convince the Town Council to bring co-ed rodeo to the San Jokin' Valley.
column2: 有人在這裡貼了一張傳單，想說服鎮議會把「男女混合牛仔競技」引進聖笑金山谷。

column1: You're not interested in co-ed rodeo. Though you've met more than your share of Rodeo Mimes you wouldn't mind hog-tying and branding!
column2: 你對男女混合牛仔競技沒興趣。不過你倒是遇過不少牛仔默劇演員，你還挺樂意把他們五花大綁、烙上印記！

column1: This is the back of Mom's Cafe. She used to have a door here instead of a window, but nobody wanted to come in Mom's Rear Entry. (Hey! Stop thinking that!)
column2: 這是老媽餐館的後方。這裡原本是扇門，不是窗戶，但沒人想從老媽的「後門」進去。（喂！別再往那方面想了！）

column1: Knocking on the wall here will dent Mom's durable and attractively-painted Masonite siding.
column2: 敲這面牆只會敲凹老媽那堅固又漆得漂漂亮亮的美耐板牆面。

column1: This is Sam's Rear. And this is Sam's Rear with a couple of barrels by the back door. Any questions?
column2: 這裡是山姆的後方。而這裡是山姆的後方，後門邊還擺著幾個木桶。有問題嗎？

column1: If you want to get into the Saloon from here, try the back door.
column2: 如果你想從這裡進酒館，試試那扇後門。

column1: This small yard opens up to Bluff Street on the north side; the south side faces the back end of the Saloon and Mom's Cafe. The Hotel flanks the east side and the Old Abandoned Synagogue lies to the west.
column2: 這座小院子北面通往斷崖街；南面對著酒館和老媽餐館的後方。旅館在東側，西側則是廢棄的老猶太會堂。

column1: It's speechless.
column2: 它啞口無言。

column1: It ain't goin' nowhere.
column2: 它跑不掉的啦。

column1: The ground here is too hard and dry to be moved. (Much like Mom's heart!)
column2: 這裡的地又硬又乾，動不了。（跟老媽的心腸還真像！）

column1: How tempting! Fresh apple pie, still warm from Mom's oven. Why, it's as American as Mom's apple pie!
column2: 好誘人啊！剛出爐的蘋果派，還帶著老媽烤箱的餘溫。這可真是跟老媽的蘋果派一樣道地美式！

column1: Good move, Freddy! Dropping one steaming hot pie to get another!
column2: 幹得好，佛萊迪！丟掉一個熱騰騰的派，只為了拿另一個！

column1: You slyly attempt to swipe the apple pie from under Hop Singh's nose!
column2: 你狡猾地想從阿星的鼻子底下把蘋果派給摸走！

column1: Nice try, Freddy Pharkas! You want me remove your hands with Ginfu Knife? I happy to accommodate!
column2: 想得美，佛萊迪·法卡斯！你是想讓我用「金夫刀」把你的手剁下來嗎？我很樂意幫忙！

column1: On second thought, maybe that wasn't such a good idea right now.
column2: 仔細想想，現在這樣做好像不是什麼好主意。

column1: There's an ice pick stuck into a barrel here.
column2: 這裡的木桶上插著一支冰錐。

column1: You pull the ice pick out of the barrel and gingerly place it in your pocket. Just don't bend over suddenly or you'll circumcise yourself. (Of course, that won't be any skin off YOUR nose!)
column2: 你把冰錐從木桶裡拔出來，小心翼翼地放進口袋。千萬別突然彎腰，不然你會自己把自己「割」了。（當然啦，反正也不關你的「鼻」事！）

column1: Hopalong Singh's in the kitchen, cooking up a storm. (Or something equally inedible!)
column2: 跳仔星正在廚房裡卯足全力煮菜。（或者煮出什麼同樣難以下嚥的東西！）

column1: Howdy, Hopalong!
column2: 哈囉，跳仔星！

column1: Freddy Pharkas! You no hang around my kitchen! Go away! Get lost!
column2: 佛萊迪·法卡斯！你不准在我廚房裡晃來晃去！走開！滾遠一點！

column1: Nice to see you, too.
column2: 我也很高興見到你。

column1: Hop Singh's moving too fast to be caught!
column2: 阿星動作太快，根本抓不到！

column1: This window not for handing things back-and-forth! You have something for Hop Singh, you come in front entrance like normal people!
column2: 這扇窗不是用來遞東西的！你要給阿星什麼東西，就跟正常人一樣走前門進來！

column1: This not drive-up window! You ahead of time, Freddy Pharkas!
column2: 這不是得來速窗口！你來得太早了，佛萊迪·法卡斯！

column1: Hah! Missed me!
column2: 哈！沒抓到我吧！

column1: Wow! Some of Dad Gumm's Magic Elixir. This stuff can be used to cure a wide variety of conditions... the foremost being "sobriety."
column2: 哇！是岡姆老爹的神奇萬靈藥。這東西能治百病……最主要能治的就是「清醒」。

column1: You surreptitiously swipe the elixir, looking around to see if anybody is watching. Fortunately, nobody is.
column2: 你偷偷摸摸地順走了那瓶萬靈藥，還四處張望看有沒有人在看。還好，沒人在看。

column1: Some old empty half-kegs are sitting outside the Saloon.
column2: 酒館外擺著幾個空了的半桶舊木桶。

column1: Don't bother trying to open the barrels. They're empty. There's nothing left but the smell.
column2: 別費心去打開那些木桶了。它們都是空的，除了味道什麼都不剩。

column1: Very good, Freddy Pharkas!. Let us try some quickdrawing. Just make sure you hit the target and not me!!
column2: 很好，佛萊迪·法卡斯！讓我們來試試快拔槍吧。只是拜託你打中的是靶子，不是我！！

column1: I am applauding inside myself! Now for the big challenge of all-- six bottles at once!
column2: 我內心正在為你鼓掌！現在來挑戰最大的關卡——一次六個瓶子！

column1: Go ahead. Make our day.
column2: 儘管放馬過來。讓我們也風光一下。

column1: I'm one bad hombre! Do your worst!
column2: 我可是個狠角色！有多狠就使多狠吧！

column1: I'm feelin' pretty tough. But don't bust my chops.
column2: 我今天感覺挺強悍的。不過別太整我。

column1: I had too much tequila last night! Go easy!
column2: 我昨晚龍舌蘭喝多了！手下留情啊！

column1: Srini dodges your bullet!
column2: 斯里尼閃過了你的子彈！

column1: Okee the dokee, Freddy Pharkas! First, we shall see if you can successfully strike the bottles from afar with the bullets of your pistol. Then I will toss the bottles up in the air and you may try to hit them in flight. Good luck and may the best man win.
column2: 沒問題，佛萊迪·法卡斯！首先，我們來看看你能不能用手槍的子彈，從遠處成功擊中瓶子。接著我會把瓶子拋到空中，你可以試著在半空中擊中它們。祝你好運，願技高一籌者獲勝。

column1: Feeling lucky, punk?
column2: 覺得自己走運嗎，小子？

column1: Pardner, I could outgun the Magnificent Seven! Bring 'em on!
column2: 夥計，我的槍法足以贏過「豪勇七蛟龍」！放馬過來吧！

column1: Well, I won at tiddly-winks the other day. I'll give it m'best shot.
column2: 呃，我前幾天玩彈珠棋才贏了一場。我會盡力而為的。

column1: Let's face it, I'm a wuss.
column2: 說實話吧，我就是個軟腳蝦。

column1: Kid, I want you out of town by sundown!
column2: 小子，我要你日落前滾出這個鎮！

column1: Why, sure, Stranger! I'll be ridin' outta town well BEFORE sundown... leavin' your sorry carcass for the buzzards to pick apart!
column2: 那當然，陌生人！我會在日落前老早就騎馬離開鎮上……只留下你可悲的屍體，讓禿鷹去啄食！

column1: Will not.
column2: 才沒有。

column1: Will too.
column2: 就是有。

column1: Not.
column2: 沒有。

column1: Too.
column2: 就有。

column1: I refuse to play this juvenile word game with you.
column2: 我才不要跟你玩這種幼稚的文字遊戲。

column1: What are you doing now, repeating everything I say?
column2: 你現在是在幹嘛，我說什麼你都要跟著講一遍？

column1: So THAT'S why they call you "Kenny the |c2|Kid|c|!" Because you're nothing but an immature little child, an anal-retentive case of arrested development, with an unresolved Oedipal complex and probably co-dependent to boot! You were a punk when I faced you back in St. Louie, and you're still a punk!
column2: 原來這就是為什麼大家都叫你「|c2|小鬼|c|肯尼」的原因啊！因為你根本就是個長不大的屁孩，一個肛門期人格沒發展完全的傢伙，還帶著沒解決的戀母情結，搞不好還有依賴型人格！我在聖路易跟你交手的時候你就是個小混混，現在還是個小混混！

column1: Say your prayers, Outlaw.
column2: 禱告去吧，亡命之徒。

column1: NOW CUT THAT OUT!
column2: 給我住手！

column1: St. Louis? I didn't know anybody with a silver ear in St. Louis. Yet somehow you seem vaguely familiar...
column2: 聖路易？我不記得在聖路易認識什麼裝銀耳朵的人。不過你看起來就是有點眼熟…

column1: Maybe we'll have time to compare yearbook photos... IN HELL!
column2: 也許我們可以找時間比對畢業紀念冊的照片…在地獄裡比對！

column1: Your respect for frontier etiquette won't let you draw first. Wait 'till you see Kenny start to draw, then do your best!
column2: 你對西部禮節的堅持讓你不肯先拔槍。等看到肯尼動手，你再盡全力吧！

column1: And as the blood runs from your body, so do your hopes of saving Coarsegold and achieving legendary Western Hero status.
column2: 隨著血從你身上流盡，拯救粗金鎮、成為傳奇西部英雄的希望也跟著流光了。

column1: Welp, ya knocked the gun outta my hand, Hero, but it warn't good enuf to keep me from hittin' YOU first! Sorry I got a mite sloppy when I PIERCED YER EAR! Har har! Looks like you'll bleed to death in a few seconds. Guess I can now tell Penelope that yew won't be interferin' with her plans anymore.
column2: 哼，你是把我手上的槍打掉了沒錯，英雄，但這還不夠讓你搶先我一步打中我！可惜我下手的時候手滑了一下，正好轟在你耳朵上！哈哈哈！看樣子你再過幾秒就要失血而死啦。這下我可以跟潘妮洛普講，說你再也礙不了她的事囉。

column1: Penelope?!
column2: 潘妮洛普？！

column1: What did he say? Your head's swimming, but you're sure he said, "Penelope!" Could it be? Her? Could SHE be the cause of all this?
column2: 他剛剛說什麼？你頭昏眼花，但你很確定他說了「潘妮洛普」！難道是…她？難道這一切都是她搞的鬼？

column1: It's your "lucky" red neckerchief. Once again, it doesn't seem to be working!
column2: 這是你那條「幸運」紅領巾。看來這次它又不靈了！

column1: You weakly pull the neckerchief from around your neck.
column2: 你有氣無力地把領巾從脖子上扯下來。

column1: You've looked better.
column2: 你以前氣色好看多了。

column1: You poke yourself. You're still alive, but barely.
column2: 你戳了自己一下。你還活著，但也只是勉強而已。

column1: Trying to put yourself out of your misery? What are you, a man or a horse? Save yourself!
column2: 想自我了斷嗎？你到底是人還是馬？快想辦法救自己吧！

column1: It's your good ear... or what's left of it!
column2: 這是你完好的那隻耳朵…或者該說，是剩下的部分！

column1: The blood runs through your fingers. Ecccccch!
column2: 血從你的指縫間流出。噁∼！

column1: You place your lucky neckerchief on your ear and press on it to staunch the flow of blood.
column2: 你把幸運領巾按在耳朵上，設法止住血流。

column1: With your last remaining ounce of strength, you pull yourself up and stumble off towards the schoolhouse... to see Penelope.
column2: 你用盡最後一絲力氣爬起身，踉踉蹌蹌地朝學校走去…去見潘妮洛普。

column1: Penelope... Penelope, the sweet... Penelope, my beloved... Penelope... the TRAITOR!
column2: 潘妮洛普…甜美的潘妮洛普…我摯愛的潘妮洛普…潘妮洛普…叛徒！

column1: Kenny's gun is still smoking. (Of course, that's very bad for its health!)
column2: 肯尼的槍還冒著煙。（當然啦，這對它的「健康」很不好！）

column1: Your hat, like all Western heroes' hats, stays on through just about ANYthing!
column2: 你的帽子跟所有西部英雄的帽子一樣，不管發生什麼事都不會掉！

column1: Kenny the Kid looms over you, grinning cruelly.
column2: 小鬼肯尼居高臨下地站在你面前，露出殘忍的笑容。

column1: You've never seen Main Street from this angle: lying half-dead in the middle of the street, your life swimming before your eyes as your blood pools in the dust... What a view! You imagine you'll never see a view like THIS again as long as you live!
column2: 你從沒從這個角度看過大街：半死不活地躺在路中央，血在塵土裡積成一灘，過去的種種在眼前一幕幕閃過…真是壯觀！你猜這輩子大概再也看不到這種「美景」了！

column1: You can hardly move. You can't reach anything beyond yourself.
column2: 你幾乎動彈不得，碰不到自己以外的任何東西。

column1: Kenny has managed to shoot off a sizable portion of your GOOD ear!
column2: 肯尼一槍轟掉你「完好」那隻耳朵一大塊！

column1: You shoot the gun out of Kenny's hand! Unfortunately, you did it just after HE shot YOU!
column2: 你一槍把肯尼手上的槍打掉了！可惜，你是在他先打中你之後才做到的！

column1: Kenny looks down at you with pure, undisguised malice and disgust.
column2: 肯尼低頭看著你，眼神裡毫不掩飾地充滿惡意與嫌惡。

column1: Welp, Mister Bigshot Gunslinger, looks t'me like yer bark was worse'n yer bite. Wait'll I tell the Boss how easy I whupped your butt, yew sorry excuse for a hero. Now die here in the dirt like the puny li'l pig yew are! See ya in hell, pal! (VICIOUS LAUGH)
column2: 哼，這位大牌槍手先生，看來你是雷聲大雨點小啊。等我回去告訴老大，說老子多輕鬆就把你這個爛英雄給撂倒了。現在就在這塵土裡像隻可憐的小豬一樣死去吧！地獄見啦，老兄！（狂笑）

column1: He spits into the dust, and trudges off cockily.
column2: 他朝塵土裡吐了口口水，趾高氣揚地走開了。

column1: Your eyes are getting heavy...
column2: 你的眼皮越來越沉重…

column1: You poke yourself in the eye. Nice going!
column2: 你戳到自己的眼睛。真有你的！

column1: A trickle of blood runs from your mouth.
column2: 一絲血從你嘴角流下。

column1: Flubble-ubble-ubble-ubble!
column2: 呼嚕嚕嚕嚕！

column1: Now that you've got THAT out of the way, do you think you could try to save yourself?
column2: 好啦，這件事解決了，你能不能想辦法救救自己？

column1: This is your pharmacy. Where you work. Hence the name, "Pharkas' Pharmacy."
column2: 這是你的藥局，你工作的地方。所以才叫做「法卡斯藥局」。

column1: You and that are not on speaking terms.
column2: 你跟那個東西已經沒話好說了。

column1: Quit picking at everything. That's the sign of an obsessive/compulsive personality disorder. But, that's... okay.
column2: 別再什麼都要摸一下了，這是強迫症的徵兆。不過……算了，沒關係。

column1: This door leads to your back office, laboratory, and the stairs to the second floor.
column2: 這扇門通往你的後方辦公室、實驗室，還有通往二樓的樓梯。

column1: You thought an Iced Cream Stand would attract customers. Mostly, it attracts cockroaches. Especially now that the Iced Cream deliveries have stopped.
column2: 你原本以為冰淇淋攤能招來顧客，結果大多招來的是蟑螂。尤其現在冰淇淋都停止進貨了。

column1: Yes, you often feel like ripping this Iced Cream Stand down and binging on the dregs of the leftover toppings. But you have to watch your heroic, girlish figure.
column2: 沒錯，你常常很想把這個冰淇淋攤拆了，把剩下的配料一口氣吃光。但你得顧著自己那英雄又纖細的身材。

column1: Ahh, your Diploma from the University of Hicksville School of Apothecary Sciences and Other Good Guesses. The old alma mater. What memories!
column2: 啊，這是你在「鄉巴佬大學藥劑與亂猜學系」拿到的畢業證書。母校啊，真是回憶滿滿！

column1: But it's hung so well!
column2: 但它掛得多好看啊！

column1: The top shelf is where you keep all the newest, most scientifically advanced medications safe from shoplifters:
column2: 最上層架子放的是你那些最新、最先進的藥品，安全地擺著防小偷：

column1: You won't need that one.
column2: 那個你用不著。

column1: Here on the second shelf, close at hand, is where you keep the most expensive medicines out of reach of the customers:
column2: 這第二層架子伸手就拿得到，放的是你最貴、顧客卻拿不到的藥品：

column1: NEW YORK CITY?!?!
column2: 紐約市？！？！

column1: Nope, won't need any of that particular one.
column2: 不，那一種你用不上。

column1: The items on the top shelf here are one or two weeks past their expiration dates:
column2: 這裡最上層架子上的東西，過期一到兩個禮拜了：

column1: You don't need any of these items, and even if you did, they've expired.
column2: 你不需要這些東西，就算需要，它們也過期了。

column1: On the lowermost shelf of this case, you keep slightly scratched, dented, or previously-used items:
column2: 這個櫃子最底層放的是有點刮傷、凹陷，或用過的東西：

column1: Chemists who keep up on their trade journals (like you always mean to do) know that these preparations aren't worth the bottles they're bottled in.
column2: 有在追蹤業界期刊的藥劑師（就像你「一直打算」要做的那樣）都知道，這些藥根本連裝它們的瓶子都不值。

column1: On the middle shelf, you store discontinued items:
column2: 中間那層架子放的是停產的商品：

column1: Savvy druggists (like you) eschew the use of trashy medicinals like these.
column2: 精明的藥劑師（比如你）都會避免使用這種爛藥。

column1: Up on the top shelf here, you keep your overstock:
column2: 這裡最上層放的是你的庫存過剩品：

column1: Pharmacists in the know, like yourself, know that there's no value to these phony curatives. That doesn't stop you from selling them, though!
column2: 內行的藥劑師（比如你自己）都知道這些假藥毫無價值。不過這不妨礙你照樣賣給客人！

column1: This hand-painted sign adds a real touch of friendly, folksy atmosphere to the place. It also spells "Pharmacy" phonetically, inbreeding being as popular as it is around here.
column2: 這塊手繪招牌給店裡添了幾分親切樸實的氣氛，上面還用注音式拼法拼出「藥局」兩個字──畢竟這一帶近親聯姻風氣頗盛。

column1: Certainly you're desperate for a sign of some sort, but not THIS kind of sign.
column2: 你的確很需要某種「跡象」，但絕對不是這種「招牌」。

column1: It's the back counter where you, Freddy Pharkas, Frontier Pharmacist Extraordinaire, dispense your wares.
column2: 這是後方櫃檯，你──佛萊迪·法卡斯，超凡的邊疆藥師──就是在這裡發藥的。

column1: There's nothing there to be taken. You keep your business tidy... which is easy to do when there ain't much business!
column2: 那裡沒什麼好拿的。你把生意打理得井井有條…畢竟生意本來就沒多少！

column1: The items on the second shelf are about a month past their saleable shelf life:
column2: 第二層架子上的東西，過了可販售期限大約一個月：

column1: You don't need any of these items, and even if you did, they're expired.
column2: 你不需要這些東西，就算需要，它們也過期了。

column1: The items on the third shelf are 3-4 months past their usable shelf life:
column2: 第三層架子上的東西，過了可用期限三到四個月：

column1: The bottom shelf holds the items that are a year or more past their shelf lives, OR have been found to be poisonous and/or illegal, OR have inexplicably reproduced on their own:
column2: 最底層架子放的東西，不是過期一年以上，就是被驗出有毒或違法，或是莫名其妙自己繁殖出來的：

column1: You don't need to use any of these items, and even if you did, you'd expire.
column2: 你完全不需要用這些東西，就算需要，用了你也會「過期」。

column1: You've always wanted a counter gate; now you have one. And now you know they're a pain in the butt.
column2: 你一直很想要一道櫃檯小門，現在你有了。而現在你也知道，這種東西真的很煩人。

column1: Your overhead designer lamps are rarely used, since the pharmacy closes at sunset.
column2: 你那些頭頂上的設計師吊燈很少用到，畢竟藥局日落就打烊了。

column1: No need to turn on the lamps. The dry rot gives off a dandy phosphorescent glow.
column2: 不必開燈，木材腐朽本身就散發出一種挺不錯的螢光。

column1: That's another table upon which to display your many valuable patent medicines and innovative treatments.
column2: 那是另一張桌子，用來展示你那些珍貴的成藥和創新療法。

column1: It took you weeks to get the bottles arranged just so. Don't blow it now.
column2: 你花了好幾個禮拜才把瓶子排成這樣，現在別搞砸了。

column1: This multi-instrument piano-roll-style juke machine is called a "Symphonium." Trouble is, the company that sold it to you went out of business after producing only one roll. And how many times can one person listen to "Does Your Chawin' Tobacco Lose Its Flavor On the Bedpost Overnight"?
column2: 這台多樂器紙捲式點唱機叫做「交響機」。麻煩的是，賣你這台機器的公司只做了一捲紙捲就倒閉了。而且一個人到底能聽幾遍「你嚼的菸草，過了一夜放在床柱上還有味道嗎」這種歌？

column1: The Symphonium hasn't worked since 1885, when old Manny Rivberg put his fist through it.
column2: 這台交響機自從一八八五年老曼尼·瑞夫柏格一拳打穿它之後，就再也沒動過。

column1: Ol' Manny Rivberg... That Ol' Manny Rivberg. He just keeps...
column2: 「老曼尼·瑞夫柏格啊…那個老曼尼·瑞夫柏格。他就是一直…」

column1: That's enough! Say any more and we'll have to pay a royalty!
column2: 夠了夠了！再講下去我們可要付版權費了！

column1: Here, on top of your "Reduced!" table:
column2: 這裡，是你「特價出清」桌的桌面：

column1: Nope, that's not one of the pills, poultices or preparations you'll need.
column2: 不，那不是你需要的藥丸、膏藥或製劑。

column1: On top of this cabinet, you have a stunningly arranged display of Old Snuffy's Limproot Hair Oil Creme (in the 8 oz., 16 oz., and Giant 64 oz. "Baby Huey" jars), as well as a few dusty boxes of Rustler's Stove Chocolates.
column2: 這個櫃子上方，精心陳列著「老鼻煙軟根髮油霜」（有8盎司、16盎司，以及巨無霸64盎司的「大寶寶」罐裝），還有幾盒積了灰的「牛仔爐灶巧克力」。

column1: You won't need any Limproot Hair Oil Creme or Rustler's Stove Chocolates today.
column2: 今天你用不到軟根髮油霜，也用不到牛仔爐灶巧克力。

column1: On the upper shelf of the left-hand cabinet, you find:
column2: 在左手邊櫃子的上層架子，你找到：

column1: You briefly consider shoplifting some of these items, but hey, you really already own them, so where's the excitement?
column2: 你一度想順手牽羊拿走幾樣，但話說回來，這些東西本來就是你的，這樣有什麼刺激感？

column1: On the bottom shelf of the left-hand cabinet are:
column2: 左手邊櫃子最底層放的是：

column1: You don't need any underarm oatmeal packs; you took care of THAT little problem this morning! And fortunately, you don't need any of this other stuff either!
column2: 你不需要腋下燕麥敷包，那個小問題你今天早上已經處理過了！而且很幸運，其他這些東西你也都用不上！

column1: It's the President's wife. She's the head of the "Just Say No to Ether" campaign.
column2: 這是總統夫人。她是「向乙醚說不」運動的發起人。

column1: Mrs. Cleveland, I just want you to know that your "Just Say No to Ether" campaign has really inspired me. I'm totally committed to wiping out anesthetic abuse in our lifetime.
column2: 克里夫蘭夫人，我只想讓您知道，您的「向乙醚說不」運動真的深深啟發了我。我這輩子都會全心投入根除麻醉藥物濫用。

column1: Keep talking to photographs and you WILL be committed!
column2: 你再繼續跟照片講話，你才真的會被「收容」！

column1: Leave her where she is, as a shining beacon to all who gaze upon her serene countenance. (Incidentally, have you heard about her scandalous affair?)
column2: 讓她繼續掛在那裡吧，對所有仰望她那安詳容顏的人來說，她就是一盞明燈。（對了，你聽說過她那樁醜聞緋聞嗎？）

column1: It's Saint Joseph, patron saint of chewable aspirin.
column2: 這是聖約瑟，咀嚼式阿斯匹靈的守護聖人。

column1: If you pick it up, all the luck will run out of the bottom.
column2: 你要是把它拿起來，好運就會全從底部漏光。

column1: This bottle is filled with this century's most incredible medical breakthrough.
column2: 這個瓶子裡裝的是本世紀最驚人的醫學突破。

column1: You won't be needing any leeches in this game.
column2: 這個遊戲裡你用不上水蛭。

column1: Back then, this is what was known as a "support system."
column2: 在那個年代，這就是所謂的「支撐系統」。

column1: Seems sturdy enough... for now.
column2: 看起來還算牢靠…目前是啦。

column1: This sign clearly lets the townsfolk know that the prescription counter is in the back of the store.
column2: 這塊招牌清楚地告訴鎮民，配藥櫃檯在店的後方。

column1: Someday, maybe there'll be a glass tube there, bent in the shape of the word "Prescription," filled with a rare gas that will glow in brilliant colors. Wouldn't that be wonderful? Boy, that'd make people actually WANT to buy drugs!
column2: 也許有一天，那裡會裝上一根玻璃管，彎成「處方箋」這幾個字的形狀，裡面灌著稀有氣體，會發出絢麗的光芒。那該有多棒啊？天哪，這樣一來大家搞不好還真的會想買藥呢！

column1: We were going to put in this elaborate animation of you touching the giant finger, like the creation mural on the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel depicting God touching Adam's finger with lightning bolts crackling all around. But, screw it.
column2: 我們本來打算做一段精緻的動畫，讓你觸碰那根巨大的手指，就像西斯汀教堂天花板上那幅創世壁畫，畫著上帝用閃電觸碰亞當的手指那樣。不過，算了，懶得做。

column1: Thisi is a deluxe shelving unit, featuring polished mahogany inlays, filigreed endcaps, extra-wide midheight shelf and no-skid recessed legs. (Shelving units for FREDDY PHARKAS provided by Crate & Whisky Keg.)
column2: 這是一套豪華層架，採用拋光桃花心木鑲嵌、雕花收邊、加寬中層架板，還有防滑收邊桌腳。（FREDDY PHARKAS 的層架由「板條與威士忌酒桶公司」提供。）

column1: They're already arranged in a pleasing yet sales-conducive manner.
column2: 它們已經擺得賞心悅目又有助於銷售了。

column1: This is a deluxe shelving unit, featuring polished mahogany inlays, filigreed endcaps, extra-wide midheight shelf and no-skid recessed legs. (Shelving units for FREDDY PHARKAS, FRONTIER PHARMACIST provided by Crate & Whisky Keg.)
column2: 這是一套豪華層架，採用拋光桃花心木鑲嵌、雕花收邊、加寬中層架板，還有防滑收邊桌腳。（FREDDY PHARKAS， FRONTIER PHARMACIST 的層架由「板條與威士忌酒桶公司」提供。）

column1: On the upper shelf of the right display case, you keep some of your hot sellers:
column2: 右邊展示櫃的上層架子，放的是你的熱銷商品：

column1: Your survival instincts narrowly prevent you from using any of the items on this shelf.
column2: 你的求生本能勉強阻止你使用這層架子上的任何東西。

column1: On the lower shelf of the right display case, you keep some old, reliable, steady sellers:
column2: 右邊展示櫃的下層架子，放的是老字號、穩定熱賣的商品：

column1: You wouldn't recommend any of these preparations to your worst enemy.
column2: 這些藥你連對最恨的敵人都不會推薦。

column1: Hey, Pharkas! M'butt's killin' me.
column2: 嘿，法卡斯！我的屁股快痛死我了。

column1: He does know how to make an entrance, doesn't he?
column2: 他還真懂得怎麼引人注目地登場，是吧？

column1: Sorry to hear that, Smithie.
column2: 真遺憾，鐵匠史密。

column1: Yeah, so gimme some o' dat Preparation G.
column2: 嗯，那就給我來點那個「G痔瘡膏」吧。

column1: It's Smithie the Blacksmith, owner of Smithie's Blacksmith and a durned clever fellow. He seems to be in pain.
column2: 這是鐵匠史密，「史密鐵匠鋪」的老闆，是個腦筋挺靈光的傢伙。他看起來很痛苦。

column1: Why not your usual six-pack of liniment, Smithie?
column2: 怎麼不跟平常一樣來六瓶擦劑就好，史密？

column1: Wall, Mr. Pharkas, I'ma fixin' to take a long ride. I'ma gonna leave town. The Sheriff shut me down for operatin' without a Smithie License, whutever the hell that is. So I sold that lousy property offn to that cheap snake of a banker, P. H. Balance, down to the Bank of Bob. And good riddance, sez I!
column2: 哎呀，法卡斯先生，俺打算出遠門一趟，準備離開這鎮子了。警長說俺沒申領什麼「鐵匠執照」──管他那是啥玩意兒──就把俺鋪子給關了。所以俺把那塊爛地賣給那個摳門的銀行家蛇鼠一窩的P. H.貝倫斯，就是「阿波銀行」那個，賣給他了。俺說啊，走了正好，眼不見為淨！

column1: I'll be sorry to see y'all go, Smithie.
column2: 你要走了，我還真捨不得呢，史密。

column1: Yeah, well, this town's goin' ta hell in a hand-me-down, anyway. Sumpthin's wrong with them horses out there, they's pooting up a storm. Cain't hardly take the smell, I wuz like to pass out around there!
column2: 唉，反正這鎮子也是每況愈下啦。外頭那些馬也不知道是咋回事，一直放屁放個沒完，那味道簡直薰得俺快昏過去！

column1: That ain't whut I come in here fer! C'mon, Pharkas, I'm itchin' to blow this taco stand. Gimmee my Preparation G, willya?
column2: 那不是俺進來要說的事！快點啦，法卡斯，俺等不及要閃人了。把俺的G痔瘡膏給俺，行不行？

column1: Frederick!
column2: 佛萊德瑞克！

column1: Thank you, Frederick, this looks perfect! You are a scholar and a gentleman.
column2: 謝謝你，佛萊德瑞克，這看起來完美極了！你真是個學識淵博又有紳士風度的人。

column1: Shucks, I'm just a poor pharmacist tryin' to please m' favorite customer. Will I see you again soon?
column2: 哎呀，俺只是個窮藥師，想讓自己最寶貝的客人開心而已。我們很快還會再見面嗎？

column1: I think that can be arranged, Frederick. See you soon.
column2: 我想這可以安排，佛萊德瑞克。到時候見。

column1: I'll be waiting. S'long, now, Penelope.
column2: 我會等妳的。先這樣了，潘妮洛普。

column1: Why, Miss Primm, you sure are lookin' purty today!
column2: 哎呀，普林姆小姐，妳今天可真是漂亮啊！

column1: Now, Frederick, you can call me Penelope if you please. After all, I think we're... to that point in our relationship.
column2: 好啦，佛萊德瑞克，你可以叫我潘妮洛普沒關係。畢竟，我想我們之間……已經到了那個階段了。

column1: She must be talking about the hayride you both went on last month... or the square dance you both went to last week... or the cow-tipping expedition you both went on last night!
column2: 她說的想必是你們上個月一起坐的乾草車、上禮拜一起去的方塊舞，還是昨晚一起去的推牛惡作劇吧！

column1: Well, then, to what do I owe the pleasure of your company this fine morning?
column2: 那麼，是什麼風把妳吹來，讓我這美好的早晨有妳作伴？

column1: This isn't a social call, I'm afraid. I have this rather important prescription Doc Gillespie gave me. I was hoping you could fill it as soon as possible.
column2: 恐怕這不是一趟社交拜訪。我這裡有張大夫吉勒斯比開給我的重要處方箋，希望你能盡快幫我配好。

column1: My pleasure, Penelope.
column2: 樂意之至，潘妮洛普。

column1: I apologize for the scruffiness of the Prescription. Doctor Gillespie was in his cups again.
column2: 抱歉這張處方箋寫得有點潦草，吉勒斯比醫生又喝多了。

column1: No trouble, Penelope, that's as usual.
column2: 沒關係，潘妮洛普，他一向如此。

column1: I'll just wait right here if you don't mind, Frederick.
column2: 如果你不介意，我就在這裡等囉，佛萊德瑞克。

column1: Well now, I admit you're somewhat of a distraction to me, Penelope, but I'll do m'best!
column2: 這個嘛，我得承認妳對我來說是有點分心啦，潘妮洛普，不過我會盡力的！

column1: Penelope hands you the prescription.
column2: 潘妮洛普把處方箋遞給你。

column1: Penelope! It's so good to see you again!
column2: 潘妮洛普！能再見到妳真好！

column1: I'm afraid this isn't good news, Frederick. This prescription you filled for me?
column2: 恐怕不是什麼好消息，佛萊迪。你幫我配的這帖藥……

column1: Yes? What about it?
column2: 怎麼了？有什麼問題嗎？

column1: Well, one of the children tasted a bit -- just a bit, mind you, on the tip of his finger, just to see what it tasted like.
column2: 這個嘛，有個孩子嚐了一點──注意，就只是沾在指尖上一點點，只是想知道味道而已。

column1: And?
column2: 然後呢？

column1: I had to send him home. Chills, fever, bloody stool, the whole thing. I do hate to be a pest, but I'm terrified that this may be incorrectly prepared. Could you take another look at it?
column2: 我只好讓他回家了。發冷、發燒、血便，什麼症狀都出現了。我實在不想煩你，可是我很擔心這是不是配錯了。你能不能再看一次？

column1: For you... anything.
column2: 為了妳……什麼都行。

column1: Unfortunately, you were so taken with Penelope's angelic presence that you forgot to charge her the 19 cents she owed you!
column2: 可惜的是，你被潘妮洛普那天使般的存在迷得神魂顛倒，忘了跟她收她欠你的19分錢！

column1: Frederick! Oh, Frederick!
column2: 佛萊德瑞克！喔，佛萊德瑞克！

column1: Penelope, dearest! My heart leaps at seeing you in my humble store again.
column2: 潘妮洛普，我親愛的！看到妳又光臨我這寒酸小店，我的心都要跳出來了。

column1: I'm afraid it's not a happy occasion, Frederick. This prescription seems letter-perfect, except for the amount. Can you take another look at it? I'd hate for either one of us to be cheated.
column2: 恐怕這次來不是什麼開心的事，佛萊德瑞克。這張處方箋看起來每個字都對，只有份量不對。你能不能再看一次？我可不希望咱們倆有誰吃虧。

column1: Goodness! I'll remake it right away, Penelope, and I'll get it perfect. This time, for sure! Wait right here.
column2: 天哪！我馬上重配，潘妮洛普，這次一定做到完美！妳就在這裡等一下。

column1: It's Penelope, the love of your life! Right here in your very own pharmacy! And she's as beautiful as the day she stepped off the stage!
column2: 是潘妮洛普，你此生摯愛的女人！就站在你自己的藥局裡！她還是跟當初下馬車那天一樣美麗！

column1: I sure have been having a swell time with you these past few weeks, Penelope!
column2: 這幾個禮拜跟妳在一起，我過得真是開心極了，潘妮洛普！

column1: Why, thank you, Frederick. I have, too.
column2: 哎呀，謝謝你，佛萊德瑞克。我也是。

column1: I do believe I have a... a growing... uh... a growing AFFECTION for you!
column2: 我確實覺得自己……對妳有種……呃……日漸增長的愛慕之情！

column1: That's sweet of you, Frederick. I think you're very cute... for a pharmacist, that is. Considering that you've only got one ear. And you're scrawnier than the other men around town.
column2: 你真貼心，佛萊德瑞克。我覺得你挺可愛的……以一個藥師來說啦。畢竟你只剩一隻耳朵，而且比鎮上其他男人都瘦弱。

column1: (TO SELF) She thinks I'm cute! She thinks I'm cute!
column2: （自言自語）她覺得我很可愛！她覺得我很可愛！

column1: How's school, Penelope?
column2: 學校還好嗎，潘妮洛普？

column1: Oh, how I love filling those impressionable young minds with knowledge, their eager faces turned upward in the quest to learn. It's so satisfying!
column2: 喔，我最喜歡把知識灌進那些純真的小腦袋裡了，看著他們求知若渴地抬頭望著我，真是太有成就感了！

column1: I was wondering if you were going to go to the Rotary Club luncheon next week, and if so, if you had anybody else to go with.
column2: 我在想妳下禮拜會不會去扶輪社的午餐聚會，如果會的話，妳是不是已經有人陪妳一起去了。

column1: Forgive me, Frederick, I do so hate to be short with you, but I DO need this prescription... otherwise I'd love to stay and chat. Please don't think me impertinent!
column2: 原諒我，佛萊德瑞克，我實在不想這麼匆忙，可是我真的需要這張處方箋……不然我很樂意留下來聊天。請別覺得我沒禮貌！

column1: Not at all, it's my fault for prattling on so. I'll get right to it.
column2: 哪裡的話，是我不好，話太多了。我馬上就去辦。

column1: I really can't wait to get my ha...
column2: 我實在等不及想拿到我的手……

column1: Frederick, |c2|please!|c| I need to get back to school as soon as possible!
column2: 佛萊德瑞克，|c2|拜託！|c|我得儘快回學校去！

column1: Of course, of course, of course. Right away, Penelope.
column2: 當然，當然，當然。馬上就好，潘妮洛普。

column1: Please, Frederick! Not in public! And not in broad daylight! And never, ever before our nineteenth date!
column2: 拜託，佛萊德瑞克！不要在大庭廣眾之下！也不要在光天化日之下！而且絕對不能在我們第十九次約會之前！

column1: I'm sorry, Frederick, I'm only interested in picking up my prescription just now. I'll be happy to look at your toys any other time!
column2: 抱歉，佛萊德瑞克，我現在只想拿我的處方箋。你那些玩意兒，改天我很樂意再看！

column1: Yes, Frederick, it's my prescription. Do you think you could fill it for me?
column2: 是的，佛萊德瑞克，這是我的處方箋。你能幫我配一下嗎？

column1: If I'm any sort of a pharmacist, I should be able to. I'm not sure what's taking me so long.
column2: 要是我還算個藥師的話，這應該難不倒我。我也不知道自己怎麼會拖這麼久。

column1: Good day, Freddy... Freddy Pharkas!
column2: 日安，佛萊迪……佛萊迪·法卡斯！

column1: That's better, Freddy Pharkas.
column2: 這樣好多了，佛萊迪·法卡斯。

column1: That'll be 22 cents, Miss Back.
column2: 一共是22分錢，貝克小姐。

column1: Put it on my tab, I don't have it with me right now.
column2: 記在我帳上吧，我現在身上沒帶錢。

column1: Well, g'day to you, Ms. Back! What can I do for you today?
column2: 那麼，日安啊，貝克小姐！今天我能為妳做點什麼？

column1: Well, Freddy Pharkas, Doc Gillespie, that no-good, gin-soaked sodden ol' lush, wrote me this damn prescription that'll probably cost me an arm and a leg. Here. Take this prescription, the rotgut from that old wino doctor is making my new ensemble stink to high heaven.
column2: 哼，佛萊迪·法卡斯，那個沒用、成天泡在琴酒裡的老酒鬼吉勒斯比大夫，開了這張要命的處方箋給我，大概又要花我一大筆錢了。拿去，把這張處方箋收下，那個老酒鬼醫生開的爛藥，把我這身新行頭都薰得臭氣沖天。

column1: Mr. Pharkas!
column2: 法卡斯先生！

column1: Yes, Helen?
column2: 是，海倫？

column1: I accidentally gave a bit of this so-called "medicine" to one of my pets. AND IT DIED! Obviously, this is not fit for consumption. Now take back my prescription and get it RIGHT this time. Or you'll feel the wrath of my handbag!
column2: 我不小心把一點這個所謂的「藥」餵給我的一隻寵物吃，結果牠死了！很顯然這東西根本不能吃。現在把我的處方箋收回去，這次給我配對！不然你就等著嚐嚐我手提包的厲害！

column1: I'm so sorry, Ms. Back. I'll take another stab at it, and I'll remove the charge from your tab until I get it right.
column2: 真的很抱歉，貝克小姐。我會再試一次，在配對之前，這筆錢我先不記在妳帳上。

column1: Humph!
column2: 哼！

column1: Frederick Pharkas!
column2: 佛萊德瑞克·法卡斯！

column1: Yes, Mom? What can I do for you now?
column2: 是，老媽？我現在能為妳做什麼？

column1: Are you trying to pull the sheep over my eyes?
column2: 你是想拿整隻羊蒙我的眼睛嗎？

column1: Huh?
column2: 嗄？

column1: This prescription! Oh, the medication seems just fine, but the quantity is wrong. I want exactly how much is prescribed, no more, no less. Is that understood?
column2: 這張處方箋！藥本身看起來沒問題，可是份量不對。我要的是處方上寫的份量，不多也不少。聽懂了嗎？

column1: Jeepers, I'm sorry, Mom. I'll do it right this time, just you wait and see.
column2: 天啊，對不起，老媽。這次我一定會做對，你等著瞧。

column1: See that you do! And don't you dare charge me for this until you get it RIGHT!
column2: 你最好說到做到！在你搞對之前，休想跟我收錢！

column1: I won't, I won't, consider it stricken from your tab.
column2: 不會不會，就當這筆帳一筆勾銷。

column1: This is Helen Back, proprietor of Mom's Cafe.
column2: 這位是海倫·貝克，老媽餐館的老闆娘。

column1: To get good food in Coarsegold, you have to go to Helen Back!
column2: 想在粗金鎮吃到像樣的東西，你得「上天堂又下地獄」跑一趟——不，是去找海倫·貝克才對！

column1: So, how's the restaurant business?
column2: 餐館生意還好嗎？

column1: Heh. Don't ask.
column2: 嘿，別問了。

column1: Okay, sorry.
column2: 好啦，抱歉。

column1: I swear my delicate constitution ain't up to the heat and flies this year. Hop Singh's spendin' more time swattin' flies than he is in the kitchen, he hardly has time to wash his hands. 'Course we ain't gettin' nuthin' delivered on time anymore 'cuz of the train; we gotta get our produce by Pony Express, and it ain't too pretty oncet gets here.
column2: 我跟你說啊，我這把老骨頭今年真的撐不住這種悶熱跟蒼蠅了。阿星在廚房裡趕蒼蠅的時間比煮菜還多，忙到連洗手的時間都沒有。現在火車也不來了，什麼東西都送不準時，食材都得靠驛馬快遞送，送到的時候啊，賣相都不怎麼樣了。

column1: Pony Express: When It Positively, Absolutely Has to Be There By The Industrial Revolution.

column2: 不過我也不想抱怨啦。快幫我把藥配一配吧，乖孩子。

I'M SOMEONE'S MOTHER, for corn sake! So show me some RESPECT and just KEEP your HANDS to yourSELF! Now fill my prescription or I'll break your fingers.

column1: Does that look anything like my prescription?
column2: 這東西哪裡像我的藥方了？

column2: 我來就是為了拿藥，我才沒興趣被你推銷別的東西！

column1: That's not mine. Now get back to my prescription.
column2: 那不是我的。快回去弄我的藥方。

column2: 你該不會指望「我」來配這帖藥吧！

column2: 佛萊迪，親愛的！把你那藥師的俏屁股滑過來這兒，我有點事要找你幫忙。

column1: Thank you, Freddy dear!
column2: 謝了，親愛的佛萊迪！

column2: 這樣是22分錢，莎蒂，不過看在你的份上，算你19分就好。

column1: Whaddaya say we just sorta "take it out in trade," Freddy? I'm a mite short this week.
column2: 佛萊迪，咱們乾脆「以物易物」怎麼樣？我這禮拜手頭有點緊。

column1: Well...
column2: 這個嘛……

column1: Thank you, Freddy, you're a lambikins. Catch you tonight, maybe? Ta-ta!
column2: 謝了，佛萊迪，你真是個小可愛。今晚見，說不定喔？拜拜！

column1: Morning, Sadie. What've you got?
column2: 早啊，莎蒂。你帶了什麼來？

column1: I gotta prescription here I need filled... sumpin' that'll increase my womanly powers, iffn you know whut I mean. Be a dear and fill it for me right away, won't you? I simply can't wait to try it out.
column2: 我這兒有帖藥要配……是那種能增加女人味的東西，你懂我意思吧。乖，快幫我配一配好嗎？我實在等不及要試試看了。

column1: Your wish is my command, Madame!
column2: 夫人的願望就是我的命令！

column1: You take the prescription from the Madame. What a busy morning! You haven't had to fill this many prescriptions since Custer's troops stayed at the Dirty Sheets Hotel.
column2: 你從夫人手裡接過藥方。真是忙碌的一個早上！自從卡斯特將軍的部隊住進「髒床單旅館」以來，你就沒配過這麼多藥方了。

column1: Oh, Freddy!
column2: 喔，佛萊迪！

column1: Sadie! Back so soon?
column2: 莎蒂！這麼快就回來了？

column1: I hate to say this, but one of the girls tried a swig of this. Now I'm down one girl! I'll have to send out to St. Louis for another! Would you mind very much looking at this and seeing what's up, honey?
column2: 我也不想這麼說啦，可是有個姑娘試喝了一口這個，現在我少了一個姑娘！我還得寫信去聖路易再找一個來補！親愛的，你能不能幫我看看這到底是怎麼回事？

column1: Hmmm, very strange. OK, I'll give it another try. Dunno what went wrong...
column2: 嗯，真奇怪。好吧，我再試一次。不曉得是哪裡出了錯……

column1: Freddy, sweetums?
column2: 佛萊迪，小甜心？

column1: Sadie! I wasn't expecting to see you again so soon!
column2: 莎蒂！沒想到這麼快又見到你！

column1: I hate to tell you, but one of the girls tried a smidge of this, just for fun. Now she's got a goatee. Can you figure out why this stuff seems to |c0|decrease|c| womanliness rather than |c0|increase|c| it?
column2: 我也不想講啦，可是有個姑娘鬧著玩試了一點點，現在她長出山羊鬍了。你能不能查出來，為什麼這東西是|c0|減少|c|女人味，而不是|c0|增加|c|呢？

column1: That's a tough one. I'll do what I can, though. Hmmmmm.
column2: 這可難倒我了，不過我會盡力的。嗯……

column1: You reclaim the prescription from Mme. Ovaree.
column2: 你從歐薇莉夫人手中拿回藥方。

column1: It's Madame Sadie Ovaree, proprietor of Ye Olde 'Orehouse, and your closest friend and confidant. In fact, she knows EVERYTHING about you!
column2: 這位是莎蒂·歐薇莉夫人，「老字號窯子」的老闆娘，也是你最要好的知己。老實說，她把你的底細摸得一清二楚！

column1: How's business, Sadie?
column2: 生意怎麼樣啊，莎蒂？

column1: Oh, it has its ins-and-outs! (CHUCKLES) Oh, my, I do make a good funny now and then, don't I?
column2: 喔，有進有出的啦！（輕笑）天啊，我偶爾也是會講出好笑話的嘛，是吧？

column1: Yes, Sadie, you sure do.
column2: 是啊，莎蒂，你的確會。

column1: Now now, Freddy Pharkas! Normally I'd love to oblige, but I'm off-duty right now. Feel free to drop by tonight, though!
column2: 別這樣嘛，佛萊迪·法卡斯！平常我很樂意奉陪，可惜我現在下班了。晚上再來坐坐嘛！

column1: Freddy, darlin', you know I just LOVE to see your stuff, but let's stick to business for the moment, shall we?
column2: 佛萊迪，親愛的，你知道我最愛看你那些寶貝了，不過咱們還是先談正事吧，好嗎？

column1: Why don't you keep it 'til you're finished with it?
column2: 你何不留著它，等用完了再說？

column1: Srini's on the other side of the counter. So be polite if you want to do that, and join him.
column2: 斯里尼在櫃檯另一頭。想這麼做的話就有禮貌一點，過去找他吧。

column1: Your faithful Indian companion, Srini, is hard at work preparing your store for its grand reopening... someday soon, you hope.
column2: 你忠心耿耿的印度夥伴斯里尼，正賣力為藥局的盛大重新開幕做準備……你希望是很快的某一天。

column1: Shall we go do some target practice, Srini? I'm all set, I think.
column2: 斯里尼，咱們去練練靶好嗎？我想我準備好了。

column1: Looks like you are ready to begin commencing the start of our target practice outing, Freddy. Please to meet me forthwith nearby to the cemetery, where I have scoped out a location of perfection!
column2: 看樣子你已經準備要開始著手展開咱們的練靶行程了，佛萊迪。請速速到墓園附近與我會合，我已經看好一處絕佳地點了！

column1: Srini!
column2: 斯里尼！

column1: Dude!
column2: 老兄！

column1: Everything going OK in here?
column2: 這裡一切都還好嗎？

column1: What is it looking like? I am having everything under control. You have merely to go be a hero and I will continue holding up the fort.
column2: 看起來是怎樣呢？我這邊一切都在掌控之中。你只管去當你的英雄，我會繼續守著這裡。

column1: Thanks!
column2: 謝了！

column1: Srini, are you going to help me put out the fire, or what?
column2: 斯里尼，你到底要不要幫我滅火啊？

column1: There is much stock work yet to be done.
column2: 還有很多存貨的工作尚待完成。

column1: It's midnight.
column2: 現在是半夜。

column1: I am still on Pakistani time.
column2: 我還在用巴基斯坦時間呢。

column1: That's a pretty poor excuse for not helping me put out the fire!
column2: 這藉口爛透了，虧你想得出來不幫我滅火！

column1: I have many other excuses ready if you do not like that one.
column2: 如果你不喜歡這個，我還準備了很多其他藉口。

column1: Never mind, I'll do it myself.
column2: 算了，我自己來。

column1: The fire's out, but I don't feel like sleeping.
column2: 火滅了，不過我一點都不想睡。

column1: Yes, too much excitement for Freddy. You will be overtired tomorrow morning.
column2: 是啊，佛萊迪今天太興奮了。你明天早上一定會累壞的。

column1: I hate it when that happens.
column2: 我最討厭這種事發生了。

column1: Try to relax and reduce stress. Visit friends.
column2: 放輕鬆點，紓解一下壓力。去拜訪朋友吧。

column1: It's midnight! What kind of friends can I visit this time of night?
column2: 現在是半夜耶！這種時間我能去拜訪哪門子朋友？

column1: Indeed that is a question you have well asked.
column2: 這問題你問得確實好。

column1: Srini, I think I'm ready to get dressed.
column2: 斯里尼，我想我準備好換裝了。

column1: Very good then! You start to dress and I will assist you in shortest order.
column2: 那太好了！你先開始換，我會盡快前來協助你。

column2: 斯里尼，我現在想換上我的牛仔裝。

column2: 我看你還沒準備好！你八成是缺了一雙時髦的牛仔靴。

column1: Dang!
column2: 該死！

column2: 斯里尼！嘿，我的偽裝已經全部到齊了！

column2: 才沒那回事呢，佛萊迪·法卡斯！

column1: Why the hell not?

column2: 你渴望當個槍手，卻連一把槍都沒有！你把槍給忘到哪兒去了？

column1: Oh. Whoops. Be right back.
column2: 喔，糟了。我馬上回來。

column1: Hey, Srini! Let's get me dressed up, I'm ready to get into disguise.
column2: 嘿，斯里尼！幫我換裝吧，我準備好要偽裝了。

column1: No may do, Freddy Pharkas!
column2: 不可以行呢，佛萊迪·法卡斯！

column1: What? Why not?
column2: 什麼？為什麼不行？

column1: You still lack for a way to disguise the mostly-missing right ear.
column2: 你還缺個辦法，來遮住你那幾乎不見的右耳。

column1: Srini! Let's get me into outfit, I'm ready to start blowing away some varmint butt!
column2: 斯里尼！幫我把衣服穿上，我準備好要去轟爛幾個壞蛋的屁股了！

column1: Doggone it!
column2: 見鬼了！

column1: Srini, I've got everything I need... silver ear, pistols, clothes, and boots. Let's get me dressed!
column2: 斯里尼，我要的東西都齊了……銀耳朵、手槍、衣服、靴子。幫我換裝吧！

column1: Not yet, not yet!
column2: 還不行，還不行！

column1: You will want to wear something lucky. Have you any such thing?
column2: 你會想戴件幸運物的。你有這樣的東西嗎？

column1: Not on me. Hmmmm. Doggone you anyway, Srini!
column2: 沒帶在身上。嗯……真是的，斯里尼，你很煩耶！

column1: Durn it, I wish I knew how.

column1: How do you propose I should deal with them?
column2: 那你說我該怎麼對付他們？

column2: 我覺得幽默是化解火爆脾氣的辦法。不過我只是個卑微的藥局助手，也許我把情勢看得太遠了些。

column1: Srini, let's go practice target-shooting.
column2: 斯里尼，咱們去練練打靶吧。

column1: That is a good leisure-time activity for us to do, yes all right! But how are we even to begin without such that until you locate some sort of shooting mechanism, I must wonder?

column1: I am loving your charcoal, Freddy Pharkas! It is most crumbly and clean-smelling!
column2: 我很喜歡你這塊木炭，佛萊迪·法卡斯！它碎得恰到好處，聞起來又乾淨！

column1: Thank you, Srini!
column2: 謝了，斯里尼！

column1: I have no use for the strap of leather. Perhaps you should save it for an emergency that requires leather in some way.
column2: 這條皮帶對我沒什麼用處。或許你該留著它，以備哪天需要皮革的緊急情況。

column1: What would I do without you?
column2: 沒有你我該怎麼辦才好？

column1: I do not wish it. Please to use it by yourself.
column2: 我不想要這個。請你自己留著用。

column1: Do not give that to me, Freddy Pharkas! You are the dispensing pharmacist in these parts!
column2: 別把那東西給我，佛萊迪·法卡斯！這一帶配藥的可是你！

column1: (DR SEUSS STYLE) I do not eat beef, snails, or ham. I do not eat them, Fred I am.
column2: （蘇斯博士風格）我不吃牛肉，不吃蝸牛，也不吃火腿。我不吃這些，我是佛萊迪。

column1: Perhaps you may put these to good use soon!
column2: 或許你很快就能好好利用這些東西！

column1: You do? Humph and humph! I have never thought of this!
column2: 你會啊？哼哼！我還真沒想過這一點！

column2: 你有一條繩子了！接下來還會發生什麼事呢？

column1: What do you mean?
column2: 你這是什麼意思？

column1: Do not ever mind, it was a rhetorical answer!
column2: 別放在心上，那只是個修辭性的回答！

column1: Hey there, some buckaroo! With that lasso, you are looking very cowboy-style!
column2: 嘿，牛仔小子！拿著那條套索，你看起來可真有牛仔的樣子！

column1: A metallic canister of some substance! That is certainly high-tech for the 1800s! Are you sure it is not an anachronism?
column2: 裝著某種物質的金屬罐！這對1800年代來說絕對是高科技啊！你確定這不是穿越時空的東西？

column1: Not really.
column2: 不算是。

column1: Well then! I do not know what more to add!
column2: 那好吧！我也不知道還能多說什麼了！

column1: Ah, yes, the shipment of baking soda. It was delivered while you were out.
column2: 啊，對了，這批小蘇打粉送到了。是你不在的時候送來的。

column1: It's a little much.
column2: 這東西有點太多了。

column2: 你這下算是告訴我了！

column2: 那我不要這些了。你們美國女人本來就夠瘦了。

column1: Ah, wax, a most remarkable substance. You are truly fortunate to possess some.
column2: 啊，蠟，真是了不起的東西。你能擁有一些，真是幸運。

column2: 你把手槍瞄準斯里尼……然後開槍！

column1: Translation: you need a GUN, Einstein!
column2: 翻譯成白話文：你需要一把「槍」啦，愛因斯坦！

column2: 喔！你有黏土了！這下你真的是我所想的那種人了！

column1: You have taken it for some reason. I am not needing it back. I am no Indian-giver. Please keep it until you find a use for it.
column2: 你出於某種理由拿走了它。我不需要它還回來。我可不是那種送出去又要討回的人。請留著它，直到你找到用途為止。

column2: 啊，我看你這是在做脫蠟鑄造啊！你真是個男子漢！

column1: I believe you should have something different than your current shoes, something other than your current clothes, the pistols you used during the practicing you recently completed, and something for good luck! Then wear your ear, and I will know you are ready to be all dressed up like a big cowboy!
column2: 我認為你應該要有雙不同的鞋子、一套不一樣的衣服、你最近練習用的那把手槍，還有件幸運物！然後戴上你的耳朵，我就知道你準備好要打扮成一個大牛仔了！

column1: Ah, yes! It will be ready on Tuesday! Hee hee hee! I have made a funny. Excuse my jocularity. I do not know whence this piece of paper comes.
column2: 啊，對了！星期二就會好了！嘻嘻嘻！我又講了個笑話。原諒我的幽默感。我實在不知道這張紙是從哪兒來的。

column1: Yes, they are truly boots worthy of a Western Hero. May you have an opportunity to wear them with pridefulness.
column2: 是啊，這雙靴子確實配得上一位西部英雄。願你有機會驕傲地穿上它們。

column1: You are walking around with a shovel! Surely that is unusual.
column2: 你拿著一把鏟子到處走！這肯定不尋常。

column1: That Freddy! I never know what to expect from you so far!
column2: 那個佛萊迪啊！我從來都猜不透你下一步會做什麼！

column1: I do not wish to be left holding the bag. But you are a thoughtful employer for making the offer of such a rare and unusual substance to me.
column2: 我可不想被丟下來獨自扛責任。不過你願意把這麼罕見又特殊的東西讓給我，真是個體貼的老闆。

column1: I do not need a bag. All I need is all I have.
column2: 我不需要袋子。我需要的，就是我現在擁有的一切。

column1: It is looking better and better, more like an ear all the time! Freddy Pharkas, you are truly a Renaissance lost-wax caster!
column2: 它看起來越來越好了，越來越像一隻耳朵了！佛萊迪·法卡斯，你真是個文藝復興式的脫蠟鑄造大師！

column1: WHAT?
column2: 什麼？

column1: Ha ha, I am pulling down your legs! You have carved correctly!
column2: 哈哈，我這是在扯你的後腿呢！你雕得很正確！

column1: That's be 15 cents, Smithie. But I don't suppose you can pay me.
column2: 這樣是15分錢，史密。不過我猜你大概付不出來吧。

column1: Are yew sayin' I can't pay m'bills fair and square, Pharkas? Heh! Here, I'm a-gonna settle up tabs with you anyway, since I'm leavin' town. Here's whut I owes ya.
column2: 你這是在說俺沒法老老實實付清帳單嗎，法卡斯？哼！來吧，反正俺要離開這鎮子了，俺就跟你把帳結一結。這是俺欠你的。

column1: Smithie pays you his tab. A whole $4.87! Holy moly, a windfall! YOU'RE RICH! (Well, kinda sorta.)
column2: 史密把欠你的帳結清了。整整4塊87分！我的天啊，這下發財了！你發財啦！（嗯，算是啦。）

column1: And if yew takes my advice, yew'll get outta this town, Pharkas. Sheriff's closin' people up right and left. Sumpthin' stinks. An' I mean them horses, 'cuz they's fartin' up a storm! I'm tellin' ya, I wuz like to pass out. Sumbuddy musta put sumpin' in their feed! I don't know what, but I'll tell ya, don't go strikin' no matches out there!
column2: 你要是聽俺的勸，就快離開這鎮子吧，法卡斯。警長正到處抓人關起來呢。有些事情不對勁。俺說的是那些馬，牠們放屁放得跟颳風似的！俺跟你說，俺差點沒昏過去。一定是有人在飼料裡摻了什麼東西！俺是不知道摻了啥，但俺告訴你，千萬別在那附近點火柴！

column1: Good luck to ya, Pharkas. You wuz always one o' the gooduns.
column2: 祝你好運，法卡斯。你一直都是個好人。

column1: Good luck to you, Smithie. Your strong back and gruff-but-good-hearted demeanor will be sorely missed.
column2: 祝你好運，史密。你那身強壯的背脊，還有粗聲粗氣卻心地善良的性子，大家會非常想念的。

column1: But you wuz a strange 'un!
column2: 不過你這人也真是怪！

column1: Fire inspection! I'm here to check out chur fire safety, per the new town regulations. Whoa! Lookee here! It'sa good thing I came. Pharkas, I'ma gonna havta shut this place up tighter than a pissant's scrotum.
column2: 消防檢查！俺是照鎮上新規定，來檢查你這兒的消防安全的。哇！瞧瞧這個！還好俺來了。法卡斯，俺得把這地方關得比什麼都還嚴實。

column1: But, Sheriff! How could you? What's the charge? I haven't done anything wrong!
column2: 可是，警長！你怎麼能這樣？罪名是什麼？我又沒做錯什麼事！

column1: Fire hazard, my boy; fire hazard! Why, this buildin's a terrible fire hazard, Pharkas! Looks tah me like this whole damn buildin's made outta wood!
column2: 消防隱患啊，小子，消防隱患！哎呀，這棟房子根本是個嚴重的火災隱患，法卡斯！俺看這整棟該死的房子根本就是木頭蓋的嘛！

column1: But, Sheriff! Every building in this town is constructed of wood!
column2: 可是，警長！這鎮上每棟房子都是木頭蓋的啊！

column1: I dunno nuttin' 'bout that, son. Tough luck, Pharkas. From now on, just keep the front door locked.
column2: 俺可不管那個，小子。運氣不好啊，法卡斯。從現在起，把前門鎖好就是了。

column1: But what am I supposed to do, Sheriff? This is my livelihood.
column2: 那我該怎麼辦才好，警長？這可是我的生計啊。

column1: If'n I was yew, I'd talk to the bank. Ga'day!
column2: 要是俺是你，俺會去跟銀行談談。祝你順心！

column1: It's a silver medallion, recently awarded to Srini by the American Society of Salves, Holistic Ointments, Liniments and Emollients Salesmen. It was in honor of his impressive and yet oddly comforting display of Ol' Gampy's Fisherman Throat Gullet Descaler Lozenges.
column2: 這是一面銀質獎章，最近由「美國藥膏、整體藥膏、擦劑與潤膚劑推銷員協會」頒發給斯里尼。表彰他令人印象深刻、卻又奇妙地讓人安心的「老甘皮漁夫喉嚨除垢喉片」展售表現。

column1: You carefully remove the medallion from the wall.
column2: 你小心翼翼地把獎章從牆上取下來。

column1: Srini will never miss this.
column2: 斯里尼絕不會發現這東西不見了。

column1: Freddy Pharkas! What in an entirely unsatisfactory afterlife are you doing with my finely-earned silver medallion?
column2: 佛萊迪·法卡斯！你這是在搞什麼鬼名堂，拿著俺辛辛苦苦掙來的銀質獎章？

column1: It's going to a good cause, Srini. It's going to help make Coarsegold a safer, saner place to live.
column2: 這是為了好事，斯里尼。它能幫忙讓粗金鎮變得更安全、更清醒一點。

column1: I am hoping so, Freddy, for all the sakes!
column2: 我也希望如此，佛萊迪，看在大家的份上！

column1: You can't reach the medallion from here. Perhaps you should set up some sort of pincers and mount it on a pivoting armature and get it that way. Or you might try walking over there before taking it.
column2: 你在這裡搆不到獎章。或許你該弄個鉗子，裝在一個能轉動的支架上，用那種方式來取。不然你也可以試試走過去，再把它拿起來。

column1: It's a tube of Preparation G, "The Wells-Fargo Wagon Driver's Friend for Over Half a Decade."
column2: 這是一條「G藥膏」，「威爾斯法哥馬車伕的好夥伴，超過半個十年的信賴」。

column1: You pick up a tube of Preparation G, in the handy 25 oz. "Crabby Elephant" size.
column2: 你拿起一條「G藥膏」，是方便攜帶的25盎司「暴躁大象」尺寸。

column1: You can't reach the Preparation G from back here.
column2: 你在後面這裡搆不到「G藥膏」。

column1: Excuse me, Sadie, I've got to run out for a bit. Hang on, I'll be right back.
column2: 不好意思，莎蒂，我得出去一下。等等，我馬上回來。

column1: Okay, Freddy, but hurry back.
column2: 好啊，佛萊迪，不過要快點回來喔。

column1: Penelope, I have to run out for just a minute or two. You'll wait for me, won't you?
column2: 潘妮洛普，我得出去一兩分鐘。你會等我的，對吧？

column1: Forever, Frederick! But do hurry back, won't you?
column2: 我會等你一輩子，佛雷德里克！不過還是快點回來，好嗎？

column1: Helen, I've got to run out for a minute. I'll be right back, okay?
column2: 海倫，我得出去一下。我馬上回來，好嗎？

column1: Perhaps. Perhaps not. Perhaps I'll be here when you return. Perhaps I'll take my business to another pharmacy. We'll just have to find out, won't we?
column2: 也許吧。也許不會。也許你回來的時候我還在這兒。也許我會把生意轉到別家藥局去。這就得看情況囉，是吧？

column1: I'll be back in a minute, Smithie. Hang in there.
column2: 我一會兒就回來，史密。撐著點。

column1: You dang well better be, Pharkas! These piles is killin' me, dammit! I'm fixin' to nail someone to a wall unless I gets some RELIEF!
column2: 你最好快點回來，法卡斯！這痔瘡快把俺搞死了，該死！俺再得不到「舒緩」，就要把人給釘到牆上了！

column1: Mind the store, won't you, Srini? I'm off to uphold justice and stuff.
column2: 斯里尼，幫我顧一下店好嗎？我要去伸張正義什麼的。

column1: Okee the dokee!
column2: 沒問題的啦！

column1: A short while later...
column2: 過了一會兒……

column1: Srini! Who let you in?
column2: 斯里尼！是誰放你進來的？

column1: Your most gracious Native American, Running Gag, permitted me egress from the outside of the street. It was then that I allowed him to knock himself off for the remainder of the day, since we are still closed.
column2: 是你那位最和善的美洲原住民朋友「跑跑哏」，准許我從街上那頭進來的。之後我便讓他今天剩下的時間都自行離去，反正我們還沒開門營業。

column1: That's fine, Srini. Look, I've reached a decision. My life is in danger. Hell, the whole town's in danger! I must take up gunslinging, and I'll need your help.
column2: 沒關係，斯里尼。聽著，我已經下定決心了。我的性命有危險。見鬼，整個鎮子都有危險！我必須重操槍手的舊業，我會需要你的幫忙。

column1: Pardon this for being said, Freddy Pharkas, but you are a humble Pharmacist. Shooting as perfectionally as a gunslinger is a skill requiring most years of tireless practice. You are ill-equipped. Perhaps you should make peace with your chosen deity and prepare to go to the great Pharmacy Counter in the sky.
column2: 恕我直言，佛萊迪·法卡斯，你不過是個卑微的藥劑師。要像槍手那樣射得完美無缺，是需要多年不懈練習的技藝。你根本準備不足。或許你該跟你信奉的神明和解，準備前往天上那座偉大的藥局櫃檯了。

column1: Srini, you'll have to trust me on this. I used to be a gunslinger before I took up Pharmacology. If I did it before, I can do it again. It shouldn't take long to brush up my skills. I've just gotta find my guns, and do a little practice shootin'.
column2: 斯里尼，這件事你就相信我吧。我在改行做藥劑學之前，曾經是個槍手。我以前做得到，現在也能再做一次。重新練回手感應該花不了多少時間。我只需要找到我的槍，再稍微練練靶就行了。

column1: Very well, Freddy Pharkas. When you are prepared, meet me at the edge of town and together we shall practice what little must be left of your shooting skills, yes.
column2: 好吧，佛萊迪·法卡斯。你準備好了，就到鎮外邊來找我，咱們一起練練你那所剩無幾的槍法，如何。

column1: You were just informed that your prescription-fillin' work was SHODDY. You're not going to hand back the same bad prescription, are you? No, you're not.
column2: 你才剛被告知這帖藥配得亂七八糟。你該不會想把同一帖爛藥原封不動退回去吧？不，你才不會這樣做。

column1: I'm back, Sadie. Sorry for the delay, I just had to check a few things out.
column2: 我回來了，莎蒂。抱歉來遲了，我剛去查了些事情。

column1: Perfectly okay, Freddy, hon. I was just admiring the way you display your goods!
column2: 沒關係啦，佛萊迪，親愛的。我只是在欣賞你展示商品的手藝呢！

column1: Look who's talking!
column2: 你還好意思說！

column1: I'm back, Penelope!
column2: 我回來了，潘妮洛普！

column1: I'm glad, Frederick. I was concerned. Is everything all right?
column2: 太好了，佛萊迪。我剛才還擔心呢。一切都還好嗎？

column1: Everything's fine, now that we're together again.
column2: 一切都好，咱們重聚了就好。

column1: (Blecch! Acccck! Horrrrk!)
column2: （噁！嗚啊！咳嗝！）

column1: Sorry, I just had an errand to run.
column2: 抱歉，我剛去辦點事。

column1: It's about time. Where the hell have you been? I've been worried sick. For all I knew, you were lying dead in a ditch somewhere.
column2: 總算回來了。你到底跑哪去了？我都快擔心死了。搞不好你人已經倒在哪條水溝裡沒氣了呢。

column1: (Geez, no wonder they call her "Mom!")
column2: （天啊，難怪大家都叫她「老媽」！）

column1: Hiya, Smithie! I'm back! Everything okay?
column2: 嗨，史密！我回來了！一切都好嗎？

column1: No, everything's NOT okay, Freddy! M'tushie feels like I sat on a branding iron! Gimmee my Preparation G! I |c2|need|c| my Preparation G, Pharkas!
column2: 不，一點都不好，佛萊迪！我的屁股感覺像被烙鐵燙過一樣！快給我我的G軟膏！我|c2|需要|c|我的G軟膏，法卡斯！

column1: Okay, okay!
column2: 好啦，好啦！

column1: You return!
column2: 你回來啦！

column1: Yep.
column2: 是啊。

column1: It is good to look upon your eternally smiling countenance of face again!
column2: 能再次看見你那張永遠掛著笑容的臉，真是太好了！

column1: Yeah, yeah, I missed you, too.
column2: 是啦是啦，我也想你了。

column1: That Srini! What a guy! He's made a grand and yet peculiarly inviting display of "Ol' Gampy's Fisherman Throat Gullet Descaler Lozenges." He must have heard about that promotional contest being run by the American Society of Salves, Holistic Ointments, Liniments and Emollients Salesmen. (Think about it.)
column2: 那個斯里尼！真有一套！他把「甘皮老船夫牌魚喉去鱗喉片」擺得又氣派又莫名地引人注目。他大概是聽說了「美國藥膏、順勢療法軟膏、擦劑與潤膚劑推銷員協會」在辦促銷比賽。（自己想想這縮寫是什麼。）

column1: Don't touch Srini's handiwork! You never know when one of the roving judges will stop by and check out the display!
column2: 別碰斯里尼的傑作！你永遠不知道巡迴評審什麼時候會突然跑來看這個展示！

column1: Groovy!
column2: 帥呆了！

column1: (GHOULISH VOICE) I'll swallow your soul!
column2: （陰森的聲音）我要吞噬你的靈魂！

column1: This is the cozy little back room of your pharmacy, where you do your heavy thinking. In other words, you don't spend much time here!
column2: 這是你藥局裡溫馨的小後房，你在這裡進行深度思考。換句話說，你其實很少待在這兒！

column1: You open your mouth to say something to it, but words fail you.
column2: 你張嘴想說點什麼，卻一個字也擠不出來。

column1: The pharmacy is falling apart as it is; don't pick at it, you'll just make it worse.
column2: 藥局本來就快散架了；別再摳它，只會讓情況更糟。

column1: That's your laboratory, where you concoct and bottle your formulas.
column2: 那是你的實驗室，你在這裡調配並裝瓶你的配方。

column1: These stairs lead up to your tiny bedroom.
column2: 這道樓梯通往你那間小臥房。

column1: It's a lamp. And a bodaciously ugly one, at that!
column2: 那是一盞燈。而且醜得非常有個性！

column1: The lamp doesn't work. You make a mental note to change the filament. The last piece of cotton thread you used in the bulb only lasted about 45 minutes.
column2: 這盞燈不會亮。你在心裡記下要換燈絲。上次用在燈泡裡的那段棉線，只撐了大概45分鐘。

column1: Some buxom lady's portrait. Notice how the painting seems to follow you around the room? And I don't mean her eyes!
column2: 一幅豐滿女士的肖像。有沒有發現這幅畫好像會跟著你在房裡轉？我說的可不是她的眼睛！

column1: Don't move it, it's covering up the remains of a failed experiment in which you tried to cure the common cold by building up a resistance to mucus.
column2: 別動它，它擋著一場失敗實驗的殘跡——你當初想靠培養對鼻涕的抗性來治感冒。

column1: It's a picture of some nearby big rock.
column2: 那是附近一塊大石頭的畫。

column1: Don't move it, it's covering up the remains of a failed experiment in which you attempted to apply a tourniquet to a sucking chest wound.
column2: 別動它，它擋著一場失敗實驗的殘跡——你當初想用止血帶處理胸部穿刺傷。

column1: Your reference book shelf, complete with such top-ten medical reading as:
column2: 你的參考書架，上頭擺著這些十大醫學讀物，像是：

column1: The only book you'll need to finish this game is the Home Medical guide that came packed in the box. Oh, and perhaps a good 10-volume encyclopedia of Western folklore, if you happen to have one.
column2: 要破完這款遊戲，你唯一需要的書就是包裝盒裡附的《居家醫療指南》。喔，如果手邊剛好有一套十冊的西部民俗百科全書，也許也用得上。

column1: It's your hand-hooked rug. One of Madame's hookers handed it to you!
column2: 這是你手工鉤織的地毯。是歐薇莉夫人那邊一位小姐親手鉤給你的！

column1: You peek underneath the rug, but other than a trap door, you see nothing at all. You wisely decide to avoid investigating it until another day. Waitaminnit, a TRAP DOOR? Oh, that's just the way the floorboards are laid. Never mind, there's no trap door there.
column2: 你掀開地毯偷看，除了一道活門之外什麼也沒有。你明智地決定改天再研究這件事。等等，活門？喔，那只是地板拼接的樣子啦。沒事，那裡根本沒有什麼活門。

column1: You keep a pitcher of water in a basin, so you can occasionally wash your face.
column2: 你在臉盆裡放了一壺水，好讓你偶爾洗把臉。

column1: But you just washed your face last February!
column2: 可是你上次洗臉才二月而已耶！

column1: Why, it's your old roll-top desk. What happened to that roll you recently left on top of it? You've must've eaten it!
column2: 哎呀，是你那張老舊的捲蓋書桌。你最近放在上面的那個捲餅跑哪去了？你一定是把它吃掉了吧！

column1: You keep your anatomical models in here. But don't worry, you're not the only one in town with a few skeletons in your closet!
column2: 你把解剖模型放在這裡。別擔心，鎮上「衣櫃裡藏著骷髏」的可不只你一個！

column1: You haven't been able to open this closet since you tested your new formula, Loony Glue, on it several years ago.
column2: 自從幾年前你在這個櫃子上測試新配方「瘋狂膠水」以來，你就再也打不開它了。

column1: This old table is left over from your college days.
column2: 這張舊桌子是你大學時代留下來的。

column1: Leave that table along until FREDDY PHARKAS, INFERIOR DECORATOR.
column2: 別去碰那張桌子，除非哪天出了《佛萊迪·法卡斯：蹩腳裝潢師》。

column1: This chair was left here by the previous owner of the pharmacy, Franklin Pharquat.
column2: 這張椅子是藥局前任老闆富蘭克林·法夸特留下來的。

column1: You rarely use it. It's uncomfortable, unstable, and unattractive.
column2: 你很少用它。它坐起來不舒服、不穩，而且其貌不揚。

column1: It's an old letter, cobwebbed, yellowed and faded.

column1: What it is, Freddy! I will be getting on that now!

column2: 你把抽屜鎖上了。

column2: 你試著調配一種能治馬兒脹氣的藥。但在你想出辦法「好好呼吸」之前，你根本沒辦法靠近那些馬用它！於是你把它丟了，打算等你弄到某種防毒面具之後再重新調一批。
