column1: We won't let you remove any of the free plugs for other games.
column2: 我們可不會讓你拿走這些幫其他遊戲打的免費廣告。

column1: |c0|General George Armstrong Custer|c| |c1|is looking for|c| |c2|a Few Good Men!|c| Able-bodied Young Men desired for vacation to idyllic Little Big Horn. Intelligent, competent leadership. Wipe out a couple dozen Sioux, how hard can it be? BYOB (Bring Your Own Blunderbuss). Benefits. Contact your local recruiting office.
column2: |c0|喬治·阿姆斯壯·卡斯特將軍|c| |c1|正在招募|c| |c2|優秀好漢！|c| 徵求身強體壯的年輕人，前往世外桃源小巨角河渡假。領導才智出眾、能力過人。剿滅個幾十個蘇族戰士，能有多難？請自備武器（獵槍請自理）。福利優渥。請洽當地招募處。

column1: Hey! Believe it or not, some people ENJOY seeing that crap! Sure, a hundred years from now, they'll probably look back at that kind of entertainment and laugh... but for now, it passes the time!
column2: 嘿！信不信由你，有些人就是喜歡看這種東西！沒錯，一百年後大家回頭看這種娛樂大概會笑出來……可是現在嘛，拿來打發時間剛剛好！

column1: Melancholia? Vapors? Cold? Headache? Neuritis? Neuralgia? Dad Gumm it!
column2: 「憂鬱症？虛煩？感冒？頭痛？神經炎？神經痛？老天爺啊！」

column1: Chester has a contract with DadGummCo stipulating that this sign must remain visible at all times. For which, in return, DadGummCo provides insurance to Chester just in case somebody actually |c0|buys|c| a bottle!
column2: 切斯特跟「老天爺公司」簽了合約，規定這塊招牌必須隨時掛著讓人看見。作為交換，老天爺公司則提供保險給切斯特，以防萬一真有人|c0|買下|c|一瓶！

column1: Many's the day you'd find Willy, Chester, Smithie, and a few others in here, all with their feet up on this old pot-bellied stove, playing checkers, whittling, and expectorating. They stopped doing that after the backs of their ankles got too crispy.
column2: 以前常常能看到威利、切斯特、鐵匠史密和幾個老兄，把腳擱在這座老式圓肚火爐上，一邊下棋、雕木頭、一邊吐痰。後來因為腳踝後側都快烤焦了，他們才不這麼做了。

column1: It's not for sale, dummy, it's a permanent fixture! Kinda like Willy.
column2: 這不賣啦，笨蛋，這是固定裝置！就跟威利差不多。

column1: The heavily-stocked back counter runs along the eastern wall of the General Store. A paper bag lies there.
column2: 貨品堆得滿滿的後櫃台，沿著雜貨店東側牆面延伸。上頭擺著一個紙袋。

column1: None of the items along the back counter are for sale. Chester's stocking up for the Big Quake, which is due any day now.
column2: 後櫃台上的東西一件都不賣。切斯特正在為隨時可能發生的大地震囤貨。

column1: This coffee grinder from the 1883 Shear's Catalog makes TWO big cranks they've got in this store!
column2: 這台咖啡研磨機是從一八八三年的希爾斯型錄訂購來的，可是這家店裡像它這樣『愛發牢騷的老搖桿』可有兩支呢！

column1: This coffee grinder is Chester's private property. He won it in his divorce settlement.
column2: 這台咖啡研磨機是切斯特的私人財產，是他離婚協議裡爭取到的。

column1: (PUNCH LINE) Divorced? On what grounds?
column2: （哏）離婚？是因為咖啡『渣』太多嗎？

column1: |c0|Wanted: Dead or Alive!|c| |c0|Kwai Chang Caine|c| Alias "The Grasshopper" Alias "Hey, you! Chinaman!" Unarmed but extremely dangerous. Reward: $25 worth of Turd-All Wax, $50 worth of Ed's Kimono Pies, and a $100 gift certificate to the famous Shwingle Catalog. Over 50,000 quality items providing value, selection & economy. Shwingle, Chicago, Illinois, 60609!
column2: |c0|通緝：不論死活！|c| |c0|關長·凱恩|c| 別名「蚱蜢」 別名「喂，你，中國佬！」 雖然手無寸鐵，但極度危險。賞金：價值25元的「屎多蠟」、50元的艾德和服派、以及價值100元的知名「史溫格型錄」禮券。超過五萬件優質商品，經濟實惠、選擇多多。史溫格，伊利諾州芝加哥市，郵遞區號60609！

column1: Hey, this guy is still on the loose. He keeps popping up every few years, just when you thought he was canceled... er, caught.
column2: 嘿，這傢伙到現在還逍遙法外呢。他每隔幾年就會冒出來一次，就在你以為他已經被『取消』……呃，被逮到的時候。

column1: It's the General Store's front door.
column2: 這是雜貨店的正門。

column1: Willy, I'm in need a way to disguise my ear. Do you think you could do something creative with this, something in the shape of an ear, perhaps?
column2: 威利，我需要一個辦法來遮住我的耳朵。你覺得你能不能用這個發揮點創意，弄個耳朵形狀之類的東西出來？

column1: Offhand, I'd say, do it yer dang self! M'nap time's comin' up shortly, I've had a hard day of whittlin'. But you could mebbe do sum lost-wax castin' with this sucker'd do the trick.
column2: 俺直接跟你說，自己動手做吧！俺的午睡時間快到了，今天雕了一整天的木頭累壞了。不過你或許可以拿這玩意兒做個失蠟鑄造，應該行得通。

column1: Lost... wha?
column2: 失……什麼？

column1: Lost-wax castin', son! Whut'd you do, sleep yer way through metal shop?
column2: 失蠟鑄造，小子！你是怎麼搞的，金工課都在睡覺嗎？

column1: I guess I must've. What's "lost-wax casting?"
column2: 我想我大概是吧。什麼是「失蠟鑄造」？

column1: That's "castin'," with an apostrophe, sonny, not an "ing." Anyhoo, yew kin make all sortsa things by makin' a wax positive, using clay to make a mold, then meltin' down the metal and pourin' it inter a mold.
column2: 是加一撇的「鑄造′」，小子，不是「造型」。反正呢，你先做出一個蠟模正型，再用黏土做個模具，然後把金屬融化，倒進模具裡，就能做出各種東西啦。

column1: I think so. I'm not sure.
column2: 我想是吧。我不太確定。

column1: Welp, that's whut yur "restore" button's fer, kiddo. Now scrambooch.
column2: 呃，那就是你的『讀取』鍵派上用場的時候啦，小鬼。行了，快滾吧。

column1: I already tole ya, it'd make fer sum fine lost-wax casting'!
column2: 俺已經跟你說過了，這拿去做失蠟鑄造再好不過啦！

column1: The door swings open. From the back, you hear Chester's voice.
column2: 門被推開了。你聽見切斯特的聲音從後面傳來。

column1: Help yourself. I'll be right out.
column2: 自己隨便看。我馬上出來。

column1: It's Whittlin' Willy's authentic whittlin' knife.
column2: 這是削木威利真正在用的雕刻刀。

column1: You "borrow" Whittlin' Willy's knife for awhile.
column2: 你先『借』走削木威利的刀，用一陣子。

column1: Considering that there's nothing for sale here, you wonder why Chester even bothers keeping these brown paper sacks around.
column2: 既然這裡什麼都不賣，你不禁納悶切斯特幹嘛還留著這些牛皮紙袋。

column1: You take a complimentary paper bag.
column2: 你拿了一個免費贈送的紙袋。

column1: Those are wood shavings from Willy's skillful whittlin'.
column2: 這些是威利精湛雕工削下來的木屑。

column1: Too bad you won't need any, since they're obviously available... at substantial shavings!
column2: 可惜你用不上，反正這些東西顯然要多少有多少……根本『屑』手可得！

column1: It won't be worth taking 'till it's hardened.
column2: 這東西要等它變硬了才值得拿。

column1: This is a bottle of Mom's home-pressed apple cider. Mom is merciless to those poor apples. As she turns the press, she screams, "Die, you suckers, die!"
column2: 這是一瓶老媽自家壓榨的蘋果西打。老媽對那些可憐的蘋果毫不留情，轉動壓榨機的時候，她會尖叫著：「去死吧，你們這些傢伙，去死！」

column1: If you value your right hand -- and we |c2|know|c| you do -- don't be opening Mom's cabinets.
column2: 要是你重視自己的右手──我們|c2|知道|c|你很重視──就別打開老媽的櫃子。

column1: Rumor has it that Helen Back keeps the heads of her three dead husbands somewhere behind the Melmac plates and dishes in that china cabinet.
column2: 傳言說海倫·貝克把她三任已故丈夫的頭顱，藏在那個碗櫃裡的美耐皿盤子後面。

column1: Oh, oh, oh! You in big water now!
column2: 喔喔喔！你這下可闖大禍啦！

column1: |c2|LOOK WHAT YOU'VE DONE!!|c| Freddy Pharkas, I'll see you run out of town for this!! Hop Singh, hop to it! Get out here and clean up this mess! Damn these flies!
column2: |c2|你看看你幹的好事！！|c| 佛萊迪·法卡斯，你這次死定了，我一定把你趕出這個鎮！！阿星，還不快動起來！快出來把這團亂清乾淨！這些該死的蒼蠅！

column1: Mom offers free coffee to her regular customers. You're as regular as anyone -- 11 a.m. every morning, you head straight for the outhouse! So, as usual, you pour yourself a steamin' hot cuppa joe.
column2: 老媽會提供免費咖啡給她的常客。你可比誰都「規律」──每天早上十一點，你就直奔戶外廁所！所以呢，你照往常一樣，幫自己倒了杯熱騰騰的咖啡。

column1: Mr. Pharkas, I have no objection to your coming in here and taking a cup of coffee. But please, limit yourself to one cup at a time. Or I will have no choice but to break your skinny bones like matchsticks. Are we clear on this now? Good.
column2: 法卡斯先生，你要進來喝杯咖啡，我沒意見。可是拜託，一次只准喝一杯。不然我就沒得選，只好把你那瘦巴巴的骨頭像火柴一樣折斷。這樣說清楚了嗎？很好。

column1: You take another cup of coffee.
column2: 你又倒了一杯咖啡。

column1: Oh, sure. Mom's bottomless pot of coffee. Drink up all my profits, why don't you? Take cup after cup. What do you think, I'm running a restaurant here?
column2: 喔，可以啊。老媽這壺咖啡就是無底洞。你乾脆把我的利潤全喝光算了，是不是？一杯接一杯地喝。你以為我在這裡開的是什麼，慈善餐廳嗎？

column1: Sor-REE! Gee, Mom, get off my back! Nag, nag, nag!
column2: 抱~歉喔！天啊，老媽，別再唸我了！碎碎唸，碎碎唸！

column1: It's one of those newfangled Ol' Missuh Coffee machines. Helen sets it out every other day for free coffee.
column2: 這是那種新潮的「老爺咖啡機」。海倫每隔一天就會擺出來，提供免費咖啡。

column1: You won't need any of |c2|that|c| corn... you're getting enough corn playing this game.
column2: 你用不著|c2|那種|c|玉米……光是玩這款遊戲，你受的芭樂梗就已經夠多了。

column1: But that can is full of corn! You'll get corn-packing-juice all over everything!
column2: 可是那罐頭裡裝滿了玉米啊！你會把玉米罐頭的湯汁灑得到處都是！

column1: P&W Corn: "Firm, crisp kernels that look as good coming out as they do going in!"
column2: P&W玉米：「顆粒紮實爽脆，吃進去跟排出來一樣好看！」

column1: You see nothing on the counter worth snitching.
column2: 你看了看櫃台，沒發現什麼值得順手牽羊的東西。

column1: Mom's counter is clean and spanking-white. Helen Back is anal-retentive about cleanliness.
column2: 老媽的櫃台乾淨得發亮，一塵不染。海倫·貝克對整潔可是有嚴重潔癖的。

column1: Fer cryin' out loud! You've dropped a horse pie in the middle of Mom's Cafe! What could you have been thinking of? It wasn't lunch, that's for darn tootin'.
column2: 我的老天爺啊！你居然在老媽餐館正中央拉了一坨馬糞！你到底在想什麼？那絕對不是什麼午餐，這點錯不了。

column1: Damned flies! This place is like a stable! Maggots crawling through the door and flies circling the ceiling! What's this town coming to? Flies in the summer, snow fleas in the winter. God, but I miss Missouri! Hop Singh, haven't you put up those no-pest strips yet?!?
column2: 這些該死的蒼蠅！這裡簡直跟馬廄一樣！蛆從門口爬進來，蒼蠅在天花板上繞圈子！這個鎮是怎麼回事啊？夏天有蒼蠅，冬天有雪蚤。天啊，我好懷念密蘇里！阿星，你還沒把那些防蟲條掛上去嗎？！？

column1: Freddy Pharkas! Look what you brought in with you. What's next? Honestly.
column2: 佛萊迪·法卡斯！看看你身上又帶了什麼進來。接下來還會有什麼？真是服了你。

column1: Sorry, Mom. They on order.
column2: 抱歉，老媽。它們已經在訂購中了。

column1: There are too many to catch, and they're too fast.
column2: 牠們太多了，而且動作太快，根本抓不到。

column1: A swarm of flies makes a constant circuit inside the Cafe. They're the bane of Mom's existence! Along with customers, employees, or anyone who talks to her or has anything to do with her in any way.
column2: 一群蒼蠅在餐館裡不停繞圈子飛。牠們是老媽存在的最大剋星！客人、員工，或任何跟她說過話、有過任何往來的人，同樣也是。

column1: Hello, Flies! If I chase that nasty ol' Mom away with a stick, will you give help me find a magic key or something?
column2: 嗨，蒼蠅們！要是我拿棍子把那個討厭的老媽趕跑，你們願意幫我找把魔法鑰匙之類的東西嗎？

column1: They just buzz at you a little bit. Don't forget, this ain't fantasy, this is REALITY!
column2: 牠們只是對你嗡嗡叫了幾聲。別忘了，這裡不是奇幻世界，這是現實！

column1: Mom would cut off your testicles and serve them for lunch. Knowing the locals, they'd enjoy 'em!
column2: 老媽會把你的睪丸割下來當午餐上桌。就這裡的居民來說，他們搞不好還吃得津津有味！

column1: Helen Back, a.k.a. "Mom," loves to decorate her dining room with fresh-cut flowers. But since there are no flowers in Coarsegold, she makes do with these sprouted collard green tops.
column2: 海倫·貝克，也就是「老媽」，很喜歡用新鮮花朵裝飾她的餐廳。可是粗金鎮沒有花，她只好將就用這些發芽的羽衣甘藍菜頭充數。

column1: Hmmph. Dunno who around here will eat these, since they don't give you gas, but I'll put them in a bag of cornstarch and think about it. And I suppose a thank-you is in order, so thank you.
column2: 哼。也不知道這附近誰會吃這個，反正它們也不會讓人脹氣，不過我會先裝進玉米粉袋裡再考慮考慮。而且我想我是該說聲謝謝，那就謝了。

column1: Are you implying that my customers are in need of bicarbonate?
column2: 你這是在暗示我的客人都需要吃胃藥嗎？

column1: You've got your nerve! At least MY customers aren't sick when they walk in the DOOR!
column2: 你好意思講！至少我的客人走進門的時候還沒生病！

column1: You narrowly avoid making an obvious comeback.
column2: 你差點就要脫口說出一句顯而易見的回嘴，還好忍住了。

column1: Do you see a liquor license anywhere on the wall?
column2: 你有在牆上看到什麼賣酒執照嗎？

column1: Then take that out of here before I get my butt hauled into the pokey!
column2: 那就快把那東西拿出去，免得我的屁股被抓去蹲苦窯！

column1: Are you implying that my steaks are as tough as leather?
column2: 你這是在暗示我的牛排跟皮革一樣硬嗎？

column1: Not at all, I was just...
column2: 完全沒有，我只是……

column1: Take those smelly old things out of here before I lose any sense of aroma I might already have had.
column2: 快把那些臭烘烘的老東西拿出去，免得我僅存的一點嗅覺也跟著報銷。

column1: Those are certainly not fit for human consumption!
column2: 那些東西絕對不適合人類食用！

column1: But then, what in this Cafe IS?
column2: 話說回來，這間餐館裡到底有什麼東西適合？

column1: If it isn't carnauba wax, take it away.
column2: 如果那不是巴西棕櫚蠟，就拿走吧。

column1: It isn't.
column2: 才不是。

column1: Take it away.
column2: 拿走。

column1: We don't do any GRILLING here, you fool! We FRY!
column2: 我們這裡不用「烤」的，傻瓜！是用「炸」的！

column1: Oh, if only she would!
column2: 唉，她要是肯就好了！

column1: Do I look like a person who's lost a key?
column2: 我看起來像是弄丟鑰匙的人嗎？

column1: Not exactly, but...
column2: 也不是啦，不過……

column1: Then take it away! Honestly, some people's children.
column2: 那就拿走啊！真是的，有些人家教養出的孩子。

column1: That's not going to be ready 'til Tuesday.
column2: 那個要到星期二才會好。

column1: Oh. I was hoping to...
column2: 喔，我是希望……

column1: It was a joke. A JOKE! Do you even understand what a joke is? Honestly.
column2: 那是個笑話。笑話啦！你到底懂不懂什麼叫笑話？真是的。

column1: That's clay! What am I supposed to do with it? Are you implying my complexion isn't what it ought to be?
column2: 那是黏土耶！你要我拿它做什麼？你是在暗示我的膚色不夠好嗎？

column1: No, I'm...
column2: 不是，我是……

column1: Then take it away. I've never been so insulted in all my life.
column2: 那就拿走。我這輩子還沒被這樣侮辱過。

column1: Nothing HERE needs cleaning! We thoroughly wash everything before serving it. Isn't that right, Hop Singh?
column2: 這裡沒有什麼東西需要清潔！我們上菜前都徹底洗過了，對吧，阿星？

column1: You told me not to waste water except when health department man...
column2: 你跟我說過除非衛生局的人來，不然不要浪費水……

column1: It was a rhetorical question, dammit. Hop Singh: back to work. Freddy: stop pestering me.
column2: 那是反問句啦，該死。阿星，回去工作。佛萊迪，別再煩我了。

column1: I wouldn't be caught DEAD in an outfit like that! What do I look like, some sort of cowboy?
column2: 我死也不會穿那種衣服！我看起來像牛仔嗎？

column1: No, cowboys don't put on their makeup with putty knives!
column2: 不像，牛仔才不會用抹刀上妝呢！

column1: If you don't like it, you don't have to drink it.
column2: 你不喜歡的話，不喝就是了。

column1: You idiot, it's the HORSES that are sick, not my customers! They're all happily dining on my freshly-cooked specialties.
column2: 你這笨蛋，生病的是馬，不是我的客人！他們都開開心心地在吃我現做的招牌菜呢。

column1: Well, I never!
column2: 哼，真是沒見過！

column1: Maybe that's why she's so tense and irritable all the time.
column2: 也許這就是她整天緊繃易怒的原因。

column1: I don't need that! I never get indigestion!
column2: 我不需要那個！我從來不消化不良！

column1: You eat here, don't you?
column2: 你不是在這裡吃飯嗎？

column1: Heavens no! I send out. What do you think I am, crazy?
column2: 老天，才不是！我都叫外送。你當我瘋了不成？

column1: I don't want your steenkin' empties!
column2: 我才不要你那些臭空瓶！

column1: You've got something absolutely putrid in that bag, Freddy Pharkas!
column2: 你那袋子裡裝的東西臭死了，佛萊迪·法卡斯！

column1: So you want me to take it out of the restaurant?
column2: 所以你要我把它拿出餐館？

column1: You might as well. We've already prepared the Blue Plate Special for today.
column2: 你最好這麼做。我們今天的招牌套餐都已經準備好了。

column1: Well, that's a fine how-do-you-do! Walking in here with a doggie bag and expecting me to fill it for you.
column2: 哼，真是好樣的！拿個打包袋走進來，還指望我幫你裝滿。

column1: I wasn't...
column2: 我沒有……

column1: Oh, of course you were. I don't want to hear another word about it.
column2: 喔，你當然有。我不想再聽你多說一個字。

column1: We're SAFE in here, you dolt! There's no gas in here!
column2: 我們在這裡很安全，你這呆子！這裡沒有瓦斯！

column1: Really? Has she tried the Chili 'n Broccoli Surprise?
column2: 真的嗎？她試過「辣椒花椰菜驚喜」了沒？

column1: That filth will attract flies! Get it out of here at once! You are truly disgusting! I'm flabbergasted! I'm speechless!
column2: 那髒東西會招蒼蠅的！馬上拿出去！你真是噁心到家了！我目瞪口呆！我無言以對！

column1: As if!
column2: 才怪！

column1: Tell me, what do I need an ice pick for when I've got Hop Singh's hands? They're deadly weapons! They're registered!
column2: 你說說看，我有阿星這雙手，還要冰錐做什麼？那雙手可是致命武器！還登記有案呢！

column1: I don't remember needing anything from the Pharmacy right now. So pawn it off on one of your other victims!
column2: 我不記得現在需要藥局的任何東西。拿去甩給你其他受害者吧！

column1: I already told you that I don't want that. Would you like me to find a NEW PLACE to put it?
column2: 我已經跟你說過我不要那個了。你要我幫你找個新地方塞嗎？

column1: I don't think so.
column2: 我看不用了。

column1: Good! I don't relish the thought either.
column2: 很好！我也不想去想那畫面。

column1: I've got plenty of knives here already. I'm not ill-equipped, you know! Honestly.
column2: 我這裡刀具多得很。我可不是沒傢伙可用，你知道嗎！真是的。

column1: I don't need a ladder. Whatever Hop Singh or I can't reach, we just throw things at.
column2: 我不需要梯子。阿星跟我搆不到的東西，我們就用丟的。

column1: Get that rope away from me. I'm no heifer!
column2: 把那條繩子拿開。我又不是小母牛！

column1: Not much!
column2: 才沒有咧！

column1: What am I supposed to do with a leather strap? Honestly.
column2: 你要我拿皮帶做什麼？真是的。

column1: Normally I'd LOVE to read somebody else's mail. But I'm just a bit busy right now.
column2: 平常我最愛偷看別人的信了。可是我現在有點忙。

column1: Helen Back, proprietor of Mom's Cafe, is better known as Mom.
column2: 海倫·貝克，老媽餐館的老闆娘，大家都叫她「老媽」。

column1: If she was my Mom, I'd run away from home!
column2: 她要是我老媽，我早就離家出走了！

column1: So your assistant won a medal. Big deal. Hop Singh's won more Cordon Bleu awards than you can shake a spatula at.
column2: 所以你的助手拿了個獎章，了不起啊。阿星拿過的藍帶獎章，多到你數不清。

column1: You don't owe me any money. You haven't bought anything from me in ages! You just come in here for the free coffee! Honestly.
column2: 你沒欠我錢。你已經好久沒跟我買過東西了！你只是來這裡蹭免費咖啡的！真是的。

column1: Take that ragged old napkin away. I'd never use such a garish piece of garbage. Honestly!
column2: 把那條破爛的舊餐巾拿走。我才不會用那種俗氣的破布呢。真是的！

column1: I don't know what that is, but I don't find it the least bit funny!
column2: 我不知道那是什麼，但我一點也不覺得好笑！

column1: Figures.
column2: 早就猜到了。

column1: Where did that come from? That looks like one of Hop Singh's!
column2: 那是哪來的？看起來像是阿星的東西！

column1: I must confess, I took it. I need it. I promise to repay you.
column2: 我得承認，是我拿的。我需要它。我保證會還你。

column1: You'd better! I don't want THAT one back anymore, you've dented it!
column2: 你最好是！那個我可不要了，你都弄凹了！

column1: Seriously? You want to shoot this sweet old lady? The one everybody calls "Mom?" Yeah, good idea, but you just can't!
column2: 你是認真的嗎？你要對這位善良的老太太開槍？大家都叫她「老媽」的那位？嗯，想法是不錯，可你就是不能這麼做！

column1: Take this smut out of here instantly! Wait a second, let me see those. Got 'er, got 'er, want 'er, got 'er, want 'er, had 'er, need 'er, want 'er, got 'er, got 'er. OK, thanks! Now get that smut out of here immediately!
column2: 把這些低俗東西馬上拿出去！等等，讓我瞧瞧。有了、有了、想要、有了、想要、有過、需要、想要、有了、有了。好，謝啦！現在馬上把這些低俗東西拿出去！

column1: My backside is scarcely in need of lubrication! Honestly.
column2: 我的屁股才不需要什麼潤滑呢！真是的。

column1: I don't cook with water. I cook with 100% fatback. So we won't be needing any of your half-assed concoctions in here!
column2: 我做菜不用水。我用百分之百的豬背油。所以我們這裡用不著你那半調子的玩意兒！

column1: Take that filthy thing out of here. It's got graveyard clay all over it!
column2: 把那髒東西拿出去。上面全是墓地的黏土！

column1: Morning, Helen!
column2: 早啊，海倫！

column1: Freddy Pharkas! Since when are we on a first-name basis? Only my closest friends may call me "Helen." You and I are acquaintances, nothing more. Therefore, you should address me as "Mom."
column2: 佛萊迪·法卡斯！我們什麼時候變得可以直呼名字了？只有我最親近的朋友才能叫我「海倫」。你我不過是點頭之交罷了。所以你該叫我「老媽」。

column1: Land's sake, I'm sorry, Hel... er, Mom!
column2: 我的老天，抱歉，海……呃，老媽！

column1: That's better. Now, what did you want?
column2: 這樣才對。好了，你想要什麼？

column1: Uh... When I remember, I'll let you know.
column2: 呃……等我想起來再跟你說。

column1: Honestly, some people.
column2: 真是的，某些人哪。

column1: Hel... Mom! Did you know that the Hotel's been shut down?
column2: 海……老媽！你知道飯店被停業了嗎？

column1: Why, of course I did! Where on earth have you BEEN, Freddy Pharkas?
column2: 哎呀，我當然知道！你到底跑到哪裡去了，佛萊迪·法卡斯？

column1: Any idea of who did it, or why?
column2: 知不知道是誰幹的，還是為什麼？

column1: Sheriff Shift and Phineas were there, talking about it being a fire hazard and something about there being back rent owed. But I'm no gossip. Don't go by what I'm telling you!
column2: 席夫特警長跟菲尼亞斯當時都在，說什麼消防安全問題，還有拖欠房租的事。不過我可不是愛嚼舌根的人。你可別拿我說的話當真！

column1: Have you heard anything else?
column2: 你還聽到什麼別的嗎？

column1: I'm no gossip, Freddy Pharkas, and I've got work to do. Why don't you go do yours? Yes, I believe that's the best idea. You get along and get back to work.
column2: 我可不是那種愛嚼舌根的人，佛萊迪，我還有活要幹呢。你怎麼不去做你自己的事？對，我看這樣最好。你走吧，回去工作。

column1: Mom, I apologize for leaving that little souvenir with you.
column2: 老媽，我很抱歉留了那個小「紀念品」給你。

column1: I'm not talking to you right now. I'm ashamed to be your Mom. Now you just turn right around and go outside and THINK about what you've done for awhile. You can come back in here when you decide to behave like a human being again.
column2: 我現在不想跟你說話。當你的媽我覺得丟臉。你給我轉身出去，好好想想自己做了什麼。等你決定重新做人了，再進來。

column1: Mom, there was a fire last night that almost burned the whole town down.
column2: 老媽，昨晚有場火幾乎把整個鎮給燒了。

column1: Don't you think I saw that for myself on the way to work this morning? Honestly!
column2: 你以為我今早上班路上沒親眼看到嗎？真是的！

column1: Fortunately, I was able to put the fire out with a little baking soda.
column2: 幸好，我用了一點小蘇打就把火撲滅了。

column1: So THAT'S the stench I've been smelling! What an inconsiderate clod you can be. That burnt baking-soda smell is simply nauseating. It's no wonder I've got no customers today.
column2: 原來我一直聞到的臭味就是那個！你這個人怎麼這麼不體貼。那股燒焦小蘇打的味道真讓人反胃。難怪我今天一個客人都沒有。

column1: I thought I was doing the town a favor.
column2: 我還以為自己是在幫鎮上的忙呢。

column1: Well, next time, think a little harder.
column2: 哼，下次多用點腦子想想。

column1: Mom, I'm going to be leaving town awhile. Just wanted to tip m' hat and say thanks.
column2: 老媽，我要離開鎮上一陣子。就想跟你脫帽致意，說聲謝謝。

column1: Fool, you're not even wearing a hat.
column2: 傻瓜，你根本沒戴帽子。

column1: And in case I don't see you again, I think you're a brave, feisty, spry li'l lady.
column2: 萬一我們沒機會再見，我想說你是位勇敢、潑辣、精神抖擻的小姑娘。

column1: Why, you condescending twerp, I'm not a "little lady," and if you ever call me "feisty and spry" again, you'll need a blacksmith to help you swallow your lunch.
column2: 你這自以為是的小混蛋，我才不是什麼「小姑娘」，你要是再敢叫我「潑辣、精神抖擻」，就得找鐵匠幫你把午飯塞回喉嚨了。

column1: Yes, well... so long, now.
column2: 是，好啦……那就再會了。

column1: Whatever.
column2: 隨便啦。

column1: Mom, where are all your customers?
column2: 老媽，你的客人都跑哪去了？

column1: Damned if I know. They all jumped up at more or less the same time and ran to the outhouse. It's not my fault, though. They hadn't even et yet. Just had a glass of water, and bam, they're gone. If you tell anyone about it, you're dead meat on a hook.
column2: 我哪知道。他們差不多同一時間跳起來，衝去茅廁。不過這不是我的錯。他們根本還沒吃東西呢。就喝了杯水，然後咻一下就不見人影。你要是敢跟別人說，我就把你掛鉤上當肉乾。

column1: That sounds fair.
column2: 聽起來很公平。

column1: Mom, you'd better keep everyone inside 'til I can get this horse flatulence thing straightened out.
column2: 老媽，你最好把大家都留在裡面，等我把這馬匹脹氣的事情搞定。

column1: Not that it's any of your business, but I'll be keeping my customers in here as long as I can. 'Course, if they just keep ordering weak tea and Uwanna Biscuits, I'll toss their butts into the street. Can't make any money selling tea and frickin' biscuits!
column2: 這不關你的事，不過我會盡量把客人留在裡面。當然，他們要是一直點淡茶跟「你懂的」餅乾，我就把他們踢到街上去。賣茶跟該死的餅乾哪賺得了錢！

column1: Mom, what do you know about ants?
column2: 老媽，你對螞蟻了解多少？

column1: Keep your voice down, Freddy Pharkas. That was a long time ago, and I paid the fine and got rid of the ants.
column2: 小聲點，佛萊迪·法卡斯。那是很久以前的事了，我付了罰款，也把螞蟻清乾淨了。

column1: No, I meant wild ants.
column2: 不，我是說野生的螞蟻。

column1: You're talking crazy talk. There's no such thing as domesticated ants. Ants is ants. Now get out before you scare away the customers.
column2: 你在胡說八道什麼。哪有什麼家養的螞蟻。螞蟻就是螞蟻。快出去，免得把客人都嚇跑了。

column1: What customers??
column2: 什麼客人啊？？

column1: Mom, Mom!
column2: 老媽，老媽！

column1: Let me guess. You only have one cavity.
column2: 我猜猜看。你只有一顆蛀牙。

column1: Huh? No, I wanted to know if you have any salt. There's a stampede of snails a-comin', and I need to stop 'em.
column2: 啊？不是，我是想問你有沒有鹽。有一大群蝸牛要衝過來了，我得阻止牠們。

column1: I don't know anything about no stampede. Unless they're stopping here to eat, I don't even care. As for salt, you KNOW we're a salt-free community! That's why everyone's so laid back. Low blood pressure. And we aim to keep it that way.
column2: 我對什麼蝸牛群一無所知。除非牠們是來這裡吃飯的，不然我才懶得管。至於鹽嘛，你明明知道我們是個無鹽小鎮！這就是為什麼大家都這麼悠哉，血壓又低。我們打算繼續保持下去。

column1: Dang! Well, what could I use?
column2: 該死！那我能用什麼？

column1: Beer works for me. I just spread a little of it out along the back porch and the little buggers just follow it right off!
column2: 我都用啤酒。我就在後門廊灑一點，那些小東西就乖乖跟著走了！

column1: Jeez, Mom, thanks.
column2: 老天，老媽，謝啦。

column1: Now git outta here!
column2: 現在快滾出去！

column1: Helen, have you ever thought of putting escargot on the menu?
column2: 海倫，你有沒有想過在菜單上加個法式蝸牛？

column1: You've already taken it, I don't want it back. Like I said, take it out of here, I'm sick of the sight of it. Honestly!
column2: 你已經拿走了，我不要拿回來。我說過了，拿出去，我看到就煩。真是的！

column1: We don't serve beer in here, Freddy Pharkas.
column2: 我們這裡不供應啤酒，佛萊迪·法卡斯。

column1: It's water, it's just in a beer bottle.
column2: 這是水，只是裝在啤酒瓶裡而已。

column1: Do you think I was born yesterday, Freddy Pharkas?
column2: 你當我是昨天才出生的嗎，佛萊迪·法卡斯？

column1: Obviously not.
column2: 顯然不是。

column1: Well! I never!
column2: 哼！真是沒見過！

column1: Well! Maybe you SHOULD!
column2: 哼！也許你就該多見識見識！

column1: I must say, Freddy Pharkas, that's pretty clever of you. You DID get points for that, didn't you?
column2: 我得說，佛萊迪·法卡斯，這招挺聰明的。你該加分了吧？

column1: Yes, Ma'am.
column2: 是，夫人。

column1: I should hope so.
column2: 那是當然。

column1: That looks like Saloonware, not Cafeware.
column2: 那看起來是酒館的東西，不是餐館的。

column1: No no! Only need bicarbonate AFTER eating food, not during preparation phase!
column2: 不不！碳酸氫鹽要吃完飯「之後」才需要，不是在準備階段！

column1: Prefer plum wine! You got any plum wine?
column2: 比較想要梅酒！你有沒有梅酒？

column1: Uh... no.
column2: 呃……沒有。

column1: Thought not! Nobody in town ever get plum wine! Bah!
column2: 就知道沒有！鎮上沒人搞得到梅酒！哼！

column1: Not mine! Hop Singh's feet bound to take smaller size!
column2: 不是我的！阿星的腳要穿小一號的！

column1: Hmm... not need bullets, not called for in repertoire of recipes!
column2: 嗯……不需要子彈，食譜裡用不到！

column1: Not need wax, unless you got carnauba wax for pastries. You got any carnauba wax?
column2: 不需要蠟，除非你有做糕點用的巴西棕櫚蠟。你有巴西棕櫚蠟嗎？

column1: Same all over town! Feh!
column2: 全鎮都一樣！呸！

column1: Ahh, perfect for hibachi! You got hibachi?
column2: 啊，拿來烤肉正好！你有火缽嗎？

column1: Um... nope.
column2: 嗯……沒有。

column1: Nobody got Hibachi in Coarsegold. Sad, sad!
column2: 粗金鎮沒人有火缽。可悲，可悲！

column1: Not need key! Hop Singh welcome everywhere in Coarsegold. You welcome everywhere in Coarsegold?
column2: 不需要鑰匙！阿星在粗金鎮到處都受歡迎。你在粗金鎮到處都受歡迎嗎？

column1: Nooooo, I couldn't say that.
column2: 不……這我可不敢說。

column1: Didn't think so! Hop Singh most popular in town!
column2: 就知道你不敢！阿星是鎮上最受歡迎的人！

column1: Ah, so! Be ready Tuesday! Sorry, little joke. Cousin Lo Fat have laundry in New York. Hop Singh not know what claim check for.
column2: 啊，是喔！星期二準備好！抱歉，開個小玩笑。表弟羅發在紐約開洗衣店。阿星不知道領據是幹什麼用的。

column1: Ooh, Freddy Pharkas make lousy pudding! Very gummy, bad flavor.
column2: 哦，佛萊迪·法卡斯做的布丁真難吃！又黏又難吃。

column1: That not mine! Hop Singh use cleaver, not gun!
column2: 那不是我的！阿星用菜刀，不用槍！

column1: Very bad taste! Turquoise and beige. Try black and red and yellow. Now that is color combination.
column2: 品味真差！綠松石配米黃。試試黑配紅配黃。那才叫配色。

column1: You not like it, you don't have to drink it. Hop Singh not want it back.
column2: 你不喜歡，不喝就好。阿星不要拿回去。

column1: I look like horse to you?
column2: 我在你眼裡像匹馬嗎？

column1: Nay. I mean, no.
column2: 不。我是說，不像。

column1: Good! Then take away!
column2: 好！那就拿走！

column1: Not in front of food!
column2: 別在食物前面弄這個！

column1: Hop Singh fit as fiddle! Not needing nostrums!
column2: 阿星身體好得很！不需要什麼偏方！

column1: We not accept empties. Sorry!
column2: 我們不收空瓶。抱歉！

column1: Ooh, take away before Mom sees! Mom keep very neat restaurant, not appreciate bag of flatulent.
column2: 哦，趁老媽還沒看到快拿走！老媽的餐館整潔得很，才不欣賞一袋屁味。

column1: We already have plenty doggie bags.
column2: 我們打包袋多得很。

column1: Hop Singh have advanced filtration nostrils, not need gas mask. Thank you kindly anyway!
column2: 阿星的鼻子過濾功能一流，不需要防毒面具。不過還是謝謝你的好意！

column1: No, no, no, no, no! Take away! Mom make me clean that up if you leave it here!
column2: 不、不、不、不、不！拿走！你放在這裡老媽會叫我清理！

column1: Hop Singh use karate to chop ice, not needing ice pick.
column2: 阿星用空手道劈冰，不需要冰錐。

column1: You already offer that to me! What, you no take "no" for answer? No, no, no!
column2: 你已經給過我這個了！怎麼，你聽不懂「不要」嗎？不、不、不！

column1: You not want to threaten Hop Singh. I break bones like that.
column2: 你不會想威脅阿星的。我一根手指就能把骨頭折斷。

column1: Not needing ladder. Everything in kitchen down low.
column2: 不需要梯子。廚房裡的東西都擺得很低。

column1: Always wanted one of these! You have one made out of silk?
column2: 一直想要這種東西！你有沒有絲做的？

column1: Oh, gee, not on me.
column2: 喔，天哪，我身上沒有。

column1: Too bad. You find silk lasso, let me know. Hop Singh got kinky idea.
column2: 真可惜。你找到絲套索，記得跟我說。阿星有個刺激的點子。

column1: That pretty pitiful whip. Much too short and flat.
column2: 那條鞭子真可憐。太短又太扁了。

column1: So sorry, cannot read that. Lost contacts.
column2: 真抱歉，看不清楚。隱形眼鏡弄丟了。

column1: It's Hopalong Singh, Helen's faithful cook from the Far East. He used to work as a professional chef for a chain of Ponderolla restaurants.
column2: 他是阿星（全名霍帕龍·星），海倫忠實的遠東大廚。他以前在「彭德羅拉」連鎖餐廳當過專業主廚。

column1: Very nice medallion! Congratulate Srini for me!
column2: 勳章真漂亮！替我恭喜斯里尼！

column1: Not need your money. Mom pay me better than I make in San Francisco. Develop "Nouvelle Frontier" cuisine. Very popular!
column2: 不需要你的錢。老媽付的薪水比我在舊金山賺得還多。我還開發了「新邊疆料理」，很受歡迎！

column1: Nice quality neckerchief. Where you steal it from?
column2: 領巾質料真好。你從哪偷來的？

column1: Steal it? Don't be silly. It's mine!
column2: 偷？別傻了。那本來就是我的！

column1: Uh-huh. Never seen you with neckerchief before.
column2: 嗯哼。從沒看過你戴領巾。

column1: I had it put away for safekeeping. It's my lucky neckerchief.
column2: 我把它收起來保管。這是我的幸運領巾。

column1: Ah, no wonder you have so little luck lately.
column2: 啊，難怪你最近這麼倒楣。

column1: No, thank you. Hop Singh not in laughing mood just now.
column2: 不，謝了。阿星現在沒心情笑。

column1: That pie look awfully familiar! Look like one I just made awhile ago and now is missing! Where you find it?
column2: 那個派看起來眼熟得很！好像是我剛做好又不見了的那個！你從哪找到的？

column1: Uh... my Mom sent it to me. Yeah, that's it, my Mom sent it to me.
column2: 呃……是我老媽寄給我的。對，就是這樣，我老媽寄給我的。

column1: Let me smell that! (SNIFF SNIFF) Say! You Mom almost as bad a baker as I am! I cannot bake pie to save life!
column2: 讓我聞聞！（嗅嗅）嘿！你老媽做的糕點跟我一樣爛！我做派爛到要命！

column1: You level the pistol at Hop Singh.
column2: 你把手槍對準阿星。

column1: Do not try it! Wearing bulletproof apron! Hah!
column2: 想都別想！我穿的是防彈圍裙！哈！

column1: Not interested in looking at pictures of American women.
column2: 沒興趣看美國女人的照片。

column1: They're French, not American.
column2: 她們是法國人，不是美國人。

column1: Even worse! You got pictures of chocolate desserts?
column2: 那更糟！你有巧克力甜點的照片嗎？

column1: Uh... no, sorry.
column2: 呃……沒有，抱歉。

column1: Nobody in Coarsegold got pictures of chocolate desserts. Phooey!
column2: 粗金鎮沒人有巧克力甜點的照片。哼！

column1: That for tea?
column2: 那是泡茶用的？

column1: Well, it's for the town's water supply.
column2: 呃，是要給鎮上的供水用的。

column1: Then no concern to me.
column2: 那就不關我的事。

column1: Nice rope, so?
column2: 繩子不錯，然後呢？

column1: Shovel very dirty. Please to remove it from restaurant before Mom have hissy fit.
column2: 鏟子髒得很。請在老媽發飆前把它拿出餐館。

column1: Hmm, mediocre quality snail. Very tough, make chewy appetizers. You show to Mom, she make buying decisions. Hop Singh just work here.
column2: 嗯，普普通通的蝸牛，很老又韌，只夠做嚼不動的前菜。你拿去給老媽，她做主意，阿星在這裡就是做工的。

column1: Howdy, Hop! How's the restaurant business?
column2: 嘿，阿星！餐館生意怎麼樣啊？

column1: Pretty slow! Not much business. Seem like town closing up and blowing away.
column2: 很差！沒什麼生意。感覺整個鎮好像要關門收攤，隨風飄走了。

column1: You've noticed that too, have you?
column2: 你也注意到了，是吧？

column1: Oh, yes. First Old Abandoned Mine, then Assay Office, then Post Office, then Tall & Thin Shop, then Theatre, yesterday Hotel. What next?
column2: 喔，是啊。先是廢棄舊礦坑，然後驗金所，然後郵局，然後高瘦服飾店，然後劇院，昨天輪到旅館。下一個是什麼？

column1: Well, I intend to get to the bottom of this.
column2: 這件事，我打算查個水落石出。

column1: Maybe hurry, before Mom's next to go! Hop Singh not want to lose his job!
column2: 你最好快點，免得下一個輪到老媽！阿星可不想丟了這份工作！

column1: Can I ask you a question, Hop Singh?
column2: 我可以問你一個問題嗎，阿星？

column1: What's that?
column2: 什麼問題？

column1: It's an inquiry, an interrogative sentence calling for an answer. But that's not important right now. I'd like to know if you've got something against pronouns, contractions and conjunctions. You use so few of them.
column2: 就是一種疑問句，需要你回答的問句。不過這不是重點。我想知道，你是不是對代名詞、縮寫和連接詞有什麼意見？你用得也太少了。

column1: (IN BEAUTIFUL BRITISH ACCENT) I can anytime I like. It's simply that Helen Back paid me handsomely to come and act like an "authentic" Chinese chef. Granted nobody actually speaks like this, but she seems to THINK people speak like this. So, hey, she cuts the checks, I just play along. (CHINESE AGAIN:) That answer question?
column2: （一口標準英倫腔）我想講的時候隨時都能講標準的。只是老媽花大錢請我來扮演一個「道地」的中國廚子。老實說，沒有人真的這樣講話，但她就是認為中國人講話該是這個調調。嘿，反正她付錢，我就配合演一下。（切回洋涇濱腔調：）阿星這樣回答，可以嗎？

column1: Perfectly. Thanks!
column2: 完美，謝了！

column1: Freddy Pharkas again! What with you? I have restaurant to run, you still have Pharmacy to run, yes?
column2: 又是佛萊迪·法卡斯！你又怎麼了？阿星有餐館要顧，你不是也有藥局要顧嗎？

column1: Er... yes.
column2: 呃……是啊。

column1: Then get back to it! I busy here!
column2: 那就回去顧你的！阿星這裡忙著呢！

column1: Hop Singh, you're not mad at me, are you?
column2: 阿星，你該不會在生我的氣吧？

column1: |c0|OUT! OUT! OUT!|c| Hop Singh not want you slinging the bull in here no more.
column2: |c0|滾！滾！滾出去！|c|阿星不想再聽你在這裡胡扯瞎掰了。

column1: But it was an accident! It slipped, okay?
column2: 可是那是意外！它自己滑掉的，好嗎？

column1: Slip? Slip? What you carrying that plop around for in first place? How stupid can one pharmacist get? Honestly!
column2: 滑掉？滑掉？你一開始幹嘛帶著那坨東西到處跑？一個藥師能笨到什麼地步？真是服了！

column1: Uh-oh, he's been hanging around Mom too long!
column2: 糟了，他跟老媽混太久，講話都學她了！

column1: Say, Hop! Hear about the big fire last night?
column2: 欸，阿星！聽說昨晚那場大火了嗎？

column1: Oh yes! Very dramatic.
column2: 喔，聽說了！超戲劇性的。

column1: I came to the rescue, though. Put out the fire single-handedly!
column2: 不過是我出手相救的。我一個人就把火撲滅了！

column1: Ohhh, very good. We all proud of you. You BMOC!
column2: 喔喔，真厲害。大家都以你為榮。你現在是BMOC了！

column1: BMOC?
column2: BMOC是啥？

column1: Big Mensch Of Coarsegold!
column2: 粗金鎮第一大好人的意思啦！

column1: Hop Singh, I'll be leaving town for a while.
column2: 阿星，我要離開小鎮一陣子。

column1: Okay! Hate long goodbyes! Sayonara!
column2: 好啊！阿星最討厭拖拖拉拉的道別！莎唷娜拉！

column1: I'll miss you, too.
column2: 我也會想你的。

column1: Sayonara!
column2: 莎唷娜拉！

column1: You've been just like a chef to me.
column2: 你對我來說，就像個廚師一樣。

column1: SAYONARA! Arrivederci! Adios! Hasta la vista!
column2: 莎唷娜拉！再會啦！阿迪歐斯！下次見啦！

column1: Gee, I don't know much Chinese, Hop, so I don't know what you just said, but... goodbye.
column2: 天啊，我沒學過什麼中文，阿星，所以不知道你剛才講了什麼，不過……再見啦。

column1: GOODBYE!
column2: 再見！

column1: Hey, Hop Singh! Don't serve any water 'til I've had a chance to check it out. I think something's up with the water supply.
column2: 欸，阿星！先別供應任何水，等我檢查過再說。我覺得水源可能出了問題。

column1: No problemo! This California. We not serve water with meals unless customer beg.
column2: 沒問題！這裡是加州。除非客人求我們，不然本來就不會附水。

column1: Hop Singh, I just want to warn you NOT to go outside and NOT to let your customers go outside 'til we've cleared the air.
column2: 阿星，我只是想提醒你，絕對別出門，也別讓客人出門，等我們把空氣清乾淨再說。

column1: We having big argument or something?
column2: 我們是在吵什麼大架嗎？

column1: No, not that I know of.
column2: 沒有啊，我不知道有這回事。

column1: Then why need to clear the air?
column2: 那幹嘛要「把空氣弄乾淨」？

column1: Never mind. Go outside all you like.
column2: 算了，你想出去就出去吧。

column1: Thank you for kind permission!
column2: 多謝你大發慈悲的許可！

column1: Hey, Hop Singh, you know anything about getting people off of anthills?
column2: 欸，阿星，你知不知道怎麼把人從蟻丘上弄下來？

column1: Not hardly!
column2: 完全不知道！

column1: Thanks, you're a big help.
column2: 謝了，你真是幫了大忙。

column1: You not talk to me like that. I got big cleaver.
column2: 你不准這樣跟我說話，阿星可是有把大菜刀的。

column1: Have you heard, Hop Singh? Thar's a stampede a-comin'!
column2: 阿星，你聽說了沒？牛群暴衝要來啦！

column1: Nobody tell Hop Singh nothing back here. Hop Singh could fall over and die and rot and nobody would even know for days.
column2: 在這後面沒人跟阿星說半句話。阿星就算倒地死掉爛掉，大概也沒人會發現，搞不好好幾天都沒人知道。

column1: Well, I'm telling you now.
column2: 好啦，我現在不就在跟你說了。

column1: Ye, yeh. Go and leave Hop Singh to suffer in silence. So what if everybody ignore me? So what if nobody talk to me back here, except Mom when she want something? So what if Hop Singh slave over hot steam table all day and work fingers to the bone?
column2: 是啦，是啦。你就走吧，留阿星一個人默默受苦。大家都不理我又怎樣？這後面除了老媽要使喚我以外，沒人跟阿星講話又怎樣？阿星整天在滾燙的保溫台前累得跟牛一樣，做到十指都要斷掉又怎樣？

column1: I thought you were going to suffer in silence.
column2: 我還以為你要默默受苦呢。

column1: OK for you, Freddy Pharkas! You get yours, you see! You just like all the rest! Vamoose!
column2: 好啊，你狠，佛萊迪·法卡斯！你等著瞧，總有一天會有報應！你跟其他人沒兩樣！滾開！

column1: That brand of beans we use! Some coincidence!
column2: 那正好是我們用的那個牌子的豆子！真巧啊！

column1: I got this can here. Mom gave it to me.
column2: 我這裡有個空罐子，是老媽給我的。

column1: Oh! Impressed. Mom not give old empty tin can to just anyone. Must really like you!
column2: 喔！真讓人佩服。老媽可不是隨便什麼人都給空罐子的。她一定很喜歡你！

column1: Hop Singh not beer-drinker!
column2: 阿星才不喝啤酒！

column1: This is water, not beer.
column2: 這是水，不是啤酒。

column1: Oh-ho, you very sneaky, try to get Hop Singh drunk and give away cooking secrets.
column2: 喔∼你很奸詐喔，想灌醉阿星，套出烹飪秘方。

column1: That's truly not what I had in mind.
column2: 我真的沒那個意思。

column1: Do you no good! Hop Singh not HAVE any cooking secrets! Play it by ear! Guess that twice the work for you, eh? Heh!
column2: 對你一點用都沒有！阿星根本沒有什麼烹飪秘方！全靠隨機應變！看來你要多費一倍工夫囉？嘿嘿！

column1: Very clever! Hop Singh hope you get big points for that.
column2: 很聰明嘛！阿星希望你這招能拿到不少分數。

column1: A-yep!
column2: 啊，對啊！

column1: Good, good! You be hero yet!
column2: 很好，很好！你這樣下去，遲早會變英雄的！

column1: Hop Singh have no need of empty glass.
column2: 阿星用不著空杯子。

column1: You can't reach anything in the kitchen from here.
column2: 你在這裡搆不到廚房裡的任何東西。

column1: Mom's kitchen is spotlessly clean and efficiently-run.
column2: 老媽的廚房一塵不染，運作得有條不紊。

column1: The kitchen counter. (Let's see... you count 1 kitchen!)
column2: 廚房流理台。（讓我數數看……你數到1個廚房！）

column1: There's nothing on the counter you need.
column2: 流理台上沒有你需要的東西。

column1: Hopalong Singh (Hop, for short) doesn't take kindly to people invading his inner sanctum.
column2: 「霍帕龍·星」（大家都簡稱阿星）可不喜歡有人闖進他的私人聖地。

column1: Nobody goes into my kitchen without my permission. |c0|Nobody,|c| do you hear?
column2: 沒有我的允許，誰都不准進我的廚房。|c0|誰都不准，|c|聽到了嗎？

column1: Heed her warning. The last customer who crossed Mom ended up on the Blue Plate Special.
column2: 最好聽她的警告。上一個惹毛老媽的客人，最後成了「今日特餐」。

column1: These swingin' kitchen doors do nothing to keep the smells in the kitchen.
column2: 這幾扇廚房彈簧門，完全擋不住味道飄出來。

column1: You poke her in the shoulder pad. Ewww! It's all mushy and bloated! Charlotte doesn't even glance at you. She's too busy talking with her mouth full.
column2: 你戳了戳她的墊肩。噁！軟軟爛爛、鼓鼓脹脹的！夏洛特連看都沒看你一眼，她正忙著滿嘴食物講八卦呢。

column1: Yes, it's SOOOO tempting! But you'll have to restrain your murderous impulses. It's just not in character.
column2: 是啊，真的超級誘人！不過你還是得壓抑住殺意，這不符合你的人設。

column1: She's too intent on getting her just desserts to care about that.
column2: 她一心只顧著吃她的甜點，才沒空理你這個。

column1: Charlotte Russe, one of the local gossips, is stuffing her face with dessert, a sponge cake and whipped cream monstrosity. It makes your arteries seize up just looking at her!
column2: 夏洛特·露絲，鎮上的長舌婦之一，正大口塞著甜點——一坨海綿蛋糕加鮮奶油的恐怖巨物。光看著她吃，你都覺得自己的血管要塞住了！

column1: Hello, Mrs. Russe. That sure is a lovely dessert you're wearing today!
column2: 你好啊，露絲太太。你今天「穿」的這道甜點還真是漂亮呢！

column1: (GARBLED) Mmph gluphum truph aphuphuphum.
column2: （含糊不清）嗯呣咕嚕嚕呣咕嚕呣。

column1: You poke Sarah in the back, but she doesn't stop talking for a moment. What concentration! What dedication! What a MOUTH!
column2: 你戳了戳莎拉的背，但她講話一刻也沒停。真是專心！真是敬業！真是一張大嘴巴！

column1: That would be justice, wouldn't it? Sarah's stabbed so many people in the back, it would only be fair for someone to turn the tables. But a first-degree murder charge might interfere with your efforts to save the town just now.
column2: 這樣也算是一種正義吧？莎拉在背後捅了那麼多人一刀，也該有人反過來對付她一下才公平。不過，一項一級謀殺罪名，恐怕會妨礙你現在拯救小鎮的大業。

column1: She's far too busy cutting down people she hardly knows to bother with the likes of you. Maybe you should offer her a saucer of milk!

column1: Uh-oh. He's slipped into one of his "Mister Potter" moods.
column2: 糟了，他又進入『波特先生』模式了。

column1: Well, you don't shcare me! You kin take yer lousy bulletsh and your crummy ol' Building & Loan and get out of my offish!
column2: 哼，你嚇不倒我的！把你那些爛子彈跟破儲貸社通通帶走，滾出我的辦公室！

column1: It's clay.
column2: 這是黏土。

column1: You're a liar, thash what you are! Ish CLAY!
column2: 你根本就是個騙子！這明明是黏土！

column1: I guess you're right.
column2: 我想你說得對。

column1: You bet your ash I'm right. Now take it away from me, whatever it is.
column2: 我說得沒錯，灰都不用燒。快把那玩意兒從我面前拿走，管它是什麼。

column1: Whoa! A shilver medallion! You mus' be shum hotshot!
column2: 哇！一枚銀質獎章！你一定是個大人物！

column1: Actually, it belongs to Srini, my faithful Indian companion.
column2: 其實這是斯里尼的，我那忠心的印度夥伴。

column1: Ahh, shum hero! Shtealin' from hish own shidekick! <|c2|hic|c|>
column2: 啊，好一個英雄！居然偷自己夥伴的東西！<|c2|hic|c|>

column1: Auuugh! You killed the tin man!
column2: 啊啊啊！你把錫人殺了！

column1: What? I made this. This is my ear.
column2: 什麼？這是我做的，這是我的耳朵。

column1: Well, why ishn't it on the shide of your head, where it belongsh?
column2: 那它怎麼沒長在你的頭側呢，它該待的地方？

column1: Good question.
column2: 問得好。

column1: These are my old gunslinging clothes.
column2: 這是我以前當槍手時穿的衣服。

column1: I don't want your CHARITY, George Bailey! Gwan back to your drafty ol' Building and Loan! What are you but a warped, frushtrated young man! Go on, run! <|c2|hic|c|> <|c2|belllch|c|>
column2: 我才不要你的施捨，喬治·貝里！滾回你那間四處漏風的儲貸社去！你不過是個扭曲、鬱悶的年輕人！去啊，跑啊！<|c2|hic|c|><|c2|belllch|c|>

column1: Oh, yeah. <|c2|hic|c|> That vashectomy will be ready on Tueshday.
column2: 喔對了。<|c2|hic|c|>那個結紮手術星期二就可以了。

column1: What? I didn't order a vasectomy.
column2: 什麼？我根本沒預約結紮手術。

column1: Waitaminnit... <|c2|bellllch|c|> Who are you? Wha... you're not Sam! Get outta here!
column2: 等一下……<|c2|bellllch|c|>你是誰啊？什…你不是山姆！滾出去！

column1: Say, thanks much, Doc.
column2: 欸，真是謝了，大夫。

column1: Anytime, m'boy, anytime! <|c2|burrrp|c|>
column2: 隨時都行，孩子，隨時都行！<|c2|burrrp|c|>

column1: Hey, you shtole my bootsh! <|c2|hic|c|> How did you do that?
column2: 欸，你偷了我的靴子！<|c2|hic|c|>你怎麼辦到的？

column1: These are MY bootsh. I mean, my BOOTS.
column2: 這是我的靴——子。我是說，我的靴子。

column1: Oh. Then what did you do with my whishky?
column2: 喔。那你把我的威士忌怎麼了？

column1: It's right in front of you. And all over you.
column2: 就在你面前啊。而且灑得你全身都是。

column1: Thash good, lesh keep it that way.
column2: 這樣挺好，就繼續這樣吧。

column1: Aauuugggh! A bloody bandage!
column2: 啊啊啊！血淋淋的繃帶！

column1: It's my lucky red bandanna.
column2: 這是我的幸運紅頭巾。

column1: A red banana? <|c2|hic|c|> Don't eat it, ish not ripe yet.
column2: 紅香蕉？<|c2|hic|c|>別吃啊，還沒熟呢。

column1: How do you ekshpect me to read thish? <|c2|bellllch|c|> Shumbody wrote all over it.
column2: 你要我怎麼看得懂這個？<|c2|bellllch|c|>上面被人亂寫一通。

column1: Ow! Shtop hittin' me with that.
column2: 唉唷！別再拿那個打我了。

column1: Pyew! Wussat?
column2: 呸！這什麼玩意？

column1: It's a sickness bag.
column2: 這是嘔吐袋。

column1: I think shumbody wuz already shick in it!
column2: 我看已經有人在裡面吐過了！

column1: Whaddayoo want me to... <|c2|hic|c|>... me to do with THAT?
column2: 你要我……<|c2|hic|c|>……拿那個幹嘛？

column1: I want to sober you up. C'mon, put this bag over your head or breathe into it or something.
column2: 我想讓你醒醒酒。來，把這袋子套在頭上，或朝裡面呼吸都行。

column1: Whuffor? So's I kin shee whut a hellhole of a town I'm shtuck in? So I kin shee whut a mesh I've made of my life?
column2: 幹嘛？好讓我看清楚自己困在這個鳥地方？好讓我看清楚自己把日子過成什麼爛樣？

column1: No, so you can stop writing illegible and incorrect prescriptions ... and get rid of the hiccups.
column2: 不是，是要你別再開那些看不懂又出錯的處方箋……順便把打嗝治好。

column1: Thash you all over, you shelfish shwine... alwaysh thinkin' of yourshelf! <|c2|hic|c|>
column2: 你這人就是這樣，自私的傢伙……滿腦子都是你自己！<|c2|hic|c|>

column1: Aaaaugh! You melted one of the horshes! Ah, you liquidated it, eh? Very reshorshful. <|c2|hic|c|>
column2: 啊啊啊！你把一匹馬融化了！啊，把牠變成液體啦？真有辦法。<|c2|hic|c|>

column1: Actually, I was hoping the stench would sober you up.
column2: 其實我是希望這股臭味能讓你醒醒酒。

column1: It shmells like roses to me. <|c2|burrrrp|c|>
column2: 我聞起來像玫瑰一樣香呢。<|c2|burrrrrp|c|>

column1: It's amazing how drunk you must be for this to smell good to you.
column2: 你到底得醉成什麼樣子，才會覺得這味道好聞，真是不可思議。

column1: I didn't shay it shmelt GOOD! I said it shmelt like ROSE'S! Ish my favorite brand of whishky, I'm drinking shum now.
column2: 我又沒說好聞！我是說聞起來像『玫瑰牌』！那是我最愛喝的威士忌牌子，我現在正喝著呢。

column1: Arrrrgh! Ish an ear! Wheresh the ranshom note?
column2: 啊啊啊！是一隻耳朵！贖金紙條呢？

column1: This is a wax ear, not a real ear. Does it look anatomically correct to you?
column2: 這是蠟做的耳朵，不是真的耳朵。你覺得它解剖構造正確嗎？

column1: Very convinshing! Of coursh, I knew it was fake all along.
column2: 很……很有說服力嘛！當然啦，我早就知道那是假的。

column1: But there's a new aroma about the Doc that indicates that maybe you DID fool him, just for a few seconds!
column2: 不過大夫身上飄出一股新的味道，顯示你「這幾秒鐘」搞不好真的唬到他了！

column1: I can't tell anything about thish, Pharmamarmamarmashist! <|c2|hic|c|> I'd need to shee the preshcription. <|c2|bellllch|c|>
column2: 我搞不清楚這是什麼名堂啦，藥……藥……藥劑濕使！<|c2|hic|c|> 我得瞧……瞧瞧處方箋才行。<|c2|bellllch|c|>

column1: It's "Zircon" Jim Laffer. Years from now, his brother Ezekial will sire a son... who will beget Ethan... who will beget Bartholomew... who will beget Lawrence. That's right! He's Leisure Suit Larry's great-great-grandfather!
column2: 那是「鋯石」吉姆·拉弗。多年以後，他弟弟以西結會生下一個兒子……那兒子會生下伊森……伊森會生下巴瑟洛謬……巴瑟洛謬又生下勞倫斯。沒錯！他就是風流拉里的曾曾祖父！

column1: Howdy, stranger. New in town?
column2: 你好啊，陌生人。剛到鎮上吧？

column1: Hi! I sure am, and I'm looking for a hot time. I've been noticing some of your fine Coarsegold fillies, and I wouldn't mind an introduction! Perhaps you could put in a good word for me with one of them?
column2: 嗨！沒錯，我正想找點刺激的樂子。我一直在留意你們粗金鎮這些漂亮的小妞，要是能介紹一下我可不介意！能不能幫我跟其中一位美言幾句？

column1: 'Course, I know a lotta you boys gotta PAY for your fun, but I figger a guy with my looks and breath, hey, they should be payin' ME, y'know? Right? Right! By the by, my name's Laffer... Zircon Jim Laffer. Don't believe I caught yours.
column2: 當然啦，我知道你們這些小夥子玩樂都得花錢，不過我尋思像我這副長相跟口氣，該是她們倒貼我才對吧？對吧？沒錯！對了，我叫拉弗……「鋯石」吉姆·拉弗。還沒請教尊姓大名呢。

column1: Whoops, I think I smell something burning, or something. Catch you later.
column2: 哎呀，我好像聞到什麼東西燒焦的味道。回頭見啦。

column1: Whew! What rock did HE crawl out from under?
column2: 嘖！他是從哪塊石頭底下爬出來的啊？

column1: You prod him, just to see if he's real or some sort of waxwork.
column2: 你戳了戳他，想看看他是真人還是什麼蠟像。

column1: Hey, there! Don't be touching me, fella! Don't want the womenfolk to be gettin' the wrong idear! I'm a MAN'S man, y'know? I mean, I'm a woman's man, but a MANLY man. Say, did I catch your name? Mine's Laffer... Zircon Jim Laffer.
column2: 嘿，那邊那位！別碰我啊，老兄！我可不想讓女人家誤會什麼！我可是個「男人中的男人」，你懂吧？我是說，我喜歡女人，但骨子裡是個有男子氣概的男人。對了，還沒請教你的大名？我叫拉弗……「鋯石」吉姆·拉弗。

column1: Uh, sorry, I was looking for somebody else.
column2: 呃，抱歉，我在找別人。

column1: Whew!
column2: 呼！

column1: If I give you this, will you go away?
column2: 要是我把這個給你，你會走開嗎？

column1: Are you kidding? You give me one of THOSE, and I'll be your friend forEVER! Bosom buddies! Ol' pal, ol' bean! Together, whatever the weather! Two of a kind! You and your shadow! Inseperable!
column2: 你在開玩笑嗎？你給我這種東西，我這輩子都跟你當朋友！知心好友！老搭檔、老夥伴！風雨同路！一對活寶！你跟你的影子！誰也分不開！

column1: You hurriedly stick it back in your pocket, rather than face further companionship!
column2: 你趕緊把它塞回口袋，免得又惹出更多交情！

column1: What an excellent idea! But if you do that, Leisure Suit Larry will never have been born, and you'll throw Sierra On-Line into a time-space paradox from which it will never recover.
column2: 好主意啊！不過要是你真這麼做，風流拉里就永遠不會出生，還會把雪樂山公司捲進一場永遠解不開的時空悖論裡。

column1: Sam Andreas owns and runs the Golden Balls Saloon. He's smart, savvy, and generous to a fault.
column2: 山姆·安德烈亞斯是金球酒館的老闆兼經營者。他精明幹練，而且大方到近乎過頭。

column1: Well, if it ain't Sam Andreas, the bartender's bartender!
column2: 哎呀，這不是山姆·安德烈亞斯嗎，酒保中的酒保！

column1: If it ain't, I'm having a severe identity crisis.
column2: 要不是的話，那我可就有嚴重的身分認同危機了。

column1: How the heck are ya?
column2: 你這傢伙過得怎樣啊？

column1: Tolerable well. Yourself?
column2: 還算過得去。你呢？

column1: Can't complain. Pharmacy business seems to be pretty good lately.
column2: 沒什麼好抱怨的。藥局生意最近看來挺不錯。

column1: Ah. Well, the pharmacy business has always been a little TOO interesting for me to hear about, so hey, don't be a stranger.
column2: 啊。這個嘛，藥局的生意對我來說一向「有趣」過頭了點，所以啊，別跟我這麼見外。

column1: Say, Sam, I think I'll take an Ovaltine.
column2: 對了，山姆，我看我就來杯阿華田吧。

column1: In a cracked glass?
column2: 用有裂痕的杯子裝嗎？

column1: Yes, with a hair in it, too.
column2: 對，裡面再加根頭髮。

column1: And the usual lipstick smear on the glass?
column2: 杯緣照例抹點口紅印？

column1: Yep, and a ring of dried soap around the inside lip.
column2: 沒錯，杯口內側再留一圈乾掉的肥皂垢。

column1: On a coaster?
column2: 要墊杯墊嗎？

column1: No, I like leaving rings on your bar.
column2: 不用，我就愛在你吧台上留水漬圈。

column1: Rocks with that?
column2: 要加冰塊嗎？

column1: No, but some ice cubes would be nice.
column2: 不用，不過來點冰塊倒是不錯。

column1: We're outta ice cubes.
column2: 我們的冰塊用完了。

column1: Then I'll take it straight.
column2: 那我就喝純的吧。

column1: Out of Ovaltine, too.
column2: 阿華田也沒了。

column1: Oh. Okay, I'll check back later!
column2: 喔。好吧，那我晚點再來看看！

column1: Feel free.
column2: 隨時歡迎。

column1: Got any Ovaltine in stock yet?
column2: 阿華田進貨了嗎？

column1: Oh, yes, in the last ten minutes we got in a whole wagonload.
column2: 喔，有啊，過去十分鐘才剛進了滿滿一馬車。

column1: Really? Wow.
column2: 真的假的？哇。

column1: No. I was being sarcastic because you were asking a stupid question.
column2: 不是啦。我只是在諷刺你問了個蠢問題。

column1: Sam, Sam! Don't let anyone go out on the street 'til I give you the say-so. The town's being smothered in horse gas. I don't know how it's happened, but I'm gonna do something it 'afore we all choke to death.
column2: 山姆，山姆！在我點頭之前，別讓任何人上街。整個鎮都被馬屁味燻得快窒息了。我不曉得是怎麼回事，但我得在大家被嗆死之前想個辦法。

column1: Yeah, I thought somebody'd burnt some popcorn or something. Silent-but-deadly, for sure. But don't worry about my customers, Fred. They're not going anywhere.
column2: 嗯，我還以為是誰把爆米花燒焦了咧。肯定是那種「無聲卻要命」的貨色。不過別擔心我這些客人，佛萊迪，他們哪兒也不會去。

column1: Sam! There's a stampede headed for town! Don't go outside!
column2: 山姆！一大群牛正朝鎮上狂奔而來！別出去！

column1: We're open 24 hours a day, Fred. I never go outside. Besides, the sun dries out my beautiful skin.
column2: 我們二十四小時營業，佛萊迪。我從不出門。再說，太陽會把我這身美肌曬乾的。

column1: I'm just saying, y'know, for your own safety.
column2: 我只是說說，你知道的，為了你的安全著想。

column1: Gotcha. Tell you what: I'll stay in here and serve drinks and collect money. You run around outside like a chicken with your head cut off and save the town. Okay? Okay.
column2: 懂了。這樣吧：我留在這裡倒酒收錢，你去外面跟隻沒頭蒼蠅似地跑來跑去救鎮上的人。可以吧？可以。

column1: Sam, have you noticed what's going on in this town?
column2: 山姆，你注意到這鎮上發生什麼事了嗎？

column1: A-yep.
column2: 啊，是啊。

column1: Sheriff Shift's closed up half the businesses in town, including mine.
column2: 謝夫警長把鎮上一半的店都關了，包括我的藥局在內。

column1: A-yup.
column2: 啊，對啊。

column1: Somebody deliberately poisoned the horse's feed with lentils and tried to gas the whole town!
column2: 有人故意在馬飼料裡摻了扁豆，想用臭氣把整個鎮給薰倒！

column1: A-yip.
column2: 啊，是喔。

column1: I think somebody's trying to wreck Coarsegold, and us along with it.
column2: 我覺得有人想毀掉粗金鎮，順便把我們一起拖下水。

column1: A-yeah?
column2: 啊，真的假的？

column1: We've got to do something about it. We've got to band together and save ourselves.
column2: 我們得做點什麼才行。我們得團結起來，自己救自己。

column1: And you're just the guy to help me.
column2: 而你正是能幫我這個忙的人。

column1: A-nope.
column2: 啊，不要。

column1: Then I guess I'll have to find someone else to help me.
column2: 那我看只好去找別人幫忙了。

column1: A-mebbe.
column2: 啊，也許吧。

column1: Sam, anything unusual going on?
column2: 山姆，有什麼不尋常的事嗎？

column1: A lot of my customers have headed off to the outhouse to "wash their hands," or so they say.
column2: 我不少客人都跑去戶外茅房「洗手」了，至少他們是這麼說的。

column1: That can't be so odd.
column2: 這也沒什麼好奇怪的吧。

column1: Well, usually they just wash their hands out against the side of the building. Must be a number two kinda thing.
column2: 嗯，平常他們都直接對著牆邊「洗手」。這回大概是「大號」那種事吧。

column1: Hmmm... hmmm...
Sam, come quick! The assay office is on fire!
column2: 山姆，快來！驗金所著火了！

column1: Geez, Fred, I'd love to help, only I'm watching the saloon.
column2: 天哪，佛萊迪，我也很想幫忙，但我得看著酒館。

column1: There isn't going to BE a Saloon if we don't put this fire out.
column2: 要是我們不把火撲滅，酒館遲早也保不住。

column1: You'll think of something. Just throw your weight around a little. I'm not worried.
column2: 你會有辦法的。使點分量壓一壓場面就行了。我一點都不擔心。

column1: Grrrrrrrrr!
The fire's out at the Assay Office, Sam. You can stop panicking.
column2: 驗金所的火滅了，山姆。你可以不用再慌了。

column1: Oh, yes, the fire at the Assay Office. I was all in a tizzy for a while there.
column2: 喔，對了，驗金所那場火。我剛才可真是慌了好一陣子。

column1: Sam, I'm gonna be going away for a while.
column2: 山姆，我要離開一陣子。

column1: OK. We'll forward your mail.
column2: 好。我們會幫你轉信。

column1: Aren't you going to ask why I'm leaving?
column2: 你不問問我為什麼要走嗎？

column1: What for? You're going to tell me anyway.
column2: 問了幹嘛？反正你也會自己說出來。

column1: I'm a marked man. Sheriff Shift, P.H. Balance and somebody called "The Boss" are out to get me. So I'm skipping town.
column2: 我現在是個被盯上的人。謝夫警長、P.H. Balance，還有個叫「老大」的傢伙都想對付我。所以我打算離開這鎮子。

column1: Smart move. Give my regards to Broadway.
column2: 聰明之舉。幫我向百老匯問聲好。

column1: To what?
column2: 向哪裡問好？

column1: Never mind. Good luck to you.
column2: 沒事，算了。祝你好運。

column1: Howdy, Sam.
column2: 你好啊，山姆。

column1: You still here? I thought you were leaving town.
column2: 你還在這兒？我還以為你要離開鎮上了。

column1: I am, I am! Don't rush me! You're not going to see me around these parts. No sir-ee, Bob. I'll be gone with the wind. Outta town by sundown. Whoosh. No more Freddy Pharkas.
column2: 我要走啊，我要走！別催我！以後你在這一帶再也見不到我了。沒錯，絕對不會。我會像風一樣消失。日落前就出鎮。咻地一聲。再也沒有佛萊迪·法卡斯這個人了。

column1: Sounds like a plan.
column2: 聽起來是個計畫。

column1: Okay, Sam, you beat it out of me.
column2: 好吧，山姆，算你厲害，問出我的底細了。

column1: Say what?
column2: 你說什麼？

column1: I'll tell you the truth, because I know I can trust you.
column2: 我就跟你說實話吧，因為我知道你信得過。

column1: You do, do you?
column2: 是嗎，信得過我？

column1: I'm not REALLY leaving town at all. I'm going to put on a disguise and save the town once and for all. You won't know it's me, though, by the time I'm finished.
column2: 我其實根本沒打算離開這鎮子。我要喬裝改扮，徹底把這鎮子救回來。不過等我弄好之後，你可就認不出是我了。

column1: Fine.
column2: 好。

column1: In case I don't survive, I just want you to know that I respect you tremendously. You're a fine person. I'm honored to call you my friend.
column2: 萬一我沒能活下來，我只想讓你知道，我非常敬重你。你是個好人。能稱你一聲朋友是我的榮幸。

column1: And you are?
column2: 那你是哪位？

column1: Pharkas! Freddy Pharkas!
column2: 法卡斯！佛萊迪·法卡斯！

column1: Oh, right, right. Well, thanks, Fred, and good luck to you.
column2: 喔，對對對。那，謝了，佛萊迪，祝你好運。

column1: Sam! What the devil is going on here?
column2: 山姆！這裡到底是搞什麼鬼？

column1: Do I know you?
column2: 我認識你嗎？

column1: How could you let this... this scoundrel... swindle people out of their homes and life savings?
column2: 你怎麼能讓這個……這個惡棍……騙走大家的房子跟畢生積蓄？

column1: I'm Fr... waitaminnit, no, never mind, you don't know me. But the folks of Coarsegold are losing their shirts to this lying, thieving, cheatin', low-down, no-good, scum-sucking drifter!
column2: 我是法……等等，不，算了，你不認識我。反正粗金鎮的鄉親們正被這個滿口謊話、偷雞摸狗、坑蒙拐騙、下三濫、沒出息的流浪漢騙得傾家蕩產！

column1: Please, sir, don't talk that way about the Saloon's new owner.
column2: 先生，拜託別這樣說酒館的新老闆。

column1: I just work here now.
column2: 我現在只是在這裡打工而已。

column1: If you have any complaints or suggestions, feel free to put them in writing and I'll be happy to pass them along to the new management.
column2: 要是你有什麼抱怨或建議，歡迎寫下來，我很樂意轉達給新的經營團隊。

column1: Sam, what's going on outside? You got any idea?
column2: 山姆，外面到底怎麼回事？你有頭緒嗎？

column1: All I know is that someone paid some cowhands to stop in the middle of their cattle drive, come into town and shoot the place up. Dunno why.
column2: 我只知道有人花錢請了幾個牛仔，半路丟下趕牛的活兒，跑進鎮上四處開槍。不曉得為什麼。

column1: It's dangerous out there! A person might get shot!
column2: 外面很危險耶！搞不好會中槍的！

column1: Duh. But I figure they'll get bored sooner or later, or they'll shoot each other, or something.
column2: 廢話。不過我猜他們遲早會玩膩，不然就是互相打起來之類的。

column1: Hey, buddy, this isn't that kind of a bar.
column2: 嘿，老兄，這裡可不是那種酒吧。

column1: No, thanks. That stuff's too strong. I'll stick to grain alcohol as my beverage of choice, thank you very much.
column2: 不用了，謝謝。那玩意兒太烈了。我還是喝我的穀物酒就好，謝了。

column1: Looks like a roller-skate key to me. But you don't skate, do you? I didn't think so. So I must be wrong, right?
column2: 我看這像是溜冰鞋的鑰匙。不過你又不溜冰，對吧？我猜也是。所以我大概看錯了，是吧？

column1: Dammit, Freddy, I'm a Bartender, not a doctor.
column2: 天殺的，佛萊迪，我是個酒保，不是醫生。

column1: Looks like Doc's handwriting to me. But what do I know? I'm a bartender, not a licensed graphologist.
column2: 我看這像是大夫的筆跡。不過我懂什麼？我只是個酒保，又不是有執照的筆跡鑑定師。

column1: Hmm. One of these days, ol' Doc's gonna get a bit too soused and write a bad prescription, and there's really gonna be trouble. Malpractice insurance can really kill a guy.
column2: 嗯。總有一天，老大夫會喝得太醉，開錯處方箋，那時候麻煩就大了。醫療疏失險真是要人命啊。

column1: Nah, that's enough for Doc. I'm cuttin' him off for the time being. But feel free to keep the souvenir glass.
column2: 不，大夫喝夠了。我暫時不賣他了。不過那個紀念杯你留著沒關係。

column1: Say! That's pretty smart. Hope you got a lot of points for that.
column2: 唷！這招真聰明。希望你因此拿到不少分數。

column1: Doc's been messing up his prescriptions again, eh? Maybe I should cut him off for a while.
column2: 大夫又把處方箋搞砸啦？也許我該暫時不賣他酒了。

column1: No thanks, Freddy. But hey, if you get in any of that Dissolve-A-Goiter, my Mom could use some.
column2: 不用了，謝謝，佛萊迪。不過啊，你要是有消腫甲狀腺劑，我老媽用得上。

column1: I don't drink on the job.
column2: 我上班不喝酒。

column1: This isn't beer, this is water.
column2: 這不是啤酒，這是水。

column1: Yeah, these domestic beers are weak as hell. But hey, I stock what I can get.
column2: 對啊，這些本地啤酒淡得跟水一樣。不過呢，能進什麼貨我就賣什麼。

column1: If I had a goat, I'm sure he'd thank you. But I don't, so you just hang onto that. Okay? 'Kay.
column2: 要是我有隻山羊，牠一定會謝謝你。可惜我沒有，所以這個你自己留著吧。好嗎？好。

column1: That's mine, but you can keep it if you want. No ice around here anyway. But hey, if we ever get any icebergs drifting down Blackwater Creek or something, I'm going want that thing back.
column2: 那是我的，不過你想留著也行。反正這裡也沒什麼冰。不過啊，要是哪天黑水溪飄來冰山之類的，我可要把那玩意兒討回來。

column1: Charcoal? Well, thanks muchly, Fred, but I couldn't possibly accept such a gracious gift.
column2: 木炭？啊，多謝了，佛萊迪，不過我實在不能收下這麼貴重的禮物。

column1: No, but it's a thought.
column2: 不是，不過這倒是個想法。

column1: Well, sleep on it.
column2: 那，好好想想吧。

column1: A leather strap. You going to try the trick with the chicken, the leather strap, and the trampoline?
column2: 一條皮帶。你該不會想玩那個雞、皮帶跟彈簧床的把戲吧？

column1: What trick is that?
column2: 那是什麼把戲？

column1: Never mind.
column2: 沒事，算了。

column1: Don't need it, Fred. I figure I'm safe as long as I stay inside and don't use the lower two-thirds of my lungs.
column2: 用不著，佛萊迪。我想只要待在裡面，別用到下面三分之二的肺，我就安全了。

column1: Been making chemical deflatulent again, I see. Well, the only difference between men and boys is the size of their chemistry sets.
column2: 我看你又在調製化學消脹氣劑了。這個嘛，男人跟男孩的差別，就在於化學實驗組的大小。

column1: I think I'll stick to the usual maraschino cherries, olives, and twists of lime. But hey, thanks for thinking of me.
column2: 我看我還是用老規矩，櫻桃、橄欖跟萊姆片就好。不過啊，謝謝你想到我。

column1: Hey, Sam! Gimme a case of the beer you just got in from St. Louis!
column2: 喂，山姆！給我一箱你剛從聖路易進的啤酒！

column1: One case of Loebrau for the pharmacist, comin' up.
column2: 一箱羅布勞啤酒，給藥劑師，馬上來。

column1: Sam hands you a case of Loebrau, "The Beer That Gave St. Louis Blues."
column2: 山姆遞給你一箱羅布勞啤酒——「讓聖路易喝出藍調的啤酒」。

column1: Now, you know that this beer doesn't come corked, right? They're using some new-fangled pinched metal tops.
column2: 話說在前頭，這啤酒可不是軟木塞封口的喔。他們現在用的是那種新式的壓夾金屬蓋。

column1: No problem, Sam. I'll take care of it.
column2: 沒問題，山姆。我會處理好的。

column1: Okay, fine. That'll be $4.87.
column2: 好，沒問題。一共4.87元。

column1: Here ya go.
column2: 拿去吧。

column1: Nice bankroll. Come back anytime.
column2: 荷包挺鼓的嘛。歡迎隨時再來。

column1: No refunds, Fred. Like to help, but no can do.
column2: 概不退費，佛萊迪。我也想幫忙，但實在沒辦法。

column1: Sorry, Fred. They're no-deposit, no-return.
column2: 抱歉，佛萊迪。這些是不押瓶、不退瓶的。

column1: Bring 'em around in another, oh, ninety years or so, once the recycling laws are enacted.
column2: 大概再等個九十年吧，等回收法通過了再拿來吧。

column1: Got yourself a nice key there. Hang onto it. I use one just like it to open these new-fangled beer bottles!
column2: 你這鑰匙不錯嘛。留著吧。我就是用這種鑰匙開這些新式啤酒瓶的！

column1: Let's see. Ladder?
column2: 我瞧瞧。梯子？

column1: Bingo.
column2: 賓果。

column1: That was fun. Let's play that again sometime.
column2: 真好玩。改天再玩一次吧。

column1: A rope. Nice. Mine is longer, but of course you had no way of knowing that.
column2: 一條繩子。不錯。我的比較長，不過你當然沒辦法知道這件事。

column1: A lasso. You taking up wrangling?
column2: 一條套索。你是要去當牛仔了嗎？

column1: Hm. Can you say, "Yippie-ki-yay?"
column2: 嗯。你會說「呀呼咿呀嘿」嗎？

column1: Yippie-ki-yay.
column2: 呀呼咿呀嘿。

column1: I knew you could.
column2: 我就知道你會。

column1: Looks like some sort of water purifier. Nice job. You've made the sewers safe to drink again.
column2: 看起來像是某種淨水器。做得好。你讓下水道的水又能安心喝了。

column1: Looks like a pressurized canister of nitrous oxide.
column2: 看起來像是一罐加壓的一氧化二氮鋼瓶。

column1: Baking soda? Hey, if it was Baking Soda you wanted, why didn't you just say so? I've got a few tons of it under the counter here, just taking up space.
column2: 小蘇打粉？嘿，你要是想要小蘇打粉，幹嘛不早說？我這櫃檯底下就堆了好幾噸，占地方得很。

column1: Sam takes the postcards and quickly thumbs through them...
column2: 山姆接過明信片，飛快地翻閱了一遍……

column1: Got 'er... Want 'er... Got 'er... Got 'er... Want 'er... Got 'er... Want 'er... Got 'er... Want 'er... Got 'er.
column2: 有了……想要……有了……有了……想要……有了……想要……有了……想要……有了。

column1: He hands the cards back to you.
column2: 他把卡片還給你。

column1: Hey, you collect melted wax, too?
column2: 嘿，你也收集融化的蠟嗎？

column1: I hadn't thought about it.
column2: 我倒沒想過這個。

column1: You might want to. You've got a nice start there.
column2: 你該考慮一下。你這已經有個不錯的開頭了。

column1: Let's see. It's a knife, right?
column2: 我瞧瞧。這是把刀，對吧？

column1: Hmm. The last time I saw a key like this, it was sticking out of my roll-top desk at home. But hey, don't listen to me. I'm just a humble bartender.
column2: 嗯。我上次看到這種鑰匙，是插在我家那張捲蓋書桌上。不過啊，別聽我的。我不過是個卑微的酒保。

column1: That looks to me like one of the bank's safety-deposit box keys. But what do I know? I'm a bartender, not a locksmith.
column2: 我看這像是銀行保險箱的鑰匙。不過我懂什麼？我是酒保，不是鎖匠。

column1: You point the gun at Sam... and fire.
column2: 你把槍對準山姆……然後開槍。

column1: Whoa. I'm scared.
column2: 哇。嚇死我了。

column1: I've got a bullet-proof vest, hombre. I've been working here too long to be caught off-guard.
column2: 我穿了防彈背心，老兄。我在這幹太久了，可沒那麼容易被嚇到。

column1: Hot apple pie?
column2: 熱蘋果派？

column1: Want some fries with that?
column2: 要不要配點薯條？

column1: Thanks, but no thanks. My doctor tells me caffeine makes me jittery. 'Course, he might just be saying that because he's looking at me through jittery eyes.
column2: 謝了，但不用。我的醫生說咖啡因會讓我神經兮兮的。當然，他會這麼說，搞不好只是因為他自己也用一雙神經兮兮的眼睛看我。

column1: A fine cleaning kit you have there, Fred. Keep it. Maybe someday someone'll buy you a gun.
column2: 這清潔工具組挺不錯的，佛萊迪。你留著吧。說不定哪天有人會買把槍送你。

column1: Think a handful of bullets makes you some sort of badass hombre?
column2: 以為抓一把子彈就能讓你變成什麼狠角色了？

column1: Thanks for bringing this by, Fred, but no thanks. Maybe we could use it later, at playtime, after we've had our milk and put our heads down on the tables.
column2: 謝謝你拿這個來，佛萊迪，不過不用了。也許等我們喝完牛奶、趴在桌上睡午覺的「玩耍時間」再用得上吧。

column1: Nifty little medallion. Yours?
column2: 挺別緻的小獎章。是你的嗎？

column1: Not exactly.
column2: 不完全是。

column1: Well. Guess our little Freddy's all grown up and started out on a life of crime.
column2: 這樣啊。看來咱們家小佛萊迪已經長大了，還幹起犯罪的勾當了。

column1: No, thanks. I'm having mine bronzed. When the time comes, of course.
column2: 不用了，謝謝。我的那個要拿去鍍銅。當然啦，等時候到了再說。

column1: Is there something wrong with what I've already got on?
column2: 我現在身上穿的有什麼問題嗎？

column1: Not especially...
column2: 也沒有特別……

column1: Then you hang onto 'em. Besides, I like man-made fibers.
column2: 那你自己留著吧。再說，我還挺喜歡人造纖維的。

column1: Thanks, it'll be ready Tuesday. Nah, just yanking your reins. I don't know anything about this claim check.
column2: 謝了，禮拜二就會好。不，開玩笑的啦。這張取件單我什麼都不知道。

column1: Boots. Thanks for sharing that with me.
column2: 靴子。謝謝你跟我分享這個。

column1: You're not going to show me your handkerchief trick, are you?
column2: 你該不會又要跟我玩那套手帕戲法吧？

column1: Thanks anyway!
column2: 還是謝了！

column1: Sam scans the letter quickly.
column2: 山姆很快地瞄過信件。

column1: A letter to you from Phil Graves. So? Thanks for sharing it with me.
column2: 菲爾·葛雷夫斯寫給你的信。所以呢？謝謝你跟我分享啊。

column1: Yep, I've got one, too. It does get a little deep around here sometimes, doesn't it?
column2: 嗯，我也有一封。這裡有時候的確會有點深，你說是吧？

column1: I prefer the less pungent, more mellow, fart-in-a-bag. Thanks for thinking of me, though.
column2: 我比較喜歡沒那麼嗆、口味溫和一點的「屁在袋中」。不過還是謝謝你想到我。

column1: Nice of you to consider me, Fred. But I don't get motion sickness. You hang onto it.
column2: 你有想到我真好，佛萊迪。不過我不會暈車暈船，你自己留著吧。

column1: Is this for me? What a pal. Tell ya what, though, why don't you keep it for me? I've already got all that manure that Sadie, Smithie, Doc, and Chester brought me last month.
column2: 這是要給我的？夠朋友。不過這樣吧，你幫我保管就好？莎蒂、鐵匠史密、大夫跟切斯特上個月送我的那堆糞肥我都還留著呢。

column1: Looks like you've been doing some lost-wax casting. Not bad, for an amateur.
column2: 看來你有在玩脫蠟鑄造啊。以業餘的來說算不錯了。

column1: Doing some lost-wax casting, are you? What a guy.
column2: 在玩脫蠟鑄造啊？真有你的。

column1: Nice mold. You're a multitalented individual, Fred.
column2: 模子做得不錯。你還真是多才多藝，佛萊迪。

column1: It's a good likeness, but is it art?
column2: 做得挺像的，但這算是藝術嗎？

column1: No, thanks. I've always heard it's unsafe to drink other people's prescriptions.
column2: 不了，謝謝。我一直聽說喝別人的處方藥不安全。

column1: Not in the market, thanks.
column2: 我沒興趣買，謝了。

column1: Looks like somebody scratched. And badly, too.
column2: 看來有人棄權了，而且輸得很慘。

column1: You've got more important things to do right now than play with those balls!
column2: 你現在有更重要的事要做，別在那邊玩球了！

column1: This roulette table is for Casino Night.
column2: 這張輪盤桌是賭場之夜專用的。

column1: Now's a bad time to go for a spin. You've got responsibilities!
column2: 現在不是轉輪盤的時候，你可是有正事要辦！

column1: This dice game is known as Chuck-A-Luck. Since you're living in Coarsegold, you've apparently chucked your luck already.
column2: 這種骰子遊戲叫「幸運骰」。既然你住在粗金鎮，看來你的運氣早就被丟光了。

column1: It won't do you any good. The dice are missing and this isn't Casino Night.
column2: 玩了也沒用，骰子不見了，而且今天也不是賭場之夜。

column1: It's a Moose head. The only domestic brand Sam serves!
column2: 這是一顆麋鹿頭。山姆這裡唯一供應的「國產」貨色！

column1: Glancing around to make sure nobody's looking, you turn to the moosehead and say...
column2: 你左右張望確定沒人在看，然後轉頭對麋鹿頭說……

column1: Hey, moose! Decided to quit while you were "a head?" (CHUCKLE)
column2: 嘿，麋鹿！決定要見好就「首」啦？（輕笑）

column1: You chuckle quietly until you hear the moose reply, "Hey, buddy, you're really funny! Why, that's the first time I've heard that joke... TODAY!!"
column2: 你正暗自竊笑，卻聽見麋鹿回答：「嘿，老兄，你真幽默！要知道，這個笑話我今天可是……第一次聽到！！」

column1: It's way out of reach. Just like prosperity.
column2: 那太高了，搆不到，就像榮華富貴一樣，可望不可及。

column1: Here, moosey moosey! Have some cashola!
column2: 來，麋鹿麋鹿！賞你點銀兩！

column1: The moose just looks at you as if to say, "I don't need your money. All I need is a home to hang my head on."
column2: 麋鹿只是看著你，彷彿在說：「我不需要你的錢，我只需要一面牆掛我的頭。」

column1: That would certainly be adding insult to injury!
column2: 那樣做簡直是傷口上灑鹽！

column1: It's a hat rack, where the patrons hang their hats, coats, gun belts... and the occasional short stranger!
column2: 這是頂帽架，客人們把帽子、外套、槍帶都掛在上面……偶爾還會掛個矮個子的陌生人！

column1: It wouldn't do to be caught walking off with somebody's hat, coat, gun belt... or whatever.
column2: 要是被抓到順手牽走別人的帽子、外套、槍帶……什麼的，可就不妙了。

column1: This is no time to be messing with that!
column2: 現在不是碰那個的時候！

column1: It's a likeness of Chastity, one of the girls over at Madame Ovaree's. She's so lifelike, you feel as if you could just reach out and touch her. And you'd save $2.00 that way, too!
column2: 這是貞蒂的畫像，歐薇莉夫人那邊的姑娘之一。畫得栩栩如生，讓你感覺伸手就能摸到她。而且這樣還能省下兩塊錢呢！

column1: Chastity, Chastity, Chastity.
column2: 貞蒂，貞蒂，貞蒂。

column1: Shh, don't talk to me while I'm painting.
column2: 噓，我畫畫的時候別跟我說話。

column1: That'll be twenty bucks for a quick feel of the painting.
column2: 想摸一下這幅畫，二十塊錢。

column1: Sorry. Never mind, then.
column2: 抱歉，那就算了。

column1: Doesn't matter, there's nothing behind the painting anyway.
column2: 沒差，反正畫後面什麼也沒有。

column1: This is another of the Saloon's rugged, rough-hewn tables. It's reserved for down-on-their-luck losers, imbeciles, sad sacks, hopeless cases, and deadbeats. That is to say: General Admission.
column2: 這是酒館裡另一張粗製濫造的桌子，專門保留給倒楣鬼、蠢蛋、可憐蟲、沒救的傢伙跟賴皮鬼。也就是說：一般入場。

column1: You try to move it, but the layers of beer on the floor only allow it to move an inch or so, making a sound like velcro being pulled apart. If you've ever been to a beer hall or movie theatre, you know the feeling.
column2: 你想搬動它，但地板上一層層乾掉的啤酒只讓它挪動了一吋左右，發出像魔鬼氈被撕開的聲音。如果你去過啤酒屋或電影院，就知道那種感覺。

column1: The Saloon is filled with rugged rough-hewn tables. This particular one is reserved for rowdy, ugly, nasty and mean drunks. In other words, it's open seating.
column2: 酒館裡滿是粗製濫造的桌子。這一張是保留給粗魯、醜陋、討人厭又兇惡的醉漢的。換句話說，自由入座。

column1: This table is glued to the floor by thousands of layers of mostly-dried beer.
column2: 這張桌子被幾千層幾乎乾透的啤酒黏在地板上了。

column1: This is the Wheel of Fortune table. Guess the right number and Sam will tell you your fortune.
column2: 這是命運之輪桌。猜對號碼，山姆就會幫你算命。

column1: There's nothing on the table worth taking. And the table itself isn't even worth taking.
column2: 桌上沒什麼值得拿的東西，桌子本身也不值得拿。

column1: This honky-tonk piano is 82-and-a-half keys of pure musical entertainment.
column2: 這台酒館鋼琴有八十二點五個琴鍵，純粹的音樂娛樂。

column1: Sorry, you're not allowed to play the piano. This is a Union set, folks!
column2: 抱歉，你不能彈這台鋼琴。各位，這可是工會的地盤！

column1: This is a chandelier. Most nights you can find at least one or two drunk 'n rowdy cowhands swinging from this thing. Business must be a mite slow today.
column2: 這是一盞吊燈。大多數夜晚都能看到一兩個醉醺醺的牛仔在上面盪來盪去。今天生意大概有點冷清。

column1: You're not nearly drunk enough to do any chandelier-swinging. And you can't get drunk... you're the Designated Hero!
column2: 你醉得還不夠格去盪吊燈。而且你根本醉不了……你可是「指定英雄」！

column1: A beautiful mural from the Starving Artists of Oxnard. They used to hold sales a couple times a year over in the lobby of the Dirty Sheets Hotel.
column2: 這是一幅來自「牛津鎮飢餓藝術家」的美麗壁畫。他們以前每年都會在「髒床單旅館」大廳辦一兩次特賣會。

column1: There's nothing behind the painting (except for a $2.00 price tag).
column2: 這幅畫後面什麼也沒有（除了一張兩塊錢的價格標籤）。

column1: It appears to be a tiny picture of some field mice playing poker.
column2: 看起來是一幅田鼠打撲克牌的小畫。

column1: What, and steal an original Stuart Little oil painting?
column2: 什麼，偷走一幅真跡的「小老鼠斯圖特」油畫？

column1: Sam Andreas's burnished maplewood bar is the one bar to belly up to when you're bellying up to more than one!
column2: 山姆·安德烈亞斯這張擦得發亮的楓木吧檯，是你要一連跑好幾家酒吧時，最值得倚靠的那一家！

column1: Try as you might, you can't seem to take the bar. Sam must've nailed it in place so that nobody throws it at nobody else during a brawl.
column2: 你費盡力氣，還是搬不動這張吧檯。山姆一定把它釘死了，免得打群架時有人把它扔向別人。

column1: Sam has stocked the bar with every brand of cheap rotgut listed in the Mr. Fresno's Saloonkeeper Guide:
column2: 山姆把《弗雷斯諾先生酒館經營指南》裡列出的每一種廉價劣酒都備齊了：

column1: Even though you're one of his more refined customers, if you try taking one of those bottles, you'll be doing shots of hot lead the hard way -- directly through the abdomen!
column2: 就算你算是他比較有格調的客人，要是敢拿走那些酒瓶，你就會硬生生地「乾一杯」熱鉛──直接灌進肚子裡！

column1: It's the Wheel of Fortune, used mostly on the Golden Balls' Wednesday Casino Night. But don't come in on Tuesday; that's Kink Night. They strap Whittlin' Willy to the Wheel of Fortune, and... Oh, never mind, you don't want to know!
column2: 這是命運之輪，主要用在「金球酒館」每週三的賭場之夜。不過別在星期二來，那是「怪癖之夜」。他們會把削木威利綁在命運之輪上，然後……啊，算了，你不會想知道的！

column1: You're tempted to spin the wheel and shout, "Big money! Big money!" But you hate looking like an absolute moron.
column2: 你很想轉動輪盤大喊：「大錢！大錢！」但你討厭讓自己看起來像個十足的白痴。

column1: This is the world-famous Golden Balls Stage. Most days, you can find major vaudeville acts here, bringing their own unique brands of music, comedy, dance, and magic to the deserving folks of Coarsegold.
column2: 這是舉世聞名的「金球舞台」。大多數日子裡，這裡都有知名的雜耍表演，為粗金鎮的鄉親們帶來各具特色的音樂、喜劇、舞蹈與魔術。

column1: That's not the way to get onto the stage. It takes practice, practice, practice.
column2: 那不是上台的辦法。要上台，得練習、練習、再練習。

column1: Welcome to Sam Andreas's Golden Balls Saloon. He was going to call it "Sam Andreas's Nugget," but decided that had disgusting sexual overtones.
column2: 歡迎光臨山姆·安德烈亞斯的「金球酒館」。他原本想叫它「山姆·安德烈亞斯的金塊」，但後來覺得那個名字有噁心的性暗示。

column1: Most saloon fixtures won't talk to the customers.
column2: 大部分酒館裡的擺設都不會跟客人說話。

column1: That's Sam's property. Keep your prescription-fillin' hands offa it.
column2: 那是山姆的東西，你那雙開藥的手離它遠一點。

column1: This looks suspiciously like a door.
column2: 這看起來十有八九就是扇門。

column1: Say! That's Wheaton "Aces" Hall, the infamous riverboat gambler!
column2: 咦！那是惠頓「王牌」霍爾，惡名昭彰的河船賭徒！

column1: How peculiar. Why would a riverboat gambler, especially one as successful and popular as Aces, come to a two-bit burg like Coarsegold? This can't be a coincidence. Someone must've sent him a wire. But WHY?
column2: 真奇怪。像王牌這樣既成功又出名的河船賭徒，怎麼會跑來粗金鎮這種不入流的小地方？這絕不是巧合，一定有人拍電報找他來的。但是……為什麼？

column1: How's the game going, slick?
column2: 牌局打得怎麼樣啊，帥哥？

column1: Who wants to know?
column2: 你問這個幹嘛？

column1: Just interested.
column2: 只是好奇而已。

column1: Well, it's going very nicely, Justin. I've won the deeds to the Saloon, the Cafe, the School, and several other plots of land. My employer will be pleased. I should have the rest of the town sewn up in a few minutes.
column2: 嗯，賈斯汀，牌局進行得挺順利的。我已經贏到酒館、餐館、學校，還有好幾塊地的地契了。我的雇主一定會很滿意。再過幾分鐘，我就能把全鎮都收進口袋了。

column1: Who's your employer?
column2: 你的雇主是誰？

column1: Sorry, that information is covered under the terms of boss-hustler privilege.
column2: 抱歉，這項資訊受「老闆與騙徒特權保密協議」保護。

column1: Doesn't it bother you that you're bilking these people out of their homes and businesses?
column2: 你騙走這些人的家業，難道都不會良心不安嗎？

column1: I've seen their homes and businesses. Trust me. I'm doing them a favor.
column2: 我見過他們的家跟店。相信我，我這是在幫他們一個忙。

column1: I'm making a citizen's arrest. You're cheating, I know it.
column2: 我要以公民身分逮捕你。你出老千，我心裡有數。

column1: Citizen's arrest? Citizen's arrest? (CHUCKLE)
column2: 公民逮捕？公民逮捕？（輕笑）

column1: Don't even try it. The Sheriff knows I'm here. In fact, I have his blessing.
column2: 想都別想。警長知道我在這裡，事實上，我還得到他的祝福呢。

column1: Lay a hand on me and they'll be sifting your corpse for buckshot.
column2: 敢動我一根手指頭，他們就會從你屍體裡篩散彈了。

column1: Geez! In Europe, I hear men touch each other all the time, and hardly ever shoot each other for it.
column2: 天啊！聽說在歐洲，男人常常互相碰來碰去，也很少會為此開槍打對方。

column1: Yeah, well, over here, we're much more civilized.
column2: 是啊，不過在這裡，我們可文明多了。

column1: Get away from me, kid, ya bother me.
column2: 離我遠一點，小鬼，你煩到我了。

column1: You can't shoot him in cold blood, Freddy. It runs contrary to every fiber of your being! Besides, there are better ways to impress the ladies!
column2: 你不能冷血地開槍打他，佛萊迪。這跟你的本性完全相違背！再說，討女孩子歡心還有更好的辦法！

column1: It's Doc's whisky glass, mostly empty right now.
column2: 這是大夫的威士忌杯，現在幾乎空了。

column1: You pick up the whisky glass.
column2: 你拿起了威士忌杯。

column1: It's one of Sam's rickety old tables.
column2: 這是山姆那些搖搖晃晃的舊桌子之一。

column1: There's nothing on it worth taking, and you can't move it.
column2: 上面沒什麼值得拿的東西，你也搬不動它。

column1: It's the table usually reserved for the guys who play poker. And the women who love them!
column2: 這張桌子通常是留給打撲克的男人，還有愛他們的女人！

column1: You're not the type to gamble. In other words, you're POOR!
column2: 你不是那種會賭博的人。換句話說，你「窮」！

column1: You don't want to start playing Poker with this guy. He's known far and wide as a cheat. In fact, if you could catch him red-handed, you might be able to stop him before he wins away every last piece of property in town!
column2: 你可不會想跟這傢伙玩撲克。他出老千的惡名遠播。事實上，要是你能當場抓到他作弊，或許就能阻止他把全鎮最後一塊地也贏走！

column1: There won't be another poker game here for quite awhile.
column2: 這裡有好一陣子不會再開撲克局了。

column1: Ah'm gonna have to arrest yew for attempted murder, stranger. Yew shouldna' oughtta shot him in cold blood like that. Gamblin, ah kin overlook; suspicious accidents, ah kin overlook; unfortunate co-inky-dinks, ah kin overlook. But you shot this boy straight out, son. Hate to hear whut th' Judge is gonna have to say about this! Why, I think yer gonna HANG, boy!
column2: 俺得以殺人未遂的罪名逮捕你了，陌生人。你不該那樣冷血地開槍打他。賭博嘛，俺可以睜隻眼閉隻眼；可疑的意外，俺也能睜隻眼閉隻眼；倒楣的巧合，俺照樣睜隻眼閉隻眼。但你這回是明目張膽開槍打這小子，孩子。真不想聽法官會怎麼說這事！哎呀，俺看你這下要「上吊」啦，孩子！

column1: This is a chandelier. Most nights you can find at least one or two drunk 'n' rowdy cowhands swinging from this thing. Business must be a mite slow today.
column2: 這是一盞吊燈。大多數夜晚都能看到一兩個醉醺醺的牛仔在上面盪來盪去。今天生意大概有點冷清。

column1: It's way over your head. Like most of these jokes!
column2: 那太高了，你搆不到，就跟這裡大多數的笑話一樣──你也「聽」不懂！

column1: It's Baa-Bara Mandrill and the Baa-bettes, stars of stage, screen and barnyard!
column2: 這是「咩芭拉·曼德瑞爾」與「咩咩女郎」，舞台、螢幕與牧場三棲巨星！

column1: Shear it off! Shear it |c2|ALL|c| off!
column2: 剪光牠！把牠剪個|c2|精光|c|！

column1: Don't touch 'em, you'll throw off their timing. Besides, the lanolin will make your hands soft and squishy like a girl's.
column2: 別碰牠們，你會打亂牠們的節奏。而且，羊毛脂會讓你的手變得像女生一樣軟綿綿的。

column1: It's Neville Shute, The Piano Player. He's Doing the Best He Can!
column2: 這是內維爾·舒特，鋼琴師。他已經盡力而為了！

column1: Play it, Neville.
column2: 彈吧，內維爾。

column1: Neville, in order not to lose track of the piece he's playing, says nothing. However, he raises his eyebrows as if to say, "Certainly, sir, I'll be happy to play whatever selection you'd care to hear, and what's more, I'll make this old piano sound like a whole orchestra!"
column2: 內維爾為了不彈亂手上這首曲子，什麼也沒說。不過他挑了挑眉毛，彷彿在說：「當然了，先生，您想聽什麼我都樂意彈，而且我還能讓這台老鋼琴聽起來像一整支管弦樂團呢！」

column1: Don't throttle him, he's doing the best he can.
column2: 別掐他脖子，他已經盡力而為了。

column1: Neville Shute earns a good salary, plus tips. He doesn't need your contributions.
column2: 內維爾·舒特薪水不差，還有小費，他不需要你的「贊助」。

column1: Hey! You're not supposed to shoot him! If you don't like his music, turn down your volume!
column2: 嘿！你不該開槍打他的！要是不喜歡他的音樂，把你的音量調小一點就是了！

column1: It's Ollie Oxenfree, the guy who owns the fig farms on the northern side of Collier Bluff! He's the worst gambler in town! He'll lose the entire North 40 in no time!
column2: 這是奧利·奧克斯弗里，柯利爾崖北邊那片無花果農場的主人！他是全鎮最爛的賭徒！他很快就會把整片北方四十畝地都輸光！

column1: Ollie, listen to me! Don't do it! It's not worth it!
column2: 奧利，聽我說！別這樣做！這不值得！

column1: Don't waste your breath. Ollie needs what little concentration he has just to hang onto his farm a few minutes longer.
column2: 別白費脣舌了。奧利那點僅剩的專注力，全用來讓他的農場多撐個幾分鐘。

column1: Ollie ignores you. Apparently he's a little preoccupied with this "losing your home and livelihood" business.
column2: 奧利不理你。看來他正忙著處理「賠上家園跟生計」這檔事，有點分身乏術。

column1: Don't bother trying to distract Ollie with doodads and knicknacks. His attention is firmly established elsewise.
column2: 別費心用些小玩意兒去分散奧利的注意力了，他的心思早就穩穩地放在別處了。

column1: Ollie's not worth shooting. However, he IS worth hanging. Maybe in the sequel?
column2: 奧利不值得你開槍打他。不過他倒是很值得被吊死。也許留到續集再說吧？

column1: Hey, these chairs don't have any chewing gum stuck to the undersides! But look out for wads of chewing tobacco.
column2: 嘿，這些椅子底下倒是沒黏口香糖！不過要小心嚼菸草的殘渣。

column1: Those chairs are for drinking customers only, and if I'm not mistaken, you're the Designated Hero this week.
column2: 那些椅子只留給喝酒的客人坐，而如果我沒記錯，你這禮拜可是「指定英雄」。

column1: Gambling away his Keg 'n Barrel shop is Cooper "Coop" Cooper. He, his wife, his children, and his parents all work in his barrel shop. He's a cooper, she's a cooper, they're all coopers. (Wouldn't you like to be a cooper, too?)
column2: 正在把自己「木桶行」輸光的是庫珀「庫普」庫珀。他、他老婆、他的孩子還有他爸媽，全都在他的木桶行裡幫忙。他是箍桶匠，她也是箍桶匠，一家子全是箍桶匠。（你難道不想也當個箍桶匠嗎？）

column1: Hey, Cooper! Don't do it! You'll lose everything!
column2: 嘿，庫珀！別這樣！你會輸光一切的！

column1: He ignores you. You're spoiling his lack of concentration!
column2: 他不理你。你正在破壞他那「毫無專注力」的專注力！

column1: Don't bother him now, he's trying to recoop his losses!
column2: 現在別煩他，他正想辦法「箍」回他的損失呢！

column1: Cooper apparently isn't interested in "Show 'n Tell."
column2: 庫珀顯然對這種「拿出來獻寶」的把戲沒興趣。

column1: But... but Cooper's got a wife and kids! Maybe that's why he's in the Saloon?
column2: 可是……可是庫珀有老婆孩子啊！也許這就是他跑來酒館的原因？

column1: That's Muff Potter. Nice to see him and Joe getting along again! He owns -- or at least, he DID own until he started gambling today -- a huge tract of land along the south side of town, where Chinatown used to be.
column2: 那是莫夫·波特。真高興看到他跟喬又和好了！他擁有──或者說，在他今天開始賭博之前「曾經」擁有──鎮上南邊一大片土地，就是以前的中國城那一帶。

column1: Hey, Muff! Don't play with this guy, he cheats!
column2: 嘿，莫夫！別跟這傢伙玩，他會出老千！

column1: Muff nods his head in agreement, then returns to playing. Muff's never been too bright.
column2: 莫夫點頭表示同意，然後又繼續賭了下去。莫夫向來不太聰明。
